Each exported gadget carries: dashboard id (decimal text), dashboard owner's user key, gadget id (text), position (column and row; 0 when Jira has none), module key, all user preferences as a string map (copied), the OpenSocial spec URI text (or none) and the colour constant name (e.g. `color1`, or none). These become the `<gadget>` elements of the backup's `gadgets` section, which cloud-data-migrator writes only on the Forge path.

For a Jira user-history type (e.g. `UserHistoryItem.PROJECT`, `ASSIGNEE`, `USED_USER`) and a user, the module returns the entity ids of that user's Jira history items (`UserHistoryManager.getHistory(type, user)`) as an insertion-ordered set in Jira's order (most recent first), duplicates removed. A null type or user gives an empty set; a user key that no longer resolves gives an empty set.
The mapping variant converts each id with the given function and drops ids mapped to null, keeping the order (used by option sources to turn ids into valid projects or users).

Results are cached per (history type name, user key) in a local (per node) cache that expires an entry 60 s after its last access (adjustable through a tuning dark feature named after the implementing class plus `.timeout`, in seconds, which is not contract; the JVM property `structure.cache.expiration-override` overrides all such timeouts). Clearing all plugin caches empties it; clearing one user's caches removes only that user's entries. A failure while loading yields an empty set (logged), not an exception.

For a project id and a user the module returns the set of ids of the agile boards that gh-integration reports for that user and project (boards whose filter covers the project). A null project id or user, an unknown project or a user key that no longer resolves gives an empty set.

Results are cached per (project id, user key) in a local cache with a 60 s expire-after-access (tunable like recents-search-service's cache; JVM property `structure.cache.expiration-override` wins); clearing all caches empties it, clearing a user's caches removes that user's entries; a loading failure yields an empty set.

The module renders the edit control of an option-picker field (single or multi select) from the plugin's Velocity template `/templates/structure/field/options-edit.vm` and returns the trimmed HTML. The template receives: `spec` (the option source spec as JSON), `endpoint` = `search` when the source is searchable (more options than its search threshold, always for users) else `list`, `values` (the selected values; empty for null), `pickerClass` = `s-option-single-select` or `s-option-multi-select`, `multiple` (false/true), `field`, `optionSource`, `valuesString` (the selected values' option ids joined with `, `), plus the Jira edit-issue rendering helpers.

The module creates the short-lived per-key caches used by recents-search-service and suggested-sprint-boards-service: each is a local cache named `<owner class>.cache` whose entries expire 60 s after last access (timeout dark feature `<owner class>.timeout`; JVM property `structure.cache.expiration-override` wins), loaded on demand; a load failure returns the caller's default value (logged) instead of throwing; clearing can drop all entries or only the entries whose key matches a condition.

For an asynchronous REST request without `jobId`, the handler submits the request's computation to job-manager on the named executor and waits for its result; with a `jobId` it does not start anything and waits for that job instead.

The wait is bounded by the REST async timeout, read once at start-up from dark feature `structure.rest.async.timeout` in milliseconds (default 3000). When the job finishes within the wait its result is returned and the job is cancelled/forgotten in job-manager (so its id becomes unknown). When it does not, the handler answers with only the job id: REST 200 with `async-job-ticket` `{"jobId": n}`; the job keeps running and a later call with that id waits again.

A `jobId` unknown to job-manager (never existed, already collected, or lost by restart) throws `StructureErrors.JOB_NOT_EXISTS` with message `Job <id> is not found.` (REST 404, code 4603). A `jobId` of a job whose result is of a different type than the endpoint expects throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` 'Incorrect job ID for this resource' (REST 400).

If the job failed, its cause is rethrown as is when it is a `StructureException`, an invalid-data error, an error-response error, any `RuntimeException` or an `Error`; any other checked cause is wrapped in `StructureErrors.GENERIC_ERROR` with the cause's message. An interrupt while waiting re-sets the thread's interrupt flag and throws `StructureErrors.GENERIC_ERROR` without message.

For testing, JVM system property `structure.testing.rest.async.forceDelay` (milliseconds, read when the handler is created; default 0 = off) makes every newly started job sleep that long before computing (logged), so clients exercise the job-id protocol.

The checker answers whether the current user may see <product> UI: true exactly when the helper's '<product> is available to the current user' check is true (the plugin is enabled and the user has the app's 'use' permission). Its licence part is always satisfied (the replacement has no licence checks). It drives the issue-page decorator condition (`adjustIssuePageCond`).

The checker answers whether Structure should appear on the issue page: the value of dark feature `structure.feature.showOnIssuePage` (an application property, else a JVM system property; true only when it equals `true` ignoring case; default true when neither is set), read on every call. It does not look at the user. It drives the issue-page web resources (`adjustIssuePage`).

Rendering the login page for the external <product> gadget (shown when an anonymous viewer must sign in) renders the gadget login Velocity template (bundled resource `/templates/structure/macro/gadgetlogin.vm`, read as UTF-8) with two parameters: `action` (the calling web action) and `page` (the login page model below), and returns the HTML. A missing template resource fails with `NullPointerException`.

The login page model is built from Jira: the login properties that Jira's `LoginService` computes for the (possibly null) logged-in user and the original HTTP request (obtained by reflection; if that is impossible, `IllegalStateException` 'Failed to get LoginProperties instance from LoginService'), an `I18nHelper` for that user, the application option `jira.show.contact.administrators.form`, and the login strategy from dark feature `structure.jira.login.strategy` (`embedded` or `explicit`, any case; any other value, default `auto`, means embedded on Jira below 10.2, so embedded on the pinned Jira 9.12).

The model exposes: the context path; public mode; 'forgot password' shown unless user or password management is external; 'remember me' shown when cookies are allowed; captcha shown when Jira's elevated security check is shown and the strategy is not explicit; captcha timestamp = now; the admin contact form flag; 'auth resource used' = explicit strategy; an error message only for POST requests that did not log in: communication error `gadget.login.error.communication`, other login error `gadget.login.error.misc`, failed by permissions `gadget.login.invalidloginpermissions` (with Jira's contact-admin link), else `gadget.login.invalidcaptcha` when the captcha is shown or `gadget.login.invalidlogin`; and the minimum TOTP code length from dark feature `structure.jira.login.totp.minSymbols` (default 6).

An option source is chosen by the spec's `sourceKey`: `PROJECTS`, `ISSUE_TYPES`, `PRIORITIES`, `VERSIONS`, `COMPONENTS`, `SPRINTS`, `USERS`, `GROUPS`, `FIELD_OPTIONS`, or `EMPTY` (a source with no options that is not selectable, so REST answers `empty-ok`). A null spec or an unknown key gives no source. Spec JSON: `{"sourceKey":…,"projectId":<long or null>,"filters":{…}}`; a filter flag is on when its value is boolean true or the string `true`.

'Project visible to the user' means: the project exists, the user has the view-issues project action and Jira's BROWSE_PROJECTS permission in it (anonymous users as Jira grants them). Unless the caller overrides the security check (REST never does), projects, versions and components outside visible projects are dropped, and project-dependent lists for an invisible project are empty.

Issue types, priorities, versions and components: with a `projectId` the options are those of that project (issue types of its scheme, priorities of its priority scheme, its versions, its components), empty when the project does not exist or is not visible; without `projectId` they are empty, unless the security check is overridden, in which case all of them in Jira are used.

`PROJECTS`: all projects including archived ones (only active ones when `excludeInactive` is on), filtered by `checkCreateIssues` (user has CREATE_ISSUES), `checkStructureConfig` (project enabled for <product>) and visibility. Option id = project id; name = project key (lookup by name uses the key); label = `<name> (<KEY>)`; icon = Jira's small project avatar URL. Group: `s.w.options.group.projects.archived` for archived projects, else `s.w.options.group.projects.recent` when the project is in the user's Jira project history (recents-search-service), else `s.w.options.group.projects.all`; ordered recent, all, archived, then by project name. Suggestions = the user's recent projects that are valid options, in history order.

`ISSUE_TYPES` (with `excludeSubtasks` dropping sub-task types) and `PRIORITIES`: option id = the constant's id, name = its name, label = its translated name, icon = its complete icon URL, no group, ordered by name.

`VERSIONS`: option id = version id, name and label = version name; `excludeInactive` drops archived versions. Group key: `s.w.options.group.versions.archived` for archived, `s.w.options.group.versions.released` for released, else `s.w.options.group.versions.unreleased`. The ordering is meant to be unreleased, released, archived, but it looks up group keys spelled `s.ext.options.group.versions.*`, so no key matches and versions are ordered by name only (as the original does). Lookup by name uses Jira's versions-by-name and returns the first exact-name match that passes the filters; with a `projectId`, a version is a valid option only if it belongs to that project.

`COMPONENTS`: option id = component id, name and label = component name; `excludeInactive` drops archived components; group `s.w.options.group.components.archived` for archived components, none otherwise; ordered by name (the archived group's intended position is likewise lost). Lookup by name uses Jira's case-insensitive component-name search, then requires an exact-name match; with a `projectId` a component must belong to that project.

`SPRINTS`: all sprints known to gh-integration (`excludeInactive` drops closed sprints); option id = sprint id, name = sprint name, label = gh-integration's formatted sprint name for the user. When the spec's project is visible, sprints of the boards suggested for that project and user (suggested-sprint-boards-service) get group `s.w.planning-task.relevant-sprints.group.suggestions` and sort first, then by name. Suggestions are always empty (the suggested sprints are never offered first in the picker) (as the original does).

`USERS`: all Jira users (`excludeInactive` drops inactive users; `checkAssignable` with a `projectId` keeps only users with ASSIGNABLE_USER in that project). Option id = user key, name = username, label = `<display name> (<username>)` or, when the caller may see e-mail addresses, `<display name> - <email> (<username>)`; icon = `<base url>/secure/useravatar?ownerId=<user key>`; ordered by display name; always searchable. The source is selectable only when the caller has Jira's global USER_PICKER (browse users) permission. Search uses Jira's `UserSearchService.findUsers` with the given limit, empty query allowed, inactive users included unless `excludeInactive`, e-mail matching when e-mails are visible, restricted to the spec's project when given, unsorted, permission check ignored, then the filters applied.

User suggestions: with `checkAssignable`, the caller first, then the caller's Jira history of assignees, then of used users, without duplicates; otherwise the history of used users only; keys that do not resolve to a user that passes the filters are dropped.
`GROUPS`: all Jira groups; option id, name and label = group name; lookup by id or name asks Jira's `GroupManager` directly (no filter); ordered by name.

`FIELD_OPTIONS`: with filter `customField` (a custom field id) the options of that field's configuration relevant to the spec's project (only when visible, else the global context) and filter `issueTypeId`; an unknown field gives none; without `customField` all options of all fields. `excludeInactive` drops disabled options. Option id = option id (-1 when null), name and label = option value; ordered by the option's configured sequence. With `customField` an option is valid only if it is in that list.

For every source except users and groups: an option is valid when it passes the source's filters and, when the spec has a `projectId`, the project rule (versions/components must belong to the project; other sources must be in the source's collection); lookup by id returns the option only if valid (projects, versions, components, sprints, users resolve the id through Jira; the others search the filtered collection by id text). A source is searchable (the picker uses search instead of a full list) when it has more options than its threshold, dark feature `structure.options.search.threshold` (default 50). Placeholders are localized in the current user's locale from `s.w.planning-task.<project|issueType|priority|versions|components|sprint>.placeholder`, `s.w.memoDetails.fields.user.hint` for users, none for groups and field options.

When the caller asks for collection caching, each source instance reads its underlying Jira collection once and reuses it for all later calls on that instance; otherwise every call reads Jira again. REST (`/rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/*`) uses fresh, uncached sources per request.

The spec used for a planning-task / generic item field: no spec when the field's type has no option source key; for `FIELD_OPTIONS`, filters `customField` = the field id, `excludeInactive` = true and `issueTypeId` when given; for field `project`: `checkStructureConfig`, `checkCreateIssues`, `excludeInactive`; for field `assignee`: `excludeInactive`, `checkAssignable`; otherwise by source: PROJECTS `checkStructureConfig`+`excludeInactive`, VERSIONS/COMPONENTS/USERS/SPRINTS `excludeInactive`, ISSUE_TYPES `excludeSubtasks`. The `projectId` is kept only for ISSUE_TYPES, PRIORITIES, VERSIONS, COMPONENTS, FIELD_OPTIONS, SPRINTS and the `assignee` field.

All option lists of this module draw on 'the projects in scope': the projects structure-configuration currently has enabled for <product> that the current user can browse (BROWSE_PROJECTS), recomputed on every call.

The supported fields are the Jira navigable fields available to the current user that have an option source: system fields `project`, `status`, `issuetype`, `versions`, `fixVersions`, `priority`, `reporter`, `creator`, `assignee`, `labels`, `components`, `resolution`, and custom fields whose type is (first match wins) multi-user, user, multi-group, version, labels, multi-select, select, cascading select, project, an Advanced Roadmaps team field (when that app's teams are available), the Jira Software sprint field, a Tempo team field (when Tempo Teams is available) or an Assets object field (when enabled). When Structure is not enabled for all projects, a custom field is listed only if one of its associated projects is in scope (so a global-context custom field, which has no associated projects, is left out (as the original does)). A field-list failure gives an empty list (logged).

Looking up one supported field by id returns the field when it exists, has an option source, and is either a system field, a global-context custom field, or a custom field associated with a project in scope; otherwise null.

For list-based fields, searching filters each group's options to those whose label has a word starting with the trimmed query (regex word boundary followed by the literal text, case-insensitive); an empty query keeps all. With a page size the group keeps at most that many options; the group's `total` stays the number of options before the text filter. Unknown or unsupported fields give no groups.

Fields with a 'no value' option add it (id `special:EMPTY`) at the start of every returned group, beyond the page size, when its label lower-cased contains the query lower-cased (the query is not trimmed here): `versions`, `fixVersions` and version custom fields 'No version' (`common.filters.noversion`), `components` (`common.filters.nocomponent`), `resolution` (`common.resolution.unresolved`), `reporter` (`reporter.types.noreporter`), `assignee` (`assignee.types.unassigned`), `creator`, user, multi-user and multi-group custom fields (`userpicker.empty`), Assets fields (`sw.ext.gen.filter.by-field.options-no-value`).

Options: `project` (and project custom fields): one per project in scope, id = project key, label = project name, icon `/secure/projectavatar?pid=<id>&size=small`. `status`: the distinct statuses linked to the workflows of the in-scope projects and their issue types, in Jira's status order, id = status id, label = name, metadata JSON `{"color":<status category colour name>}`. `issuetype`: the issue types of the in-scope projects' schemes, as two groups, standard types first then sub-task types, labelled with the localized `sw.ext.gen.filter.by-field.group.standard-issue-types` / `...subtask-issue-types` (a group is absent when it has no types); id, label and icon from the type.

`versions`/`fixVersions`/version custom fields: unarchived versions of the in-scope projects, one option per distinct version name (the first one seen keeps its id), sorted by label with plain string order. `components`: components of the in-scope projects, one per distinct name, sorted by label with the user's collator. `priority`: the distinct priorities of the in-scope projects' priority schemes, in Jira's priority order. `resolution`: all resolutions in Jira's order. Ids are the Jira ids; labels the names; priorities and resolutions carry their icon URL.

Select, multi-select and cascading-select custom fields: the options of every field configuration relevant to any issue context of the in-scope projects, child options listed after their parent; options with the same (parent value, value) are merged keeping the smallest option id. Groups of options sharing a top-level value are ordered by that value (user's collator), and within a group the parent comes before its children, children by value. A top-level option's id is its option id and label its value; a child's id is `<parent id>:<child id>` and label `<parent value> - <child value>`. An unknown custom field gives no options.

`labels` and labels custom fields: searching returns Jira's label suggestions for the current user and query (for a custom field, for that field), sorted by label, cut to the page size, with `total` = the number of suggestions; ids and labels are the label text. Sprint field: searching asks Jira Software for sprints whose name matches the query, sorted by label (collator), cut to the page size; id = sprint id, label = name, metadata JSON `{"board":<board name or empty>,"state":<state lower case>}`. Advanced Roadmaps teams, Tempo teams (those the user can see) and Assets objects (with icon `rest/insight/1.0/objecttype/<type id>/icon.png?size=16`) list their objects with numeric ids.

User-type fields (`reporter`, `assignee`, `creator`, user/multi-user/multi-group custom fields) have no searchable list: searching returns no groups at all. Their ids are `author:` and `group:`. Resolving ids: `author:` ids resolve only when the caller may perform Jira's user AJAX search and the user exists (label = display name, html = `` + HTML-escaped `Display Name (username)` or with e-mail when visible + ``); `group:` ids resolve only for groups the caller may see (label = group name); other ids are dropped.

Resolving option ids of a field returns one option per requested id in request order, except `special:EMPTY`: a known id gives its option, an unknown or invisible one a placeholder with that id and label `option_<id>`; when `special:EMPTY` was requested and the field has a 'no value' option, that option is appended at the end. Fields without a resolver (labels) resolve every id to an option with id = label = the id. Sprint ids resolve through Jira Software for the current user.

Building the JQL for chosen option ids of a field gives one OR-combined where clause: the field's IN condition for the non-empty ids (converted as below; ids that do not convert are skipped, and the condition is omitted when none remain) plus the field's IS EMPTY condition when `special:EMPTY` is among them; an unknown field gives no query. Conversions: `project` keys used as is; `status` and `resolution` ids become names; version ids become version names (`affectedVersion`/`fixVersion`/`cf[n]`); component ids become names (`component`); select options become their values (`cf[n] in (...)`); cascading ids become `cf[n] in cascadeOption("parent","child")` or `cascadeOption("value")` per id; labels, priorities and issue types use the ids as given; sprint, team and Assets ids become numbers (`cf[n] in (…)`), Assets ids converted to object keys. Custom fields are referred to as `cf[<number>]`.

For user-type fields: `author:<key>` ids become usernames in one IN condition (`reporter in (...)`, `assignee in (...)`, `creator in (...)`, `cf[n] in (...)`), unknown keys skipped; each `group:<name>` adds `reporter in membersOf(...)`-style conditions (`reporterInGroup`, `assigneeInGroup`, `<field> in membersOf("<name>")`), except multi-group custom fields where it adds `cf[n] = <name>`; `special:EMPTY` adds the IS EMPTY condition; all OR-combined.

Every request of the manage-structures page (`/rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/*`) first requires that <product> is available to the current user (helper); otherwise it throws `StructureErrors.STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED` (REST 403, code 4010).

The table rows come from: `all` = every structure the user can view (VIEW), archived included, in structure-manager's order; `recents` = the user's recent structures (recents-manager); `favorites` = the user's favourites including archived ones (favorite-manager); `one` = the single structure loaded with VIEW permission (an unknown or invisible id gives the structure-manager `StructureException`, REST 404). `recent-ids` returns just the recent structure ids, most recent first.

Only the `all` source is rate-limited, per user (anonymous callers share the bucket `anonymous`), with interval dark feature `structure.rest.manageStructures.rateLimit.intervalMs` (default 500 ms; a negative value disables the limit). A call is refused when the same bucket has a call still running, or when its previous call ended less than the interval ago; it fails with REST 429, text/plain, header `Retry-After` = whole seconds (remaining time truncated to seconds, plus 1; for a still-running call the full interval truncated plus 1) and the localized message `s.structure.error.rate-limit` ('Too many search requests. Please retry in about N second(s).'). A call's end time is recorded when it finishes, whether it succeeded or failed.

The rate limiter's memory is cleared entirely when all plugin caches are cleared and for one user when that user's caches are cleared; a background job every 37 minutes forgets buckets whose last call ended more than 37 minutes ago (running calls are kept). With a negative interval no job is scheduled.

Each row (`managed-structure-row`) has id, name, archived, ownerKey, `myAccess` = the structure's effective permission for the user, `favorite` (favorite-manager, for the current user), `stars` = favourite popularity, `adjustable` = structure property `manualAdjustments.enable` equals `true` (ignoring case), and `adjusted` = manual adjustments exist, computed only when adjustable (false otherwise). `lastOpened` and `lastOpenedForSort` come from structure property `lastPolledMillis` (epoch ms; only positive values count): the date formatted with Jira's DATE style for the logged-in user and the ISO-8601 date `yyyy-MM-dd`; without it `lastOpened` is null and `lastOpenedForSort` is `0`. Rows keep the source order.

When synchronization is enabled or any synchronizer is installed (helper), each row lists the structure's installed synchronizers with id, `desc` = the localized one-line description of the synchronizer and its configuration, and `extra` = its detail lines joined with `, `; otherwise `synchronizers` is empty.

`problems` holds `USER_DELETED` when the owner key does not resolve to a user (including a structure without owner), else `USER_INACTIVE` when the owner is inactive, and `STOPPED` when generation of the structure's forest (unsecured structure spec) is blocked in the generation manager; empty otherwise.

For a logged-in user each row lists the structure-copy processes that are accessible to the user and copy from that structure (id and progress state, `structure-copy-progress`); anonymous users get none. `addons` lists, for each installed integration-details provider that has a product icon, in order of provider key, the provider's plugin name for every structure it reports as integrated.

The table's `users` are built with rest-user-builder (as seen by the current user): for Jira administrators and users with the global USER_PICKER permission, one entry per distinct owner key of the rows plus the current user; for others only the current user's entry, or none when anonymous.

Page details for a list of structure ids: more ids than dark feature `structure.search.page-details-max-limit` (default 20) throws `IllegalArgumentException` 'Too many structures on page' (REST 400 'Invalid request data'). Each id the user can view (VIEW) gets `descriptionHtml` = the description rendered by Jira's `atlassian-wiki-renderer` (HTML-escaped when that renderer is missing) and `effectors` = the number of rows of item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector` in the structure's stored forest (0 when it cannot be determined); ids the user cannot view are left out silently.

Getting one structure: a null or non-positive id throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` (message `id`); otherwise the structure is loaded with VIEW permission (structure-manager errors propagate) and returned as `structure-summary` with permissions/owner as requested (owner only when the caller can browse users: Jira ADMINISTER or USER_PICKER, or is the owner), the caller's generator-configuration, effector-configuration and effector-execution permissions on it, `descriptionHtml` (wiki-rendered, or escaped without renderer) and the caller's favourite flag.

The structure selector list (`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`): an anchor issue the caller cannot see (helper reports an issue error) is dropped. `recent` = the caller's recent structures; `favorites` = the caller's favourites (`totalFavorites` = their full count); `containingAnchor` (only with an accepted anchor) = viewable structures containing the anchor issue, those in the recent list first in recent order, then the rest in structure-manager's order (`totalContainingAnchor` = full count); `defaults` = the default structure of the project (`forProject` key, else the anchor issue's project) followed by the global default when different, each only if the caller can view it and it is not archived (without project only the global default). `maxItems` = max(4, Jira's `jira.max.issue.filter.dropdown.items` (default 10) / 2 − 1); recent, favourites and containing lists are cut to `maxItems` + 2. `structures` holds one summary per structure referenced by the lists.

Structure search: lists structures with at least the requested permission (unknown names fail as invalid data), archived ones only when asked; a non-blank trimmed name keeps structures whose name contains it ignoring case, or, with `filterById`, whose decimal id contains it; ids in `skip` (separated by `.`, zero and non-numbers ignored) are removed; with `filterById` and a numeric name the structure with exactly that id is moved first, the rest keeping their order. Page size = the requested limit (default 10) capped by dark feature `structure.search.max-limit` (default 100); page n (1-based, values below 1 mean 1, absent means first) returns that slice; a page beyond the end is empty; `haveMore` is true only when items remain after the slice, otherwise absent.

Structure search is rate-limited per user like manage-structure-service's `all` table, with its own interval dark feature `structure.rest.searchStructures.rateLimit.intervalMs`, default 0: so by default only a concurrent search by the same user (or another anonymous caller) is refused, with 429 and `Retry-After: 1`.

Favourite read and write first require that the structure is accessible with VIEW (else REST 403 text/plain `structure <id> does not exist or you don't have enough permissions to view it`; also for a null id). Reading answers false for anonymous callers. Setting stores the requested state through favorite-manager and echoes the request; for anonymous callers nothing is stored and false is returned.
Marking a structure recent passes the id and current user to recents-manager without any permission check; a null id does nothing.

Quick transformations are kept in structure property `quick-transforms` (structure-property-service). Reading requires VIEW access (403 as for favourites) and returns the stored JSON text verbatim, `[]` when unset. Writing requires ADMIN access (403 otherwise); a null body throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` 'Request body was null', an unparsable body 'Cannot parse quick transforms', and a body in which any id repeats, counting top-level items and the transformations inside groups together, 'Quick transformations with duplicated IDs were found for structure <id>'; otherwise the parsed list is re-serialised to compact JSON and stored.
'Is the description shown' requires VIEW access (403 otherwise) and answers whether structure property `showDescription` equals `true` (ignoring case); false when unset.

Creating a structure requires the helper's 'create structure' permission for the caller (else `StructureErrors.NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE`, REST 403 code 4006), checked before the body; a null body throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` 'Request body was null'. The new structure gets the body's properties: `name` is required (missing: invalid-data error 'Name is required', REST 400 `Invalid request data`) and must not be empty ('Name cannot be empty'); description, edit-requires-parent-issue-permission and permission rules are applied when present (null rules skipped); owner = the caller when logged in, is saved, and is returned with permissions and owner included and favourite false.

Updating a structure: a null body throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` 'Request body was null'; the structure is loaded with ADMIN permission (errors propagate); the body's present properties are applied (an empty `name` fails with invalid data 'Name cannot be empty', REST 400; a missing name keeps the old one); `isArchived`, when present, sets the archived flag, and changing it from false to true disables all the structure's synchronizers (sync-manager) after saving. `owner`, when present, is applied only if the caller is a Jira administrator, or has USER_PICKER and either administers the structure or is its owner; a `user:` prefix is removed and the key must resolve to an existing user, otherwise the owner is left unchanged (warning logged). Returns the saved structure with permissions and owner, and the caller's favourite flag.

Deleting: a null or non-positive id throws `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` (message `id`); a structure not accessible with VIEW throws `StructureErrors.STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; otherwise structure-manager deletes it (which itself requires ADMIN).

The `structure-synchronizer` module type declares synchronizer modules whose module object (from `class`) must be a `StructureSynchronizer`. Besides Jira's standard module attributes (`key`, `name`, `class`, `description`, resources) it reads the integer attribute `order`, the child elements `label` and `rules`, and a velocity resource named `form` (the parameters form). It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

A synchronizer's `order` attribute is parsed as a decimal integer; when it is absent the order is 0, and when it is not an integer (for example `ten`) a warning `Invalid order specified: "ten". Should be an integer.` is logged, the order is 0 and the module still loads. The built-in synchronizers use `sync-filter` 10, `sync-links` 30, `sync-gh` 40, `sync-status-rollup` 50 and `sync-subtasks` 230.

Text child elements of extension descriptors (`label` and `rules` here; also `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, the blocked-message elements, item type `displayable`, `title`, `newItemTitle` and template `label` in the other module types) are resolved per request in the current user's language: when the element has a `key` attribute and Jira's i18n text for that key differs from the key itself, that text is used (with any message parameters substituted); otherwise the element's trimmed body text is used. A missing element, or a key that has no translation and an empty body, gives the empty string (never null, never the bare key).

Through the synchronizer's `SynchronizerDescriptor`, `getLabel()` is the resolved `label` text, `getRules()` the resolved `rules` text, `getCompleteKey()` `<plugin key>:<module key>`, and `getParametersFormHtml(params)` renders the module's `form` velocity resource with the given variables.

The synchronizer choice in the sync dialogs lists the enabled `structure-synchronizer` modules whose module object can be loaded and which suit the action, in ascending `order` (equal orders keep Jira's order): for installing a synchronizer only those that are available and support automatic sync; for import/export (resync) all available ones. A module whose object fails to load is left out.

The `structure-export-renderer-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be an `ExportRendererProvider`. Besides the standard module attributes it reads any number of `column-key` and `export-format` child elements (for example `<export-format>ms-excel</export-format><column-key>field</column-key>`). It has no `order`; providers come in Jira's module order. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

The column keys and export formats of a provider are the trimmed texts of its `column-key` and `export-format` elements in document order; elements with empty text are dropped, and no element gives an empty list (which `extension-service` files under the null key or format). The lists are fixed when the module is loaded.

The `structure-item-type` module type declares item types whose module object must be a `StructureItemType`. Besides the standard module attributes it reads: child `icon` (attribute `spanClass`), text elements `displayable`, `title` and `newItemTitle`, attribute `weight`, and child `feature` (attribute `key`). It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

An item type's icon CSS class is the `spanClass` of its first `icon` element; when that class contains the whole word `s-fa`, ` s-fa-fw` is appended (`s-fa s-fa-folder` becomes `s-fa s-fa-folder s-fa-fw`; `alm alm-fw alm-memo` is unchanged). Without an `icon` element (or without `spanClass`) the type has no icon class.

The `weight` attribute is a decimal integer; an absent or non-integer weight means no weight, and types without a weight sort after all weighted ones (as `Integer.MAX_VALUE`) in the third-party item type list, which is ordered by weight and then by title.

An item type with a `<feature key="K"/>` element is hidden whenever the dark feature `K` is not true; the check is made on each request, so switching the dark feature shows or hides it without reloading. A type without `feature` is never hidden. Hidden types are left out of the third-party item type list offered to the structure widget.

The structure widget's list of third-party item types (shape `third-party-item-type`) contains the enabled item types from plugins other than `com.almworks.jira.structure` that are generic item types and not hidden, with `type` the complete module key, `title` and `newItemTitle` the resolved texts and `weight` the weight; a type whose resolved `title` or `newItemTitle` is empty is skipped with a warning.

For rows of a generic item type, the displayable text is the module's `displayable` text with the item's name as message parameter `{0}` (for example a key whose text is `Memo: {0}` gives `Memo: Groceries`); it is undefined when the item type's descriptor is not found or the item cannot be loaded.

The `structure-inserter` module type declares inserters whose module object must be an `Inserter`. Besides the standard module attributes it reads: attribute `group`, text elements `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, `add-blocked-message`, `move-blocked-message` and `remove-blocked-message`, any number of `icon` elements (attributes `key` and `spanClass`), and velocity resources `form`, `summary` and optionally `icon`. The same elements are read for `structure-extender`, `structure-grouper`, `structure-filter` and `structure-sorter`. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

The `group` attribute (menu group number) is parsed as an integer; absent means no group (null in the `generator-module-info` shape). A non-integer `group` makes loading the module fail with `NumberFormatException`, so that generator is not available.

The generator's dialog title is the resolved `dialog-title` text, or the resolved `label` when there is no `dialog-title` element; the dialog description HTML is the resolved `dialog-description-html` text, or none (null) when that element is absent.

Icons are looked up by key: each `icon` element with a `spanClass` is filed under its `key` attribute (no `key` = the default icon; an `icon` without `spanClass` is ignored; a later element with the same key replaces an earlier one). A lookup for a key falls back to the default icon when that key has none. Unlike item types, nothing is appended to the class.
A generator's icon HTML is `` for its icon class; with no icon class but a velocity resource named `icon`, that resource rendered and trimmed; otherwise the default ``.

When an action on a generated row cannot be handled, the message shown is: for add and copy the resolved `add-blocked-message`, for move `move-blocked-message`, for remove `remove-blocked-message`; when that text is empty, the generator kind's own message if it has one, else `s.ext.gen.block.no-handler` (`Cannot handle this operation.`).

In the list of generator modules (shape `generator-module-info`) a generator module appears only when its module object loads and `isAvailable()` is true, with `module` its complete key, `label` the resolved label (empty string when none), `type` `inserter` for an `Inserter` (`extender`, `grouper`, `sorter`, `filter` for the other kinds), `group` the `group` attribute and `presets` from a configurable generator; when the dark feature `structure.generator.defaults.disableUpdates` is true every preset's parameters get `disableActions` true.

The `structure-extender` module type declares generators whose module object must be a `Extender`. It reads exactly the descriptor elements described for `structure-inserter` (`group`, `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, the three blocked-message elements, `icon` elements, and the `form`, `summary` and `icon` resources) with the same defaults, icon, title and blocked-message rules. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.
An available `structure-extender` module is listed among the generator modules with `type` `extender`; all five generator module types share one generator catalogue looked up by complete key.

The `structure-grouper` module type declares generators whose module object must be a `Grouper`. It reads exactly the descriptor elements described for `structure-inserter` (`group`, `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, the three blocked-message elements, `icon` elements, and the `form`, `summary` and `icon` resources) with the same defaults, icon, title and blocked-message rules. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.
An available `structure-grouper` module is listed among the generator modules with `type` `grouper`; all five generator module types share one generator catalogue looked up by complete key.

The `structure-filter` module type declares generators whose module object must be a `Filter`. It reads exactly the descriptor elements described for `structure-inserter` (`group`, `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, the three blocked-message elements, `icon` elements, and the `form`, `summary` and `icon` resources) with the same defaults, icon, title and blocked-message rules. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.
An available `structure-filter` module is listed among the generator modules with `type` `filter`; all five generator module types share one generator catalogue looked up by complete key.

The `structure-sorter` module type declares generators whose module object must be a `Sorter`. It reads exactly the descriptor elements described for `structure-inserter` (`group`, `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, the three blocked-message elements, `icon` elements, and the `form`, `summary` and `icon` resources) with the same defaults, icon, title and blocked-message rules. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.
An available `structure-sorter` module is listed among the generator modules with `type` `sorter`; all five generator module types share one generator catalogue looked up by complete key.

The `structure-attribute-loader-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be an `AttributeLoaderProvider`. Besides the standard module attributes it reads only the integer attribute `order` (default 0 when absent; a non-integer value logs `Invalid order specified: "<value>". Should be an integer.` and counts as 0). Providers are consulted in ascending `order`. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

The `structure-query-constraint` module type declares S-JQL constraints whose module object must be a `StructureQueryConstraint`. It reads the attribute `fname`, which is the constraint's name in queries (the module's reported name is `fname`, not the `name` attribute; null when `fname` is absent), and an optional child element `<order>` whose trimmed text is an integer. It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

A query constraint's order comes from the `<order>` child element (not an attribute); without that element the order is `Integer.MAX_VALUE` (2147483647); a non-integer text logs `Invalid order specified: "<text>". Should be an integer.` and keeps 2147483647. The built-in constraints (`folder`, `memo`, `item`, `rowId`, `planningtask`) have no `<order>`.

The `structure-effector` module type declares effectors whose module object must be an `Effector`. It reads the same elements as the generator module types except the blocked messages: attribute `group`, text elements `label`, `dialog-title`, `dialog-description-html`, `icon` elements, and the `form` and `summary` velocity resources, with the same title fallback (dialog title = label when absent). It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

An effector's icon class is its default (keyless) `icon` `spanClass`, or `alm alm-fw alm-effector` when it has none; its icon HTML is ``. In REST effector listings `icon` is that class and `title` the dialog title (empty string when null).

The `structure-core-extension` module type declares modules whose module object must be a `StructureCoreExtension`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Extensions are keyed by complete module key.

When forest, item, poll or effect REST responses are assembled, every core extension is asked for data with the value found under its complete key in the request's `extensionRequests` (null when absent or when there is no `extensionRequests`). A non-null answer is put under that key in `extensionData`, in catalogue order; an exception or `LinkageError` is logged as a warning (repeated warnings for the same extension are throttled) and that extension contributes nothing. When no extension answers, `extensionData` is null.

The structure widget configuration includes, under each core extension's complete key, the map it returns for widget configuration; null or empty maps are left out, and with no contribution at all the extensions entry is absent.

The `structure-performance-log-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be a `PerformanceLogProvider`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Providers are kept as a plain list in Jira's module order.

The `structure-query-skeleton-factory` module type declares modules whose module object must be an `SQuerySkeletonFactory`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Factories are keyed by complete module key. The plugin itself declares no module of this type.

The `structure-effect-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be an `EffectProvider`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. An effect names its provider by complete module key.

The `structure-backup-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be a `StructureBackupProvider`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Providers are kept by their plugin's key. The plugin itself declares no module of this type.

The `structure-calendar-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be a `CalendarProvider`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Providers are keyed by complete module key.

A calendar's full id is `<provider complete module key>/<calendar id>` (e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:simple-calendar-provider/1`). Parsing a full id splits on `/` and requires exactly two parts, else `IllegalArgumentException` `Unsupported calendar key format <id>`; a non-numeric second part gives `NumberFormatException`; a provider key containing `/` is rejected with `IllegalArgumentException` `module key should not contain slashes!`.

The `structure-integration-details-provider` module type declares modules whose module object must be a `StructureIntegrationDetails`. It reads only Jira's standard module attributes and children (`key`, `name`, `i18n-name-key`, `class`, `description`, resources, parameters) and nothing of its own; it has a single declaration, not restricted to a Jira version. Providers are kept by module key with their plugin's name. The plugin itself declares no module of this type.

The `new-structure-template` module type declares create-structure wizard templates whose module object must be a `NewStructureTemplate`. Besides the standard module attributes (its `description` element gives the template's description) it reads the text element `label`, a download resource named `icon.png` (the template icon; its URL is Jira's relative static plugin resource URL for that resource) and one velocity resource per step, named by the step key (a template with a custom final step also has one named `__end`). It is declared twice in the plugin descriptor: once restricted to Jira `[9.0.0,10.0.0)` (the declaration that is active on Jira 9.12) and once to `[10.0.0,)`, with the same key.

The wizard's template chooser (`CreateStructure.jspa` without `__templateKey`) lists every enabled `new-structure-template` module in Jira's module order, each with its complete key, resolved label, description and icon URL; the first one is preselected when no template was chosen before. A template whose `isEnabled()` is false or throws (a `RuntimeException` or `LinkageError`, logged as `Template problem: <key>`) is shown as disabled.

The wizard finds the template by the complete module key in parameter `__templateKey` among enabled modules; when it is not an enabled `new-structure-template` module or its object cannot be loaded, the wizard shows the error `Unable to find template for the key: <key>`.

A step page is rendered from the template module's velocity resource named after the step key. When the step is `__end` and the template has no custom final step, the plugin's general step page (name, description, sharing) is used instead. A missing resource or one with a blank location gives the error `s.tpl.template.not-found` (`Unable to load template for key "<step>"`); a template module that is no longer enabled gives `s.tpl.error.module-descriptor-not-found` (`Unable to load module descriptor for key: "<key>"`).

The wizard checks `isEnabled()` only for showing the chooser; a request that names a disabled template in `__templateKey` is still stepped through and can create a structure (as the original does). Creating still requires the user to be allowed to create structures, else the error `s.manage.create.noaccess` (`You don't have permissions to create new structures`).

The wizard keeps every step's submitted fields in the parameters map under the step key. When the user switches to another template (`__prevTemplateKey` differs from `__templateKey`), only top-level entries named `name`, `description`, `roles` or `projects` are meant to be kept; since the general step's fields are stored under `__end`, not at top level, in practice all earlier step values are dropped (as the original does).

`empty-structure` is a `new-structure-template` module: label `s.tpl.empty.title` (`Empty Structure`), description `s.tpl.empty.desc` (`Create an empty structure and add content manually.`), icon resource `icon.png`. Its module object is the API's `EmptyTemplate`: always enabled, first step `__end`, so the wizard goes straight to the general step.

Finishing the general step for `empty-structure` creates a structure owned by the current user with the trimmed `name` and `description` from the step, `editRequiresParentIssuePermission` false and no rows. Sharing (`roles`): a group name available to the current user gives that group EDIT; `private.nobody` gives no permission rules; a project role id gives EDIT to that role in each selected project (`projects`, comma-separated ids). Validation: blank name `s.manage.edit.noname` (`Please enter a name for your structure`), name over 190 characters `s.manage.edit.too-long-name` (`The name should be 190 characters or less`), a role without projects on field `projects` `s.tpl.step.general.no-projects` (`Please specify at least one project`). The same general step ends `backlog-structure` and `agile-structure`.

`backlog-structure` is a `new-structure-template` module: label `s.tpl.backlog.title` (`Backlog Structure`), description `s.tpl.backlog.desc`, icon `icon.png`, step resources `project` and `group-by`. It is enabled only for users who hold the configure-generators app permission (`CoreAppPermissions.CONFIGURE_GENERATORS`).

Steps: first `project` (title `s.tpl.backlog.step.project.title`, `Build a List of Scheduled Issues`), next `group-by` (title `s.tpl.backlog.step.group-by.title`, `Group Issues`), then the general `__end` step. Back from `group-by` goes to `project`, back from `project` to the template chooser. Any other step key throws `StructureTemplateException` with `s.tpl.error.unknown-step` (`Unknown step name: "<step, HTML-escaped>"`).

The `project` step takes `backlog-project`, a comma-separated list of project ids, and `backlog-version`, a comma-separated list of version ids (optional); `backlog-projects-selection` and `backlog-versions-selection` only carry the pickers' previous selection. Moving forward with no project gives the error `s.tpl.backlog.error.project` (`Please select a project`) on field `backlog-project`. Ids must be plain longs: a value such as `1, 2` (with a space) fails with `NumberFormatException`.

The `group-by` step takes `backlog-field` (a field id, or `epic` or `sprint`) and the checkbox `backlog-allow-changes`. Moving forward with an empty field gives `s.tpl.backlog.field.error` (`Please select a field`) on `backlog-field`; when building the structure an absent field means `assignee`. The checkbox is true when it was submitted with two values (checked box plus its hidden companion), false with one value, and when not submitted at all defaults to true unless the dark feature `structure.generator.defaults.disableUpdates` is true.

The field choices offered in `group-by` are the presets of the `grouper-field` generator except `project` and custom fields (`customfield_...`), plus `Epic` (`s.ext.gen.grouper.agileepic.label`, value `epic`) when `grouper-agile-epic` is enabled and available, plus `Sprint` (`s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.label`, value `sprint`) when `grouper-sprint` is; sorted by label case-insensitively in the user's locale, keyed by field id.

The structure gets a `inserter-jql` generator (`com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-jql`, no owning structure) with stored parameters `{"limit":1000,"jql":<query>}`. The query has one clause per selected project in the submitted order, `project = "<project name>"`, followed, when versions of that project were selected, by ` AND fixVersion = "<name>"` for one version or ` AND fixVersion IN ("<a>", "<b>")` for several (in the submitted order); double quotes in names are escaped as `\"`. Several clauses are joined as `(<c1>) OR (<c2>)`; a single clause has no parentheses. Selected versions of projects that were not selected are ignored.

Building fails with `StructureTemplateException` (shown as the wizard error) when no project id was given (`Unable to get project ids to create generator for!`), a version id is unknown (`Unable to find version for id: <id>`) or a project id is unknown (`Unable to find project for id: <id>`). The structure saved by the general step remains.

The structure gets one grouper generator: for `epic` a `grouper-agile-epic` generator whose parameters are those of that generator's first preset (none when it has no presets or is unavailable); for `sprint` a `grouper-sprint` generator; for any other field a `grouper-field` generator with `fieldId` the field id. In every case the parameters include `disableActions` = not allow-changes.

`backlog-structure` adds two top-level rows to the new (empty) structure's forest (through its unsecured forest source, without permission checks): the inserter's generator item (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator` with the generator id) and after it the grouper's. It creates no view and sets no other permission than the general step's.

`agile-structure` is a `new-structure-template` module: label `s.tpl.agile.title` (`Agile Structure`), description `s.tpl.agile.desc`, icon `icon.png`, step resources `epics`, `stories` and `sorting`. It is enabled only when the user holds the configure-generators app permission and the plugin `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira` (Jira Software) is enabled; without Jira Software it is shown disabled.

Steps: `epics` (title `s.tpl.agile.step.epics.title`, `Add Epics`), `stories` (`s.tpl.agile.step.stories.title`, `Add Stories`), `sorting` (`s.tpl.agile.step.sorting.title`, `Order by Rank`), then the general `__end` step; back goes `sorting` to `stories` to `epics` to the chooser. An unknown step key throws `StructureTemplateException` `s.tpl.error.unknown-step`.

Inputs: `agile-boards` (comma-separated board ids; empty gives `s.tpl.agile.step.epics.boards.error`, `Please select at least one Agile board`, on field `agile-boards`), `agile-update-epics` (stories step), `agile-rank-sorter` and `agile-update-issues` (sorting step); `agile-boards-selection` only carries the picker selection. The checkboxes are true with two submitted values, false with one, and when absent default to true for `agile-rank-sorter` and to true unless the dark feature `structure.generator.defaults.disableUpdates` is true for the two update options. The stories and sorting steps never report errors.

Generators created (no owning structure): one `agile-board` inserter per selected board, in the submitted order, with parameters `{"limit":1000,"rapidViewId":<board id>,"insertEpics":true}`; one `extender-agile` with `{"disableActions":<not update-epics>}`; and, when the rank sorter is chosen, one `sorter-agile-rank` with `{"fieldId":<numeric id of Jira Software's default rank field>,"disableActions":<not update-issues>}`.
The rank sorter is silently left out when Jira Software's rank service cannot be obtained or has no default rank field; the structure is still created.

`agile-structure` adds to the new (empty) structure's forest, at the top level, the board inserters' generator rows in board order, then the extender row, then the sorter row when created, all as siblings (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator` items).

`personal-backlog-structure` is a `new-structure-template` module: label `s.tpl.personal-backlog.title` (`Personal Backlog Structure`), description `s.tpl.personal-backlog.desc`, icon `icon.png`, and its own final step resource `__end`. It is enabled for users with the configure-generators app permission. It has a custom final step and a single step: the first step is `__end` (title `s.tpl.personal-backlog.step.issues.title`, `Personal Backlog`); forward creates the structure, back returns to the chooser; any other step key throws `StructureTemplateException` `s.tpl.error.unknown-step`.

Inputs of the step: `personal-backlog-name`, checkboxes `personal-backlog-assigned`, `personal-backlog-reporter`, `personal-backlog-watching` (each true when its first submitted value is `true`, false for any other value, and true when not submitted), `personal-backlog-columns` (multi-valued column ids) and `personal-backlog-columns-changed` (`true` when the user edited the column list). Validation: the name must be non-blank (`s.manage.edit.noname`) and at most 190 characters after trimming (`s.manage.edit.too-long-name`), on field `personal-backlog-name`; when none of the three checkboxes is true the error `s.tpl.personal-backlog.error.track` (`Please select at least one`) goes on field `personal-backlog-track`.

The structure's name is `personal-backlog-name` as submitted (not trimmed); when the parameter is absent it is `s.tpl.personal-backlog.step.issues.backlog` with the current user's display name (`<Display Name>'s Backlog`). The name is set and the structure saved before content is added; no description and no permission rules are set (only the owner, the current user, has access).

For each checked option, in the order assigned, reporter, watching, the structure gets a top-level memo with an inserter and a grouper under it (as two children): assigned: memo `Assigned to me` (`s.tpl.personal-backlog.step.issues.+assigned+.summary`, description `...+assigned+.description`, params `iconClass` `alm-flag`, `color` `red`), `inserter-jql` with `{"limit":1000,"jql":"assignee = currentUser() and resolution is EMPTY"}` and a `grouper-field` on `status`; reporter: memo `I'm Reporter` (`alm-memo`, `blue`), JQL `reporter = currentUser() and resolution is EMPTY`, grouper on `status`; watching: memo `I'm watching` (`alm-memo`, `gray`), JQL `watcher = currentUser() and reporter != currentUser() and resolution is EMPTY`, grouper on `project`. Groupers are stored as `{"fieldId":<field>,"disableActions":<value of dark feature structure.generator.defaults.disableUpdates>}`. The rows are added to the new structure's forest through its unsecured forest source.

Memos are created through the `type-memo` item type with `summary`, `description` and `params` {`iconClass`, `color`}; when it reports errors, creation fails with `StructureTemplateException` carrying the first error message.

When the template's module object is created (normally once, when the plugin starts) it records which Jira statuses are named exactly (case-sensitive) `New`, `Open`, `Reopened`, `To Do` (0 %), `In Progress` (50 %), `Resolved`, `Done` or `Closed` (100 %), with their ids, in Jira's status order; statuses added or renamed later are not seen until the plugin restarts. It also records the bundled formula columns as `bundled/<id>`.

When `personal-backlog-columns-changed` is not `true`, the columns are `countbyleaves`, `priority`, then `progressbystatus` if at least two of the recorded statuses exist, `timeinstatus` if `In Progress` exists, then `bundled/14` and `comment`; otherwise the submitted `personal-backlog-columns` in order (none submitted means no view).

With at least one column the template creates a view named `<structure name> View` (`s.tpl.personal-backlog.view`) and makes it the structure's default view on the structure board. Columns map as follows (ids compared ignoring case): `countbyleaves` an `attribute` column with parameters `{"attribute":{"format":"html","id":"count","params":{"leaves":true}}}`; `comment` a `comment` column; `summary` the main column; `aggregatetimeoriginalestimate`, `aggregatetimeestimate`, `aggregatetimespent` `field` columns for `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent` with `aggregate` `sum`; a recorded bundled id (exact match, e.g. `bundled/14`) a `formula` column with the saved column's name and `savedColumn` `bundled/<id>`; any other id a `field` column with `field` = that id. The view has no main column unless `summary` is chosen.

`progressbystatus` becomes a `progress` column with `{"basedOn":"status","resolvedComplete":true,"includeSelf":false,"statuses":[<recorded status ids>],"percents":[<their percents>],"weightBy":"equal"}`, and is dropped when fewer than two statuses were recorded; `timeinstatus` becomes a `timeinstatus` column with `{"displayFormat":{"type":"duration"},"statuses":["status:<In Progress id>"]}`, dropped when `In Progress` was not recorded.

The column choices offered are the navigable fields available to the current user (excluding custom fields whose type has neither a view nor a column-view template, and the fields `progress` and `aggregateprogress`) labelled by their translated names, plus `countbyleaves`, `comment`, `progressbystatus`, `timeinstatus` and the bundled formula columns (`bundled/<id>`, labelled by column name), sorted by label with plain case-sensitive string comparison.

`remote-gadget-extension` (a `structure-core-extension`, complete key `com.almworks.jira.structure:remote-gadget-extension`) contributes no widget configuration and no app support information (both null).

Its request (the value under its complete key in `extensionRequests`) is a JSON array of windows, each with `forestSpec` (REST forest spec), `rowIndexes` (array of integers: positions in the forest), `attributes` (array of REST attribute specs) and `oldBackendId` (long, default 0). No request, or an empty array, gives no extension data.

For each window that has a forest spec, a non-empty `attributes` list and a non-empty `rowIndexes`, it creates a new attribute value subscription for that forest and those attributes whose rows are the row ids at the given indexes of the latest forest of that spec; indexes below 0 or not less than the forest size are skipped. Windows lacking any of the three are skipped.

When none of a window's indexes is inside the forest, a warning is logged and the window gives no subscription in the answer, but the new subscription has already been created and is left unused (as the original does).

The answer is `{"subscriptions":[...],"mapping":{<oldBackendId>:<new subscription id>,...}}` where each subscription is in the `attribute-subscription` shape with a values update: values are loaded for up to `structure.attribute.remote-gadget.valuesTimeout` ms (dark feature, default 10000, read once when the module is created, not clamped) before answering, from version zero. When no window produced a subscription the answer is null (no entry in `extensionData`). Two windows with the same `oldBackendId` keep the later mapping.

Any failure while subscribing (for example an unknown structure in the forest spec or a forest the user may not see) is logged as `Failed to create subscription` and the extension answers null; a request that cannot be read as an array of windows makes the extension call fail, which is logged and contributes nothing.

`simple-calendar-provider` offers exactly two calendars, listed in this order: id 0, name `s.ext.calendar.simple.name` (`Standard calendar 24/7`), description `s.ext.calendar.simple.description` (`Calendar that considers all time to be working hours, regardless of date, time, or time zone. This is the default calendar.`); and id 1, name `s.ext.calendar.work.name` (`Standard work calendar 8/5`), description `s.ext.calendar.work.description` (`Calendar that only considers time from 9:00 to 17:00 on working days (Monday-Friday). Uses the default Jira time zone.`). Names and descriptions are in the current user's language at the time they are asked for.
`getCalendar(0)` and `getCalendar(1)` return those calendars (the same objects every time); any other id returns null. Calendar 0 is also the plugin-wide default calendar.

Calendar 0's duration from start to finish is `finish - start` milliseconds; when finish is before start it throws `java.security.InvalidParameterException`. Neither calendar reports itself as time-zone dependent.

Calendar 1 counts only the time between 09:00 and 17:00 (8 hours) on Monday to Friday in Jira's default time zone (`TimeZoneManager.getDefaultTimezone()`, asked on each call); Saturdays and Sundays count nothing and there are no holidays. Example: Friday 16:00 to Monday 10:00 is 2 hours; Monday 08:00 to Monday 12:00 is 3 hours; Monday 18:00 to Tuesday 08:00 is 0; a full Monday-to-Friday week is 40 hours. When finish is before start it throws `java.security.InvalidParameterException`; equal instants give 0.

For calendar 1 a start before 09:00 counts from 09:00 of that day, a start after 17:00 counts from 09:00 of the next working day, and a start on a weekend counts from Monday 09:00; a finish inside a working window counts up to the finish, a finish outside one counts up to the end of the last window before it. Day boundaries follow the zone's local dates and clock times (on a daylight-saving change day the window is still 09:00 to 17:00 local).

Stored parameters: `jql` (String, the JQL text) and `limit` (integer, the maximum number of issues; null or absent means no limit). Example: {"jql": "project = TEST", "limit": 1000}. A new inserter's form starts with `limit` = 1000 and no `jql`; showing stored parameters on a form puts `jql` and `limit` (read as an integer, null when absent or not a number) there.

Building parameters from a form returns a map with exactly `jql` and `limit`: `jql` is the form value with leading and trailing horizontal whitespace removed; when non-blank it is parsed with Jira's JqlQueryParser and validated with SearchService.validateQuery as the current StructureAuth user, and a parse error (its localized parse message, or Jira's generic parse message) or the first validation error message is added under field `jql`; a present but blank value adds `s.ext.gen.jql.param.jql.error.no-jql` ('Please type in a JQL query') under `jql`; an absent value adds no error. `limit` is the form value read as an integer (null when missing, blank or not a number; no error). The map is returned even when errors were added.

Generating inserts, as a flat list of top-level rows (no nesting), the issues matching the stored JQL in the query's own ORDER BY order, searched with the plugin's sorted search as the current StructureAuth user (see `helper`); each issue appears once. With a missing, zero or negative `limit` all matches are inserted; with a positive n at most the first n. When the plugin is not enabled for all projects the query is first narrowed with the project-scope clause of `structure-configuration`. These rules are the same as for `recent-issue-inserter` (limit, hit-limit report, scope).

A blank or missing `jql` inserts nothing; JQL that no longer parses inserts nothing (a warning is logged) and nothing is thrown to the generation. A SearchException from the search is logged and leaves the fragment empty.
When a refresh inserts at least `limit` issues (limit > 0), the generation reports that this inserter hit its limit (with the limit value) as generation trouble; with no limit nothing is reported.

The inserted fragment is regenerated when a changed-items batch contains any item of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-sprint`, `:type-version`, `:type-project`, `:type-project-component` or `com.almworks.jira.stucture:type-tempo-team-membership` (misspelt as in the original); or any issue that was inserted; or an issue inside the project scope that now matches the stored JQL (checked with a match search as the current user, a failing search counting as no match). Changed issues outside the scope never cause regeneration. Same rules as `recent-issue-inserter`.

The inserter takes part in deciding user edits only when its `jql` is non-blank and parses; otherwise it offers no action handler. Its action handling cannot be switched off: the generator form reports `canHandleUpdates` false, and a stored `disableActions` = true is ignored for it.

Adding (placing) a fragment into the inserter's rows: placing it under any row (not at the inserter's own top level) yields with `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.blocked.add` ('Cannot add items to JQL query result.'). At top level: if any root of the fragment is not an issue it yields with the same message; roots that are new, not yet created issues are ignored, and if no existing issue roots remain the add is allowed with an empty effect. If any existing issue root does not match the JQL (matched with Jira security overridden) the add is blocked with that message. If all match and the fragment is flat it is allowed with an empty effect (no Jira change). If the fragment has sub-rows, the extenders that follow are asked to generate the sub-tree for those roots; the add is allowed (empty effect) only when the fragment is contained in what they generate, otherwise it yields with the add message.

Moving a row of the inserter's result (including reordering) is always blocked with `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.blocked.move` ('Cannot move issues inside JQL query result.'); removing a row is always blocked with `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.blocked.remove` ('Cannot remove issues from JQL query result.'). The add and move messages (not the remove message) are wrapped in `s.ext.gen.block.suggest-adjustment` ('{0} You can enable manual adjustments in the structure configuration.') when manual adjustment is possible in that action.

The add option is described as `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.option.add` ('Add to "{0}"') and the move option as `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.option.move` ('Move within "{0}"'), with the JQL abbreviated to at most 30 characters (longer text becomes its first 27 characters followed by '...'), texts in the current user's locale.

The inserter is marked as consuming new items: when a new item is created into a place handled by several generators, the item REST resource treats an interaction that involves this inserter as a conflict with a new-item consumer and does not offer it as a choice.

Stored parameters: `text` (String, the search text) and `limit` (integer; null or absent means no limit). A new inserter's form starts with `limit` = 1000; showing parameters on a form puts `text` and `limit` there.

Building parameters from a form returns {`text`, `limit`}: `text` is the form value unchanged (not trimmed); when it is present but blank, error `s.ext.gen.text.param.text.error.no-text` ('Please type in a text query') is added under field `text`; an absent value adds no error. `limit` is the form value read as an integer (null when missing or not a number).

The text becomes a Jira query (after trimming): text of length 2 or more wrapped in double quotes searches the summary for the inner text (summary ~ "inner"); exactly `""` gives no query. Otherwise, if the first whitespace/comma/semicolon-separated token is a valid Jira issue key (as typed, or upper-cased in Locale.US), the query is `issue in (<keys>)` with every token that is a valid key (others skipped); text starting with a single quote is never read as keys. Otherwise each whitespace-separated word w adds, ANDed together, (summary ~ w OR summary ~ "w*"), or summary ~ w alone when w already ends with `*`. Blank or missing text gives no query.

Generating inserts the matching issues as flat top-level rows sorted by issue key descending (ORDER BY key DESC added to the text query), with the same limit, hit-limit report, project-scope narrowing, search-error and regeneration rules as `inserter-jql` (matching changed issues against the text query). With no query (blank text or `""`) nothing is inserted.

With a query, user edits follow the same add, move and remove rules as `inserter-jql` (matching against the text query), with messages `s.ext.gen.inserter.text.blocked.add` ('Cannot add items to text query result.'), `.blocked.move` ('Cannot move issues inside text query result.'), `.blocked.remove` ('Cannot remove issues from text query result.') and options `s.ext.gen.inserter.text.option.add` ('Add to "{0}"') / `.option.move` ('Move within "{0}"') with the raw text abbreviated to 30 characters. Without a query it offers no action handler. Action handling cannot be disabled (form `canHandleUpdates` false, `disableActions` ignored), and it is marked as consuming new items like `inserter-jql`.

The module `inserter-recent-issues` is the generator behind `recent-issue-inserter`: its rows, `limit` handling, project-scope narrowing, timed and item-change regeneration, search errors and form handling are exactly those claimed for `recent-issue-inserter` (recently viewed issues, newest first, refreshed after 1 minute by default). Its descriptor has no label, form, summary or icon, so it is not offered in the generator UI.

When stored parameters contain a non-blank parseable `jql`, the inserter offers the same action handler as `inserter-jql` for that JQL (add only issues matching that JQL at top level, moves and removals blocked with the `s.ext.gen.inserter.jql.*` messages), although its rows come from the issue history (as the original does). Unlike `inserter-jql`, its action handling can be disabled with `disableActions` and it is not marked as consuming new items (the markers are not inherited).

Stored parameters: `rapidViewId` (long, the Jira Software board id) and `insertEpics` (boolean: true inserts only epics, false only issues that are neither epics nor sub-tasks). A new inserter's form starts with `rapidViewId` = -1 and `insertEpics` = true; showing stored parameters puts the stored `rapidViewId` (or -1 when absent) and the stored `insertEpics` value as is. The form's board list is the boards the current user sees (see `gh-integration`).

Building parameters from a form: when `rapidViewId` reads as a long and `gh-integration` returns a filter query for that board for the current StructureAuth user, the result is exactly {`rapidViewId`: id, `insertEpics`: the form's boolean (true only for a true value or text 'true' ignoring case)}. Otherwise (missing or unparsable id, -1, unknown or invisible board, board without filter) error `s.gen.ins.agile.error.no-board-selected` ('Please select a board') is added under field `rapidViewId` and an empty map is returned.
The inserter is available exactly when `gh-integration` reports board support; if that check throws a RuntimeException it is unavailable.

The issues come from the board's saved filter query (from `gh-integration`, for the current user) with a condition ANDed to its where clause: with `insertEpics` true, issue type = the epic issue type id, or 'issuetype is EMPTY' (matching nothing) when Jira Software reports no epic type; with `insertEpics` false, NOT issue type = epic type (left out when there is no epic type) AND NOT issue type in (all sub-task issue type ids) (left out when Jira has no sub-task types). The filter's ORDER BY is kept.

Generating inserts the matching issues as flat top-level rows in the filter's order, with no limit and no hit-limit report, after the same project-scope narrowing as `inserter-jql`; regeneration on item changes follows the same rules as `inserter-jql`, matching against the narrowed board query. A missing or unparsable `rapidViewId`, or a board with no filter query, inserts nothing (warning logged); a SearchException is logged and leaves the fragment empty.

For a summary, when `rapidViewId` is readable, `rapidViewName` (the board name from `gh-integration` for the current user, null when not found) and `insertEpics` are added, and then every stored parameter is copied into the summary as well.
