Otherwise (no display format or another type) the column style is `DEFAULT` and cells are `setNumber` of the attribute read in `number` format (the duration in milliseconds). Null leaves the cell empty.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `query-match` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. It uses attribute `query-match` with parameters `query` and `queryType` (each only when the column has it, values unchanged).

Without a sum: the printable cell is `setHtml` of `query-match` in `html` format; the Excel cell is `setNumber` of `query-match` in `number` format (1 for a match, 0 for no match). With `aggregate` = `sum`, both formats show `setNumber` of attribute `sum` (format `number`) with `attribute` = `query-match` in `number` format and `distinct` = the column's boolean `distinct`: the count of matching rows in the sub-tree. Excel column style `DEFAULT`, header left-aligned; null leaves the cell empty.

Header text: the column's name when non-empty; otherwise the trimmed `query` when it is 1 to 40 characters long; otherwise (empty or longer) i18n `s.w.query-match.column-type.name` (`Query match`) when there is no `queryType`, else `s.w.query-match.column.+<queryType>+.name` (`jql` gives `JQL query`, `sjql` `S-JQL query`, `text` `Text query`). For a sum column that default is wrapped as `Σ {0}` (`sw.column.opt.aggr.sum.colname`).

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `comment` and no export format (both formats); null for other keys. It shows attribute `comment` (format `html`, no parameters): printable `setHtml` in a multiline column; Excel rich text of `comment` in `html` with parameter `excel` = true. Null leaves the cell empty.
Header text: the column's name, or i18n `s.w.lastcomment.column-type.name` (`Last Comment`).

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `tempo-worklogged` and no export format. It handles the column only when `tempo-integration` reports Tempo Timesheets available (installed, enabled and the current user has timesheets access); otherwise, and for other column keys, it returns null and the column is not exported.

It requests attribute `tempo-worklogged` (format `duration`) with parameters `accounts` (list of longs), `users` (list of strings), `teams` (list of longs), each an empty list when the column has none, `billable` (boolean, false when absent), and `dateFrom`, `dateTo` (unchanged). When `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is missing it returns null.

With `aggregate` = `sum` it uses attribute `sum` (format `duration`) over that attribute with the column's boolean `distinct`. Header: the column's name, else i18n `sw.column.tempo-worklogged.name` (`Tempo Work Logged`), for a sum `Σ Tempo Work Logged`. Cells are `setDuration(ms / 1000)`, column style `DURATION`, header right-aligned, in both formats.

Declared as a `structure-export-renderer-provider` with `column-key` `tempo-timeplanned` and no export format. It handles the column only when `tempo-integration` reports the Tempo planning API available (plugin installed, enabled and the current user has planner access); otherwise, and for other keys, it returns null.

It requests attribute `tempo-timeplanned` (format `duration`) with parameters `users` (list of strings), `teams` and `roles` (lists of longs), each an empty list when absent, and `dateFrom`, `dateTo` (unchanged). When `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is missing it returns null.

With `aggregate` = `sum` it uses attribute `sum` (format `duration`) over that attribute with the column's boolean `distinct`. Header: the column's name, else i18n `sw.column.tempo-timeplanned.name` (`Tempo Planned Time`), for a sum `Σ Tempo Planned Time`. Cells are `setDuration(ms / 1000)`, column style `DURATION`, header right-aligned, in both formats.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Each time the log is built it returns a branch `Jira instance information` with exactly four leaves in this order: the <product> plugin's version (the plugin `com.almworks.jira.structure`'s `PluginInformation.getVersion()`, read once and then reused), `JIRA: <version>` (Jira's `BuildUtilsInfo.getVersion()`), the cluster line, and the current server-local time as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`. No other child is ever added.

The cluster line is `cluster: on, node: <node id>` when Jira's `ClusterInfo.isClustered()` is true (node id from `ClusterInfo.getNodeId()`), otherwise `cluster: off`. Both answers are read once per plugin start and reused.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It returns a branch `Structures` with one node per structure the current user may administer, as `structure-manager` lists all structures at `PermissionLevel.ADMIN` (non-archived, in its name order); with no such structure the result is null. Each node is titled `<name>[<id>] (owner:<owner user key>)` and is present even when it has no children.
Under each structure, in this order and each only when non-empty: `Synchronizers`, `Generators`, `Effectors`, and the manual-adjustments node.

`Synchronizers` lists the structure's installed synchronizers as `sync-observer` reports them, each titled `<sync id> ; <module key> ; <parameters as text> ; <user key>; enabled` or `...; disabled` (note: no space before the last semicolon) according to `sync-observer`'s enabled answer.

For a synchronizer with module key `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-filter` whose parameters are a map: when `filterId` > 0, the saved filter with that id and every saved filter it references are listed under the synchronizer's node; otherwise when `jql` is non-blank, the saved filters that JQL references. The node is then a branch of those filter leaves; without any it stays a leaf.

Saved filters referenced by a JQL are found by parsing it with Jira's `JqlQueryParser` and following `filter` clauses through AND, OR and NOT (not WAS or CHANGED clauses, not function operands). A string operand is trimmed, lower-cased and looked up with `SearchRequestManager.findByNameIgnoreCase`; a number operand with `getSearchRequestById`. Each found filter is included and its own query is followed the same way (each filter is fetched at most once per log build). Each leaf is `<id> ; <name> ; <query string>`; their order is not defined. Missing filters are skipped; unparsable JQL gives no leaves and logs `Unable to parse query: <jql>` at INFO.

`Generators` lists the generator rows of the structure's own forest, in forest order (depth-first): each is `<generator id> ; <module key> ; <parameters map as text> ; ancestorRows=[<ancestor row ids from the top down, comma-space separated>]` (`[]` for a top-level generator). When the generator's parameters have a non-blank `jql`, the node becomes a branch of the saved filters that JQL references.

`Effectors` lists the rows of item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector` the same way, with the effector instance's id, module key and parameters (and the saved filters of a non-blank `jql` parameter).

When a generator or effector row cannot be read or its generator or effector is not found (`MissingRowException` or `StructureException`), its entry is the leaf `0 ; error=<exception text>` (the id shown is 0). When the structure's forest cannot be read (`StructureException`) no generators or effectors are listed. When the ancestor path cannot be determined it is shown as `[-1]`.

The manual-adjustments node is titled `Manual adjustments [ON]` or `Manual adjustments [OFF]` (the per-structure setting) when manual adjustments are enabled globally, otherwise `Manual adjustments [OFF] (structure: [ON|OFF], dark feature: [OFF])`. Its leaves are the structure's adjustments, each as the compact JSON of its stored form; with no adjustments the node is omitted.

If building one synchronizer, generator, effector or adjustment entry throws an `Exception` or `LinkageError`, that entry becomes the leaf `Unexpected exception occurred. See logs for more information.` (logged at error level) and the other entries are still listed.

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It visits every saved Jira filter (`SearchRequestManager.visitAll`, no permission filtering) and returns a branch `Saved filters with structure()` with one leaf `<id> ; <name> ; <jql>` per filter whose JQL text uses the structure function, in visiting order; with none the result is null.

A JQL uses the structure function when its text, ignoring case, contains the word `structure` starting at a word boundary, followed by optional whitespace and `(`: `issue in structure(1)` and `issue in STRUCTURE ("a")` match; `mystructure(` and `structures(` do not; a null query does not. It is a text match, so the pattern inside a quoted string also matches.
Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Its log is exactly the `Forest caches` tree that `forest-stats-container` reports (null when that is null), built fresh on every call.
Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Its log is exactly the `Syncs` branch of recent synchronizer runs that `sync-observer` keeps (null when it has no entries).
Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Its log is exactly the `Forest changes updates` branch that `forest-update-observer` keeps (null when it has no entries).
Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Its log is exactly `effect-observer`'s `Effect applications` branch (null when it has no entries).
Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. Its log is exactly `effect-observer`'s `Effect preparations` branch (null when it has no entries).

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It returns a branch `Attribute System` whose children are, in order, the last cache-cleanup record of `attribute-performance-tracker` (when there is one) and then its slow requests oldest first. With neither, the result is null.

Each record is a branch titled `<total time>ms; <start>; <name>` (total time in whole ms, start formatted `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS` in the record's own time zone, e.g. `812ms; 2026-10-29 10:15:02,123; cacheCleanup`). Its children are first one leaf `<counter>: <value>` per counter, the value printed as a Java double (e.g. `removed: 12.0`), then the nested steps (the up-to-5 slowest the tracker kept) as nodes of the same form, recursively.

A record (or nested step) with no counters and no nested steps yields no node and is silently left out. If every record is like that, the `Attribute System` branch is still returned but has no children (as the original does).

Declared as a `structure-performance-log-provider`. It reports the state of the item change tracker that `item-tracker` uses, chosen once when this provider is created. On a single-node server, or on Data Center with dark feature `structure.delegatingItemTracker.enableAsyncEventsQueue` set to false, that tracker has nothing to report and the log is null.

On Data Center with the asynchronous event queue (the default), the log is a branch with a fixed title naming that tracker with four leaves in order: `node: <cluster node id>` (`?` while the node id has not been read yet), `signature: <node signature in octal>` (0 before one is assigned), `threadCount: <number of event-writer threads started so far>`, `queueSize: <events received but not yet written>` (-1 when the two versions are not comparable).

One run (resync or incremental) works in this order: (1) collect the links and the parent/child scope; (2) on incremental sync with primacy other than `links`, replay the batch's structure changes as link changes; (3) merge duplicate sibling rows of the same issue, then re-read the forest; (4) structure-to-Jira scan (primacy other than `links`); (5) Jira-to-structure scan; (6) add missing children under each parent row, in forest order of the parent rows; (7) add missing link parents at the top level; (8) handle the remaining orphan rows; (9) enforce the loop rule (only when there is anything to do: always on resync, on incremental sync only when the batch has changed issues or link events); (10) write all link creations and removals to Jira in one transaction. All structure changes happen before any link is written.

For every placement rule of this synchronizer a row counts as the issue of its item, and a loop-marker row (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-loop-marker/<rowId>`) counts as the issue of the row it points to (followed through chains of markers). Rows of any other item type (folders, generators, projects...) count as no issue: they are never moved, removed or added by the synchronizer, and a child row under such a row has no parent issue.

Each row of an issue that may be a child (passes the child filter) and is relevant (on resync always; on incremental sync when its issue or its parent row's issue changed in the batch, or either issue has links in the collected link set) is classified by its parent row's issue P (0 at the top level or under a non-issue row): (a) in place when P is one of the issue's link parents; else (b) when P may be a parent: with primacy `links` the row is an orphan; with primacy `structure` the row stays and the link P -> issue is to be created, unless P is the issue itself or this batch's structure changes removed that link, in which case it is an orphan; with primacy `none` the row is an orphan when Jira or this batch's structure changes removed the link P -> issue, else it behaves as with `structure`; else (c) the row is an orphan when the issue has at least one link parent, otherwise it stays untouched. Example (resync, primacy `links`, no filters): forest [P > X] with no link P -> X makes X an orphan; with primacy `structure` X stays and link P -> X is created.

For each row whose issue may be a parent, the link children of that issue that are not the issue of one of its direct child rows are missing. They are placed under that row right after its current last child row (whatever item that last child is), or as its first child when it has none, in ascending issue id order. Each missing child either reuses an orphan row of that issue (moved with its subtree, see orphan reuse) or is added as a new issue row; a newly added issue row gets all its own link children (in scope) as new nested rows recursively, and those nested children are ordered by the Jira link id of their link (ascending; links only planned in this run and not yet in Jira come last, by parent then child issue id). Example (resync, primacy `links`): links P->A, P->B, P->C1 with issue ids C1=100, A=101, B=102; forest [P > [C1, F], G > A] with F, G folders. A's row under G is an orphan and is moved; B is new: result [P > [C1, F, A, B], G].

When a missing child has orphan rows, one of them is moved instead of adding a row. Candidates are that issue's orphan rows in forest order; the search starts at the first orphan row that comes after the parent row in forest order and then alternates: first after, second after, last before, third after, second before, and so on. A candidate that is an ancestor of the parent row (taking moves already planned in this run into account) is skipped. An orphan row that is used is no longer an orphan. When no candidate fits, see the cycle-breaking rule; otherwise a new row is added.

Cycle breaking: walking up from the parent row, the first row that is not held in place by a link is found (a row is held when its issue may be a child, it is not an orphan, and its parent row's issue may be a parent); call it M. When the only orphan rows of the missing child are ancestors of the parent row and M exists, the last such orphan row in forest order (skipping M itself) is used: M is first moved out (with its subtree) to sit right after the topmost ancestor of that orphan row reached through rows whose issues may be parents, under that ancestor's parent (top level when none), and then the orphan row is moved under the parent row. M stops being an orphan when its issue has no link parents. Example (resync, primacy `links`, no filters): forest [X > A] with the single link A -> X (A parent of X): result [A > X], both original rows kept.

While walking up from the parent row to M (the first ancestor-or-self not held in place by a link), the issues of the rows passed (the parent row and its held ancestors, not M) are remembered. A missing child that is one of these issues is not added as an issue: a loop-marker row `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-loop-marker/<id of that ancestor row>` is added at its position instead. The same applies inside newly added nested rows (a nested child equal to a newly added ancestor gets a marker pointing to that new row). When, on that walk, an ancestor row above the parent row has the parent row's own issue, nothing at all is added under that parent row.

Worked example (resync, primacy `links`, either orphan action, no filters): links A -> B and B -> A, forest [A > B]. B is in place, the top-level A row is an orphan (A has link parent B) that cannot be reused under B because it is B's ancestor, so a new row A' with a loop marker to B is first added under B; the loop rule then merges A' into the top A row and replaces it with a marker. Final forest: [A > B > ↻A], where ↻A is a `type-loop-marker` row pointing to the top A row. No links are written.

Link parents that have no row in the structure and were not added during this run are reduced to the roots of the link graph above them (issues with no link parent, or one issue of a cycle). With primacy `links`, or `none` for roots not removed from the structure in this batch, these roots are added in one block at the top level, after the row that was the last top-level row before this run's additions, in ascending issue id order, each with its link subtree built as for missing children (orphan rows reused). Example (resync, primacy `links`, `expandParent` true): forest [X], link P -> X with P not in the structure: result [P > X], X's original row moved under the new P row.

Orphans still left after missing children are placed are first merged, issue by issue in ascending issue id, into another row of the same issue that is not an orphan (anywhere in the forest, any depth): the candidate nearest by forest index is tried first (the preceding one on a tie), then the others alternating after/before; a candidate inside the orphan's own subtree is skipped. Merging moves the orphan's children into the target and removes the orphan row. Example (resync, primacy `links`): link P -> X, forest [F > X > Y, P > X2] where X2 is a second row of X and F a folder: the X row under F is an orphan and is merged into X2: result [F, P > X2 > Y]. The merge is tried once more after the orphan action for orphans still present.

Merging a row R into a target row T (used for duplicate siblings, orphans and loops): R's children are matched to T's children by item (loop markers resolved to the item of the row they point to); a matched child is merged recursively into T's matching child, unmatched children are moved under T after its last child, keeping their order; then R is removed. Nothing happens (and the merge counts as failed) when R and T are the same row (`StructureErrors.INVALID_FOREST_OPERATION`, message `cannot merge row <R> into itself`), when either row is not in the current forest, or when T lies in R's subtree. If a child move fails, R is kept.

With `orphanAction` `remove`, an orphan row is removed (with its subtree) only when its parent row's issue may be a parent and the orphan's issue has no link parent at all among the collected links; other orphans are moved up as for `moveUp`. Orphans inside a subtree being removed are removed with it, except that orphans there that cannot be removed are rescued. Example (resync, primacy `links`, source of truth Jira): forest [P > X], no links: `remove` gives [P]; `moveUp` gives [P, X].

When an orphan row is removed, rows inside its subtree are rescued (moved out with their subtrees before the removal) when they are orphans that cannot be removed, or when they are non-orphan rows whose issue may be a parent, whose parent row is not a non-orphan row of a possible-parent issue, and which have at least one non-orphan child row of a possible-parent issue. Rescued rows go, in forest order, to the place the removed orphan would have been moved up to. Example (resync, primacy `links`, `remove`, no filters): link R -> S only, forest [P > X > F > R > S] with F a folder: X is removed with F, R is rescued: result [P, R > S].

Moving an orphan up: walking up from its parent row, rows whose issue may be a parent are passed; the orphan (with its subtree) is placed under the first ancestor that is not such a row (top level when there is none), right after the topmost passed ancestor. When the parent row itself is not a possible-parent row (top level, folder, issue failing the parent filter) the orphan stays. Orphans with the same destination are moved together in forest order; removals are applied after all moves. Example: forest [F > P1 > P2 > X] with F a folder, P1 and P2 possible parents, X an orphan: result [F > [P1 > P2, X]].

Before the scans, among the children of each row (never at the top level), rows of the same issue are merged into the first one when the issue has links in the collected set or (incremental) changed in the batch and may be a child. If the first one is a loop marker and a later one is a regular issue row, the loop marker is merged into the regular row instead. Example: [P > [X, Y, X2]] with X2 a second row of X gives [P > [X, Y]] with X2's children appended to X's children; top-level duplicates [X, X2] are left alone.

Loop rule, applied to rows of relevant issues after all moves: when a row's issue is already the issue of one of its ancestor rows that has children (the outermost such ancestor), the row is merged into that ancestor and a loop-marker row pointing to the ancestor row is added under the row's former parent at the row's former position (after its former preceding sibling, first when none); rows inside a subtree merged this way are merged without further markers. A loop-marker row that already points to that ancestor is kept (only its children, if any, are merged into the ancestor). A loop-marker row whose issue is not an ancestor's issue is converted: a new issue row is added just before it under the same parent, its children are moved under the new row, and the marker is removed (if adding fails the marker stays, if moving fails the marker is not removed).

Links are collected, then every link whose parent fails the parent filter or whose child fails the child filter is dropped, and the expansion from the structure's issues is redone over the remaining links. So `expandChild`/`expandParent` only reach issues through in-scope links. Example (`expandChild` true, primacy `links`): structure [X], links X -> C and C -> D, child filter excluding C: neither C nor D is added; without the filter the result is [X > C > D].

The synchronizer judges a story row by its nearest epic ancestor: the closest ancestor row (any depth) whose issue is an in-scope epic. Folders, other items and issues that are neither in-scope epics nor in-scope stories are transparent (a story under E > Folder > S counts as under E). An epic row is never treated as a story, and a nearer epic row hides outer ones (in E1 > E2 > S, S is under E2). A story row with no epic ancestor counts as under no epic.

Jira to structure (epics): for each epic row, its Jira stories in scope that have no correctly placed row under it are completed. Stories moved in from elsewhere are appended after the epic row's last child; stories with no row at all are inserted as new rows, in Jira's epic-link order, right after the child row of the epic row that is or holds the last story row found correctly under that epic (in forest order), or as first children when there is none. Insertions happen before moves. Example: epic E with Jira stories S1, S2, S3; forest [E > [S1, N], E2 > S3] with S2 not in the structure and N a non-story: result [E > [S1, S2, N, S3], E2].

A story row is misplaced when its nearest epic ancestor is not its Jira epic (in scope), including a story under no epic whose epic has a row. It is moved (with its subtree) under a row of its Jira epic: the nearest row of that epic before it in forest order or after it outside its own subtree, the nearer one by row distance, ties to the one before. A story whose epic is not in scope or has no row, and which is under no epic, stays. Example: forest [E, S] with S's epic E: result [E > S].

When the chosen epic row is itself an ancestor of the misplaced story (an inner epic row hides it), the story is moved to the deepest ancestor between them that is not being moved itself, whose own nearest epic is the story's epic, and that is not a row of the story itself; if there is none, under the epic row. Example: forest [E > F > E2 > S] with F a folder and S's epic E: result [E > F > [E2, S]].

A story row under an epic row it does not belong to, whose own epic is not in scope, has no row, or is none, is moved out of the epics: it goes under the parent of its outermost epic ancestor (the deepest ancestor such that it and every ancestor above it are not epic rows), after that row's last child, or to the end of the top level when the outermost epic row is a top-level row. Example: [F > E1 > S] with S in no epic: result [F > [E1, S]]; [E1 > S]: result [E1, S]. Issues are never removed by this step.

Story rows inside the subtree of a row that is being moved or bubbled travel with it: a story there that would go to the same destination is not moved separately; one bound elsewhere gets its own move. Story rows inside a moved subtree whose issues were not under examination (on incremental sync) are left in the moved subtree and recorded; after the rank step their Jira epic is set to their new nearest epic ancestor when that differs and is not none (see escapees).

Destination rows are handled from the bottom of the forest up, the top level last. When the destination row already has a direct child row of the arriving story, the arriving row is merged into it (children joined, arriving row removed) instead of being moved; several rows of the same story arriving at one destination become one row. Before and, when a move had to break a cycle, after the step, sibling rows (same parent, including the top level) of the same in-scope epic or story are merged into the first one.

Structure to Jira on incremental sync, for each row of each change in the batch (with epics synced): ADD or COPY of a story row (story in scope, its current epic none or in scope) under an epic ancestor sets the story's epic to the nearest epic ancestor; added at a place with no epic ancestor does nothing. MOVE of a story row sets its epic to the nearest epic ancestor after the move, or removes it from its epic when there is none (only when its current epic is none or in scope). REMOVE of a story row whose nearest epic ancestor before removal was its own epic removes the story from the epic, even if another row of it stays under that epic. Moving an epic row marks all its stories as moved for the rank step. With source of truth Jira, stories whose epic link Jira changed in the same batch are skipped. Example: moving S from [E1 > S, E2] to [E1, E2 > S] sets S's epic to E2.

Resync, structure to Jira (source of truth structure): only the first row of each story in forest order decides its epic: under an epic ancestor E different from its Jira epic, its epic becomes E; under no epic ancestor, it is removed from its epic only when that epic issue has a row in the structure. Then every story of an epic that has a row, which appears under no row of that epic as nearest epic ancestor, is removed from the epic. Examples: Jira S in E; forest [E, S]: S is removed from E; forest [E > S2]: the other stories of E are removed from E; forest [S, E > S'] with S' a second row of S: the first row decides and S is removed from E although a row of it is under E (as the original does).

On incremental sync, story rows that were carried along inside a subtree moved by the epics step (escapees) are written back to Jira after the rank step: each such story under an epic ancestor different from its Jira epic gets that epic; escapees under no epic keep their Jira epic. These changes are reported as their own audit actions after the batch's epic actions.

Jira to structure (rank): under each examined parent row (including the top level), the child rows of issues in the rank scope (the board filter or project query) are made to follow Jira rank order with the fewest moves: the largest set already in rank order stays (when several exist, the backtracking keeps the earlier rows of a swapped pair), every other one is moved to sit right after the row of the issue ranked just before it among these siblings, or to the very first position under the parent when it is ranked first. Rows of other items keep their relative places. Nothing is done with fewer than two issues in the rank scope. Examples (rank A < B): [B, A] gives [A, B]; [N, B, A] with N not in scope gives [A, N, B].

Which parents are re-sorted from rank: on resync, all parent rows. On incremental sync, with independent ranking: the parent rows changed by the batch or by the epics step, the parents of rows whose issue Jira updated in the batch or whose position changed in this run (moved, added, merged or re-ranked); with consecutive ranking: every parent row, but only when anything changed. The rank-scope order is read once per pass by searching the scope query and is re-read after ranks were written.

Consecutive ranking (structure to Jira): the forest order is the order of first appearance of each issue in a depth-first walk of all rows. The rank-scope non-sub-task issues, read in rank order, are re-ranked so those that are in the structure follow the forest order with the fewest moves (same rule as rank in); issues not in the structure keep their rank. Then sub-tasks in the rank scope, read in rank order, are taken in consecutive runs with the same parent issue and each run is re-ranked the same way. Any change to the structure in a batch triggers this for the whole structure. Example: top level [B, A, C], Jira rank A, B, C, D: B is ranked before A (`RankService.rankBefore(B, A)`), audit action `{type:updateRank, issue:B, newBefore:A, oldAfter:A, oldBefore:C, rankField}`; final rank B, A, C, D.

Independent ranking (structure to Jira): under each examined parent (resync: all; incremental: parent rows changed by the batch or by the epics and rank steps, and parents having a moved child row), consecutive rank-scope sibling issues give constraints 'previous before next'. Issues linked by constraints form groups; each group gets one order satisfying its constraints (when the constraints conflict, some order is picked) and its issues are re-ranked among themselves to that order with the fewest moves. Issues under unexamined parents and in other groups keep their relative ranks. Example: [P > [B, A]], rank A, B, X: B is ranked before A; X untouched.

Each planned rank move 'issue W right after V' (V none = to the front) is skipped when W is already right after V; otherwise, if W is above its target position it is ranked with `rankAfter(W, V)`, and if below with `rankBefore(W, U)` where U is the issue currently right after V in the working rank list (the first issue when V is none). The move is skipped (debug log only) when W, or the target issue V or U, is in the forbidden set. The working list is updated after each attempt, so later moves see earlier ones.

Incremental sync steps and conflict sets: events of type `GH_EPIC_UPDATED` and link events of the epic link type count as Jira epic changes, all other Jira events as Jira updates. (1) Epics are written from the batch's structure changes; (2) ranks are written for changed parents with a forbidden set of the issues Jira updated in the batch plus newly added issues (source of truth Jira) or only the newly added issues (source of truth structure); (3) epics are synced into the structure for the affected stories and epics; (4) sub-tasks forced; (5) ranks synced into the structure; (6) escapees written to Jira; (7) ranks written again with no forbidden set. Audit actions: epic actions of (1), then of (6), then all rank actions.

Incremental scope: epics and stories in scope are first taken from the structure's issues. The changed issues (Jira-changed and structure-changed in the batch) give their epics (an epic counts as its own epic); the examined stories are all Jira stories of those epics plus the changed issues that are not epics, keeping those matching the stories query; examined sub-tasks are the changed non-epic issues matching the sub-task query; examined epics are those epics matching the epics query. These are added to the scope.

The copied rows are placed among the inserter row's siblings, right after the inserter row and its own subtree, keeping the source's levels (no depth limit) and order; source top-level rows become siblings of the inserter. Example: generated forest [F > [I, Z]] with I the inserter and source structure [A > A1, B]: result [F > [I, A > A1, B, Z]].

With `rowId` not 0 only the descendants of that source row are copied, its children becoming siblings of the inserter. A `rowId` that is a leaf inserts nothing (no warning); a `rowId` missing from the source forest inserts nothing and logs a warning. Example: source [A > [A1 > A2, A3], B], `rowId` = A: inserted [A1 > A2, A3].

In a structure viewed with security, every row whose generation history includes a sub-structure inserter whose source structure (id not 0) the viewing user cannot VIEW is hidden, together with its subtree; other hidden-row rules apply on top.

When sub-structure inserters form a cycle (a structure inserts itself, directly or through other inserted structures), each inserter on the cycle that does not reuse rows (`reuseRows` false, as built from the form) inserts nothing and takes no part in edit handling; inserters with `reuseRows` true stay active.

An edit is passed to the source only when its target position touches the inserted rows: the target parent is an inserted row (then the source row it was copied from), or the inserter's own row (then the top level of the source, or the `rowId` row when set); otherwise the neighbours decide: an inserted `after`/`before` row is mapped to its source row, `after` equal to the inserter row means first position, and other rows count as none. An add whose parent is not an inserted row but whose after/before is one goes to the source's top level (or under `rowId`) next to that row. Directly under a title row whose child is the inserter, and (for an inserter created for a transformation) under any row whose subtree holds inserted rows, the position maps to the source top level, keeping only inserted neighbours; an add with an empty position (no parent, no neighbours) also goes to the source top level. Example: generated [I, A, B] from source [A, B]: adding X after A (top level) adds X to the source's top level after A.

Mapped actions are then handled by the source structure's own generators and stored rows exactly as if made there: adding or copying at a mapped position adds there; moving an inserted row to a mapped position moves its source row, and moving it outside the inserted rows removes it from the source (disown); moving a row from elsewhere into the inserted rows adds it to the source (adopt); removing an inserted row removes its source row. Copied rows in the moved fragment are replaced by their source rows, and repeated copies of one source row are dropped.

Checks before passing an edit to the source, in this order: stored `disableActions` true blocks with `s.ext.gen.block.update-disabled` (`Changes via <product> are not allowed in generator settings.`); a source that cannot be obtained (no `forestSpec`, the structure missing or not VIEW-able, or not a generated forest) blocks with `s.ext.gen.block.not-editable` (`Forest is not editable.`); a source structure id of 0 blocks with the same text; for an untransformed source spec the current user needs EDIT on the source structure, or AUTOMATE when the action's fragment contains generator or effector rows, else it blocks with `s.item.edit.error.no-edit-perm` / `s.item.edit.error.no-automate-perm` (`No "Edit"|"Automate" permission for structure {0}.` with the source structure id); a transformed source spec has no permission check here. A block stops all generators after the inserter; the edit then fails with `StructureErrors.FOREST_SOURCE_ACTION_FAILED` whose message is that text.

The inserter is not an action-handling generator, so its form gets `canHandleUpdates`=false and building parameters from a form never stores `disableActions`, whatever `allowUpdates` says; only parameters written another way (for example over REST) can carry `disableActions`=true.

`item-provider` answers only attribute id `item` and reads no params (a request with extra params is still served, following the `SimpleAttributeProvider` matching rules, C-0194/C-0195). It registers two loaders: one in the generic value format (`ValueFormat` id `value`) and one in format `any`. A request for `item:any` gets the raw-object loader, a request for `item:value` the extended-value loader; for any other requested format the extended-value loader (registered first) is chosen.

For `item` in the `value` format, the value of every row is the row's own `ItemIdentity` (the identity itself, not the resolved object), for every item type, including items that do not exist or the user cannot see; the loader resolves nothing. Its caching strategy is `MAY`.

For `item:any`, the value is the object the item resolves to for the attribute context (`ItemAttributeContext.getItem(Object.class)`): for example the Jira `Issue` for an issue, the `Project`, `ApplicationUser`, `Folder`, `GenericItem` and so on. An item that does not resolve (missing, invisible, or of a type whose app is absent) gives the undefined value. This loader supports every item type and its caching strategy is `SHOULD_NOT` (values are never kept in the value cache).

`displayable-provider` answers only attribute id `displayable` (format text) and reads no params. Every value is a localized text built with the attribute context's i18n helper (`AttributeContext.getI18n()`), so every part declares the `USER_LOCALE` context dependency. Items of types not listed in the following claims get the undefined value.

For an issue row with a key the value is `s.ext.it.issue.displayable` (`issue {0} ({1})`) with the issue key and the summary shortened to at most 30 characters the way Commons Lang `StringUtils.abbreviate(s, 30)` does (a longer summary becomes its first 27 characters plus `...`). For an issue without a key (a new issue being created) it is `s.ext.it.new-issue.displayable` (`a new issue ({0})`) with the shortened summary. The issue comes from the row's `item` attribute; for the new-issue row (`CoreIdentities.NEW_ISSUE`) whose `item` is not an `Issue`, the issue object carried by the row itself is used. An issue row whose issue cannot be obtained gets the undefined value. The value depends on the `item` attribute.
An issue whose summary is null gives the text with the summary argument null, which Jira's i18n formatting shows as the text `null` (e.g. `issue ABC-1 (null)`).

For a folder row the value is `s.ext.it.folder.displayable` (`folder {0}`). For a folder with a string item id (a generated folder) the argument is the folder name translated as an i18n key with the context's i18n helper (an unknown key comes back as is); for a folder with a long id it is the folder name unchanged. The folder comes from the row's `item` attribute, or for the new-folder row (`CoreIdentities.NEW_FOLDER`) from the row itself; otherwise the value is undefined.
Every generator item gets `s.ext.it.generator.displayable` (`a generator`) and every effector item `s.ext.it.effector.displayable` (`an effector`), whether or not the generator or effector exists.

For a row whose item type is a generic item type (memos, planning tasks and any other item type registered as a generic item type in `extension-service`) the value is the item type module's `displayable` text (its descriptor's configured displayable i18n text) formatted with the generic item's name. If the item type has no descriptor, or the generic item cannot be obtained (from the `item` attribute, or for long id `Long.MAX_VALUE` from the row itself), the value is undefined. A null text gives the undefined value.

For resolved items of the following types the value is the i18n key (whose literal name contains the `+` signs) with one argument: project `s.ext.it.+project+.displayable` (`project {0}`, the project name); component `s.ext.it.+component+.displayable` (`component {0}`, its name); version `s.ext.it.+version+.displayable` (`version {0}`, its name); issue type `s.ext.it.+issuetype+.displayable` (`issue type {0}`, the translated name); status, resolution and priority `s.ext.it.+status+.displayable`, `s.ext.it.+resolution+.displayable`, `s.ext.it.+priority+.displayable` (`status {0}`, `resolution {0}`, `priority {0}`, the raw untranslated name); user `s.ext.it.+user+.displayable` (`user {0}`, the display name); group `s.ext.it.+group+.displayable` (`group {0}`); label `s.ext.it.+label+.displayable` (`label {0}`); custom field option `s.ext.it.+cfoption+.displayable` (`option {0}`, the option value, or `Parent - Child` for a child option as `JiraFunc.OPTION_NAME`, C-0879); structure `s.ext.it.+structure+.displayable` (`structure {0}`); sprint `s.ext.it.+sprint+.displayable` (`sprint {0}`, the raw sprint name); Tempo account `s.ext.it.+tempo-account+.displayable` (`account {0}`, its name); version name `s.ext.it.+version-name+.displayable` (`version name {0}`); loop marker `s.ext.it.+loopmarker+.displayable` (`a loop marker`, no argument used). An item of these types that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

`number-sum-provider` answers only attribute id `sum`. Params read: `attribute` (the summed attribute, a nested spec object `{id, format, params}` read as `SpecParams.getAttributeParameter`, C-0961), `distinct` (boolean, default false), `type` (string: `preceding` selects a running total; any other value, or none, is the reduction strategy type of `ReductionStrategy`, default `subtree`), and with `distinct` also `rowBased` (boolean, default false). Any other param (for example `levels` and `baseLevel`) is passed along unchanged in the spec to the sum loaders and the duplicate-counting attribute.

The sum's value format is chosen in this order: (1) if the requested format is `number` or `duration`, that format is used and `attribute` is read expecting it (its stored `format` must be absent, the same, or `any`); (2) otherwise, if `attribute` carries a stored standard format that is `number` or `duration`, that format is used; (3) otherwise a `number` sum is tried, reading `attribute` as `number`, which succeeds only when its stored format is `any` (or absent/`number`). Example: `sum:text` over `{id: votes, format: number}` is served as a number sum; over `{id: x, format: duration}` as a duration sum.

The provider declines (returns no loader) when the id is not `sum`, when `attribute` is missing or not an object, when its stored format conflicts with the format chosen above, or, for a requested format other than `number`/`duration`, when `attribute` has no stored format or a stored format other than `number`, `duration` or `any`. So a dependent stored as `text` (e.g. `{id: x, format: text}`) is not summed.

Without `distinct` and with a `type` other than `preceding`, a duration sum totals the summed attribute's `Long` values as `LongSumLoader` does (C-0180/C-0181) and a number sum as `NumberSumLoader` does (C-0189 to C-0191), aggregating over the forest with the reduction strategy named by `type` (`subtree` default: the row's own value plus its sub-rows; `children`, `leaves`, `strict` as in C-0267 to C-0270). Undefined values are skipped; a sum with no defined contribution is undefined. The sum depends only on the summed attribute.

With `type` = `preceding` (and no `distinct`) the value of each row is a running total of the summed attribute over the rows that precede it in forest order plus the row itself, as `ScanningLongSumLoader` (duration, C-0192) or `ScanningNumberSumLoader` (number, C-0193) computes it.

With `distinct` = true each item is counted once within what a row totals: the value is the non-distinct sum (the same spec without `distinct` and `rowBased`) minus, for every item that occurs k > 1 times among the counted rows, (k - 1) times that item's value. Only items that occur more than once in the whole forest are considered. Example: row A (own 5) with children B (3), C (2) and B again gives 13 without distinct and 10 with distinct. With `type` = `strict` the row's own item is counted one time fewer (strict sums exclude the row itself). Duration and number variants behave alike (numbers keep their accumulated `Number` type).

A distinct sum depends on the non-distinct sum spec (same id, format and params minus `distinct` and `rowBased`) and on the `-non-unique-items` attribute (format `counts`) carrying the traversal params `type`, `levels` and `baseLevel` of the request (a `type` of `strict` or `subtree` is dropped), which `non-unique-items-provider` serves. The duplicated items' values are, by default, each item's own value of the summed attribute loaded separately for that item; when `rowBased` is true, or when the summed attribute is not an item-based attribute, they are taken instead from an extra `-non-unique-items` dependency in format `values` with the summed attribute as its `attribute` param (the values shown in the rows). The second case also logs at INFO `attempt to use SUM with a row-based attribute - forcing rowBased=true for the sum of <spec>`.

For a distinct sum, when the non-distinct total is an error or undefined that same value is returned unchanged; when loading the duplicated items' values fails, the value is the error value and a warning `-- item loader failed, there may be missing values` is logged (throttled per spec). An item whose value is undefined is not subtracted.

`error-provider` answers only attribute id `value-expand`, in format `json` (a JSON object), and needs param `attribute`: a nested spec `{id, format, params}` whose `format` names a standard value format (read as `SpecParams.getAttributeParameter` with no expected format, C-0961). Without `attribute`, or when it has no format or a non-standard one, the spec is declined. The value depends only on that inner attribute.

For each row the value is a one-key JSON object built from the inner attribute's value: an error value gives `{"error": <code>}` where code is the formula error code carried by the value (see `expr-attribute`), or -1 when the error carries none; any other undefined value (plain undefined, absent, inaccessible) gives `{"undefined": true}`; a defined value v gives `{"value": v}`. The result itself is always defined.

`main-provider` answers attribute ids `summary` (text), `description` (html, and a separate text variant when `description` is requested in format `text`), `extended-summary` (html) and `url` (text). It reads no params. Item types not listed below get the undefined value.

`summary` per item type: issue: its summary; project: its name; version: its name; label: the label; status: its name translated for the context locale; issue type: its translated name; resolution and priority: the raw (untranslated) name; component: its name; custom field option: the option value (or `Parent - Child`, C-0879); group: its name; structure: its name; version name: the name. An item that does not resolve gets the undefined value, and a null name gives the undefined value.

`summary` of a folder: for a folder with a string item id (generated folder), a name starting with `/` is returned without that first character, and any other name is treated as an i18n key and translated for the Jira logged-in user; for a folder with a long id the name is returned unchanged; an unresolved folder gives the undefined value. This part declares `USER_LOCALE` and caching strategy `MAY`.
`summary` of a user is the user's display name; for an inactive user it is `s.ext.it.user.summary.inactive` (`{0} (Inactive)`) with the display name, translated for the Jira logged-in user.

`summary` of a sprint is the sprint name formatted for the current Structure user by `gh-integration` (board name and state decoration, C-2246); with Jira Software absent sprint items do not resolve and get the undefined value. `summary` of a Tempo account is `s.ext.gen.grouper.tempo.accounts.account.summary` (`{0} {1}`) with the account name and, for an account that is not open, `(` + the translated status (`s.tempo.accounts.status.closed` `Closed` or `s.tempo.accounts.status.archived` `Archived`) + `)`; an open account gives the name followed by one space (as the original does).

`summary` of a Service Management request type is its name, only while the Service Management app is accessible (C-2316; otherwise undefined); of a generic item (any generic item type, memos and planning tasks included) its name; of an Assets (Insight) object its label (undefined when Assets is absent and the object does not resolve).

`description` (html): for a project or version, its description HTML-escaped; an empty or null description gives the undefined value. For a sprint, its goal HTML-escaped (undefined when null). For a generic item of a generic item type other than memo and planning task (whose descriptions come from other providers), its description rendered by Jira's renderer `atlassian-wiki-renderer` (looked up from `RendererManager` once when the provider is created, rendered with no issue context) or, if Jira has no such renderer, HTML-escaped; an empty result gives the undefined value.

`description` in format `text`: a sprint's goal and a version's description as plain text (as `sprint-parameters-provider` and `version-parameters-provider` serve them), and for a generic item of a type other than memo and planning task its raw description (empty or null gives the undefined value). Projects have no text description from this provider.

`extended-summary` (html) is served for generator and effector items: the value is always defined, `CONTENT` for generators and `CONTENT` for effectors, with CONTENT `?` when nothing could be produced. The loader declares the `TRAIL` context dependency; for a sub-structure inserter generator it adds the inserted structure to the trail, so a change of that structure invalidates the value.

For a resolved generator with a module descriptor, or an effector instance whose module (descriptor and effector) is installed, CONTENT is the module's `summary` Velocity resource rendered with the module's summary parameters and trimmed (leading and trailing whitespace and ` `/` `/` ` removed). Each string parameter is shown as `VALUE` (HTML-escaped), a collection as such spans joined by `, `, a blank string or empty collection as `none specified` (`s.ext.aut.none-specified`); the template also gets `i18n`, `rawParameters` and `noneSpecified`. If the rendered summary is blank, the module label is used, else its key (with a warning). Exceptions while the module adds its parameters are logged and ignored. An effector instance with a non-blank `effectorName` parameter shows that name HTML-escaped instead.

An unresolvable generator, or one without a descriptor, gets `s.ext.gen.summary.unknown` (`Unknown generator {0}`) with `MODULEKEY`, the module key the generator manager records for that generator id (`?` if none), in the current user's locale. An effector whose module is not installed gets `s.ext.eff.summary.unknown` (`Unknown effector {0}`) with the instance's module key in that span; when the effector instance itself does not resolve, the item id's simplified text is shown in place of the module key.

`url` (text): issue and project: `<base URL>/browse/<KEY>`; user: `<base URL>/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<username>`; memo and planning task: the board link of `generic-item-type-helper` (C-2687); Assets (Insight) object: `<base URL>/secure/insight/assets/<object key>`. The base URL is the attribute context's base URL. Keys and usernames are HTML-escaped (not URL-encoded); the Assets key is inserted as is. Other item types get the undefined value.

`key-provider` answers only attribute id `key` (format text) and reads no params. Values: issue and project: the Jira key; user: the username (login name, not the key); memo: `MEMO:<id>` and planning task: `PT:<id>` (C-2687); Assets (Insight) object: its object key. Items that do not resolve, and all other item types, get the undefined value.

An issue whose key is null (a new issue not yet created) gives a key value created from null: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) this throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the value is the plain undefined value.

`done-provider` answers only attribute id `done` (format boolean) and reads no params. Only issues get a value; other item types get the undefined value, and an issue that does not resolve is undefined.
By default an issue is done (true) exactly when its status's status category key is `done`; an issue with no status, or a status without a category, is not done (false).
When the dark feature `structure.doneAttribute.byResolution` is true (read once, when the provider is created; default false), an issue is done exactly when it has a resolution, whatever its status.

`editable-provider` answers only attribute id `editable` (format boolean), reads no params, and gives true or false for issues, folders, generators, effectors and generic items; other item types get the undefined value. Every part depends on the viewing user (`USER`), and the folder, generator, effector and generic-item parts also declare `TRAIL`.
An issue is editable when Jira's `IssueManager.isEditable(issue, user)` says so for the attribute context's user; an issue that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

A folder with a long id is editable when the folder exists in `folder-manager` and the current user has `EDIT` on its owning structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible(structureId, PermissionLevel.EDIT)`, false for a folder with no owning structure, C-1025); the owning structure is added to the trail, so permission changes on it invalidate the value. A folder with a string id (generated) or that does not exist gives false.

A generator is editable when its item id is a positive even long (a persistent generator; odd transient ids and ids of 0 or less give false), it resolves through the generator manager, the generator module is configurable (the duplicate-removing filter `filter-inserter-extender-duplicates` is not), and `StructureManager.isGeneratorConfigurationAllowed(owningStructure, user)` is true (C-1026). The owning structure is added to the trail. A resolution failure gives false and is logged at debug level.

An effector item with a long id is editable when the effector instance can be read and `StructureManager.isEffectorConfigurationAllowed(owningStructure, user)` is true; the owning structure is added to the trail. A missing instance or any error reading it gives false (logged at debug level); a string id gives false.

A generic item (any generic item type, e.g. memo or planning task) is editable when the current user has `EDIT` on its owning structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible(owner, EDIT)`; no owner gives false); the owning structure is added to the trail. A generic item that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

`icon-provider` answers attribute id `icon` (html) and the per-field icon attributes `project.icon`, `assignee.icon`, `reporter.icon`, `issuetype.icon`, `priority.icon`, `status.icon` and `run-as-user.icon` (all html). `assignee.icon` and `reporter.icon` also read param `print` (boolean): with `print` = true the printable variant is served, otherwise the normal one. No other params are read.

`icon` of an issue is the HTML of `issue-constant-icon-cache` for the issue's type (C-1690 to C-1693; the empty string when the issue has no type). The issue type is added to the trail, so a change of that type invalidates the value; the value declares `USER_LOCALE`.

`icon` of a project, and `project.icon` of an issue (from the issue's `project` attribute), is `` with the key and name HTML-escaped and the attribute context's base URL. `project.icon` declares no context dependencies; an issue without a project gives the undefined value.

`icon` of a user is the HTML of `user-icon-cache` (C-1694 to C-1696). `icon` of a status, issue type or priority item is the HTML of `issue-constant-icon-cache` and declares `USER_LOCALE`; resolutions get no icon (undefined).

`icon` of a version is an empty span with classes chosen by state: unreleased ``, released `... aui-iconfont-version`, archived and unreleased `... aui-iconfont-version-unreleased s-version-icon-archived`, archived and released `... aui-iconfont-version s-version-icon-archived`.

`icon` of a generator is its module's icon: when the generator module declares an icon class (for a sorter whose `desc` parameter is true, the class declared for key `desc` if any), ``; otherwise its `icon` Velocity resource rendered and trimmed; otherwise the undefined value. `icon` of an effector is `` from the descriptor of the instance's effector module; an uninstalled module gives the undefined value.

`icon` of a generic item: when its parameters hold both `iconClass` and `color` (single values), `` with both values HTML-escaped; otherwise `` with the item type module's icon class; the undefined value when the type declares none or has no descriptor.

`icon` of a Service Management request type is the request-type icon HTML (C-2325), only while the Service Management app is accessible (otherwise undefined). `icon` of an Assets (Insight) object is ``.

Per-field icons are derived from the issue's attributes: `assignee.icon` from `assignee` and `reporter.icon` from `reporter` (normal: `user-icon-cache`; with `print` = true: `user-printable-icon-cache`, C-1697), `run-as-user.icon` from `run-as-user` (`run-as-user-provider`) via `user-icon-cache`, all declaring no context dependencies; `status.icon`, `issuetype.icon` and `priority.icon` from `status`, `type` and `priority` via `issue-constant-icon-cache`, declaring `USER_LOCALE`. When the source attribute is undefined (e.g. unassigned) the icon is undefined.

`issue-field-provider` serves, for issues only and with no params read, Jira objects: `type` (format `issuetype`: the `IssueType`), `priority` (`Priority`), `project` (`Project`), `status` (`Status`), `assignee`, `reporter` and `creator` (format `user`: the `ApplicationUser` of that user key). A null field gives the undefined value. Each defined value adds the object's identity to the trail (`CoreIdentities.issueType`, `priority`, `project`, `status`, `user`), so a change of that object invalidates the value.

It also serves `votes` and `watches` (format number: the issue's vote and watcher counts as `Long`), `id` (format id: the issue id as decimal text), and, derived from the object attributes, `project` in format id (the project id as text, from `project`), `issuetype` in format id (the issue type id, from `type`) and `status` in format id (the status id, from `status`). A request for id `project` or `status` gets the object or the id variant according to the requested format (object variant for any other format). Non-issue items get the undefined value.
An issue whose id is null (a new issue) gets `id` = the text `null` (as the original does).

`issue-field-rendering-provider` turns the requested spec into a Jira field id: id `key` becomes `issuekey`; id `customfield` with param `fieldId` (a number or numeric text) becomes `customfield_<fieldId>` (a missing or non-numeric `fieldId` leaves `customfield`); any other id is the field id itself. The value is always HTML (the spec is served in format html whatever format was requested).

It declines field ids that are not `timespent`, `timeestimate` or `timeoriginalestimate` and are not among Jira's available navigable fields as `jira-configuration-cache` lists them (C-2492). Only issues get values; other item types get the undefined value.

`timespent`, `timeestimate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, and custom fields of the Epic Sum Up time type (`aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-time`, value converted as `spic-sum-up-integration` does, C-2302), render as Jira's short formatted duration (`JiraDurationUtils.getShortFormattedDuration(seconds, user locale)`), HTML-escaped and trimmed; a null or zero duration gives the empty string. These declare `USER_LOCALE`; the `excel` param has no effect on them.

User fields (system `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator`, and custom fields whose JSON schema type is `user`) are derived from the same spec in format `user` (same id and params) and rendered by `user-field-renderer` with param `view` as the view mode (C-1701, C-1702); they declare `USER`. An empty user field, or a user the renderer gives nothing for, gives the undefined value.

Any other field renders as Jira's issue navigator column does (`ColumnLayoutItem.getHtml` for that field at position 0), trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace and ` `/` `/` `. With param `excel` = true the display params `textOnly`, `readOnly` and `nolink` (all true) are passed, giving plain text without links for spreadsheet export; otherwise no display params. The field is looked up in Jira's `FieldManager` once per attribute context; a field that is not navigable gives no value. A custom field not relevant for the issue (not in its field configuration context) gives the undefined value.

When Jira's rendering throws (any exception or linkage error), the value is the empty string; a warning `error rendering field <name>(<id>) for issue <key>` is logged only the first time per field within an attribute context.

The Service Management request type field (when the app is present and the field is its request type field) renders as `ICON NAME` with the request-type icon HTML (C-2325) and the HTML-escaped name of the issue's request type (loaded by issue id, C-2319); an issue without a request type gives the undefined value.

Navigator-rendered fields declare context dependencies by field: system fields depend on the user (`USER`) when the field is `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator`, `voter`, `watcher` or `lastViewed`, otherwise only on `USER_LOCALE`; they are time-dependent (`USER_TIMEZONE` and `CURRENT_TIME`) when the field is `duedate`, `lastViewed`, `timetracking`, `created`, `updated`, `resolutiondate` or `worklog`. Custom fields whose type key starts with `com.atlassian` depend on `USER` when their type's class name contains `User` or `Group` and are time-dependent when it contains `Date` or `Time`; all other custom fields depend on `USER` and are time-dependent.
For a time-dependent navigator-rendered field whose rendered HTML is empty, the value expires after 1 day (`valueExpires(1, DAYS)`), so it is recomputed at least daily.

If a field id is listed among the available navigable fields but Jira's `FieldManager` then returns no navigable field for it (and it is not a user field), creating the loader fails with a NullPointerException instead of declining (as the original does).

`issue-field-order-provider` serves sort values (format `order`, a `Comparable`) for issues. The field id comes from the spec as in `issue-field-rendering-provider` (`key` becomes `issuekey`; `customfield` with `fieldId` becomes `customfield_<n>`, which it never answers). It answers exactly the field ids listed in the next claims and declines every other id; only `issuetype` declares a context dependency (`USER_LOCALE`). A null value gives the undefined value.

`issuekey`: the tuple (project key, issue number) as a `ComparableTuple`, so ABC-9 sorts before ABC-10; a key Jira cannot parse gives the empty tuple `ComparableTuple.NIL` (sorts first). `issuetype`: the issue type name translated for the user's locale. `status`: the status's sequence. `resolution`: the resolution's sequence, `Long.MIN_VALUE` for an unresolved issue (so unresolved sorts first). `priority`: the negated priority sequence (so the highest priority sorts first in ascending order).

`votes`, `watches`: the counts; `description`, `environment`: the raw text; `duedate`, `resolutiondate`, `created`, `updated`: the Jira timestamps; `timespent`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`: the raw values in seconds (not milliseconds); `workratio`: Jira's work ratio of the issue (`WorkRatio.getWorkRatio`).

`assignee`, `creator`, `reporter`: the user's display name (C-0876); `project`: the project name; `components`: a `ComparableTuple` of the component names in the issue's order; `labels`: a tuple of the label texts; `fixVersions` and `versions` (affects versions): a tuple of the versions' sequences. An issue with no components, labels or versions gets the empty tuple (defined, sorting first).

`issue-time-field-provider` answers attribute ids `timespent` (time spent), `timeestimate` (remaining estimate) and `timeoriginalestimate` (original estimate) for issues, served in format `duration` whatever format was requested, with any params. The value is Jira's value in seconds multiplied by 1000 (milliseconds), e.g. 3600 s gives 3600000; a null value gives the undefined value. Every other id is declined; non-issue items get the undefined value.

`date-field-provider` answers `created`, `updated` and `resolutiondate` for issues in format `time` (whatever format was requested): the Jira timestamp in epoch milliseconds, no correction; a null date (e.g. unresolved) gives the undefined value.

`duedate` is a date-only field. With param `disableDateShift` = true the value is the due date's stored timestamp in epoch milliseconds, unchanged. Otherwise (param absent or false) the due date is corrected to the viewing user's time zone as `structure-datetime-formatter` does (C-1669: the calendar date in the JVM time zone, at 00:00 in the context's time zone), and the loader declares `USER_TIMEZONE`. No due date gives the undefined value. Every other id is declined.

`enum-customfield-order-provider` answers only attribute id `customfield` in format `order`, with param `fieldId` (long). It declines other ids, other formats, a missing or 0 `fieldId`, a field id Jira's `CustomFieldManager` does not know, and custom field types not listed in the next claim. Values are for issues only; an issue for which the field is not relevant (outside its configuration context) and an empty field give the undefined value.

Sort values by the Jira custom field type (checked in this order): single select: the option's sequence; multi select: the first selected option's sequence; cascading select: (parent sequence, child sequence) as a `ComparableTuple` when a child is chosen, (parent sequence, `Long.MIN_VALUE`) when only a parent is; labels: the first label's text; project picker: the project's name (looked up by id in `ProjectManager`); version picker: the first version as the tuple (project key, version sequence, version name); single user: the user's display name; ScriptRunner user-aware script field (type class `com.onresolve.scriptrunner.customfield.UserAwareScriptField`, only when ScriptRunner is installed): its user's display name; multi user: the first user's display name; multi group: the first group's name.

For a field whose type key starts with `com.coresoftlabs.secure-fields.secure-fields` (the Secure Fields app), the loader adds the `USER` context dependency, so values are computed per viewing user; other fields add none.

Answers only attribute id `customfield`. The custom field is named by the params key `fieldId`, read as a long (a JSON number or a numeric string, e.g. 10010, not `customfield_10010`). A missing, zero or non-numeric `fieldId` makes the provider decline (no loader), and so does an id for which Jira's CustomFieldManager.getCustomFieldObject(long) returns no field. Any other attribute id is declined.

The kind of value is chosen from the custom field, first by its type key and then by its JSON schema type, in this order: Jira Software sprint (`com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-sprint`), service desk request type (`com.atlassian.servicedesk:vp-origin`), Tempo account (`com.tempoplugin.tempo-accounts:accounts.customfield`), Tempo team (`com.tempoplugin.tempo-teams:team.customfield`), Advanced Roadmaps team (`com.atlassian.teams:rm-teams-custom-field-team`), Epic Sum Up time (`aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-time`), the Epic Sum Up client-side fields (declined), then schema type `date` or `datetime` (time), numeric fields (number), schema type `user` (user), the Xray status fields (text with test-run tracking) and finally every other field (text). The requested value format does not change the kind, except for the date and Epic Sum Up text forms described separately: the loader serves the kind's own format (TEXT, NUMBER, TIME, DURATION or the user format).

Except for the service desk request type, values exist only for issue items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`) that resolve to a Jira Issue. When the field is not relevant for the issue (CustomField.isRelevantForIssueContext(issue) is false: wrong project or issue type), the value is undefined without reading the field.

For a Jira Software sprint field the value is TEXT: the names of the sprints in the field value (CustomField.getValue), in the field's order, joined with `, ` (comma and space). Elements that are not sprints are left out. A null or non-collection value, or an issue with no sprints, gives the empty text, which is a defined value, not undefined. Every sprint in the value is recorded in the loading trail as a sprint item (CoreIdentities.sprint(sprint id)), so the text is recalculated when one of those sprints changes (for example, is renamed).

For the service desk request type field (`com.atlassian.servicedesk:vp-origin`) the value is TEXT: the name of the issue's request type, as `sd-integration-supplier` reports it for the issue id (a query by issue id as the current user). No request type, or Service Management absent, gives undefined. This kind works on the issue id alone: it does not resolve the issue and does not check whether the field is relevant for the issue, but it still applies only to issue items.

For the Tempo Accounts field the value is TEXT: the toString() of the field's value for the issue (CustomField.getValue). A null value gives undefined. If reading the value throws any exception or LinkageError (for example, Tempo is disabled or its classes are missing), the value is undefined and a throttled warning `Failed to load a custom field value for <issue key>` is logged.

For the Tempo Teams field the value is TEXT: the name of the team that `tempo-integration` finds for the field value (a numeric string is read as a team id and looked up, other objects are read as a team). No team, a null value, or Tempo absent gives undefined. Exceptions while reading the field value are caught as for the Tempo account field (undefined plus a throttled warning).

For the Advanced Roadmaps Team field (`com.atlassian.teams:rm-teams-custom-field-team`) the value is TEXT: the field value's toString() is parsed as a long team id and the team's title is taken from `portfolio-integration` (team by id). A null value, a value that is not a number, or an id with no team (or Advanced Roadmaps absent) gives undefined. Exceptions while reading the value are caught as for the Tempo account field.

For the Epic Sum Up time field, when the requested format is neither TEXT nor HTML, the value is a DURATION in milliseconds: a java.lang.Double field value (seconds) times 1000, truncated to a long (e.g. 5400.0 gives 5400000). Any other value, including null, gives undefined. Exceptions while reading the value are caught (undefined, throttled warning). When TEXT or HTML is requested, the value is derived from the same spec in DURATION format and formatted as Jira time-tracking text for the current user, as `format-helper` formats durations (e.g. 5400000 gives `1h 30m` with standard settings). That text value depends on the current user. Epic Sum Up absent: the field does not exist, so the provider declines.

The provider declines (no loader) for the Epic Sum Up fields that are only rendered in the browser, which have these type keys: `aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-attachment-indicator`, `...-comments-indicator`, `...-issue-count-progress`, `...-progress`, `...-status-category-progress`, `...-story-points-progress`, `...-type-allocation` and `...-time-progress`, all with the prefix `aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-`.

For a field whose JSON schema type is `date` or `datetime`, any requested format other than TEXT gives a TIME value (epoch milliseconds) from the java.util.Date field value. A value that is not a Date gives undefined. A `datetime` field's timestamp is returned unchanged. For a `date` field the timestamp is by default shifted as `structure-datetime-formatter` corrects date-only values: the calendar date in the JVM default zone becomes the start of that date in the loading context's time zone. The value then depends on the user's time zone. With the params key `disableDateShift` true (Boolean true or the string `true`), the raw timestamp is returned and the value does not depend on the time zone.

For the Advanced Roadmaps target start and target end fields (`com.atlassian.jpo:jpo-custom-field-baseline-start` and `...-baseline-end`) in a non-TEXT format, the TIME value is the field's Date timestamp converted from a source zone to a target zone. The source zone is UTC when `portfolio-integration` says target dates need a UTC shift (from the `com.atlassian.teams` version), otherwise the JVM default zone. The target zone is the context's time zone unless `disableDateShift` is true, in which case it is the JVM default. When the two zones differ, the timestamp becomes the start of its calendar date (in the source zone) in the target zone; when they are equal it is unchanged. Only the shifted form depends on the user's time zone. A non-Date value gives undefined. The Secure Fields user dependency is not added for these fields.

When TEXT is requested for a `date` or `datetime` field (target date fields included), the value is derived from the same spec in TIME format, and undefined when that value is. It is formatted with a Jira DateTimeFormatter: a `datetime` field uses the current user's formatter with style DATE_TIME_PICKER; a `date` field with date shift (the default) uses the current user's formatter with style DATE; a `date` field with `disableDateShift` true uses Jira's system formatter for the context's locale with style DATE. Only the last depends on the locale alone; the first two depend on the user. The formatter is created once per loading context for each spec.

A field counts as numeric when its JSON schema type is `number`, or when its searcher is Jira's NumberRangeSearcher or ExactNumberSearcher, unless its type key is `com.keplerrominfo.jira.plugins.keplercf:silscriptcf` (that type is numeric only through its schema). The value is a NUMBER: a java.lang.Number field value as it is, or a String parsed as a double. A string that does not parse gives undefined and a throttled warning `Custom field:<field id> value is a string instead of a number`. Any other value, including null, gives undefined.

For a field with JSON schema type `user` (single user picker) the value is the ApplicationUser in the field (user format). The user is recorded in the loading trail as a user item (by user key), so the value is recalculated when that user changes. A value that is not an ApplicationUser, including null, gives undefined.

Every other custom field (text, selects, multi-user and multi-value pickers, versions, labels, cascading and so on) gives TEXT. The field's REST representation is read (CustomField.getJsonFromIssue(issue, false, null)) and its standard data is turned into text by `value-text-converter` for this custom field type. A missing representation or data gives that converter's answer for null, which is undefined. The Jira entities the converter records go into the loading trail, so the text is recalculated when one of them changes.

The Xray status fields `com.xpandit.plugins.xray:test-set-status-custom-field`, `com.xpandit.plugins.xray:test-execution-status-custom-field` and `com.xpandit.plugins.xray:test-plan-status-custom-field` are loaded as TEXT, like other fields. In addition, their values declare a global trail of every item of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:xray-test-run`, so any change to an Xray test run item invalidates them. Without Xray these fields do not exist.

When the custom field's type key starts with `com.coresoftlabs.secure-fields.secure-fields` (Secure Fields app), the values also depend on the current user, so they are computed and cached per user. This applies to the sprint, date (time value), number, user, text and Xray kinds. It does not apply to the request type, Tempo, Roadmaps team, Epic Sum Up or target date kinds. Other fields get no such user dependency from this rule.

For the sprint, date, target date, number and user kinds, an exception thrown by CustomField.getValue is not caught by the provider; it reaches the attribute framework, which handles a failing loader. Only the Tempo account, Tempo team, Roadmaps team and Epic Sum Up time kinds catch read failures and give undefined.

Answers only attribute id `progress`, in three forms: format id `progress` (an internal aggregate holding a progress and a weight per row), format id `issue-progress-data` (internal per-issue data: own progress, overriding progress, own weight), and any other requested format, which is served as a NUMBER. The NUMBER is the progress part of the `progress`-format value with the same params: a fraction from 0 to 1 (e.g. 0.25), undefined when there is none, NaN, or outside 0..1.

The params key `basedOn` selects the method: `timetracking`, `resolution`, `percentfield`, `status` or `category` (exact, case-sensitive). With any other value, or without it, the provider declines the `progress` and `issue-progress-data` forms, so the NUMBER form has no source value. There is no default method.

The params key `weightBy` sets how children are weighted: `equal` (all equal; also used when the key is absent or has any other value), `time` (an issue's time spent plus remaining estimate in milliseconds, only when that total is above 0, otherwise no weight), or `field`, with the field id in `weightByField` (e.g. `customfield_10002`). A `field` weight is the field's numeric value: a Number, or a String parsed as a double. The field must be a numeric custom field: type key `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:float`, or JSON schema type `number` other than the Jira Software rank fields and the import-id field. Otherwise (unknown id, not numeric, or `weightByField` missing) creating the loader fails with StructureProviderException `field <id> not found or not supported`. With `basedOn` = `timetracking`, `weightBy` is ignored and the weight is always the time.

Time tracking: an issue's own progress is computed from its time spent S and remaining estimate R (Issue.getTimeSpent, Issue.getEstimate, in seconds). When both are set: S/(S+R) clamped to 0..1, or no progress when S+R is 0. When only S is set and above 0: 1. When only R is set and above 0: 0. Otherwise there is no progress.
