When the params key `resolvedComplete` is true, a resolved issue (Issue.getResolution not null) has progress 1, whatever its children.

Resolution: an issue's own progress is 1 when it has a resolution and 0 otherwise. A resolved issue always shows 1, whatever its children (`resolvedComplete` is not needed). An unresolved issue with children shows the weighted average of the children; its own 0 is not counted.

Percent field: the params key `percentField` holds a field id. When it is absent, creating the loader fails with StructureProviderException `empty percent field id`. When the field is not a numeric custom field, it fails with `field <id> not found or not supported`. An issue's progress is the field value divided by 100 and clamped to 0..1 (Number values, or numeric String values; 50 gives 0.5, 150 gives 1). An issue with a value shows it, whatever its children. With `resolvedComplete` true, a resolved issue shows 1 instead. Issues without a value show their children's weighted average.

Status or category: the params `statuses` (list of status ids as strings) and `percents` (list of integers) are paired by position, up to the shorter list; for `category`, `categories` (status category ids, e.g. `3`) and `categoryPercents` are used instead. An issue's own progress is percent/100 for its status id (Issue.getStatusId) or its status category id, clamped to 0..1. A status or category not in the lists gives no own progress. Non-numeric entries of the percent list are skipped before pairing. With `resolvedComplete` true, a resolved issue shows 1, whatever its children.

The params key `includeSelf` (boolean, default false) applies to `timetracking`, `status` and `category`. When true, a parent row's own progress joins its children's, with its own weight or, when it has none, the children's average weight (1 if no child has a weight). When false, a parent row's own progress is ignored. For `resolution` and `percentfield` the parent's own progress never takes part (only overrides apply).

A parent row's progress is a weighted average of its children's (progress, weight) values. A child with both contributes progress x weight and its weight. A child with a progress but no weight counts with the average weight of the weighted children (1 when there are none). Children with no progress are left out, except under `timetracking` on an issue row, where they count as progress 0 (with their own weight, or the average one). Negative numbers count as 0. The result is clamped to 0..1, is 0 when the total weight is at most 0.00001, and results below 0.00001 are reported as exactly 0. Example (equal weights): children 0.5 and 1 give 0.75; with time weights 1h at 0.5 and 3h at 1, the result is 0.875.

A leaf row (no children) shows its own progress. Under `timetracking`, an issue leaf with no time-tracking data shows 0. Otherwise, a leaf without progress has none (NUMBER undefined). A parent whose children all lack progress shows nothing, except under `timetracking` on an issue row, where it shows 0. An issue's overriding progress (resolved with `resolvedComplete`, resolved under `resolution`, or its own percent value) replaces any computed value.

Each row also passes a weight up to its parent. A leaf passes its own weight (none under equal weighting). For `resolution` and `percentfield`, a parent passes the sum of its children's weights (unweighted children counted at the average) plus its own weight when at least one child had a real weight, and only its own weight otherwise. For the other methods, a parent passes the summed weight (including itself when `includeSelf` counted it) when at least one child had a real weight, and no weight otherwise.

Generator and effector rows have no progress (undefined), and so do not take part in their parent's average. Rows that are not issues (folders, projects, users and so on) have no own data: they show the weighted average of their children, never an override, and under `timetracking` missing child progress is not counted as 0 for them.

The per-issue progress data is read from the issue (time tracking, resolution, status, the percent or weight field) and should be cached, so it changes when the issue changes. The row values are aggregates that are recomputed when a descendant's data or the forest changes.

Answers only attribute id `worklogged` and serves it as a DURATION (milliseconds, long), whatever format is requested. Only issue items have a value: the total time spent of the issue's work logs (WorklogManager.getByIssue) whose start date is in the period and that pass the author filter, each log's time spent in seconds times 1000. Logs with no time spent are skipped. No matching logs gives 0 (a defined value).

Optional filters, at most one of which may be given: `author` (a user key, matched against the work log's author key ignoring case), `group` (a group name: the log's author must be in the group per Jira's GroupManager.isUserInGroup), or `role` (a project role id or name: the author must be in that role in the log's issue's project per ProjectRoleManager.isUserInProjectRole). A `role` value that parses as a long is looked up by id, otherwise by name. When more than one of the three keys is present, or the role is not found, the provider declines (no loader). With none of them, every log counts.

With the params key `period` set to a preset and `timeZone` set to a time zone id (read with java.util.TimeZone.getTimeZone, so an unknown id means GMT), the period is relative to the current time in that zone. Each period runs from local midnight (inclusive) to local midnight (exclusive): `today` is today; `yesterday` is yesterday; `this_week` is from the first day of the current week to the same day next week; `last_week` is the week before; `this_month` and `last_month` run from the 1st of the month to the 1st of the next; `this_year` and `last_year` run from 1 January to 1 January of the next year. Preset names are exact and case-sensitive.
For `this_week` and `last_week`, weeks start on Monday when Jira's application option `jira.date.time.picker.use.iso8061` is true, and on Sunday otherwise.

When `period` is absent or empty, the period comes from `dateFrom` and `dateTo` (both `yyyy-MM-dd`), read in the zone `timeZone`. It runs from the start of `dateFrom` to the start of the day after `dateTo`, so both days are included. A work log counts when its start date is at or after the start and before the end.

When no period can be formed, the issue gets no value (not 0). That happens when `timeZone` is missing or empty, when `period` names an unknown preset (the dates are then not used), when `dateFrom` or `dateTo` is missing, or when a date does not parse as `yyyy-MM-dd`.

A preset period is worked out once per attribute loading context, from the system clock (System.currentTimeMillis) at the first issue that needs it. All issues loaded together use the same period. Nothing invalidates the values when a period boundary such as midnight passes.
Serves the internal attribute id `user-added-automation` in format id `user-added-automation`, whose value is an ItemIdentity. Rows whose item is not a generator or an effector get no value.
A generator item with a transient long id (positive and odd, i.e. a generator created on the fly rather than saved) gives undefined.

For other generator and effector rows, the row is traced back through transient copies. While the row is a TransientRow whose creator row id is not a persistent id (persistent ids are positive and even), the trace moves to the row's original row (RowManager.getRow(originalId)). The value is the row's item identity (e.g. generator/12) when the trace ends on a row with a persistent row id, meaning a user saved this automation in the structure. It is undefined when the trace ends on a transient row made by a persistent generator, meaning another generator produced it.
If a row on the trace is missing (RowManager throws MissingRowException), the value is an error value and a throttled warning `cannot trace back to original item` is logged.

An internal aggregate with id `children-automations-hint` and format id `children-automations-aggregate` depends on `user-added-automation`. A row that is a user-added generator or effector holds just itself. Any other row collects the user-added generators and effectors among its direct children, in row order. Automations deeper down are not collected, because a child's own collected list is not passed up. A row with none gets undefined. This value may be cached.

The attribute `children-automations-hint` in HTML format exists only for rows with at least one user-added generator or effector among their direct children (not for the automation rows themselves). It is `

` + text of `s.ext.aut.hint.header` (`The contents of structure under this row are automated.`) + `

`. When there are generators, it continues with `

Generators in use:

` (`s.ext.aut.hint.gen.header`) and a `
    ` with one `
  • ` per generator. When there are effectors, it continues with `

    Effectors in use:

    ` (`s.ext.aut.hint.eff.header`) and a `
      ` with one `
    • ` per effector. Texts are in the current user's language.

Each generator entry is `` + the generator's icon HTML + `` + the generator's summary, the same summary `main-provider` shows for that generator row. The generator is resolved from its generator item id. A blank or missing icon gives an empty span. A blank or missing summary gives `(Some automation)` (`s.ext.gen.hint.no-summary`).

Each effector entry has the same span, holding the icon span from the effector module's descriptor, followed by the effector's summary: its `effectorName` parameter HTML-encoded when not blank, otherwise the summary built by the effector module, wrapped as an effector summary span. An effector that cannot be resolved or has no summary shows `Unknown effector <module key>` (`s.ext.eff.summary.unknown`), or `Unknown effector` (`s.ext.eff.summary.unknown-no-module`) when the instance is missing.

Answers only the internal attribute id `-non-unique-items`. The params key `type` picks the traversal. `strict` makes creating the loader fail with StructureProviderException `Non-unique loaders must not be used with 'strict' parameters`. `preceding` selects the running (scanning) form. Any other value uses the aggregate form with the reduction type of that name (`subtree` when absent, `children`, `leaves`). The format must have the id `counts` (a map from item identity to occurrence count) or `values` (a map from item identity to a value); any other format is declined.
Only items that occur more than once in the whole forest are reported. A row whose item is unique in the forest adds nothing, so a subtree where every item occurs once gets undefined.

In `counts` format with the aggregate form, a row's own contribution is {its item: 1} when the item is not unique. Contributions are merged by adding counts per item, following the reduction type (`subtree`: the row and its subtree; `children`: the direct children's own contributions; `leaves`: the leaves). Generator and effector children are ignored, and the first error among child values is returned. Example: an item placed twice under a parent gives {item: 2} on that parent.

In `counts` format with `type` `preceding`, the value is a running map over the rows in forest order (with the `levels` and `baseLevel` rules of scanning loaders). Each passing row whose item is not unique raises that item's count by 1. Unique rows keep the preceding map.

In `values` format, the attribute whose values are collected is the nested attribute spec under the params key `attribute` (an object with `id`, optional `format`, optional `params`; the stored format is used). When it is missing or cannot be built, the provider declines. The aggregate form also depends on the `counts` form with the same `type`, `levels` and `baseLevel` (a `type` of `subtree` or `strict` is dropped).

In `values` format with the aggregate form, a row's own contribution is {its item: that item's value of the nested attribute} when the item is not unique (the value may be null). The result maps each non-unique item of the traversal to its value and has exactly as many entries as the `counts` result. When the counts are absent or empty, the result is undefined. The first error among child values is returned unchanged. With assertions enabled (as the tests run), a result whose size differs from the counts throws AssertionError.

In `values` format with `type` `preceding`, the value is a running map in forest order. Each passing row whose item is not unique adds {item: its nested attribute value} the first time the item is met; later occurrences keep the first value.
Serves attribute id `run-as-user` in the user format, for generator items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator`) only. Values depend on the loading trail.

For a saved generator (positive even long id), the value is the owner of the structure that holds the generator. The structure is read for the current user with VIEW access through `structure-manager`, and its owner user key is looked up with Jira's UserManager.getUserByKey. When the user is found, the structure and the user are recorded in the loading trail, so the value changes when either changes.

The value is undefined for transient generators (odd ids), string ids, generators not held by a structure, a structure the current user cannot view or that does not exist (any StructureException), and an owner key whose user no longer exists. A structure with no owner key also gives undefined, but the structure is still recorded in the trail.

Serves attribute id `original-generator-kind` as TEXT. For a row that a generator produced, the value is a code for the kind of generator that first produced it, taken from the generation history of the forest being loaded (the first generator row id in the row's provenance): `e` extender, `g` grouper, `i` inserter (sub-structure inserters included), `s` sorter. Other generator kinds, rows with no history, a first entry of 0, or loading without generation information give undefined.
The generator row is looked up with RowManager.getRow. If it is missing, the MissingRowException is not caught and reaches the attribute framework.

Serves attribute id `basic-generation-info` as a JSON object for rows created by a generator (TransientRow with a non-zero creator row id). The creator row is looked up (RowManager.getRow) and its generator read. The object has `creator`: `ssi` (sub-structure inserter), `extender`, `grouper` or `inserter`, left out for other kinds. It has `label`: the generator's semantic label, when it has one (only groupers give one, from the grouper's label for its parameters).

The value is undefined for rows not created by a generator, when the creator row is missing (MissingRowException), when the creator row is not a generator, and when the object would be empty (e.g. a sorter with no label).
Its values are never cached (caching strategy SHOULD_NOT); they are computed on every load.

For status items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-status`) that resolve to a Jira Status, the attribute `extended-summary` (HTML) is Jira's status lozenge. It is rendered with the Soy template `JIRA.Template.Util.Issue.Status.issueStatusResolver` from module `jira.webresources:issue-statuses`, with data `issueStatus` = Status.getSimpleStatus(), `isSubtle` false, `isCompact` false and `maxWidth` `medium`. The HTML is trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace and of the entities ` `, ` ` and ` `.

If the template renderer throws SoyException, the value is an error value and a warning `problem rendering status <status>` is logged. A status item that does not resolve gives undefined. Other item types are not served by this module.

`count` (NUMBER, without `leaves`) is the number of rows under a row, at any depth. Generator, effector and loop-marker rows, and everything under them, are not counted. A leaf row gives undefined, not 0. A row that is itself a generator, effector or loop marker gives undefined. A row whose only children are automations gives 0. Example: a parent with two children, one of which has three children, gives 5.

`count` with the params key `leaves` true counts only leaves. A row's value is the sum of its children's values, where a counted leaf child counts 1 and a child that has children counts its own value. The same exclusions and undefined cases apply as for the plain count. With assertions enabled (as the tests run), a child with a defined but null count throws AssertionError.

`depth` and `level` (NUMBER) are the same: 1 for a top-level row, plus 1 for each level below. Both are undefined for title rows (semantics 1), the super-root (row id -1), generators, effectors and loop markers. They depend on the whole forest.

`itemtype` (TEXT) is the row's item type in short form for any item: the `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-` prefix removed, e.g. `issue`, `folder`, while other keys stay whole. `itemid` (TEXT) is the item identity in short form, e.g. `issue/10001` or `user//jsmith`. `issueid` (NUMBER) is the issue id for issue items and is not given for other items. These three values may be cached.

The loaders are matched by attribute id: `count`, `depth`, `level`, `itemtype`, `itemid`, `issueid`. A `count` request whose params include `leaves` true gets the leaves count; any other `count` request (including `leaves` false) gets the plain count. Other ids are declined.

Serves `seq` (TEXT): the outline number of each row, propagated down the forest. Top-level rows are numbered `1`, `2`, ... in order. A child of a numbered row gets the parent's number, a dot and its own position among its numbered siblings (e.g. `1.2.3`).

Title rows (semantics 1), generators, effectors and loop markers get no number (undefined) and do not use up a number, so the next sibling takes it. The children of an unnumbered row start again from `1` with no prefix.

Answers attribute id `links-count` only when NUMBER is requested; other formats are declined. The params key `linkTypeId` (long; absent or 0 means all link types) keeps only links of that type. The key `inward` keeps inward links when true and outward links when false (any value that is not true, including null); when the key is absent, both directions are counted.

For issue items the value is the number of matching links from Jira's IssueLinkManager.getInwardLinks(issueId) plus getOutwardLinks(issueId), as a long (0 when none). The count is taken from the issue id without checking whether the user can see the linked issues. Other item types are not served.

`expr-attribute` answers every attribute spec whose id is `expr` (any params, any requested format) and declines every other id. Params read: `formula` (text of the formula, in the language of `expr-parser`; absent means a null formula, which evaluates to undefined per C-1902), `variables` (an object mapping variable names to nested attribute specs, see the variables claim; absent means no variables) and `debug` (boolean, default false). No other params key is read.

A formula that does not parse or fails validation still gets a loader (the spec is not declined and no exception is thrown): every row's value is the formula error 1 (parse error), the loader has no attribute dependencies (variables and aggregations are not requested because the prepared formula reports none, C-1903), and it declares only the fixed context dependencies (TRAIL and USER_TIMEZONE, plus USER_LOCALE when `debug` is true).

Each key of the `variables` object names a variable; the name is put in canonical form (trimmed, lower-cased with US rules, C-1923) and its value is read as a nested attribute spec object (`id`, optional `format`, optional `params`, as `SpecParams.getAttributeParameter` reads it with no expected format). Entries that do not form a valid spec are ignored (the variable is then unbound and evaluates to undefined, C-1930). Only variables that the formula actually uses as free variables become dependencies; mappings for unused names are dropped. When two keys canonicalize to the same name, one of them wins (unspecified which).

Each used variable's attribute spec is requested in the generic value format (`ValueFormat` id `value`) after the conversion of `extended-value-tools` (C-2059: a spec for a Jira Software Epic Link custom field becomes `epicIssue`), whatever format the variable mapping named. The loader's attribute dependencies are exactly these converted variable specs plus one spec per usable aggregation (next claim).

Every aggregation written in the formula (C-1919) becomes an attribute dependency whose spec is built by `expr-aggregation-provider` (C-2030 to C-2039) from the aggregation's inner expression, its modifiers and the formula's own `variables` object, unchanged; the dependency is requested in the aggregation's own format (not converted to the generic format). The aggregation's value is bound under the aggregation's text, so the formula sees it in place of the aggregation. An aggregation whose name is unknown, or whose spec cannot be built (for example a modifier it does not allow), adds no dependency and evaluates to error 11 (C-1930); the rest of the formula still evaluates.

A variable's attribute value becomes a formula value as follows: undefined (null) gives undefined; a Number gives a number (Float/Double through their decimal string form; BigDecimal unchanged; other integer types by their long value); a String gives text; a Boolean gives 1 for true and 0 for false; an `ItemIdentity` gives an item; a List gives an array of the converted elements (null elements become undefined); a Map with String keys gives a struct. If any element of a list or map converts to an error, or the value has an unsupported type, or a map has a non-String key, or a Double is NaN or infinite, the variable evaluates to error 5 (attribute error).

When a variable's or aggregation's attribute value is an error: if the error value carries a formula error as its loader data (as values of another `expr` attribute do), the variable evaluates to that same formula error (same code); otherwise it evaluates to error 11 (aggregation error) when the bound name contains `{` (an aggregation) and to error 5 (attribute error) for a plain variable.

The value format of the result is the requested spec's format when it is one of: number, duration, time, JSON object, order, any, text, boolean, or the generic value format (`value`); any other requested format (for example html) is replaced by text, i.e. the loader produces values for the spec with format text.

Converting the formula result: undefined gives an undefined value in every format except JSON object; an error result gives an error `AttributeValue` whose loader data is that formula error value; a lambda result gives error 7 (with the error as loader data). Otherwise: text format gives the text representation (C-1946); number gives the value converted to a number by the number rules (C-1945) as a BigDecimal, undefined when it has no number; duration and time give that number truncated to a long (milliseconds); boolean gives true/false by truthiness (C-1942); order gives the ordering key of the value per the ordering rules (C-1948).

In the `any` format and in the generic value format the result is passed through structurally: a number as BigDecimal, a text as String, an item as its `ItemIdentity`, an array as a List of the converted elements (undefined elements as null, nested arrays as nested lists), a struct as a Map of String to converted values. An error or lambda anywhere inside an array or struct makes the whole value an error (loader data: that error, or error 7 for a lambda).

In the JSON object format the value is always a map (never an error value): a number gives `{"value": <number>}`; a text `{"value": <text>}`; an array or struct `{"value": <its text representation>}`; an item `{"value": <its display text>}` (error 10 if it has none); undefined gives `{"undefined": true}`; an error gives `{"error": <code>}`; a lambda gives `{"error": 7, "lambda": <the lambda's text form>}`.

The loader declares the context dependencies TRAIL and USER_TIMEZONE always, plus USER, USER_LOCALE, USER_TIMEZONE and CURRENT_TIME for each that the formula's functions depend on (C-1925), plus USER_LOCALE when `debug` is true. So a formula using `now()` is recalculated as time passes and one using `me()` per user, while a formula using none of these is shared by all users with the same time zone.

The loader's caching strategy is SHOULD (values may be cached and reused). The original would use MUST_NOT for a formula depending on external content, but no function of the library declares such a dependency, so in practice every formula attribute reports SHOULD.

Every item whose field, display text or ordering the formula reads (through `access`/`x.field`, text conversion of an item or sorting items) is added to the loading context's trail, so the formula value is recalculated when any of those items changes. In bulk field reads, only items that actually produced a value are added.

Reading a field of an item from a formula asks the item's item type (from the plugin's registered item types) to resolve the item and give the field value. If the item type does not support formulas, or the item does not resolve (missing or not visible: the item type returns null), the field is undefined, the item's display text is its simplified string form (`ItemIdentity.toSimplifiedString`) and its ordering key is the empty tuple (`ComparableTuple.NIL`). Field names are passed in canonical form.

Reading one field of many items at once groups the items by item type (keeping the given order of items within the result): for each type the item type is first asked for the field in bulk; if it cannot, the items not yet loaded are resolved in one bulk call when the item type supports bulk access, and then the field is read item by item. Array field values are flattened and compacted, and undefined and error values are dropped from the result list (C-2009). An item type that does not support formulas contributes nothing. An empty list gives an empty result; a single item is read on its own.

Resolved items are reused across all formula values computed in the same loading pass (shared by all `expr` attributes of that pass). After each value, when more than `structure.expr.maxEntitiesCount` items are held (dark feature, integer, default 10000, read when the provider is created), the least recently used ones are discarded until half that number remain. Items whose identity is not suitable for caching are always resolved afresh. Missing items are remembered as missing.
During normal (bulk) loading, the value for a generator, effector or loop-marker row (`CoreIdentities.isAutomation` or `isLoopMarker` of the row's item) is undefined, without evaluating the formula.

With params `debug` true, the value is not the formula result but a map (in every format) `{"expr": <formula text>, "values": [...]}`: one entry per source range of the formula that was evaluated, each `{"from": <start offset>, "to": <end offset>, "executions": [...]}` with one entry per evaluation of that range, each `{"value": <text>}` plus `"context": "Context: " + the variables in scope as `name = value` joined by `; ` when there are any (prefix from i18n `s.w.formula.debug.context-prefix` = `Context:` in the user's language). Ranges that are empty are not recorded.

In debug mode each recorded value is shown as text: texts and numbers abbreviated to 30 characters (Apache `StringUtils.abbreviate`, ending with `...`) and HTML-encoded; undefined as `undefined`; an error as `` + the label from i18n `s.w.formula.cell.error.++.label` (e.g. `???` for 1, `func?` 2, `args?` 3, `div/0` 4, `var!` 5, `func!` 6, `type?` 7, `regex?` 8, `error!` 9, `value!` 10, `aggr?` 11, `limit!` 12, `array!` 13) + ``; an item as its display text; an array as its elements joined with `, ` (nested arrays in parentheses), cut after the text reaches 30 characters with `,...[]`; a struct as `{key: value, ...}` sorted by key with at most 5 entries then `,...[]` (`{}` when empty); a lambda at a valid range as the formula's source text of that range. Numbers are printed as a duration (`format-helper` user duration), a short date-time, `true`/`false` or a plain number, according to the format of the variable, aggregation or debug-aware function at that node (plain when unknown).
In debug mode the attribute value is always a defined value (the map), also when the formula evaluates to an error; the error appears only in the recorded texts.

`issue-field-text-provider` answers specs with exactly these ids (any params, any requested format) and declines all others: `versions` (Affects Versions), `fixVersions`, `components`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator`, `description`, `environment`, `issuetype`, `labels`, `priority`, `project`, `resolution`, `security`, `status`. Ids such as `summary`, `key`, `customfield` are declined.

The value is text format, only for issues (other item types and issues that do not resolve for the user are undefined, C-0179): the issue's field value (Affects Versions, Fix Versions, components, assignee, reporter, creator, description, environment, issue type, labels, priority, project, resolution, security level id, status) converted by `value-text-converter` (C-2040 to C-2043): names for versions, components, constants and project (several joined with `, `), user keys (not display names) for the user fields, label texts, the plain text of description and environment, and the security level id as its decimal text. A missing value is undefined; an empty collection is the empty text.

The loader declares the TRAIL context dependency, and every Jira entity met while converting (versions, components, users, priority, status, resolution, project, labels ...) is recorded in the trail (C-2042), so the text is recomputed when such an entity changes, e.g. a version is renamed.

`issue-field-item-provider` takes the Jira field id from the spec: `attachments` means `attachment`, `key` means `issuekey`, `customfield` with param `fieldId` N means `customfield_N`, and any other id is used as the field id itself. It then asks `field-information-provider` (C-2063 to C-2065) for that field and answers only when the field is described with read access and an item-valued value form; otherwise (unknown fields, text, number, date and duration fields, `comment`, Advanced Roadmaps team, Epic Sum Up fields) it declines.

Answered fields (Jira 9.12): system `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator` (a user item), `priority`, `status`, `resolution`, `issuetype`, `project` (the matching constant or project item), `attachment`/`attachments` (list of attachment items), `labels` (list of label items), `components` (list of component items), `versions` and `fixVersions` (list of version items); custom fields of type single user (user item), multi-user (list), project picker (project item), single version (first version as one item), multi-version (list), select (option item), cascading select (the deepest selected option as one option item), multi-select (list of option items), single issue picker (issue item), single group (first group as one group item), multi-group (list), labels (list of label items), sprint (list of sprint items, `CoreIdentities.sprint` of each sprint id, only when Jira Software is present), Service Management request type (`com.atlassian.servicedesk:vp-origin`, a request type item, when Service Management is present) and Assets object fields (list of Assets object items, when Assets is present).

The value is in the generic value format (`ValueFormat` id `value`, whatever format was requested), only for issues (other item types or unresolvable issues give undefined, C-0113): a single-valued field gives one `ItemIdentity`, a multi-valued field a List of `ItemIdentity` in the order Jira returns the field's values (labels by label text). A field with no value, or a multi-valued field with an empty collection, gives undefined (not an empty list). A custom field value of an unexpected Java type is treated as no value.

The loader's caching strategy is MAY and it declares no extra context dependency of its own. The Jira objects read are offered to the loading pass's item cache under their item identities, so formulas reading fields of those items do not look them up again.

`comments-item-provider` answers only specs with id `comments` (any params, any format) and gives values in the generic value format (`value`): for an issue, a List of comment items, each `ItemIdentity.longId("com.almworks.jira.structure:type-comment", <comment id>)`. Other item types and issues that do not resolve get undefined.

Before values are computed, the comments of all requested issues are read in one query from Jira's `Action` entity (OfBiz `OfBizDelegator.findListIteratorByCondition`) with condition `issue IN (<issue ids>)`, without any other filter and without ordering, so the list for an issue is in database order. An issue with no visible comment gets undefined (not an empty list). If values are requested without that bulk step having run, the value is an error.

A comment is included only if the current user may see it: a comment with a project role level (`rolelevel`) is kept only when the user is in that role for the issue's project (asked once for all issues' projects via `ProjectRoleManager.createProjectIdToProjectRolesMap(user, projectIds)`); a comment with a group level (`level`) is kept only when that exact group name is among `GroupManager.getGroupNamesForUser(user)`; a comment with neither is kept. For an anonymous user, a group-restricted comment among the issues makes the group lookup fail with NullPointerException, so loading fails (as the original does).

The loader declares the USER context dependency (values are per user) and caching strategy MAY. Each visible comment read is also built into a Jira comment object (author, update author, body, group level, role level, created, updated, issue) and offered to the loading pass's item cache, so formulas reading comment fields use it without a further lookup.

`worklog-objects-provider` answers only specs with id `worklogs` (any params, any format) and gives values in the generic value format (`value`): for an issue, a List of work-log items, each `ItemIdentity.longId("com.almworks.jira.structure:type-worklog", <worklog id>)`. Other item types and issues that do not resolve get undefined.

The work logs of all requested issues are read in one query from Jira's `Worklog` entity with condition `issue IN (<issue ids>)`, in database order. A work log restricted to a project role (`rolelevel`) is kept only when the current user has that role in the issue's project; one restricted to a group (`grouplevel`) only when the user is in that group (exact name); unrestricted ones are kept. An issue with no visible work log gets undefined; values requested without the bulk step are an error. For an anonymous user a group-restricted work log makes loading fail with NullPointerException (as the original does).

The loader declares the USER context dependency and caching strategy MAY. Each visible work log row is built into a Jira work-log object (issue, id, author, comment body, start date, group level, role level and its project role, time worked, update author, created, updated) and offered to the loading pass's item cache for formulas.

`change-history-provider` answers only specs with id `history` (any params, any format) and gives values in the generic value format (`value`): for an issue, a List of change-history group items (`CoreIdentities.changeHistoryGroup(<change group id>)`, type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-group`), in the order Jira returns the histories. Other item types and unresolvable issues get undefined; an issue without history gets undefined (not an empty list).

The histories of all requested issues are read with one call `ChangeHistoryManager.getChangeHistoriesForUser(issues, null)` (no user passed, so no per-user filtering of history entries by this module) and grouped by issue id. Each history read is offered to the loading pass's item cache under its item identity. Values requested without that bulk step are an error. Caching strategy MAY; no extra context dependency.

`issue-parent-provider` answers only specs with id `parent` (any params, any format), in the generic value format (`value`): for an issue that is a sub-task (Jira reports a parent id) the value is the parent issue's item `CoreIdentities.issue(<parent id>)`, whether or not the user can see the parent; for other issues, other item types and unresolvable issues it is undefined. Caching strategy MAY.

`epic-issue-provider` answers specs with id `epicIssue` (an issue's epic) and `epicStories` (an epic's issues), any params, any format, always producing the generic value format (`value`); other ids are declined. Only issue items are supported; other item types are not served by it.

Both use the Jira Software epic link type as `gh-integration` reports it (C-2239). When Jira Software is absent or the link type (or its id) cannot be resolved, both values are undefined for every issue.

`epicIssue` of an issue is the issue item of the source issue of its inward epic links: of the epic-link links pointing to the issue (read in bulk for all requested issues through `issue-links-bulk-source`, ordered by link id), those whose other end the current user cannot see (`forest-permissions-cache`, honouring a security override in effect) are dropped and the first remaining one is the value. No such link gives undefined.

`epicStories` of an issue is a List of issue items: the destination issues of its outward epic links, ordered by link id, keeping only issues the current user can see. An issue with no such visible issue gets undefined (not an empty list).
Both loaders declare the USER context dependency (values are per user) and caching strategy MAY. If values are computed without the bulk step having run, they are undefined.

`subtasks-provider` answers only specs with id `subtasks` (any params, any format) for issue items, in the generic value format (`value`): a List of the issue's sub-task issue items in Jira's sub-task order (link `sequence`), read in bulk for all requested issues through `issue-links-bulk-source` (outward links of the sub-task link type). The sub-tasks are not filtered by the user's permissions. An issue with no sub-tasks gets undefined (not an empty list).

The sub-task link type is the first link type from `IssueLinkTypeManager.getIssueLinkTypes(false)` that Jira marks as the sub-task link type; when there is none, every value is undefined. Caching strategy MAY; no extra context dependency.

`issue-link-objects-provider` answers specs with id `issuelinkobjects` (links of non-system link types only) and `allissuelinkobjects` (links of all link types, system ones such as sub-task and epic links included), any params, any format; other ids are declined. Values are in the generic value format (`value`), only for issue items: a List of issue-link items `CoreIdentities.issueLink(<link id>)`, each link once, in either direction.
For `issuelinkobjects` a link is left out when its link type is unknown to `IssueLinkTypeManager.getIssueLinkType(id)` or `isSystemLinkType()` is true.

Links of all requested issues are read in bulk (both directions) through `issue-links-bulk-source`. Every issue at either end is checked with `forest-permissions-cache` for the current user without a security override; a link is kept only when both of its ends are visible (so an issue the user cannot see shows no links).

An issue's links are sorted by the issue at the other end, using Jira's issue-link sort order (the comparator of Jira's link collection built from Jira's `ApplicationProperties`, i.e. the configured `jira.view.issue.links.sort.order`); when that comparator cannot be obtained, by issue key. Links whose other-end issue could not be loaded go last.
An issue with no visible links gets an empty list (not undefined), also when the bulk step did not run. The loader declares the USER context dependency and caching strategy MAY.

`remote-link-objects-provider` answers only specs with id `remoteissuelinkobjects` (any params, any format), only for issue items, in the generic value format (`value`): a List of remote-link items `CoreIdentities.remoteLink(<remote issue link id>)`; an issue with no remote links gets an empty list. Caching strategy MAY; no context dependency of its own.

By default the remote links of all requested issues are read in one query from Jira's remote issue link table (`Entity.REMOTE_ISSUE_LINK` through Jira's `EntityEngine`, `issueid IN (...)`), ordered by `globalid` then `id`, grouped per issue; the links read are offered to the loading pass's item cache. When that bulk step did not run, values are empty lists.

When the dark feature `structure.remoteLinksAttribute.preloadDisabled` is true (read once when the provider is created), each resolved issue is read on its own with `RemoteIssueLinkManager.getRemoteIssueLinksForIssue(issue)`, in the order that service returns; unresolvable issues then give undefined.

`user-property-provider` answers specs with id `user-property` whose params have a non-empty `propertyName` and a nested attribute spec under `userKey` (read in text format: a stored `format` other than `text` or `any` makes it absent); otherwise it declines. The value is text format and depends on that `userKey` attribute.

For each row the `userKey` attribute's text is taken as a Jira user key; the value is Jira's user property `jira.meta.<propertyName>` of that user (`UserPropertyManager.getPropertySetForUserKey(key)`), as `String.valueOf` of the property's actual value. When the property set is null, the property does not exist or its value is null, the value is undefined. When the `userKey` value is undefined or an error, the value is undefined.

A `PropertyException` while reading is ignored (undefined value); any other exception is logged as a throttled warning `<property>: cannot read value for user <key>` and gives undefined. The loader never gives an error value of its own.

The loader declares the TRAIL context dependency and adds the user item (`CoreIdentities.user(<key>)`) to the trail, so the value is recomputed when that user changes. When the dark feature `structure.userPropertyAttribute.disable` is true (checked on each value), every value is undefined and no property is read.

`formatted-number-provider` answers specs with id `formatted-number` whose params hold a nested attribute spec under `attribute` (with its `format` stored, since no expected format is given) and a `type` of `number`, `percentage`, `datetime` or `duration`; it declines when `attribute` is missing or invalid, `type` is absent or another text. Other params: `rounding` (integer, default 0, clamped to 0..9) for number and percentage; `style` (date style name for `format-helper`, C-1658/C-1659, unknown or absent means date-short) for datetime; `workTime` (boolean, default false) for duration. The value is text format; the nested attribute is requested in the generic value format (after the `extended-value-tools` conversion, C-2059).

`number` formats with Java's `NumberFormat.getNumberInstance(<user locale>)` and `percentage` with `NumberFormat.getPercentInstance(<user locale>)` (so 0.25 gives `25%`), both with exactly `rounding` fraction digits, rounding half up and no digit grouping (1234.5 with rounding 2 in English gives `1234.50`). A value the format refuses gives undefined.

`datetime` treats the number as epoch milliseconds (long value) and formats it with `format-helper`'s date format for the current user and the given `style`. `duration` treats it as milliseconds: with `workTime` true as Jira time-tracking text in the user's locale (C-1663), otherwise as calendar time (C-1664).

Value handling: a Number is formatted; a String is parsed (number/percentage with `Double.parseDouble`, datetime/duration with `Long.parseLong`) and formatted when it parses, otherwise returned unchanged; a List gives its non-null elements formatted and joined with `, ` (the empty text for an empty list), but undefined if any element is neither a Number nor a String; booleans, items and maps give undefined. When the nested attribute has no value (undefined or error) the result is undefined (the loader yields).
The loader declares the USER_LOCALE context dependency always and USER_TIMEZONE in addition when `type` is `datetime`.

`notes-provider` answers specs with id `itemProperty` whose param `name` is a valid item property name: not blank and at most 160 characters (the Notes column uses `notes`; notes created by users use `dc_note_<id>`, SPEC.md). Otherwise it declines. The value is text format, for items of every item type.

The value is the text stored by `notes-manager` for (the loading context's structure id, the row's item, the property name); undefined when nothing is stored. With no structure in the context (structure id 0) the value is an error. The provider does no permission check of its own on the note.
When the item's identity text contains `|`, the property key cannot be formed and loading the value throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`ItemId: <id> should not contain '|' character.`).
The loader declares only the STRUCTURE context dependency (values differ per structure, not per user) and uses the default caching strategy.

Answers attribute ids `max` and `min` only. The compared attribute is the nested attribute under params key `attribute` (taken with its own stored format). It is accepted only when that format is one of text, number, duration, time, order or generic (`any`); a missing nested attribute or any other format (e.g. html, boolean) gives no loader (null). Other params are not read except `type` (the reduction strategy, see below).

The scope is the standard reduction strategy chosen by the spec's `type` parameter (`subtree` by default, also `children`, `leaves`, `strict`, as `ReductionStrategy` defines them): by default a row's `max`/`min` covers the row's own value and the values of all its descendants. Values of child rows that are generators or effectors are left out and the first child error is passed up, as for every `ReducingAggregateLoader`.

Values are compared with `TotalOrder.withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison()` (strings lower-cased in the root locale, numbers of any class compared numerically, then `TotalOrder.COMPARATOR`: numbers before strings before other classes). The result is the original value, not the lower-cased one. Example: among `Beta`, `alpha`, `GAMMA` max is `GAMMA` and min is `alpha`; among 3, 10 and 7.5 max is 10.

Undefined (null) values are skipped; when no value in scope is defined the result is undefined. Mixed types follow the total order, so with `max` a text value wins over any number (numbers sort first) and with `min` a number wins over any text.
On equal comparison values (e.g. `abc` and `ABC`), `max` returns the one met last in scope order (the row's own value first, then children in forest order) and `min` returns the one met first.

When the requested format of `max`/`min` equals the nested attribute's format, the values compared are exactly the values returned: the loader depends only on the nested attribute and reduces its values.

When the requested format differs from the nested attribute's format (e.g. `max` requested in the generic format over a nested attribute in order format, as formula `max{}` does), the row is chosen by comparing the nested attribute's values in its own format, and the result is the chosen row's value of the same nested attribute in the requested format. A row counts only when both its comparison value and its requested-format value are defined; rows missing either are skipped. The resulting loader may be cached (`AttributeCachingStrategy.MAY`).

For the different-format case the provider also answers its own helper attribute, which carries params `attribute` (comparison attribute), `desired` (the same attribute in the requested format), `predicate` (`max` or `min`) and `type` copied from the request; the helper's value per row is the (comparison value, requested value) pair chosen over the scope. It is given no loader when `attribute` or `desired` is missing, `predicate` is empty or not `max`/`min`, or the comparison format is not supported. The helper's id is not contract.

Answers attribute id `aggregation-value-path` only, always in the generic (`any`) format. Params: `attribute` (the nested attribute, required, read in the generic format; missing gives no loader), `withSuperRoot` (boolean, default false) and `withoutTitle` (boolean, default false).

It is a propagate loader: each row's value is the nested attribute's value for that row (defined, undefined or error as the nested attribute gives it), and it additionally links to the parent row's value-path value so that ancestors can be walked from any row (used by `parent-provider` and the ancestors scope of `aggregate-function-provider`). The row's own loader data from the nested attribute is kept alongside the link.

The chain stops (no parent link) at top-level rows; with `withSuperRoot` true the invisible super-root row (row id -1) is loaded too and top-level rows link to it, and it is the top of the chain. With `withoutTitle` true, a title row (semantics 1) gets the plain undefined value with no link, and rows directly under a title row are treated as the top of the chain.
Its only attribute dependency is the nested attribute (in the generic format); its values change whenever that attribute's values or the forest's parent links change (default propagate caching).

Answers attribute id `aggregation-parent` only, in the generic (`any`) format. Params: `attribute` (nested attribute in its own format; missing gives no loader), `level` (Integer; deprecated synonym `depth`, used only when `level` is absent or not an Integer; default -1) and `withoutTitle` (boolean). Only `java.lang.Integer` values are honoured; another number type (e.g. a Long) counts as absent.

A negative level -n gives the value of the nested attribute n rows up from the row: -1 is the parent, -2 the grandparent. When the chain ends before n steps the result is undefined. Because a non-positive level includes the invisible super-root in the chain, -1 on a top-level row gives the nested attribute's value for the super-root row (usually undefined), not undefined by construction.

A positive level n counts down from the top: 1 is the row's top-level ancestor, 2 the next row below it on the path, and so on; the path includes the row itself, so n equal to the row's depth gives the row's own value and n greater than it gives undefined. Level 0 gives the value for the super-root row (the chain then includes the super-root).

With `withoutTitle` true the title row (semantics 1) is not part of any path: level 1 under a titled forest is the first row below the title, -1 on a row directly under the title is undefined, and the title row's own value is undefined.

It is a derived loader depending only on `aggregation-value-path` with the same nested attribute, `withSuperRoot` = (level <= 0) and the same `withoutTitle`. The chosen ancestor's value is returned as that ancestor's nested-attribute value, with its own loader data; an error value of that ancestor is returned as that error, and errors of rows passed over are ignored.

Answers attribute ids `aggregation-array` (generic format) and `aggregation-join` (text format) only; both need a nested attribute under params key `attribute` (missing gives no loader). Other ids get null.

Params read, with defaults: `type` (scope, String: `subtree` default for `aggregation-array`, `ancestors` default for `aggregation-join`; also `children`, `leaves`, `strict`), booleans `distinct`, `flatten`, `compact`, `reverse`, `withoutTitle` (all false), Integers `fromLevel` (deprecated `fromdepth`, default 1) and `toLevel` (deprecated `todepth`, default 0); for `aggregation-join` also texts `separator` (default `, `), `beforechildren` (default `(`) and `afterchildren` (default `)`). A value of the wrong Java type (e.g. a non-String `type`, a Long level) counts as absent.

Scope `preceding` or any other unknown `type` makes loader creation throw `IllegalArgumentException` with message `unsupported tree type '<type>'` (for `aggregation-join` with `distinct` or scope `ancestors`, when its derived `aggregation-array` is created).

`aggregation-array` with scope `subtree`, `children`, `leaves` or `strict` is a reducing aggregate whose reduction strategy is selected by `type` as `ReductionStrategy` defines it. With `subtree` a row's array is its own value followed by its children's arrays in forest order (pre-order), e.g. A with children B (child D) and C gives [A, B, D, C]; `children` gives the children's own values; `leaves` the leaves' values (a leaf gives its own); `strict` the descendants without the row itself. Generator and effector child rows are left out; a child error is passed up.

When collecting, every collected value that is a list is spliced in one level (its elements are taken instead of the list; deeper lists stay nested) and other values are taken as single elements; the `flatten` flag itself does not change this. With `compact` null (undefined) elements are dropped; with `distinct` repeated elements (by `equals`) are dropped, keeping the first. Without `compact`, undefined values appear as null elements. An empty input gives an empty array.

If the number of elements after flattening all nested lists completely exceeds the formula array size limit (dark feature `structure.expr.arraySizeLimit`, default 100000, see `expr-constraints`), the row's value is an error whose data is error 13 (array size limit exceeded). The same limit applies to `aggregation-join` with a descendant scope, counting the number of values being joined at one row.

`aggregation-array` with `reverse` true is derived from the same `aggregation-array` without `reverse` (same nested attribute, `type`, `flatten`, `distinct`, `compact`, `withoutTitle`, and levels for `ancestors`) and returns that list in reverse order; when that value is not a list the result is undefined, and its error is passed through.

Scope `ancestors` is a derived value over `aggregation-value-path` of the nested attribute (with `withSuperRoot` true only when `fromLevel` is 0, and the same `withoutTitle`): the list of values on the path from the top-level ancestor down to the row itself, inclusive, cut to the level range. If any value on the path is an error, that error is the result.

Level range for `ancestors` (path positions numbered 1 = top-level row ... N = the row): a positive level L means position L, a level 0 or negative L means position N+L (0 = the row, -1 = its parent). The result is positions from..to inclusive; a from before the start is clamped to the start; when to is before from, beyond the row, or before the start, the result is undefined. `fromLevel` 0 is special: the super-root's value is put first and the range starts there, and a positive `toLevel` keeps counting from the top-level row. Examples on a path R > P > X evaluated at X: defaults give [R, P, X]; `toLevel` -1 gives [R, P]; `fromLevel` -1 gives [P, X]; `fromLevel` 2 `toLevel` 2 gives [P]; `fromLevel` 4 gives undefined.

`aggregation-join` with scope `subtree`, `children`, `leaves` or `strict` and without `distinct` aggregates the nested attribute in text format with the selected reduction strategy. Where a row's own text is combined with its children's results (subtree, and the merge of strict), the text is `<own><beforechildren><child1><separator><child2>...<afterchildren>`, and a row with no children gives just its own text; where only children are combined (children, leaves, strict) the texts are joined with the separator without brackets. Example with defaults, A with children B (child D) and C, scope subtree: `A(B(D), C)`.

In joins every undefined value is written as `?`: in a subtree join a leaf with undefined value gives `?` and a parent with undefined value gives `?(...)`. Joining an empty list gives undefined. `reverse` reverses the order of the joined children texts at each level but never moves the row's own text.

`aggregation-join` with scope `ancestors` (the default) or with `distinct` true is derived from an `aggregation-array` of the same nested attribute, scope and `withoutTitle` (with `reverse` passed on; with `distinct` also `flatten`, `distinct` and `compact` set; for `ancestors` also `fromLevel`/`toLevel`), whose elements are written with `toString()` (undefined as `?`) and joined with `separator` only (no brackets). An empty array gives undefined, a non-list gives undefined, and an error of the array is returned as the error. Example: ancestors join at X on path R > P > X gives `R, P, X`.

Answers attribute id `manually-adjusted` (any requested format gets the boolean loader). For every row the value is true when the forest's generation data lists that row id among the rows a user adjusted by hand (moved or changed against the generators' result), otherwise false; when the forest has no generation data (e.g. a forest without generators) it is false for all rows. Every row gets a defined value, whatever its item type.
It is a single-row loader that depends on the whole forest, so its values are recomputed whenever the forest (including its generation data) changes.

Answers attribute id `wiki-render` (HTML format) whose params key `attribute` names a nested attribute, read in text format. With no nested attribute, or when Jira's `RendererManager.getRendererForType("atlassian-wiki-renderer")` returns null at loader creation, no loader is given (null).

The value is the nested attribute's text rendered by that renderer with `render(text, null)` (no issue context), for every row and item type the nested attribute covers. When the nested text is undefined, null or an error, the loader yields no value; a null render result also gives no value.

Answers, for rows of item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version-name`, only the aggregate variants: `summary` with param `aggregate` = true (text), `icon` with `aggregate` = true (HTML) and `description` with `aggregate` = true (HTML); plain `summary`, `icon`, `description` without that param are not answered. It also serves two internal helper attributes, the issue ids under the row and their project ids (ids not contract).

The issues of a version-name row are collected over the forest: for a row whose item is a version name or whose semantics is 2 (group row), it is the set of the item ids of its direct children that are issues (children that are group rows excluded) plus, recursively, the issues collected by its child version-name or group rows; other rows contribute nothing. Generated version-name rows from the version grouper thus see the issues grouped under them.

The projects of a version-name row are the projects of those issues, each issue resolved as the current user (unresolvable issues are skipped). The matching versions are, for each project id in ascending order, the versions of that project (Jira `VersionManager.getVersions(projectId)`) whose canonical name (`CoreIdentities.canonicalVersionName`) equals the version-name item's name, ordered by version id. The 'first' version is the first of these whose description is not blank (after normalising whitespace), else the first one.

Aggregate `summary` of a version-name row is the name of the 'first' matching version (with its original case); when there are no issues, no projects or no matching versions, it is the version-name item's own name (its canonical, lower-cased form).

Aggregate `icon` is an empty span. Each version's classes are `aui-icon aui-icon-small` plus `aui-iconfont-version-unreleased` (unreleased) or `aui-iconfont-version` (released), with ` s-version-icon-archived` appended when archived. If all matching versions have the same classes the result is ``; if they differ, or there are no issues/projects/matching versions, it is the mixed icon ``.

Aggregate `description` combines the matching versions' descriptions, grouped by key = description with whitespace normalised and lower-cased (root locale); blank descriptions are ignored and when all are blank (or nothing matches) it is undefined. If only the 'first' version's key occurs, the value is its description as is; otherwise it is the first version's `<description> (<PROJECTKEY>)`, then `, ` and, for each other key in order of first appearance, the description of the lowest-id version having it with ` (<PROJECTKEY>)` (without the suffix when the version has no project), joined with `, `. The whole text is HTML-escaped.

The project lookup depends on the current user (`AttributeContextDependency.USER`) because issues are resolved with that user's visibility; the issue and project helper values may be cached (`MAY`) and summary, icon and description should be (`SHOULD`). Values change when the rows under the version-name row change.

Answers attribute id `timeinstatus` for issues. Params: `statuses` (list of texts), `targetEnabled` (boolean), `targetStatuses` (list of texts, read only when `targetEnabled` is true), `reopen` (boolean), `useCurrentStatus` (boolean), `calendar` (text). Each status entry is `status:<status id>` (looked up with Jira `StatusManager.getStatus`) or `category:<category id or key>` (a number is looked up with `StatusCategoryManager.getStatusCategory(id)`, otherwise `getStatusCategoryByKey`); unknown statuses or categories and entries with another prefix are ignored with a logged warning. An empty or missing list matches no status.

In HTML format the value is the duration formatted as calendar time (see `format-helper`: whole minutes and larger units, a magnitude under one minute formatted as zero); in every other requested format (duration, number, text, ...) the loader gives a duration in milliseconds (duration format).

A blank or missing `calendar` uses the default calendar of `simple-calendar-provider` (plain elapsed time, not time-zone dependent). Otherwise it is `<calendar provider complete module key>/<calendar id>`, e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:simple-calendar-provider/1`, resolved through the enabled calendar providers; a calendar the provider does not find, or a value not of that form (not exactly one `/`, non-numeric id), gives no loader (null). A provider key that is not installed makes loader creation fail with `NullPointerException` (as the original does).

Stays are worked out from the issue's status history (Jira `ChangeHistoryManager.getChangeItemsForField(issue, "status")`, each change's time, from-status id and to-status id, in the order Jira returns them). The first stay starts at the issue's creation time and each change ends one stay and starts the next. When Jira returns null the value is undefined.

Without options, the value is the sum, over all completed stays whose status matches `statuses`, of the stay's duration measured by the calendar (`Calendar.getDuration(start, end)`), plus, when the issue's current status matches, the time from the last change (or creation) up to now. Example: created 10:00 in Open, to In Progress 11:00, to Open 12:00, back to Done 12:30, statuses [Open] gives 1h30m.
With `targetEnabled` true a completed stay counts only when the change that ended it went to a status matching `targetStatuses`; the current, still-open stay is never counted.

With `reopen` true, stays are grouped into runs of consecutive stays in matching statuses; the first run is not counted and every matching stay from the second run on is counted (i.e. only time after the issue came back to the chosen statuses). The current stay counts by the same rule (when target statuses are off). Example with statuses [In Progress]: In Progress 1h, Review, In Progress 2h, Done gives 2h.

With `useCurrentStatus` true the `statuses`, `targetStatuses` and `reopen` options are ignored: the value is the time spent in the issue's current status over all completed stays in it plus the ongoing stay up to now.

Values with an ongoing counted stay expire after 1 minute (recomputed with the current time); values without one expire after 1 day. The duration loader depends on the current time, and on the user's time zone when the calendar is time-zone dependent; the history helper may be cached (`SHOULD`).

Each time a duration loader is created it records the current user for usage statistic `timeInStatus.users`, also for `timeInStatus.statusUsers` when any source or target entry starts with `status:`, and for `timeInStatus.categoryUsers` when any starts with `category:` (unique-user counts, see `statistics-manager`).

Answers attribute id `status-category` for issues: in number or order format the value is the category id of the issue's status (`StatusCategory.getId()`, a Long, served in number format); in HTML format the lozenge below; in every other format the category's name (`getPrimaryAlias()`) as text.
The HTML is ` `, with the category's colour name and primary alias HTML-escaped (`TextUtils.htmlEncode`), e.g. `...lozenge-green">Done`.
An issue without a status, or whose status has no category, gets an error value (not undefined). Items that are not issues are not supported.

Answers attribute id `project-category` (text) for issues and for planning tasks (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`). The value is the name of the project category of the issue's project, or of the planning task's project (task found with `planning-task-manager`).
No project (null) gives an error value; a project without a category gives undefined; a planning task that is not found gives undefined.

The project item (`CoreIdentities.project`) and, when present, the project category item (`CoreIdentities.projectCategory`) are added to the value's trail, so the value is recalculated when the project or the category changes.

Answers attribute id `transition-date` (time format, epoch ms; requests in any format get the time loader) for issues. Params: `status` (status id, or else a status name matched ignoring case, first match in `StatusManager.getStatuses()` order) or, when `status` is absent, `category`; `transition` = `latest` (default) or `first`; any other `transition` value is treated as `latest` with a logged warning. An unknown status, an unknown category name, or neither param gives no loader (null).

`category` is matched lower-cased (root locale) against fixed aliases: `todo`, `to do`, `new` = category key `new`; `in progress`, `in_progress`, `inprogress`, `indeterminate` = `indeterminate`; `complete`, `done` = `done`; `undefined` = `undefined`. It then covers every status whose category has that key (possibly none, which gives an always-undefined value).

The value is the time of the earliest (`first`) or latest (`latest`) entry of the issue's status history (`field-change-list` with `fieldId` = `status`) whose status id is one of the selected ones. The first history entry stands for the creation, so an issue created in the selected status has that entry's time when it never left, or as its first transition. No match, or history unavailable, gives undefined.

Answers attribute id `field-change-list` (list format) for issues, param `fieldId` (required: missing gives no loader), the name passed to Jira's `ChangeHistoryManager.getChangeItemsForField(issue, fieldId)`. The value is a list of (value, timestamp ms) entries: first an initial entry, then one per change item whose field equals `fieldId` and whose creation time is not null, in Jira's order, with value = the change's raw `to` value and its creation time. Jira returning null gives an error value.

The initial entry's value is the first change's raw `from` value, and when there are no changes it is the issue's current status id, whatever `fieldId` is (as the original does). Its time is the issue's creation time (0 when null), or the first change's time if that is earlier.

Answers attribute id `query-match`. Params: `query` (text, with leading and trailing horizontal whitespace removed) and `queryType` (`jql`, `sjql` or `text`, see `various-query-parser`). A missing or empty query gives a loader whose value is undefined for every row; a missing `queryType` gives no loader (null); a query that `various-query-parser` cannot parse (it throws `StructureException`, e.g. an unknown type or a syntax error) gives the always-undefined loader, logged at info.

In boolean format (and every format other than HTML) each row's value is true when the row is among the rows the query matches in the current forest and false otherwise; the title row (semantics 1) is always undefined. The query runs for the current user over the forest without its title row (when the forest's only root is a title row it is removed, its children moving up).
In HTML format the value is `` for rows whose boolean value is true and no value otherwise.

Matching is computed once per loading pass: when the loading context knows the base forest spec and non-zero forest and items versions, the result comes from `query-result-cache` (for the spec without its title and the forest without the title root); otherwise, or when the cache gives no answer, the query is parsed and run directly. A `StructureException` while doing so is logged and every row of that pass gets an error value. The loader depends on the whole forest and on the current user.

Answers attribute id `comment` for issues: in HTML format if requested, otherwise in text format. The value is the issue's last comment the current user may see, loaded in bulk for the batch of issues with `bulk-comment-reader`; it depends on the current user.

Text is the raw comment body. HTML is the body rendered with Jira's `RendererManager.getRenderedContent(rendererType, body, issue.getIssueRenderContext())`, where the renderer type is that of the `comment` field in the issue's field layout (`FieldLayoutManager.getFieldLayout(issue).getFieldLayoutItem("comment")`), e.g. wiki markup rendered when the comment field uses the wiki renderer.
An issue with no visible comment (or not part of the preloaded batch) gives undefined; when no bulk result is available (the loading context could not preload) the value is an error.
Answers attribute ids `version-start`, `version-release` and `version-description` for items of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version` (resolved to Jira `Version`); other ids get null.

`version-start` / `version-release` in time format (and every format other than text and HTML) are the version's start date / release date in epoch ms, undefined when not set. Unless param `disableDateShift` is true, the date is shifted for display: its calendar date in the JVM time zone becomes the start of that date in the user's time zone (see `structure-datetime-formatter`), and the value depends on the user's time zone.

In text format the date (same params, time format) is formatted as a date (Jira date style) by `structure-datetime-formatter`: for the user's zone and locale when date shift is on, else Jira's system zone with the user's locale; it depends on the user's locale (and user). In HTML format it is that text HTML-escaped. An undefined date gives no value.

`version-description` (text, whatever format is requested) is the version's description as stored (`Version.getDescription()`), undefined when null. The same raw text is what the text form of `description` gives for version rows (served through `main-provider`).

Answers attribute ids `sprint-start`, `sprint-end` and `sprint-goal` for items of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-sprint` (the Jira Software sprint the item resolves to; without Jira Software such items do not resolve and get no value); other ids get null.

`sprint-start` / `sprint-end` in time format (and every format other than text and HTML) are the sprint's start / end instant in epoch ms (no date shift), undefined when not set; they declare a dependency on the user's time zone. In text format the time is formatted as a date (Jira date style) for the user's zone and locale (`structure-datetime-formatter`, always user-based); in HTML format that text HTML-escaped.
`sprint-goal` (text) is the sprint's goal, undefined when null. For sprint rows `description` (served through `main-provider`) is the goal: HTML-escaped in HTML format and raw in text format.

Answers attribute id `project-lead` only in HTML or text format (other formats get null), for items of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project` (resolved to Jira `Project`). The value is the display name of the project lead: raw in text, HTML-escaped in HTML. A project without a lead gives no value. The lead's user item (`CoreIdentities.user`) is added to the trail, so the value changes when that user changes.

Answers attribute ids `tempo-worklogged` and `tempo-timeplanned` for issues, always as a duration in milliseconds; both need params `dateFrom` and `dateTo` (texts, ISO dates `yyyy-MM-dd` as `tempo-integration` expects) and without either there is no loader (null). The module is always registered; whether Tempo is installed is decided per load.

`tempo-worklogged` reads params `accounts` (list of integer account ids), `users` (list of user keys), `teams` (list of integer team ids) and `billable` (boolean) and asks `tempo-integration` once per loaded batch for the work logged by those filters in the date range on the batch's issue ids (billable seconds when `billable` is true). Each issue's value is the seconds times 1000; an issue absent from the answer gets 0.

`tempo-timeplanned` reads params `users` (user keys), `teams` and `roles` (lists of integer ids) and asks `tempo-integration` once per batch for the time planned in the date range on the batch's issues. Each issue's value is the planned seconds times 1000; an issue absent from the answer gets 0.

When `tempo-integration` gives no answer (Tempo Timesheets or Planner not installed or enabled, the current user has no access, bad dates, or any Tempo failure), every issue's value is undefined. Values depend on the current user.

Invalidation trail: `tempo-worklogged` values are recalculated when the Tempo work attribute `ACCOUNT`, the global permission `TEMPO_TIMESHEETS_ACCESS` or the project permission `PROJECT_VIEW_ALL_WORKLOGS` change (`AuxiliaryIdentities.tempoWorkAttribute`, `globalPermission`, `projectPermission`); `tempo-timeplanned` values when any group (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-group`), any Tempo team membership or team permissions (`*`), the global permission `TEMPO_PLANNER_ACCESS` or the project permission `PROJECT_VIEW_ALL_WORKLOGS` change.

For any requested attribute it derives a field id: the attribute id itself, except `key` becomes `issuekey` and `customfield` with a single numeric param `fieldId` N becomes `customfield_N`. When `structure-field-manager` has no field of that id the provider gives no loader; otherwise the loader serves items of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`, reading the field from the item's field view (`generic-item-field-accessor-manager`); an item that does not exist gives undefined, a null field value no value.

In text format (for fields other than date fields) the value is the `value-text-converter` text of the field value, except duration and single-sprint fields, which use their field type's display text (see `structure-field-type-manager`). A date field requested in text format is served as its own value format instead (as in the last claim of this module), not as text.

In HTML format: a single-user field gives the user rendered by `user-field-renderer` with the spec's `view` param and adds the user item to the trail; any other field gives its field type's HTML view, or its Excel view when param `excel` is true (`structure-field-type-manager`). When the field type's value format is the item format (`value`), the value's item identity is added to the trail. HTML values depend on the current user.

In any other format the value is the field type's extended value in the field type's own value format (e.g. an item identity for item-valued fields, epoch ms for dates); values in the item (`value`) format may be cached (`MAY`).

Time-zone handling: unless param `disableDateShift` is true, a date-only field in time or number format, and a date-time field in text or HTML format, are computed in the user's time zone (and depend on it); everything else uses the JVM default time zone.

For memos and planning tasks (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo`, `:type-planning-task`) it serves `project` (Jira `Project`), `type` (Jira `IssueType`), `priority` (Jira `Priority`), `reporter` and `assignee` (Jira `ApplicationUser`), read from the item's own `project`, `issuetype`, `priority`, `reporter` and `assignee` fields through `generic-item-field-accessor-manager` (so a value hidden or invalid in the field configuration reads as null). A request for these ids gets these loaders whatever its params or format.

An item that does not exist gives undefined; a field with no value gives no value. A non-null value's item (`CoreIdentities.project`, `issueType`, `priority` or `user`) is added to the trail, so the value is recalculated when that project, issue type, priority or user changes.

Answers attribute id `history` for memos and planning tasks, always in the item (`value`) format. The value is the list of the item's history records as items `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group/<record id>`, in the order `generic-item-history-manager` delivers them for the item (by timestamp); an item without records gives undefined.

Records are loaded in bulk once per batch of items with `generic-item-history-manager`'s load-for-items, and each record object is put in the loading pass's item cache under its record identity. When the batch was not preloaded the value is an error. Values may be cached (`MAY`).

For memos and planning tasks it answers `creator`, `created` and `updated`, each computed from the item's `history` attribute (item format): the record items are resolved and examined in history order. `created` (time format, epoch ms) is the timestamp of the create record (the last one if several); `updated` (time format) is the greatest timestamp of all records; `creator` is the author key of the create record. Without a create record `created` and `creator` have no value. Other ids get null.

`creator` in the item (`value`) format is the user item `CoreIdentities.user(authorKey)`; in HTML format the user rendered by `user-field-renderer` with the spec's `view` param, or the raw user key when Jira's `UserManager.getUserByKey` finds no user, adding the user item to the trail and depending on the current user; in any other format the author's user key as text.

When the `history` value has no value (undefined or error) that value is passed through as the result; a history value that is not a list gives undefined. Values in the item format may be cached (`MAY`).

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:summary-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts effect parameters `issue` (issue id, a `Long` or numeric text; required), `summary` (the new text, read as a single string; absent or null means clear), `sendNotifications` (boolean, default false) and `conflicts` (a list, added by optimization). These match `CoreEffects.setIssueSummary`; no other parameters are read.
