Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: the `issue` parameter is read as a long (C-0964 rules); when it is absent or unparsable the effect is an error `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` with argument `issue` ("No value for required parameter \"issue\"."). Otherwise it is resolved through the item resolver as the issue item with that id; if the resolver gives nothing (no such issue, or the current user may not see it) the error is `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue` ("Issue does not exist or you have no permission to see it.").

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: all parameters are resolved, in the order `issue`, `conflicts`, `sendNotifications`, then (custom fields) `customField`, then the provider's own parameters; when any fails, `resolve` returns `EffectResponse.error` with the first failure's text, the effect's description and the affected items, and Jira is not asked anything else. The description is computed even then, using the raw parameter text for a parameter that failed (the issue's raw id, or `<?>` when absent, in place of the issue key).

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: the affected items of every response (error, empty or valid) are a one-element list with the issue item identity for the `issue` parameter's id, taken from the parameter even if the issue cannot be resolved; when the `issue` parameter is absent or unparsable the list is empty.

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: when the requested value equals the issue's current value (by the comparison each provider states), `resolve` returns `EffectResponse.empty` with the description and affected items and makes no Jira validation call; otherwise the change is validated and applied as `effect-provider-helper` does (C-2646 to C-2648: Jira issue update keeping all other values, `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` when the field is not on the edit screen, undo built before the update, `IssueService.update` with `ISSUE_UPDATED` and mail sent only when `sendNotifications` is true), and a valid response carries the success message.

Shared by the system-field providers (assignee, priority, description, environment, resolution, summary, due date, reporter, status): the description, success and conflict texts use i18n keys `s.ext.effect.+<value parameter key>+.` followed by `description.value`, `description.empty`, `conflict.value`, `conflict.empty`, `success.value` or `success.empty` (the literal `+` signs are part of the key). Arguments: the issue key, then the value's text when there is one, then (conflict keys only) the conflicting values' texts joined by `, `. `.empty` is used when the value's text is null (parameter absent). `getSuccessMessage()` is the success key; `getDescription()` is the conflict key when the effect has a non-empty `conflicts` list, else the description key.

Texts (key `s.ext.effect.+summary+.`): description `Change summary of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear summary of {0}`, conflict `Change summary of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with summaries: {2})` / `Clear summary of {0} (conflicts with summaries: {1})`, success `Changed summary of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared summary of {0}`. The value text is the `summary` parameter as given.

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: in a conflict text each conflicting value is described as the provider describes its own value (resolving the raw value through the same parameter rules, falling back to the raw text when it does not resolve), and the empty marker `{"empty": true}` or a null entry is shown as `s.ext.effect.empty-value` (`<empty>`) in the user's language.

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: the HTML description of an effect without a non-empty `conflicts` list is the HTML-encoded localized description text. With conflicts it is rendered in the warning layout of `effect-provider-helper` (C-2653) using the provider's `description.value` key: the leading arguments (field name for custom fields, then issue key) HTML-encoded, and the value argument replaced by `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="<value key>">` holding first the effect's own raw value as a `selected` option and then one option per conflict; each option's `value` is the HTML-encoded raw value (`{empty=true}` for the empty marker, `null` for null), the empty marker and null carry `data-empty="true"`, and its text is the HTML-encoded value description.

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: `optimize` groups effects by the `issue` parameter (system fields) or by `issue` and `customField` (custom fields) and merges each group with `effect-provider-helper`'s single-value rule on the value parameter key (C-2651, C-2652): the last effect wins and the other distinct values go into `conflicts`. The other parameters of the kept effect (for example `sendNotifications`) are those of the last effect.

Shared by every single-value effect provider in this group: adjusting an effect (as when the user picks a value in the conflict select) returns a copy of the effect with each given parameter set to the given value; all other parameters, `conflicts` included, are kept.

The current value is the issue's summary; the new value equals it when both read as the same string with null read as empty. Applying sets the summary in the issue input parameters (null when the parameter is absent; Jira's validation then decides, a required summary normally failing with Jira's message). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueSummary(issue, <summary before the change>)`.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:description-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `description` (the new text, read as a single string; absent means clear; empty text is accepted), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssueDescription`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML description are as summary-effect-provider states them for all single-value providers.

The current value is the issue's description; null and empty text count as equal, so setting `""` on an issue with no description (or clearing a description that is empty) gives `EffectResponse.empty` and changes nothing.

Applying puts the new text (or null) as the description into Jira issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `description`, also used as the field name in `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value`). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueDescription(issue, <description before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+description+.`, arguments issue key, value text, conflicts): description `Change description of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear description of {0}`, conflict `Change description of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with descriptions: {2})` / `Clear description of {0} (conflicts with descriptions: {1})`, success `Changed description of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared description of {0}`. The value text is the `description` parameter as given.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:environment-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `environment` (the new text, read as a single string; absent means clear; empty text is accepted), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssueEnvironment`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML description are as summary-effect-provider states them for all single-value providers.

The current value is the issue's environment; null and empty text count as equal, so setting `""` on an issue with no environment (or clearing a environment that is empty) gives `EffectResponse.empty` and changes nothing.

Applying puts the new text (or null) as the environment into Jira issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `environment`, also used as the field name in `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value`). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueEnvironment(issue, <environment before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+environment+.`, arguments issue key, value text, conflicts): description `Change environment of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear environment value of {0}`, conflict `Change environment of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with environments: {2})` / `Clear environment value of {0} (conflicts with environments: {1})`, success `Changed environment of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared environment value of {0}`. The value text is the `environment` parameter as given.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:assignee-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `assignee` (a user key; absent or empty text means unassign), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.assignIssue`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML layout are as summary-effect-provider states them.

A non-empty `assignee` value is resolved through the item resolver as the user item with that key; when no user is found the effect is error `s.ext.effect.error.no-user` with the key ("User \"{0}\" could not be found."). A blank-but-not-empty value such as a space is looked up as a key too.

The current value is the issue's assignee; old and new are equal when both are null or both have the same user key. Applying sets the assignee by the user's username (`IssueInputParameters.setAssigneeId(username)`, null to clear) in issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `assignee`); Jira's own validation (assign permission, assignable user, a required reporter) decides and its messages become the error. The undo is `CoreEffects.assignIssue(issue, <assignee before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+assignee+.`, arguments issue key, user, conflicts): description `Assign {0} to "{1}"` / `Unassign {0}`, conflict `Assign {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with assignees: {2})` / `Unassign {0} (conflicts with assignees: {1})`, success `Assigned {0} to "{1}"` / `Unassigned {0}`.

In the description and success texts the user is carried as `${<user key>}` (the resolved user's key, or the raw parameter text when it did not resolve) in the arguments kept with user keys, and the shown arguments replace each `${key}` with that user's display name, or `s.ext.effect.field.user-unknown` (`unknown user`) when no such user exists; so a stored preview shows the user's current display name. Conflicting users are shown the same way, in the HTML select too.
A `assignee` parameter given as empty text clears the field, but its description uses the `.value` key with the value text `null`, e.g. `Assign PRJ-1 to "null"` (as the original does).

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:reporter-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `reporter` (a user key; absent or empty text means clear the reporter), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssueReporter`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML layout are as summary-effect-provider states them.

A non-empty `reporter` value is resolved through the item resolver as the user item with that key; when no user is found the effect is error `s.ext.effect.error.no-user` with the key ("User \"{0}\" could not be found."). A blank-but-not-empty value such as a space is looked up as a key too.

The current value is the issue's reporter; old and new are equal when both are null or both have the same user key. Applying sets the reporter by the user's username (`IssueInputParameters.setReporterId(username)`, null to clear) in issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `reporter`); Jira's own validation (assign permission, assignable user, a required reporter) decides and its messages become the error. The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueReporter(issue, <reporter before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+reporter+.`, arguments issue key, user, conflicts): description `Change reporter of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear reporter value of {0}`, conflict `Change reporter of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with reporters: {2})` / `Clear reporter value of {0} (conflicts with reporters: {1})`, success `Changed reporter of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared reporter value of {0}`.

In the description and success texts the user is carried as `${<user key>}` (the resolved user's key, or the raw parameter text when it did not resolve) in the arguments kept with user keys, and the shown arguments replace each `${key}` with that user's display name, or `s.ext.effect.field.user-unknown` (`unknown user`) when no such user exists; so a stored preview shows the user's current display name. Conflicting users are shown the same way, in the HTML select too.
A `reporter` parameter given as empty text clears the field, but its description uses the `.value` key with the value text `null`, e.g. `Change reporter of PRJ-1 to "null"` (as the original does).

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:priority-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `priority` (the priority id as text; absent means clear), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssuePriority`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML layout are as summary-effect-provider states them.

A present `priority` value is looked up with Jira's `ConstantsManager.getPriorityObject(id)`; when Jira returns null the effect is error `s.ext.effect.error.no-priority` with the raw id ("Priority \"{0}\" could not be found."). The value is described by the priority's name (`getName()`, not translated).

Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same id. Applying sets `setPriorityId(<id or null>)` in issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `priority`; when the field is not on the edit screen the error is `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with `priority` and the issue key). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssuePriority(issue, <priority before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+priority+.`, arguments issue key, value, conflicts): description `Change priority of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear priority value of {0}`, conflict `Change priority of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with priorities: {2})` / `Clear priority value of {0} (conflicts with priorities: {1})`, success `Changed priority of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared priority value of {0}`.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:resolution-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `resolution` (the resolution id as text; absent means clear), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssueResolution`. Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML layout are as summary-effect-provider states them.

A present `resolution` value is looked up with Jira's `ConstantsManager.getResolution(id)`; when Jira returns null the effect is error `s.ext.effect.error.no-resolution` with the raw id ("Resolution \"{0}\" could not be found."). The value is described by the resolution's name (`getName()`, not translated).

Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same id. Applying sets `setResolutionId(<id or null>)` in issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `resolution`; when the field is not on the edit screen the error is `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with `resolution` and the issue key). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueResolution(issue, <resolution before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+resolution+.`, arguments issue key, value, conflicts): description `Change resolution of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear resolution of {0}`, conflict `Change resolution of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with resolutions: {2})` / `Clear resolution of {0} (conflicts with resolutions: {1})`, success `Changed resolution of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared resolution of {0}`.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:due-date-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `dueDate` (epoch milliseconds, read as a long by the C-0964 rules; absent means clear), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setIssueDueDate` (C-0275). Parameter checks, affected items, optimization and HTML layout are as summary-effect-provider states them.
A `dueDate` value that is not a number (for example `"tomorrow"`) is not an error: it reads as no value, so the effect clears the due date (as the original does).

Old and new due dates are equal when both are null, or when Jira's `DateFieldFormat.formatDatePicker` gives the same text for both (so two instants on the same day in the date-picker format count as equal and give `EffectResponse.empty`).

Applying sets the due date to the date-picker text of the new value (`formatDatePicker`), or null to clear, in issue input parameters that keep every other value, validated and updated as effect-provider-helper states (field id `duedate`, also the field name in `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value`). The undo is `CoreEffects.setIssueDueDate(issue, <due date before the change>)`.

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+dueDate+.`, arguments issue key, date, conflicts): description `Change due date of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear due date of {0}`, conflict `Change due date of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with due dates: {2})` / `Clear due date of {0} (conflicts with due dates: {1})`, success `Changed due date of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared due date of {0}`. The date is shown with Jira's `DateFieldFormat.format`.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:status-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `status` (target status id as text), `resolution` (resolution id as text, optional), `screenCheck` (boolean, default true: only the text `false`, any case, or Boolean false turns it off), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`. `CoreEffects.setIssueStatus` gives `issue` and `status` only.

A present `status` id is looked up with `ConstantsManager.getStatus`; null gives error `s.ext.effect.error.no-status` with the raw id ("Status \"{0}\" could not be found."). A present `resolution` id is looked up with `ConstantsManager.getResolution`; null gives `s.ext.effect.error.no-resolution` ("Resolution \"{0}\" could not be found."). Status and resolution are described by their translated names (`getNameTranslation()`).
When the issue's current status and the target status are both present and have the same id, the effect is `EffectResponse.empty`, even if a `resolution` is given and differs from the issue's.

Otherwise a single workflow transition is looked for, and these errors are returned in this order: no workflow for the issue (`WorkflowManager.getWorkflow` null) -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.status.no-workflow` ("No workflow for {0}.", issue key); issue without a status -> `...status.null-source-status` ("Unknown status of {0}."); no `status` parameter -> `...status.null-target-status` ("Unknown target status for {0}."); current status not linked to a workflow step -> `...status.no-source-status` ("Initial status {0} is not part of the workflow for {1}.", status name, issue key); target status not linked -> `...status.no-target-status` ("Target status {0} is not part of the workflow for {1}."). So clearing the status is always an error.

The candidate transitions are the source step's actions followed by the workflow's global actions whose id is among the actions that result in the target step. None -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.status.no-transition` ("Transition from {0} to {1} is not allowed by the workflow for {2}.", source name, target name, issue key); more than one -> `...status.many-transitions` ("There are several transitions that can bring {0} from {1} to {2}: {3}. Please use issue actions menu to apply a transition.", issue key, source, target, the action names joined by `, `). With `screenCheck` true, the one transition having a non-empty view (a screen) gives `...status.requires-view` ("Transitioning {2} from {0} to {1} requires a dialog to be displayed. Please use \"{3}\" transition in the issue actions menu.", source, target, issue key, action name); with `screenCheck` false a transition with a screen is used. Names in these messages are untranslated status names.

With the transition found it validates `IssueService.validateTransition(currentUser, issueId, actionId, input)` where the input parameters are built from action parameters `{"resolution": [<resolution id>]}` when `resolution` is given (none otherwise), keep existing values for parameters not provided (`setRetainExistingValuesWhenParameterNotProvided(true, false)`) and have the status id set to the target. For a valid result the additional inputs are copied and `sendBulkNotification` is set to the `sendNotifications` value. An invalid result is an error whose text is Jira's error messages and field errors joined by `, `. No edit-screen check is made.

Applying first builds the undo, then calls `IssueService.transition(user, validationResult)`; when Jira returns an invalid result it throws a `StructureException` with `StructureErrors.ITEM_EDIT_DENIED` and localized message `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.status.no-transition` with the source and target translated names and the issue key.

The undo is a `status-effect-provider` effect with `issue`, `status` = the status before the change, `resolution` = the resolution id before the change (absent when unresolved), `screenCheck` absent when the applied effect had it true and `false` when it had it false, and `sendNotifications` = true only when the applied effect had it true (absent otherwise).

Texts (key prefix `s.ext.effect.+status+.`, arguments issue key, status name, conflicts): description `Change status of {0} to "{1}"` / `Clear status value of {0}`, conflict `Change status of {0} to "{1}" (conflicts with statuses: {2})` / `Clear status value of {0} (conflicts with statuses: {1})`, success `Changed status of {0} to "{1}"` / `Cleared status value of {0}`. The resolution is not mentioned. Optimization keeps the last effect per issue (its own `resolution`, `screenCheck` and `sendNotifications`) with the other statuses as conflicts, as summary-effect-provider states.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:text-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue` (required), `customField` (custom field id such as `customfield_10010`, required), `value` (the new text, read as a single string; absent means clear; empty text accepted), `sendNotifications` (default false) and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setTextCustomField`. The field must have a type that is a `GenericTextCFType` (single-line and multi-line text fields).

Shared by every single-value custom-field provider in this group: `customField` is looked up with `CustomFieldManager.getCustomFieldObject(id)`; an absent parameter or an unknown field gives error `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.no-field` ("Custom field does not exist."). A field whose type does not pass the provider's type test gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` with arguments (field name, field id) although the text is "Custom field \"{1}\" ({0}) is of incorrect type.", so it reads e.g. `Custom field "customfield_10010" (Story Points) is of incorrect type.` (as the original does).

Shared by every single-value custom-field provider in this group: texts use keys `s.ext.effect.cf.` + `description.value` (`Change {0} of {1} to "{2}"`), `description.empty` (`Clear {0} value of {1}`), `conflict.value` (`Change {0} of {1} to "{2}" (conflicts with values: {3})`), `conflict.empty` (`Clear {0} value of {1} (conflicts with values: {2})`), `success.value` (`Changed {0} of {1} to "{2}"`) and `success.empty` (`Cleared {0} value of {1}`), with arguments field name (the custom field's name, or the raw `customField` text, or `<?>`), issue key, value text when present, conflicts; key choice as summary-effect-provider states.

Shared by every single-value custom-field provider in this group: the change is validated and applied as effect-provider-helper states, with the custom field's id as the field id checked in the validated values and its name in `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` ("Cannot change {0} of {1}. This is likely because the field is not on the edit screen"); the value is put with `IssueInputParameters.addCustomFieldValue(fieldId, <one string or null>)`. Optimization groups by `issue` and `customField`.

The current value is the field's value on the issue (`getValueFromIssue`); null and empty text count as equal. Applying puts the text (or null) as the field's single value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setTextCustomField(issue, field, <text before the change>)`. The value text in descriptions is the parameter as given.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:number-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `NumberCFType` field), `value`, `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setNumberCustomField`. Custom field lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states for all custom-field providers.

`value` given as a `Number` is taken as its double value; absent or null means clear; otherwise its single string form is parsed as a double (`"2.5"`, `"1e3"`). Empty text or unparsable text gives error `s.ext.effect.error.bad-param` with `value` ("Incorrect value for parameter \"value\".").

Old and new are equal when both are null or when the field type's stored string forms (`getStringFromSingularObject`) are the same (so 2 and 2.0 are equal). Applying puts that stored string form (null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setNumberCustomField(issue, field, <number before the change>)`.
The value text in descriptions is the field type's stored string form of the number (its `toString()` if the field did not resolve), or the raw parameter text when the value failed to parse.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:date-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `DateCFType` field), `value` (epoch milliseconds, read as a long; absent clears; non-numeric text also reads as no value and clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setDateCustomField`. Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

For an Advanced Roadmaps target start or target end field (type key per C-2269) when `portfolio-integration` says the UTC shift is needed (C-2270), the new value is replaced by the start (00:00 UTC) of the calendar day it falls on in the JVM's default time zone, both for the equality check and for the value written; for other fields, or when Advanced Roadmaps is absent or needs no shift, the value is used as given.

Old and new are equal when both are null or the field type's stored string forms are the same (the (possibly shifted) new value against the unshifted current value). Applying puts the stored string form (null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setDateCustomField(issue, field, <date before the change>)`. The value text in descriptions uses Jira's `DateFieldFormat.format` of the unshifted value.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:date-time-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `DateTimeCFType` field), `value` (epoch milliseconds, read as a long; absent clears; non-numeric text also reads as no value and clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setDateTimeCustomField`. Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

Old and new are equal when both are null or the field type's stored string forms are the same. Applying puts the stored string form of the timestamp (null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setDateTimeCustomField(issue, field, <value before the change>)`.
The value text in descriptions is the timestamp formatted by Jira's `DateTimeFormatter` in style `DateTimeStyle.COMPLETE` for the logged-in user.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:single-select-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a field whose type is a `SelectCFType`: single select lists and radio buttons), `value` (option id, read as a long; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setSingleSelectCustomField`. Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

Shared by the option, project and version providers (single select, cascade, project picker, single version): the `value` id is resolved through the item resolver as item `<item type>/<id>` (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-cf-option` for options, `type-project`, `type-version`); when the resolver gives nothing (unknown or not visible to the current user) the error is `s.ext.effect.error.no-option` ("Option \"{0}\" could not be found."), `no-project` ("Project ...") or `no-version` ("Version ...") with the id. A `value` that is not a number reads as no value and so clears the field instead of failing (as the original does).

Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same option id. Applying puts the option id as text (null to clear) as the field value; Jira's validation decides whether the option belongs to the field's context. The undo is `CoreEffects.setSingleSelectCustomField(issue, field, <option before the change>)`. The value text is the option's value text.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:cascade-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `CascadingSelectCFType` field), `value` (the id of a parent option or of a child option, as item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-cf-option`; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setCascadeCustomField`. Option resolution is as single-select-custom-field-effect-provider states; lookup, texts and update as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

The current value is the field's child option (key `1` of the cascading value) when there is one, else its parent option (key null), else null. Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same option id.

Applying a child option puts the parent option's id under the field id and the child's id under `<field id>:1`; a parent option is put alone under the field id; clearing puts null under the field id. The undo is `CoreEffects.setCascadeCustomField(issue, field, <option before the change>)` (the child when there was one).
A child option is described as `<parent value> - <child value>`, a parent option by its value.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:project-picker-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `ProjectCFType` field), `value` (project id, resolved as item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project` as single-select-custom-field-effect-provider states, error `s.ext.effect.error.no-project` "Project \"{0}\" could not be found."; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setProjectPickerCustomField`.

Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same project id. Applying puts the project id as text (null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setProjectPickerCustomField(issue, field, <project before the change>)`. The value text is the project's name.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:single-user-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `UserCFType` field), `value` (user key; absent or empty clears; unknown key -> `s.ext.effect.error.no-user` "User \"{0}\" could not be found."), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setSingleUserCustomField`. Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same user key. Applying puts the user's username (not key; null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setSingleUserCustomField(issue, field, <user before the change>)`.

Users in description, success and conflict texts are carried as `${<user key>}` and shown as the user's display name, or `unknown user`, exactly as assignee-effect-provider states; an empty-text `value` is described as `null` there too (as the original does).

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:single-group-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `MultiGroupCFType` field), `value` (group name), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`, matching `CoreEffects.setSingleGroupCustomField`. Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

An absent or blank `value` clears the field. Otherwise the name is resolved through the item resolver as the group item with that name; no group gives error `s.ext.effect.error.no-group` ("Group \"{0}\" could not be found."). The value text is the group's name.

After all parameters resolve, a field that allows several groups (`MultiGroupCFType.isMultiple()` true) gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` with (field name, field id), as text-custom-field-effect-provider states for that message.

The current value is the first group in the field's value (null when empty). Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same name. Applying puts the group name (null to clear) as the field value. The undo is `CoreEffects.setSingleGroupCustomField(issue, field, <first group before the change>)`.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:single-version-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (a `VersionCFType` field), `isUndo` (boolean, default false), `value` (version id, resolved as item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version` as single-select-custom-field-effect-provider states, error `s.ext.effect.error.no-version` "Version \"{0}\" could not be found."; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`. `CoreEffects.setSingleVersionCustomField` gives `issue`, `customField` and `value`.

After the parameters resolve, checks in this order: a multi-version field (`isMultiple()` true) -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type`; clearing while the field's current (first) version is archived and `isUndo` is false -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.remove.archived.version` ("Cannot remove issue {0} from the archived version \"{1}\".", issue key, version name); a version whose project id differs from the issue's -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.version-project` ("Cannot add version \"{0}\" to issue {1}, because this version belongs to a different project.", version name, issue key), checked even when undoing; an archived version and `isUndo` false -> `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.add.archived.version` ("Cannot add issue {0} to the archived version \"{1}\".", issue key, version name). Replacing a current archived version by another version is not checked.

The current value is the field's first version. Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same version id. Applying puts the version id as text (null to clear) as the field value. The value text is the version's name.

The undo is `CoreEffects.setSingleVersionCustomField(issue, field, <first version before the change>)` with `isUndo` = true added when the applied effect was not itself an undo; the undo of an undo has no `isUndo`. So undoing may re-add or remove an archived version.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:script-runner-single-issue-picker-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (any custom field id), `value` (id of the issue to put in the field, read as a long; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`. Its own undo effects have `issue`, `customField` and `value` = the picked issue's id (absent when none). Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

A present `value` is resolved through the item resolver as the issue item with that id; no issue (or one the user cannot see) gives `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue` ("Issue does not exist or you have no permission to see it."). The value text is the picked issue's key.

After the parameters resolve: a field whose type's implementation class is not exactly `com.onresolve.scriptrunner.canned.jira.fields.editable.issue.SingleIssuePickerField` gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` (field name, field id); then, when `scriptrunner-integration` reports the field read-only for the issue, `s.ext.effect.error.field.readonly` ("Field {0} is read-only.", field name). When ScriptRunner is absent no field has that type, so every effect fails with the wrong-type error.

The current value is the field type's value for the issue when it is a Jira `Issue` (another kind of value logs a warning and reads as none). Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same issue id. Applying puts the field type's stored string form of the picked issue (null to clear) as the field value. The undo sets the field back to the issue picked before the change.

Module `com.almworks.jira.structure:portfolio-team-custom-field-effect-provider` (element `structure-effect-provider`, no children) accepts `issue`, `customField` (any custom field id: its type is not checked), `value` (team id, read as a long; absent clears), `sendNotifications` and `conflicts`. Its undo effects have `issue`, `customField` and `value` = the previous team's id (absent when none). Lookup, texts and update are as text-custom-field-effect-provider states.

A present `value` is looked up as a team by id through `portfolio-integration` (C-2262); none (unknown id, or Advanced Roadmaps Team Management absent) gives `s.ext.effect.error.no-team` ("Team \"{0}\" could not be found.", the id). The value text is the team's title.

After the parameters resolve, an issue that is a sub-task gives `s.ext.effect.error.subtask.team-disabled` ("The team for a sub-task is inherited from the parent issue and cannot be assigned."), for clearing too.

The current value is the field's value read as a team (its `getId()` and `getDescription().getTitle()`; a value that cannot be read so logs a warning and reads as none). Old and new are equal when both are null or have the same team id. Applying puts the team id as text (null to clear) as the field value.

The multi-value field effect providers (`labels-effect-provider`, `multi-labels-custom-field-effect-provider`, `components-effect-provider`, `affects-versions-effect-provider`, `fix-versions-effect-provider`, `multi-versions-custom-field-effect-provider`, `multi-select-custom-field-effect-provider`, `multi-user-custom-field-effect-provider`, `multi-group-custom-field-effect-provider` and `insight-object-custom-field-effect-provider`) all read these effect parameters: `issue` (the issue id, required), `add`, `remove` and `set` (each a list of value keys, a single value is read as a one-element list), `conflicts` (list), `sendNotifications` (boolean, missing = false) and, for the custom field ones, `customField` (the custom field id, e.g. `customfield_10010`); the version providers also read `isUndo` (boolean, missing = false). Value keys match the `CoreEffects` collection helpers: label texts, component / version / option ids as numbers (numeric text is accepted too), user keys, group names, Insight object keys.

For every multi-value field effect provider: a missing or non-numeric `issue` gives an error response `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` ("No value for required parameter "issue"."); an issue id that the item resolver cannot resolve for the current user (missing or not visible) gives `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue` ("Issue does not exist or you have no permission to see it."). The response's affected items are `[issue/<id>]` whenever `issue` holds a number (even when the issue cannot be resolved), else empty. All parameters are resolved and the first error in the order issue, add, remove, set, conflicts, sendNotifications, customField, isUndo is reported; the response still carries the effect description.

For the custom field providers among the multi-value ones, `customField` that is missing or names no custom field gives error `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.no-field` ("Custom field does not exist."); a custom field of the wrong type gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` with arguments (field name, field id), which the English text renders as `Custom field "<id>" (<name>) is of incorrect type.` (the arguments are in the opposite order to the wording, as the original does). Accepted types: `LabelsCFType` (labels), `VersionCFType` (versions), `MultiSelectCFType` (options, so also multi-checkboxes), `MultiUserCFType`, `MultiGroupCFType`, and the Insight type keys `com.riadalabs.jira.plugins.insight:rlabs-customfield-default-object`, `...-object` and `...-object-multi`. For the system field ones, a Jira field that `FieldManager.getField` does not find (`labels`, `components`, `versions`, `fixVersions`) gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.no-field` ("Field does not exist.").

In every multi-value field effect provider, each key in `add`, `remove` or `set` is looked up (labels are only trimmed); the first key that finds nothing gives an error with that key as argument: labels `s.ext.effect.error.bad-param`, components `s.ext.effect.error.no-component` ("Component "{0}" could not be found."), versions `s.ext.effect.error.no-version`, options `s.ext.effect.error.no-option`, users `s.ext.effect.error.no-user` ("User "{0}" could not be found."), groups `s.ext.effect.error.no-group`, Insight objects `s.ext.effect.error.no-insight-object` ("Object "{0}" could not be found"). For the numeric kinds an element that is not a number is silently skipped rather than reported.

A multi-value field effect computes the new value from the issue's current values: with `add` and/or `remove` present it starts from the current values, adds the `add` values (keeping order, no duplicates) and then takes out the `remove` values (so a value in both is removed); with only `set` the new value is exactly the `set` values; with none of the three, or `set` empty, the new value is empty (the field is cleared). When `set` is given together with `add` or `remove`: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) resolving throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled `set` is ignored.

When the computed new value holds exactly the issue's current values (same count, all current keys present, order ignored), a multi-value field effect resolves to an empty response (no change, nothing to apply) and no validation is done.

Except for system Labels, a multi-value field effect is validated and applied as an issue update through Jira's `IssueService` as described for `effect-provider-helper` (retain unprovided values, `validateUpdate` as the current Structure user, errors joined by `, `; field not on the edit screen gives `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` "Cannot change {0} of {1}. This is likely because the field is not on the edit screen" with the field name and issue key; `update` with ISSUE_UPDATED and mail sent only when `sendNotifications` is true). The whole new value is written: components with `setComponentIds`, Affects Versions with `setAffectedVersionIds`, Fix Versions with `setFixVersionIds`, custom fields with `addCustomFieldValue(fieldId, values)` where the values are label texts, version ids, option ids, user *names* (not keys), group names or Insight object keys as strings.

Applying a multi-value field effect returns an undo effect computed from the issue just before the change. For a set-style effect (no `add` and no `remove` parameter) the undo is the same effect with `set` = the previous value keys in the issue's order (parameter absent when the field was empty, i.e. undo clears). For an add/remove effect the undo swaps them: undo `add` = the `remove` keys that were actually present, undo `remove` = the `add` keys that were actually absent, `set` dropped; when only one side is non-empty the other parameter is left out, when both are empty both are empty lists. All other parameters (issue, customField, sendNotifications, conflicts...) are kept.

When a batch holds several effects of one multi-value provider, they are grouped by `issue` (and `customField`); if no group has more than one effect the list is returned unchanged. A group is merged into one effect based on its last effect: replaying the effects in order, add/remove operations after the last set-style effect are applied to that set (result: `set` = the final set, absent if empty; no `add`/`remove`); without any set-style effect the result has `add` = keys whose last operation was add and `remove` = keys whose last operation was remove (each absent when empty), in first-seen order.

While merging multi-value effects, parameter `conflicts` collects (first-seen order) the keys that were both added and removed, plus the keys of earlier set-style effects that were superseded, plus `{"empty":true}` when some set-style effect was empty but the final set is not; keys present in the final set are taken out again. `conflicts` is absent when nothing is collected. Operations that came before the first set-style effect only contribute their conflicting keys.

Multi-value effect descriptions are i18n texts: with add and remove `s.ext.effect.multi.replace.+description` ("Replace value(s) "{0}" with "{1}" in field {2} of {3}", arguments removed values, added values, field name, issue key); only add `s.ext.effect.multi.add.+description` ("Add value(s) "{0}" to field {1} of {2}"); only remove `s.ext.effect.multi.remove.+description`; set `s.ext.effect.multi.set.+description` ("Set value(s) of field {1} to "{0}" in {2}"); empty set `s.ext.effect.multi.clear.+description` ("Clear value(s) of field {0} in {1}"). Success messages use the `+success` keys with the same arguments ("Added value(s) ...", "Cleared value(s) ..."). With non-empty `conflicts` the description uses the `+conflict` key and an extra last argument: the conflict values joined by `, ` (`<empty>` for {"empty":true}). An empty `add` or `remove` list counts as absent. Values are joined with `, ` as labels, component/version/option/group names, Insight object labels; unresolvable keys show as `component <id>`, `version <id>`, `option <id>`, `object <key>`, `unknown user`, or `group {0}` (the group text is used without its argument, as the original does); the issue shows as its key (raw id when unresolved) and the field by name (`(?)` when unknown).

A multi-value effect's HTML description without conflicts is the HTML-encoded localized description. With conflicts it is the conflict layout of `effect-provider-helper` with extra CSS class `s-multivalue-conflict`, using key `...+conflict-short` ("Add/Remove conflict: ..." / "Set conflict: ..."; a clear becomes the set variant), where each value argument is `<select multiple class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="add|remove|set">` listing the effect's keys as selected options followed by the conflict keys not among them, each `<option selected|(blank) [data-empty="true"] value="<key>"><label></option>` HTML-encoded; the remaining arguments are HTML-encoded text.

`labels-effect-provider` changes the system Labels field (Jira field id `labels`) of the issue in `issue`. Its value keys are label texts (trimmed; parameter `add`, `remove` or `set`); the current value is `Issue.getLabels()`. It never reports a validation problem of its own.

Unlike the other multi-value providers, Labels are changed through Jira's `LabelService`: the new label set is validated with `validateSetLabels(user, issueId, labels)` as the current Structure user (invalid: error with Jira's messages joined by `, `), then, if the issue's edit screen (`FieldScreenRendererFactory` for EDIT_ISSUE_OPERATION) hides the Labels field, error `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with the field's name and the issue key. Applying calls `setLabels(user, result, sendNotifications, true)` after building the undo.

`multi-labels-custom-field-effect-provider` changes a labels custom field (type `LabelsCFType`, chosen by `customField`) of the issue. Value keys are label texts, trimmed; the current value is the field's labels on the issue (none = empty). It reports no validation problem of its own; the update goes through `IssueService` with the label texts.

`components-effect-provider` changes the issue's system Components (field id `components`). Value keys are component ids (numbers) found with `ProjectComponentManager.getProjectComponent`; the current value is `Issue.getComponents()`; values are described by component name.

Before updating, every component of the new value must belong to the issue's project; the first one that does not gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.component-project` ("Cannot add component "{0}" to issue {1}, because this component belongs to a different project.", component name, issue key). This also applies to components already on the issue that stay.

`affects-versions-effect-provider` changes the issue's system field `versions` (Affects Version/s). Value keys are version ids (numbers) found with `VersionManager.getVersion`; the current value is `Issue.getAffectedVersions()`; the new value is written with `setAffectedVersionIds`; values are described by version name.

`fix-versions-effect-provider` changes the issue's system field `fixVersions` (Fix Version/s). Value keys are version ids (numbers) found with `VersionManager.getVersion`; the current value is `Issue.getFixVersions()`; the new value is written with `setFixVersionIds`; values are described by version name.

`multi-versions-custom-field-effect-provider` changes a version picker custom field (type `VersionCFType`, chosen by `customField`). Value keys are version ids found with `VersionManager.getVersion`; the new value is written as the version ids in text form. A version field that is single-valued (`isMultiple()` false) is refused when a change is needed, with `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` (field name, field id), before the version rules are checked.

`affects-versions-effect-provider` checks a needed change (in this order): every version of a non-empty new value must be in the issue's project, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.version-project` ("Cannot add version "{0}" to issue {1}, because this version belongs to a different project.", version name, issue key); a new value may not contain an archived version the issue did not already have, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.add.archived.version` ("Cannot add issue {0} to the archived version "{1}".", issue key, version name); and no archived version the issue has may be dropped (including clearing the field), else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.remove.archived.version` ("Cannot remove issue {0} from the archived version "{1}"."). Both archived-version rules are skipped when the effect has `isUndo` = true.
The undo effect that `affects-versions-effect-provider` returns always carries `isUndo` = true (added when the original did not have it), so undoing a change can re-add or remove archived versions.

`fix-versions-effect-provider` checks a needed change (in this order): every version of a non-empty new value must be in the issue's project, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.version-project` ("Cannot add version "{0}" to issue {1}, because this version belongs to a different project.", version name, issue key); a new value may not contain an archived version the issue did not already have, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.add.archived.version` ("Cannot add issue {0} to the archived version "{1}".", issue key, version name); and no archived version the issue has may be dropped (including clearing the field), else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.remove.archived.version` ("Cannot remove issue {0} from the archived version "{1}"."). Both archived-version rules are skipped when the effect has `isUndo` = true.
The undo effect that `fix-versions-effect-provider` returns always carries `isUndo` = true (added when the original did not have it), so undoing a change can re-add or remove archived versions.

`multi-versions-custom-field-effect-provider` checks a needed change (in this order): every version of a non-empty new value must be in the issue's project, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.version-project` ("Cannot add version "{0}" to issue {1}, because this version belongs to a different project.", version name, issue key); a new value may not contain an archived version the issue did not already have, else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.add.archived.version` ("Cannot add issue {0} to the archived version "{1}".", issue key, version name); and no archived version the issue has may be dropped (including clearing the field), else `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.remove.archived.version` ("Cannot remove issue {0} from the archived version "{1}"."). Both archived-version rules are skipped when the effect has `isUndo` = true.

The undo effect that `multi-versions-custom-field-effect-provider` returns always carries `isUndo` = true (added when the original did not have it), so undoing a change can re-add or remove archived versions.

`multi-select-custom-field-effect-provider` changes a multi-select custom field (any type that is a `MultiSelectCFType`, which includes multi-checkboxes) chosen by `customField`. Value keys are option ids (numbers) found with `OptionsManager.findByOptionId` (any option id, not checked against the field or its context); the current value is the field's options on the issue (none = empty); options are described by their value text. It reports no validation problem of its own; the update writes the option ids.

`multi-user-custom-field-effect-provider` changes a multi-user-picker custom field (`MultiUserCFType`) chosen by `customField`. Value keys are user keys found with `UserManager.getUserByKey`; the current value is the field's users on the issue (none = empty); the update writes the users' usernames. No validation problem of its own.

In descriptions of `multi-user-custom-field-effect-provider` each user is written as `${<userKey>}` and the description is an unresolved i18n text that keeps these arguments and also carries them resolved: each `${key}` replaced by that user's display name as resolved through the item resolver for the current user, or `unknown user` (`s.ext.effect.field.user-unknown`). In conflict selectors users are shown by display name, unknown keys as `unknown user`.

`multi-group-custom-field-effect-provider` changes a group picker custom field (`MultiGroupCFType`) chosen by `customField`. Value keys are group names found with `GroupManager.getGroup`; the current value is the field's groups on the issue; groups are described by name. When a change is needed and the field is single-valued (`isMultiple()` false) it gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.custom.wrong-cf-type` (field name, field id).

`insight-object-custom-field-effect-provider` changes an Assets/Insight object custom field whose type key is `com.riadalabs.jira.plugins.insight:rlabs-customfield-default-object`, `...:rlabs-customfield-object` or `...:rlabs-customfield-object-multi`, chosen by `customField`. Value keys are Insight object keys (e.g. `ITSM-123`) looked up through `insight-integration-supplier`; an unknown key, an object the user may not see, or Insight being unavailable gives `s.ext.effect.error.no-insight-object` with the key. The current value is the field's value on the issue (`CustomField.getValue`), keeping only Insight object beans. Objects are described by label; the update writes the object keys. No validation problem of its own. Without the Insight app no such field type exists, so effects fail with the custom field errors.

`original-estimate-effect-provider` reads `issue` (issue id, required; errors as for the other issue effects: `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` / `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue`), `originalEstimate` (the new original estimate in milliseconds, a number or numeric text; absent = clear), `conflicts` and `sendNotifications` (boolean, missing = false), matching `CoreEffects` (`setOriginalEstimate`).

`original-estimate-effect-provider` reads the current value as `Issue.getOriginalEstimate()` seconds times 1000; null or 0 counts as no estimate (null). The effect is a no-op (empty response) when the new value equals the current one, or when both format to the same Jira duration text in the current user's locale (e.g. 3600000 and 3630000 both `1h`); a null and a non-null value are never equal (so setting 0 on an issue without an estimate is a change).

`original-estimate-effect-provider` applies the change as an `IssueService` update (see `effect-provider-helper`) checked against Jira field id `timetracking`, calling `IssueInputParameters.setOriginalEstimate` with the duration formatted as Jira time-tracking text in the default locale (`format-helper`: under a minute is `0m`, negatives prefixed `-`), or the empty string to clear. If the time-tracking field is not on the edit screen the error is `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with arguments `timetracking` and the issue key.

The undo of `original-estimate-effect-provider` is `CoreEffects.setOriginalEstimate` for the issue with the value before the change (absent when there was none): it has only `issue` and `originalEstimate`, so undoing never sends notifications and drops `conflicts`.

Descriptions of `original-estimate-effect-provider`: `s.ext.effect.+originalEstimate+.description.value` ("Change original estimate of {0} to \"{1}\"": issue key, the duration formatted for the current user) or `.description.empty` ("Clear original estimate of {0}"); with conflicts `.conflict.value` / `.conflict.empty` with the conflict values (durations, `<empty>` for {"empty":true}) joined by `, ` as last argument; success messages `.success.value` ("Changed original estimate ...") / `.success.empty`. Several effects for one issue in a batch merge as described for `effect-provider-helper` on parameter `originalEstimate`. With conflicts the HTML description uses the `.description.value` key with a `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="originalEstimate">` of the value and conflicts.

`remaining-estimate-effect-provider` reads `issue` (issue id, required; errors as for the other issue effects: `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` / `s.ext.gen.block.no-issue`), `remainingEstimate` (the new remaining estimate in milliseconds, a number or numeric text; absent = clear), `conflicts` and `sendNotifications` (boolean, missing = false), matching `CoreEffects` (`setRemainingEstimate`).

`remaining-estimate-effect-provider` reads the current value as `Issue.getEstimate()` seconds times 1000; null or 0 counts as no estimate (null). The effect is a no-op (empty response) when the new value equals the current one, or when both format to the same Jira duration text in the current user's locale (e.g. 3600000 and 3630000 both `1h`); a null and a non-null value are never equal (so setting 0 on an issue without an estimate is a change).

`remaining-estimate-effect-provider` applies the change as an `IssueService` update (see `effect-provider-helper`) checked against Jira field id `timetracking`, calling `IssueInputParameters.setRemainingEstimate` with the duration formatted as Jira time-tracking text in the default locale (`format-helper`: under a minute is `0m`, negatives prefixed `-`), or the empty string to clear. If the time-tracking field is not on the edit screen the error is `s.ext.effect.cf.error.no-value` with arguments `timetracking` and the issue key.

The undo of `remaining-estimate-effect-provider` is `CoreEffects.setRemainingEstimate` for the issue with the value before the change (absent when there was none): it has only `issue` and `remainingEstimate`, so undoing never sends notifications and drops `conflicts`.

Descriptions of `remaining-estimate-effect-provider`: `s.ext.effect.+remainingEstimate+.description.value` ("Change remaining estimate of {0} to \"{1}\"": issue key, the duration formatted for the current user) or `.description.empty` ("Clear remaining estimate of {0}"); with conflicts `.conflict.value` / `.conflict.empty` with the conflict values (durations, `<empty>` for {"empty":true}) joined by `, ` as last argument; success messages `.success.value` ("Changed remaining estimate ...") / `.success.empty`. Several effects for one issue in a batch merge as described for `effect-provider-helper` on parameter `remainingEstimate`. With conflicts the HTML description uses the `.description.value` key with a `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="remainingEstimate">` of the value and conflicts.

`sprint-effect-provider` reads `issue` (issue id, required), `to` (target sprint id; absent = take the issue out of its sprint), `from` (source sprint id, optional), `sameBoard` (boolean, missing = false), `conflicts` and `fromConflicts` (lists). `CoreEffects.setSprint` gives `issue` and `to`; the grouper's move effect also sets `from` and `sameBoard` = true only when the board check is wanted (absent otherwise). A sprint id that Jira Software does not know (looked up without a user, see `gh-integration`; also when Jira Software is absent) gives error `s.ext.effect.error.sprint.notfound` ("Sprint with id \"{0}\" could not be found.").

Resolving a sprint effect checks in order: sprint changes are possible (Jira Software's sprint issue service available) else `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.no-wrapper` ("Cannot change issue sprint."); the Sprint custom field exists (looked up once and then reused) else `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.no-sprint-field` ("Sprint field is not found."); the current Structure user has Schedule Issues on the issue else `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.no-permission` ("No permission to change issue sprint: {0}." with the text of `s.ext.gen.agile.block.no-schedule-perm`).

The source sprint is `from` when given, else the first sprint in the issue's Sprint field value (as converted by `gh-integration`) that is not closed, else none. When source and target are the same sprint id, or both are none, the effect is a no-op (empty response).

A needed sprint change is refused when the source sprint is closed (`s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.from-closed`, "Cannot remove issues from a closed sprint.") or the target is closed (`s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.to-closed`, "Cannot add issues to a closed sprint."). With `sameBoard` true and a target: a target sprint without board id, or (without source) a board whose filter query cannot be read for the current user, gives the text of `s.ext.gen.agile.block.no-rapid-view` ("Rapid board does not exist or you have no permission to see it."); with a source on a different board, or (without source) an issue that does not match the target board's filter (checked with the issue index as the current user), gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.unsuitable-rapid-view`; a search failure gives `s.ext.gen.grouper.agilesprint.block.rapid-view-search-error` ("Error checking rapid board.").

Applying a sprint effect, as the current Structure user: with a target it asks Jira Software to move the issue into the target sprint (`moveIssuesToSprint` with the single issue), without one to remove it from the source sprint (`removeIssuesFromSprint`). Whether Jira Software reports success is not checked, so a refused move still counts as applied.

The undo of a sprint effect (built before applying) has `issue`, `to` = the source sprint used (explicit or derived; absent when none), `from` = the original target (absent when none) and `sameBoard` = true only when the original had it true; it has no conflicts.

Sprint effect descriptions use only the explicit `from` parameter (not a derived source): `s.ext.gen.agile.effect.sprint.description.add` ("Add {0} to sprint {1}.": issue key, target name), `.move` ("Move {0} from sprint {1} to sprint {2}."), `.remove` ("Remove {0} from sprint {1}."), and with neither `.empty` ("Remove {0} from the current sprint."); with `conflicts` the `.conflict` variant of each key with the conflicting target sprints' names (`<empty>` for {"empty":true}) joined by `, ` as last argument. Success messages: `s.ext.gen.agile.effect.sprint.move` ("Moved {0} to sprint {1}." when both are given), `.add` ("Added {0} to sprint {1}." without `from`), `.remove` ("Removed {0} from sprint {1}." with the `from` name, without `to`).

Several sprint effects for one issue in a batch merge into the last one; if earlier ones had other `from` values they are listed in `fromConflicts`, other `to` values in `conflicts` (distinct, first-seen order, absent value as {"empty":true}); groups of one, or without differing values, keep the last effect unchanged. The HTML description with conflicts shows a `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="from|to">` for each side that has conflicts (an `.empty` description is shown as `.add`).

`add-comment-effect-provider` reads `issue` (issue id, required, errors as for the other issue effects) and `comment` (the comment body text) and `conflicts`. A missing, empty or blank `comment` makes the effect a no-op (empty response). It has no `sendNotifications` parameter.

A comment is validated with `CommentService.validateCommentCreate` as the current Structure user (as author) with the issue and body; when invalid the error is `s.ext.effect.error.add-comment` ("Cannot add a comment. {0}") with the first error message (or `unknown error`). Applying calls `CommentService.create(author, validation, true)` (event dispatched) and returns as undo `CoreEffects.deleteIssueComment` for the created comment (`issue` and `comment` = the new comment's id).

Several add-comment effects for one issue in a batch: a group of one is kept; otherwise the effects with a non-blank `comment` are considered (if none, the last effect is kept): the last of them is kept and, when earlier ones had other comment texts, it gets `conflicts` = those distinct texts in first-seen order, so only one comment is added per issue.

Descriptions: `s.ext.effect.+add-comment+.description.value` ("Add a comment \"{0}\""), with conflicts `s.ext.effect.+add-comment+.conflict.value` ("Add a comment \"{0}\" (conflicts with comments: {1})", other texts joined by `, `); success `s.ext.effect.+add-comment+.success.value` ("Added a comment \"{0}\""). With conflicts the HTML description is the conflict layout with a `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="comment">` of the body and the conflicting bodies.

`delete-comment-effect-provider` reads `issue` (issue id, required) and `comment` (the comment id, a number; missing or non-numeric gives `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` with `comment`). The comment is fetched with `CommentService.getCommentById(user, id, errors)` as the current Structure user: any error gives `s.ext.effect.error.get-comment` ("Cannot get a comment. {0}", first message or `unknown error`).

When the comment is not found, or `CommentService.hasPermissionToDelete` says the current user may not delete it, the error is `s.ext.effect.error.delete-comment` ("User {0} does not have permission to delete a comment for this issue.") with the user's display name or `anonymous`. The comment is not checked to belong to the `issue`.

Applying deletes the comment with `CommentService.delete(context, comment, true)` and returns as undo `CoreEffects.addIssueComment(issue, body)`: undo re-adds a comment with the same text, authored by whoever applies the undo (not the original author or date). Descriptions: `s.ext.effect.+delete-comment+.description.value` ("Delete a comment for the id: {0}") and success `s.ext.effect.+delete-comment+.success.value` ("Deleted a comment for the id: {0}") with the comment id.

`memo-field-effect-provider` reads `memo` (the item identity text, e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo/5`; a plain number is taken as a memo id), `field` (a field id known to `structure-field-manager`), `value` (the new value in the field type's stored text form, read back with that type; empty or absent means no value) and `conflicts`. Only memo and planning task items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`) are supported; building such an effect for another item type throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

Errors: an empty `field` gives `s.ext.effect.generic.field.error.no-value` ("No value for {0}" with `field`); an unknown field id `s.ext.effect.generic.field.error.cannot-resolve` ("Cannot resolve {0}: {1}", name and text); a value the field type cannot read `s.ext.effect.generic.field.error.invalid-value` ("Invalid value \"{0}\" for {1}: {2}"); another item type `s.ext.effect.generic.field.error.not-supported` ("Item identity {0} is not supported"); an item the item resolver does not give to the current user `s.ext.effect.generic.field.error.not-found` ("Item {0} is not accessible or not found", the item's key); then the update check of `generic-item-field-accessor-manager` (its first problem). A missing or unparsable `memo` throws `NullPointerException` from resolving instead of giving an error response (as the original does).

When the item's current value of the field equals the new value the effect is a no-op (empty response). Applying reads the current value again, builds the undo effect (same `memo` and `field`, `value` = the old value serialized, absent when none), then writes the new value through the item's field update. Affected items: the item.

Descriptions are `s.ext.effect.+memo+.field.set.description` ("Set value of {1} field to \"{0}\" in memo {2}") or, for planning tasks, `s.ext.effect.+planning-task+.field.set.description` ("... in planning task {2}"); with conflicts the `.field.set.conflict` variants; success `.field.set.success`. Arguments: the value's view text (`<empty>` when none, or Jira's `assignee.types.unassigned` text for field `assignee`), the field's name in the plugin's locale, the item's summary, and the raw `conflicts` list (shown as its list text). Several effects for one item and field merge on `value` as described for `effect-provider-helper`; with conflicts the HTML description shows a `<select class="s-aui-select2" data-effect-parameter="value">` with the values' view texts.

`warning-effect-provider` never changes anything: every effect resolves to an error response whose error and description are the same i18n text: key = parameter `i18nKey`, arguments = parameter `arguments` as strings (none when absent). Without `i18nKey` the text is `s.ext.effect.unknown-error` ("Unknown problem") with no arguments. This matches `CoreEffects.emitWarning`.
The affected items of a warning are the `affectedItems` parameter's entries parsed as item identities, in order; entries that cannot be parsed are skipped.
Optimizing a batch of warnings removes exact duplicates (same module key and parameters), keeping the first occurrence of each in order.

`delay-effect-provider` reads `itemId` (an item identity text) and `delay` (milliseconds, default 100). Errors, checked in this order: missing or empty `itemId` gives the plain text `No item ID`; an unparsable one `Invalid item ID: <parse message>`; a negative delay `Negative delay`. Affected items: the parsed item (none when it is invalid).

Applying a delay effect sleeps for `delay` ms (0 = no sleep; if interrupted it restores the thread's interrupt flag and returns) and returns as undo an identical delay effect (`itemId` = the item's identity text, `delay`). Description `Delay for <n> ms` (`<?>` when the delay is invalid), success `Delayed for <n> ms`, as plain texts.

`conversion-effect-provider` reads `fromType` (source item type key), `longId` (source item id), `toType` (target item type key), `initialId` (optional long id of a target-type item), `structureId` and `strategy` (`FULL_REPLACE`, `CREATE_AND_FORGET` or `REMOVE_AND_FORGET`). All but `initialId` are required; when one is missing the error is `s.ext.effect.error.no-param` ("No value for required parameter \"{0}\".") with its name (blank texts count as missing), the description is `s.ext.effect.conversion.parse.error.description` ("Conversion with parameters: {0}" with `fromType=..., longId=..., toType=..., initialId=..., structureId=..., strategy=...`, `<?>` for missing values) and there are no affected items.

Effects are built only for long-id items of types `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task` (else `IllegalArgumentException`). The planning-task conversion used by `effector-conversion` has `toType` = `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`, no `initialId`, and strategy `CREATE_AND_FORGET` when the planning task row is to be kept, else `FULL_REPLACE`.

An unknown `strategy` gives `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.no-such-strategy` ("Strategy {0} is not available"). A `fromType` other than issue or planning task makes resolving throw `NullPointerException` (as the original does). Affected items: the source item and, when `initialId` is set, the `toType` item with that id.

Descriptions by source type: issue `s.ext.effect.conversion.issue.description` ("Convert Jira issue {0} to a planning task", issue key or the id when it does not exist) / success `s.ext.effect.conversion.issue.success`; planning task `s.ext.effect.conversion.pt.description` ("Convert planning task {0} to a Jira issue", the planning task's key) / `s.ext.effect.conversion.pt.success`; for `REMOVE_AND_FORGET` the `.remove.description` / `.remove.success` keys ("Remove Jira issue {0}", "Planning task {0} has been removed"...). The HTML description puts `` into the text (issue URL `/browse/`), or the bare id when the item no longer exists.

For `FULL_REPLACE` and `CREATE_AND_FORGET` resolving prepares the new item: `toType` must be a `CreatableItemType` (else `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.wrong-item-type`, "Item type {0} is not supported"); the source's values are read: an issue through `IssueService.getIssue` as the current user (invalid: Jira's messages joined by line breaks; missing: `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.no-issue`) using the field values of `issue-to-planning-task-converter`; a planning task through `GenericItemService.getItem` (invalid: joined messages; missing: `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.no-item`; not visible to the user: `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.planning-task-not-visible`) taking each of its fields known to `structure-field-manager` in editor form. For an issue target the values are given as `pid` (from `project`), `issuetype`, and `issue` = all values (with `timetracking_originalestimate` / `timetracking_remainingestimate` defaulted from `timeoriginalestimate` / `timeestimate`); for a generic item target as `summary`, `description` and `params` = the rest. A trial row is then created without saving; its errors become the error.

For `FULL_REPLACE` resolving also requires EDIT access to structure `structureId` (else `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.structure-not-accessible`, "User {0} has no EDIT permission for structure {1}", display name or `anonymous`), an actionable forest source of that structure's skeleton (else `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.not-actionable`), and exactly one row of the source item in that forest (none: `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.row-not-found`, "Item not found or you don't have permission to browse it."; several: `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.row-not-unique`).

For `FULL_REPLACE` and `REMOVE_AND_FORGET` resolving checks that the source can be deleted, without deleting it: an issue with `IssueService.validateDelete` as the current user, a planning task with `GenericItemService.validateDelete`; failures give their messages joined by line breaks; other types `s.ext.effect.conversion.error.wrong-item-type`.

Applying runs the strategy's steps in order, stopping at the first failure: create the target item; (FULL_REPLACE) add a row for it right after the source row under the same parent, move all children of the source row under the new row, remove the source row; (FULL_REPLACE, REMOVE_AND_FORGET) delete the source item. On a failure the steps already done are undone in reverse order with security overridden (undo failures are only logged) and a `StructureException` with `StructureErrors.CREATE_ITEM_FAILED` is thrown with the failing step's message key; its arguments are passed wrapped in one extra array (as the original does).

After a successful `FULL_REPLACE` a `StructureItemConvertedEvent(structureId, source item, new item)` is published. The undo effect converts back: from the new item (for `REMOVE_AND_FORGET`: the `toType`/`initialId` item) to `fromType` in the same structure, with strategy `FULL_REPLACE` for `FULL_REPLACE`, `REMOVE_AND_FORGET` for `CREATE_AND_FORGET`, `CREATE_AND_FORGET` for `REMOVE_AND_FORGET`; `initialId` is the source id only when the undo strategy is `REMOVE_AND_FORGET`.

`effector-attribute-to-field` is a `structure-effector` with label `s.ext.eff.attribute-to-field.label` ("Attribute to Field"), dialog title `s.ext.eff.attribute-to-field.dialog-title` ("Save Attribute Value to Field"), and Velocity resources `form` (`/templates/structure/effector/attr-to-field.vm`) and `summary` (`/templates/structure/effector/attr-to-field-summary.vm`). It is always available.

Its stored parameters (`CoreEffectorParameters` names): `fieldId` (Jira field id), `attributeJson` (attribute spec as JSON `{"id":..., "format":..., "params":{...}}`, unknown properties ignored, format defaults to `text`), `jql` (optional), `sendNotifications` (boolean, missing = false) and `collectionOperation` (`add`, `remove` or `set`, any case; missing = set).

Building parameters from the form: `fieldId` empty gives a form error on `fieldId` with `s.ext.eff.attribute-to-field.error.+fieldId+.no-value` ("Please select field"), not a Jira field `...+fieldId+.illegal-value` ("Field \"{0}\" is not supported by this effector, sorry!"); `attributeJson` empty or `{}` gives `...+attributeJson+.no-value` ("Please select attribute"), unreadable JSON or an empty `id` `...+attributeJson+.illegal-value` ("Invalid attribute specification, please use the Advanced tab"); a non-empty value is stored even when it is reported illegal. `jql` is stored with leading/trailing horizontal whitespace removed, and when not blank must parse and pass `SearchService.validateQuery` as the current user (else the parse message or the first validation message on `jql`); `sendNotifications` is stored as a boolean and `collectionOperation` as given.

A new form gets `attributeJson` = `{}`, `sendNotifications` = true, `collectionOperation` = `set`; editing fills `fieldId`, `attributeJson`, `jql`, `sendNotifications` (false when missing) and `collectionOperation` (`set` when missing).
