`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}`: given id 0 or a negative id, it answers 400 with a `structure-error` of `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER`, message `id`, without looking the structure up; an unknown or invisible positive id gives 404 with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`: the entries of `structures` are basic summaries: id, name, description, the access flags, `isArchived`. They never carry `descriptionHtml`, `favorite`, `owner`, `permissions` or the generator and effector flags. Each referenced structure appears once, in no defined order, however many id lists refer to it.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`: without an accepted anchor issue, `containingAnchor`, `totalContainingAnchor` and `anchorIssue` are absent. With an accepted one, `anchorIssue` echoes it and the other two are present, also when no structure contains the issue (empty list, 0). `recent`, `favorites` and `defaults` are always present, empty when there is nothing.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`: when `forProject` is given, the anchor issue's project is not used even if the key is unknown: an unknown project key simply yields no project, so `defaults` holds only the global default. `forProject` is not checked for browse permission. With a known project whose default is absent, invisible or archived, `defaults` still holds the global default when that is viewable and not archived.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`: for an anonymous caller that passes the access gate, `recent` is empty (recents-manager stores nothing for anonymous users); `favorites` and `totalFavorites` are what favorite-manager gives for no user; defaults still follow the viewability rules.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: `permission` is matched ignoring case against all levels of `PermissionLevel`, which also accepts the deprecated `EDIT_GENERATORS`. Absent, `NONE` and `VIEW` all search at VIEW. Any other value gives 400 `Invalid request data` with message `Unknown level. Known values for level: NONE,VIEW,EDIT,EDIT_GENERATORS,AUTOMATE,ADMIN`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: the rate limit is checked first: a refused call answers 429 even when `permission` is invalid and does not list structures. A call that then fails on `permission` still counts as finished for the rate limiter, so the next call is not refused as concurrent.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: each item of `structure-summary-list` has no `descriptionHtml` and no `favorite`. The generator, effector and access flags, `isArchived`, and with `withPermissions` or `withOwner` the `permissions` and `owner` follow the same rules as `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: `limit=0` with at least one matching structure returns an empty `structures` with `haveMore` true, whatever `page` says; with no match it returns an empty list and no `haveMore`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: a negative `limit` is not clamped (as the original does). With no matching structure the reply is an empty page. With matches and no `page`, or `page` 1, the slice is invalid and the reply is 400 `Invalid request data` (an illegal argument). With matches and `page` 2 or more the start index is negative and the reply is 500 text/plain.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: a search refused by the rate limiter answers 429, `Content-Type: text/plain`, `Retry-After: <seconds>` and the body from i18n key `s.structure.error.rate-limit` (`Too many search requests. Please retry in about {0} second(s).`) in the caller's locale, with the same number in header and text.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/all` have separate rate limiters: a running search does not refuse a table call for the same user, nor the other way round. Each limiter reads its interval dark feature once, when its component is created; a later change has no effect until then.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/favorite`: an unknown or invisible structure answers 403 text/plain `structure <id> does not exist or you don't have enough permissions to view it`, not 404. A viewable one answers `{"favorite": <bool>}`.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/favorite`: a body `{}` means `favorite` false and removes the favourite. A body that reaches the resource as null fails with a null-argument error before the access check: 500 text/plain, nothing stored.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/recents`: `id` is taken from the query string. With an id it is passed to recents-manager for the caller, including ids of missing or invisible structures; without one, or for an anonymous caller, nothing is stored. All these cases answer 200 `empty-ok`.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms`: after the ADMIN check, an empty body, the JSON literal `null`, text that is not a JSON array, or an entry with a property that is not part of `quick-transform-entry` (unknown properties are refused) answers 400 `structure-error` `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER` with message `Cannot parse quick transforms`; nothing is stored.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms`: an array entry without `key`, an entry without `quick`, or a `group` entry without `transforms` fails while ids are checked with a null dereference: 500 text/plain, nothing stored (as the original does). Such entries are not dropped.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms`: what is stored in structure property `quick-transforms` is the parsed list written again as compact JSON with null properties left out, so whitespace and null members of the request do not survive; `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms` then returns that text as the JSON body. An empty array is valid and stores `[]`.
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms`: an unknown or invisible structure answers 403 text/plain with the same text as the favourite endpoints; a viewer without ADMIN may read.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/description-shown`: a viewer gets `{"descriptionShown": <bool>}`, from structure property `showDescription` as structure-resource-service states; an unknown or invisible structure answers 403 text/plain as for favourites.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: on success it answers 201, `Location` built from the relative URI `/<new id>`, and a `structure-summary` built with permission rules and owner requested (so `permissions` is there when the caller's effective permission includes ADMIN, and `owner` when visible), `favorite` false and `descriptionHtml` set.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: the body's `id`, `isArchived`, `owner`, `favorite`, `readOnly`, `editable`, `adminable` and the generator and effector flags are ignored: a new structure is never archived and its owner is always the caller. An anonymous caller allowed to create gets a structure without owner.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: a `permissions` entry with a missing `rule`, or a `set` rule without `level` or an `apply` rule without `structureId`, answers 400 `Invalid request data`; an unknown `rule` has message `Unknown rule. Known values for rule: apply,set`, an unknown `level` the message of `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure`. `rule` is matched ignoring case. Nothing is saved.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure`: missing `name` (`Name is required`) and empty `name` (`Name cannot be empty`) answer 400 `Invalid request data` and no structure is created. Only an empty string counts as empty here; a blank name passes this check and is refused by structure-manager on save.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure` and `POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/update`: the change is saved first. If the caller's effective permission on the saved structure then does not include VIEW (for example after permission rules taking away the caller's own access), building the reply fails with `StructureErrors.STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`: 404 `structure-error`, although the change stays saved.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/update`: `isArchived` false restores an archived structure and does not re-enable its synchronizers. `isArchived` true on an already archived structure does not touch synchronizers either. Synchronizers are disabled only after the save succeeded.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/update`: the reply is the saved `structure-summary` with `descriptionHtml`, permission rules and owner under the usual visibility rules, and the caller's `favorite` flag. An empty body object `{}` changes nothing and still answers 200.

`DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}`: a viewer without ADMIN gets 403 `structure-error` from structure-manager; a non-positive id gives 400 `structure-error` with message `id`; an unknown or invisible id gives 404 `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. It is never refused on licence grounds.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/one`: `id` is a query parameter of primitive type: leaving it out means 0, which answers as an unknown structure (404 `structure-error`), after the access check of code 4010. An archived structure the caller can view is returned.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/all`: the plugin-access check (code 4010) comes before the rate limit, so a caller without access gets 403 and does not use up a slot. A refused call answers 429 as `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure` does.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/recents`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/favorites`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/one` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/recent-ids` are never rate limited, even while the same user's `GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/all` is running. `recents` excludes archived structures (recents-manager); `favorites` includes them.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/favorites`: with no rows the reply is `structures` empty and `users` with only the caller (a user with no favourites), or both empty for an anonymous caller.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/recent-ids`: an anonymous caller who has access gets `[]`; the reply holds only ids recents-manager returns, so archived, deleted and invisible structures are left out.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/page-details`: exactly the limit (20 ids by default) is accepted, one more is refused. An empty array answers `{}`. A repeated id gives one entry. A null body fails with a null-argument error before the access check: 500 text/plain. The object's keys are in no defined order.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/manage-structures/page-details`: the limit is read from dark feature `structure.search.page-details-max-limit` once, when the component is created. The access check (code 4010) comes before the size check.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structureWelcome/search`: a missing, empty or whitespace-only `query` returns the recent structures of the caller from recents-manager, in that order: `result` has the first 10 and `total` their full count. Each `name` is HTML-escaped; other fields are not.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structureWelcome/search`: with a query, the text is trimmed and matched as a literal, ignoring case (Unicode-aware), against the names of structures the caller can view, not archived, in structure-manager's order. Regular expression characters have no special meaning. `result` has the first 10 and `total` counts all matches.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structureWelcome/search`: with a query, each `name` is HTML: the parts before, in and after the first match are HTML-escaped separately and the match is wrapped in `` and ``. For example the name `a<b`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/structureWelcome/search`: result items are basic summaries: no `descriptionHtml`, `favorite`, `owner`, `permissions` or generator and effector flags. Nothing is stored. With no match the reply is `{"result": [], "total": 0}`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: when the structure is not accessible with VIEW the reply is 403 text/plain `structure <id> does not exist or you don't have enough permissions to view it`, before any parameter is looked at.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: the listing is history-service's activity query for that one structure with all operations: newest first, row-invisible changes filtered for the caller, and entries left without changes skipped. `versions` is absent when no entry is delivered; the top-level `itemTypes` is `{}`.
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: `maxVersion` n lists only versions strictly below n; version n itself is not included. `maxVersion=0` therefore gives no versions.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: a negative `maxVersion`: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws `AssertionError` while the version key is built; with them disabled the key is negative and no version matches, so `versions` is absent.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: with `withVersion` and no `maxCount`, delivery stops right after the first entry whose version is less than or equal to `withVersion`, and that entry is included. If none exists, all entries are listed.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: a positive `maxCount` caps the listing at that many entries, also together with `withVersion`: the listing does not go on past `maxCount` to reach `withVersion`, and it does not stop early when `withVersion` is reached first, so `withVersion` has no effect there (as the original does).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: `maxCount` 0 or negative without `withVersion` returns exactly the newest entry (as the original does); with `withVersion` it acts as if `maxCount` were absent.
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: `minVersion` has no effect at all, whatever its value.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: each `structure-history-version` has `structure`, `version`, `timestamp`, `dateTimeFormatted` (Jira's RELATIVE style for the logged-in user) and `user` built by rest-user-builder from the entry's user key, as seen by the caller: an entry without user key gets the anonymous placeholder. `fullForest` and the per-change position fields are absent.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: `synchronizer` is absent when the entry has no synchronizer or id 0. Otherwise it is `{id, description}`, where `description` is the installed synchronizer's one-line description of its parameters, or the text of `s.sync.unavailable-synchronizer` when the instance is no longer installed or its module is missing.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: for a change whose forest has exactly one row, `itemId` is that row's item; if the row no longer exists `itemId` is absent and nothing fails. If the item is an issue the caller may see (the helper reports no issue error), `issueKey` and `issueSummary` are set; otherwise they are absent while `itemId` stays. With more than one row only `forestSize` tells the size.
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/version/{v}`: `operation` is the lower-case name `add`, `copy`, `move` or `remove`; `moveDirection` is the stored direction, 0 when there is none.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/versions`: each version's `itemTypes` lists only item types met while building that version. A type seen in an earlier version of the same reply is listed again in a later version that uses it.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/version/{v}`: no VIEW access answers 403 text/plain with the same text as the versions call. A failure from history-service is text/plain with the exception message and the status of its category: an unknown version 404, `GENERIC_ERROR` 500; never a `structure-error` object.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/version/{v}`: `v` = 0 answers 200 with history-service's synthetic entry: `timestamp` 0, the anonymous user placeholder, no `synchronizer`, `changes` empty, and the initial `fullForest` (normally empty text).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/version/{v}`: a negative `v` on a viewable structure: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) `AssertionError` propagates out of the resource, which handles only `StructureException`; with them disabled the outcome is what history-service gives, and is not determinable here.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/history/{id}/version/{v}`: each change also has `forest` and `fullForest` is set on the version, both as comma-joined `<row>:<depth>:<item>` entries (plus `:<semantics>` when positive). `parentPathFrom`, `parentPathTo`, `precedingSiblingsFrom` and `precedingSiblingsTo` are comma-separated row ids, absent when the list is null or empty. `itemTypes` covers the item types of the forests and `fullForest`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column`: lists come in source order then each source's list order: `bundled/bundled`, `stored/global`, `stored/user`. An anonymous caller allowed to use <product> gets all three, `stored/user` empty and without `createSupported`. A caller without plugin access fails with `STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED` from the stored source: 403 `structure-error`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}`: source and list key are compared exactly (case-sensitive). An unknown source, or a list key the source does not have (for example `bundled/global`), answers 404 with no body. A caller without plugin access asking for a stored list gets 403 `structure-error`; a bundled list needs no such check beyond the common gate.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}`: checks run in this order: unknown source (400 `structure-error` `StructureErrors.INVALID_PARAMETER`, message `Column source doesn't exist: <id>`); then the name rules; then, in the source, plugin access, list key and permission. So a blank name on an unknown list answers the name error, and `IllegalArgumentException` `List is not supported: <key>` becomes 400 `Invalid request data`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}` and `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}`: `name` is mandatory. Missing, empty or blank answers 400 `Invalid request data` with the message of `s.w.saved-column.error.blank-name` (`Column name cannot be blank`); longer than 190 characters, counted before trimming, with `s.w.saved-column.error.long-name` (`Column name cannot be longer than 190 characters`). Otherwise the name is stored trimmed. Nothing is stored on failure.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}` and `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}`: the plugin does not check `type`, but `C_TYPE` of `AO_8BAD1B_SAVED_COLUMN` is not null, so a missing `type` is not stored: the request fails in Active Objects. The exact reply is not determinable from the plugin; expect a server failure.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}`: the 200 reply is the new `saved-column` with `composedId` `stored/<new id>` and `listId` `stored/<list key>`; `params` is null for empty parameters and `editable` follows stored-column-source. A missing `parameters` is stored as `{}` and a missing `description` as null.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}`: after a successful create it adds 1 to statistics counters `savedColumns.create` and `savedColumns.create.<listKey>` through statistics-manager, asynchronously. Failures count nothing.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}`: `description` and `parameters` missing from the body are cleared (null and `{}`), and `name` and `type` are overwritten with the body's values; the owner stays. The order is: unknown source, name rules, then stored-column-source's checks. On the bundled source a valid body answers 500 text/plain.

`DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}`: a missing column, or another user's, answers 400 text/plain with `s.w.saved-column.error.column-not-found.delete` (`Cannot delete saved column because it does not exist`). Every other `StructureException`, including an unknown source and a global column without the permission, answers 500 text/plain with its localized message. A bundled source answers 500 by the exception mapper. After success, statistics counter `savedColumns.delete` gains 1.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/edit`: the column is read first as the caller; null means 400 text/plain `s.w.saved-column.error.not-found.edit` (`Unable to edit the saved column because it has been deleted`). A body without `name` and `description` writes the same values back and answers 200. An empty `description` clears the text to empty; `type` and `parameters` in the body are ignored.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/edit`: a non-null `name` follows the name rules of `POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{listKey}`: blank or over 190 characters answers 400 `Invalid request data`, otherwise it is stored trimmed.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/updateParameters`: the column is read first, with the same 400 as `.../edit` when null; then only the parameters are replaced, and a missing `parameters` stores `{}`. `name`, `description` and `type` in the body are ignored, also a blank `name`. An unknown source gives 400 `structure-error`, permission failures come from stored-column-source (403 `structure-error` for a global column).
`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/move/{newListKey}`: an unknown source answers 400 text/plain with `s.w.saved-column.error.not-found.edit`, not a `structure-error`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/move/{newListKey}`: on the stored source a refused move answers 400 text/plain with the error messages stored-column-source collected, joined by `. `. On the `bundled` source the move is refused with no message: 400 with an empty body.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/move/{newListKey}`: on success the column becomes global and statistics counter `savedColumns.moveTo.<newListKey>` gains 1. The body is not read, but a JSON content type is what lets the request through the platform's XSRF check.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}`, `POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/edit` and `POST /rest/structure/2.0/saved-column/{columnSource}/{id}/updateParameters`: a body that reaches the resource as null fails with a null dereference after the source check (for the last two also after the column read): 500 text/plain, nothing changed.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: the work runs as a job on the executor named `user`, under structure-async-request-handler's protocol. With a `jobId` in the body, `actionGroups` and `syncModuleKeys` are ignored. A null body fails with a null dereference: 500 text/plain.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: lists are paired from the end: the last group with the last key, and so on backwards. With lists of different length, pairing stops at the shorter list, so leading entries of the longer one are skipped without a result.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: `syncModuleKeys` of the reply is the request's list in its original order, while `actionGroups` is in processing order (last input group first), so the two lists run in opposite order; `jobId` is absent. A null `actionGroups` or `syncModuleKeys` fails the job with a null dereference: 500 text/plain.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: for a synchronizer that implements `UndoingSynchronizer`, each element of the group's JSON array is passed as a `MapObject`, in array order, to `undo`, and the reply's group is `[` + the returned objects' JSON joined by `,` + `]`. An empty array still calls `undo` with no actions.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: a key that resolves to no synchronizer, or to one that does not implement `UndoingSynchronizer`, yields for that group a one-element array with `syncModuleKey` = the key, `result` = `failure` and `reason` = `synchronizer is not an UndoingSynchronizer ` (trailing space included). Other groups go on, and the audit log records nothing for it.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: a group whose text is not a JSON array of objects yields a one-element array with `syncModuleKey`, `result` = `failure` and `exception` (with `message` when there is one, `class`, `stackTrace`, and `cause` when there is one). `undo` is not called and other groups go on.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: when `undo` throws an `Exception`, the group's result is a one-element array with `sync` = the synchronizer descriptor's label, `result` = `failure` and `exception`; it does not fail the request, and that failure action is what the audit log receives.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo`: each group handed to a synchronizer is recorded through sync-audit-log with instance id 0, structure id 0, the synchronizer's complete module key, the description `{"action": "undo", "loggedInUserKey": <caller key, empty text when none>}` and the resulting actions.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/share-with`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/projects`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/agile-boards` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/versions` have no anonymous marker, so an anonymous call gets the platform's 401. If the resource is reached with no authenticated user (the helper says so), it answers 403 with no body and searches nothing.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/share-with`: `groups` holds, in this order and only when they match: the private group, roles (rest-subjects-searcher's project-role search), groups (its group search). `query` is null in the reply.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/share-with`: the private group has no `label` and no `footer` and one item: `value` and `id` `private.nobody`, `label` the text of `s.tpl.step.general.share.private` (`Nobody`), no `title`. It matches like any other candidate on that text, so query `nob` returns it and query `xyz` does not; `maxResults` does not affect it.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/projects`: the single group, if any, is rest-subjects-searcher's project search with `query` and `maxResults` as given; there is no group when nothing matches, and the reply is then `{"groups": []}` with `query` null.
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/agile-boards`: the single group, if any, is rest-subjects-searcher's board search. Without Jira Software the reply is 200 with no groups.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/versions`: `projectIds` is split on `,`; blank entries are skipped; duplicates count once. An entry that is not exactly a decimal long, including one with surrounding spaces such as ` 5`, gives 400 `Invalid request data`. An unknown project id yields no versions. Authentication is checked before parsing. With no ids the reply has no groups.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/versions`: the count that switches on full-name matching is the number of distinct ids given, so one project named twice counts as one, and two ids of which one is unknown count as two.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/{id}`: the system-administrator gate comes first (403 `permission violation`). Then id 0 or negative answers 400 with no body, without reading the request's `jobId` and without starting a job.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/{id}`: a request without `jobId` starts a job on the executor named `attribute`, under structure-async-request-handler's protocol. With a `jobId` the path id is not used for anything but the positive check. A null body fails with a null dereference: 500 text/plain.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/{id}`: the counted forest is the latest forest of `ForestSpec.skeleton(<id>)`: the stored forest with generators not run, so generator rows count and generated rows do not. The project of each row is asked of the attribute service with `CoreAttributeSpecs.PROJECT` for that same spec.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/{id}`: each row counts in the first category that fits: issue, generator, effector, folder, memo, Confluence page (item type `com.almworks.structure.pages:type-confluence-page` with a long id); any other row counts only in `size`. A generator row also counts in exactly one of `inserters`, `extenders`, `groupers`, `filters`, `sorters` according to its kind, or in none when its kind is none of these or it cannot be resolved. `id` is the path id and `size` the forest's row count.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/{id}`: `projects` has one name per distinct project key among the rows' project values, whatever the row's kind; rows without a project add nothing. Two projects with the same name appear twice. Names are sorted with a `java.text.Collator` for the helper's locale. An empty forest gives `size` 0 and `projects` `[]`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/projects`: for a Jira administrator it answers with `enabledForAllProjects` = structure-configuration's `isEnabledForAllProjects()` and `pickedProjectIds` = the ids of its `getPickedProjectIds()` in stored order, whatever the flag says. Nothing is written.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/projects`: a null body, or a body with both `enabledForAllProjects` and `pickedProjectIds` absent, answers 400 text/plain `empty request` and changes nothing. An empty `pickedProjectIds` array is a value, not an absence: it clears the picked list and answers `{"empty": true}`.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/projects`: the flag is written first (`setEnabledForAllProjects`), then the ids are checked in array order and the first bad one stops the call: a null id gives 400 text/plain `project ID is null`, an id for which Jira `ProjectManager.getProjectObj` returns null gives 400 text/plain `project <id> does not exist`. So a request with a valid flag and a bad id keeps the flag change and leaves the picked list unchanged. Valid ids are stored with `setPickedProjectIds` in first-seen order with duplicates removed.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/projects/add`: a missing or empty array answers 400 text/plain `empty request`. Ids are checked as for the PUT (same messages, first bad id stops the call, nothing stored). New ids are appended after the current picked ids, keeping their order; `setPickedProjectIds` is called only when at least one id was new, and the answer is `{"updated": true}`, otherwise `{"updated": false}`. The all-projects flag is not touched.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/projects/remove`: a missing or empty array answers 400 text/plain `empty request`; a null id answers 400 `project ID is null`; ids of projects that no longer exist are accepted, so stale ids can be removed. `setPickedProjectIds` is called with the remaining ids in their old order only when something was removed; the answer is `{"updated": true}` or `{"updated": false}`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions`: answers one entry per permission of `CoreAppPermissions.ALL`, in that order, each with structure-configuration's `isAllowedForAnyone` and `getPermissionSubjects` (subjects in stored order; each written with only the id fields of its type; an `anyone` subject has only `subject`).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}`: an unknown key (matched exactly, case-sensitive, through `CoreAppPermissions.byKey`) answers 400 text/plain `invalid permission, valid permissions: [use, createStructure, synchronization, automation, configureGenerators, configureEffectors, executeEffectors, executeEffectorsOnQueries, manageGlobalSavedColumns]`. A known key answers the same object as that key's entry in the full list.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions`: a missing or empty object answers 400 text/plain `empty request`. Entries are validated in the JSON object's order and the first failure answers its 400 with nothing stored. Only after every entry passed are the changes applied, in entry order, for each entry first `setAllowedForAnyone` (when given) and then `setPermissionSubjects` (when given). Success answers `{"empty": true}`.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}`: the key is checked first (400 `invalid permission, ...` as for the GET), then the body: a null body or one with both `allowedForAnyone` and `subjects` absent answers 400 text/plain `empty request for permission '<key>'`; the same message applies to a null or empty entry of the bulk PUT. An empty `subjects` array is a value: it clears the list. `allowedForAnyone` false is a value too. Validation finishes before anything is written; success answers `{"empty": true}`.

Subject checks of `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions`, `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}` and `POST /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}/add`, in array order, first failure wins, each 400 text/plain: a null subject gives `null subject for permission '<key>'`; otherwise `invalid subject for permission '<key>': <reason>`, where reason is `Cannot parse rule: expected subject`, `Cannot parse rule: expected groupId` (type group), `Cannot parse rule: expected projectId` then `...expected roleId` (type projectRole; a missing `projectId` fails, 0 must be sent explicitly), `Cannot parse rule: expected userKey` (type user), `Unknown subject. Known values for subject: group,projectRole,user,anyone`, `group '<name>' does not exist` (Jira `UserManager.getGroup` null), `only groups and project roles are allowed` (well-formed `user` or `anyone`), `role <id> does not exist` (`ProjectRoleManager.getProjectRole`), `project <id> does not exist` (non-zero `projectId`, `ProjectManager.getProjectObj` null; role is checked before project).

In the bodies of `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions` and its add and remove calls, the `subject` type is recognised ignoring case (`GROUP`, `projectrole`), and fields not belonging to the type are ignored. Subjects are written back in canonical form.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}/add`: the body is checked first (missing or empty array: 400 `empty request`), then the key, then the subjects. New subjects are appended to the current list, equal ones ignored (within the body too); `setPermissionSubjects` is called only when the list grew. Answer: `{"updated": true}` or `{"updated": false}`. `allowedForAnyone` is not touched.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/configuration/permissions/{key}/remove`: same order of checks as add (body, key, subjects). Subjects only have to be well-formed (same `null subject` and `invalid subject` messages for parse failures); any of the four types is accepted and groups, roles and projects are not looked up, so entries of deleted groups can be removed. `setPermissionSubjects` is called only when something was removed. Answer: `{"updated": true}` or `{"updated": false}`.

Every `/rest/structure/2.0/configuration/...` call goes through the common gate's administrator check before the method runs (403 `permission violation` for a logged-in non-administrator, body not read), with no websudo requirement and no `use` permission needed beyond that check.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker`: the text is matched literally and ignoring case (Unicode-aware), trimmed first. With `query` null or empty nothing is filtered; a query of spaces only is treated by the local filter as an empty pattern and also keeps everything (except that users are still searched with the raw text).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker` user group: asks Jira `UserSearchService.findUsers(context, query, params)` with the raw `query`, empty query allowed, inactive users included, e-mail matching on and a maximum of limit + 1 results; then keeps users whose username, display name or email contains the trimmed text (a null email does not match) and cuts to limit. A user Jira does not return is never shown, even if it would match as a substring. `footer` is set when more users remained than were shown.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker`: emails are shown when `UserSearchService.canShowEmailAddresses` says so for the caller; the user html is built from `<display name> - <email> (<username>)` then, otherwise from `<display name> (<username>)`. `label` is always the display name.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker` group group: there is no switch to turn it off. Logged in: `StructurePluginHelper.getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser()`. Anonymous: every group of Jira `GroupManager.getAllGroups()` when `GlobalPermissionManager` grants USER_PICKER to null, else none. Filtered by name, sorted by case-sensitive plain string order of the name, cut to limit.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker` role group: left out when `noRoles` is true or the caller is anonymous; otherwise `StructurePluginHelper.getAvailableRoles()` filtered by name, sorted by case-sensitive plain string order of the name, cut to limit.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker` item `html`: only the first match in the text is wrapped, and everything is HTML-escaped: `` + escaped text before + `` + escaped match + `` + escaped rest + ``. With an empty query the empty pattern matches at position 0, so html is `Name`. `title`, `entity` and `icon` are null and `id` equals `value`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker` labels and footer: `sw.column.worklogged.select.users.label` (`Users`), `sw.column.worklogged.select.groups.label` (`Groups`), `sw.column.worklogged.select.roles.label` (`Project roles`), and for all three the footer `s.w.user-picker.more` (`There are more results. Try refining search.`), set when the filtered count exceeds the shown count. A group with no items is left out entirely.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker/project-role/{key}`: a key that parses as a long asks Jira `ProjectRoleManager.getProjectRole(long)` only (a role whose name is numeric cannot be found by name); any other key, including a number too big for a long, asks `getProjectRole(String)`. A null answer gives 400 with the `Invalid request data` error object and message `No project role for id or name`. No permission beyond the common gate is checked; anonymous callers who pass the gate may look up roles.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker/users`: Browse Users (Jira global USER_PICKER for the current user, null when anonymous) is checked first, so without it even an empty `keys` answers 403 with no body. An empty or absent `keys` answers `[]`; a blank-only one too.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/author-picker/users`: `keys` is split on commas without trimming; blank pieces are skipped; a repeated key gives a repeated entry. Each key is resolved as given. For a known user the avatar URL carries the key unencoded and one `ts` shared by the whole reply; the inactive name form is `s.ext.it.user.summary.inactive` (`{0} (Inactive)`) in the caller's locale. An unknown key's avatar URL is `<base url>/secure/useravatar?avatarId=<Jira anonymous avatar id>`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/list`: `spec` is parsed as JSON into the option source description; asks option-source-service for a source for the current user with its normal security checks and no collection caching. Answers all options sorted by the source's order; each option's `value` is the id's string form, `group` the source's group message key (untranslated), `icon` its icon, `html` null. No limit applies.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/list`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/search` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/suggestions`: `spec` absent, empty, invalid JSON, JSON of the wrong type, or with properties other than `sourceKey`, `projectId` and `filters` (parse failure, logged as a warning), and a source that is missing or not selectable, all answer 200 `{"empty": true}`, not an array.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/search` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/suggestions`: N is the smaller of the source's threshold (dark feature `structure.options.search.threshold`, default 50) and the page size (dark feature `structure.options.portion.size`, default 10).

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/search`: `query` null or blank (spaces too) gives the suggestions answer with no ids, so `html` is null. Otherwise, for the user source, `UserSearchService`-backed search gets the raw query and N; for other sources every option whose label contains the trimmed text, literally and ignoring case, is taken. Results are sorted in the source's order and then cut to N, with `html` = `` + escaped label with the first match in `` + ``. A user the search returns whose label lacks the text still appears, with html having no match span.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/suggestions`: takes the source's suggestions first; if there are fewer than N and the source is not users, adds all its options; removes duplicate ids keeping the first; cuts to N. Then adds, beyond N, each `ids` entry not already there for which the source's lookup by id finds an option (unknown or invalid ids are dropped). The whole list is sorted in the source's order, `html` null.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/options-picker/suggestions`: `ids` is parsed as a JSON array; absent, empty, invalid JSON or not an array means none. Each element is compared as a string: a number by its text, a nested array or list by its first element, and null elements (or empty lists) are skipped.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/projects-picker`: 'all' is Jira `ProjectService.getAllProjectsForAction(user, VIEW_PROJECT)` (an invalid outcome means none); 'recent' is `UserProjectHistoryManager.getProjectHistoryWithPermissionChecks(VIEW_PROJECT, user)`. Both keep projects for which structure-configuration's `isProjectEnabled` holds and whose name or key contains the trimmed `query` literally ignoring case, sorted by name with the caller's collator. Blank `query` keeps all enabled ones.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/projects-picker` limit L: with `applyLimit` false, the number of matching 'all' projects; else `maxResults` capped at 20, 20 when missing or not positive. The recent group, present when recent matches exist, shows up to L. The all group has its limit reduced by the full number of matching recent projects, not the number shown; recent projects are removed from it by id. Example: L = 5 with 7 recent matches gives only a recent group with 5 items and footer 5 of 7.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/projects-picker` texts: group labels `s.manage.edit.select.projects.recent.label` (`Recent Projects`) and `s.manage.edit.select.projects.all.label` (`All Projects`), footer `s.manage.edit.select.projects.footer` (`Showing {0} of {1} matching projects`) with shown and matching counts. An item's html is the text of `s.manage.edit.select.projects.html` (`{0} ({1})`), escaped, with the first match over that whole text in `<b>`; a blank query gives no `<b>`. `icon` is Jira `AvatarService.getProjectAvatarURL(project, SMALL)`; `title` and `entity` are null.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/group-picker`: the groups are `StructurePluginHelper.getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser()`. The trimmed `query` matches as a literal substring ignoring case. With a non-blank query the matches are ordered by name length, shortest first, ties in the order of that list; with a blank query the list's order is kept, nothing sorted, and html is only the escaped name.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/group-picker`: the instance limit is dark feature `structure.create.namesSearch.resultLimit` (20 when unset, zero or negative), read once when the searching component is created. `maxResults` lowers it only when positive and below it. When more match than the limit, `footer` is `s.manage.edit.select.groups.footer` (`Showing {0} of {1} matching groups`); otherwise there is no footer. The group label is `s.manage.edit.select.groups.label`. Nothing matching gives `groups` empty.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/group-picker`: the resource has no anonymous marker, so the platform refuses an anonymous call with 401 before the method runs. The method's own check, for the case it is reached with no user (`StructurePluginHelper.isAuthenticated()` false), answers 403 with no body.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/label-picker`: without `customFieldId` it answers Jira `LabelManager.getSuggestedLabels(user, null, query)`; with it, `getSuggestedLabels(user, null, customFieldId, query)`. The user is the current `StructureAuth` user, the issue id always null, `query` passed unchanged (null when omitted), and Jira's order is kept. The id's field is not checked to be a labels field.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field`: lists field-value-options' supported fields, sorted with Jira's `Field` natural order (by name). `id` is the field id; `label` is the translation of the field's name key when `I18nHelper.isKeyDefined` says it is defined, else `getName()`.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field/options`: a blank `fieldId` (missing or spaces) answers 400 text/plain `fieldId should not be blank`. A null `query` becomes empty; a null, zero or negative `limit` means no limit. The rest is field-value-options' search, wrapped as `{"groups": [...]}`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field/options`: a blank `fieldId`, or a null or empty `fieldValues`, answers 400 text/plain `fieldId or fieldValues should not be blank`. A JSON `null` body is not checked and ends as the mapper's 500. The rest is field-value-options' id resolution.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`: keys come from Jira `ApplicationProperties.getStringsWithPrefix` for each of the four prefixes plus `System.getProperties()` names with that prefix; protected keys are dropped; a failure reading application properties (logged) or their absence leaves the JVM keys. Sorted by plain string order, no duplicates. A key stored with an empty value counts as unset: its `value` falls to the JVM property (or null) and `removable` is false.

Protected keys for `GET /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` and its POST, PUT and DELETE: full match of `com.almworks.structure` + optional `.<letters, digits, _, +, ->` + `.license` + optional `.<anything>`; full match of `com.almworks.atlas-yourkit` + optional `.<anything>`; keys starting with `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.`; keys ending in `:build`. So `com.almworks.structure.license` and `com.almworks.structure.foo.license.x` are protected and `com.almworks.structure.foo.bar.license` is not.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`, `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` and `DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` check the key the same way, untrimmed and case-sensitive: blank or null answers 400 text/plain `str.admin.dark.error.empty` (`Please enter a valid key.`); a wrong prefix or a protected key answers 400 text/plain `str.admin.dark.error.wrong.prefix` (`Please enter a valid key for the <product> suite.`). A key with leading spaces therefore fails on prefix.
`POST /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`: for a valid key answers its state as in the list, also when the key is set nowhere (`value` null, `removable` false). Nothing is stored.

`PUT /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`: a null body answers 400 with no message. A valid key goes to Jira `ApplicationProperties.setString(key, value)` as sent, including a null or empty value; an empty value then behaves as unset. Failures, and application properties being unavailable, are logged and the call still answers 204. The JVM system properties are never changed.

`DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`: a valid key gets `ApplicationProperties.setString(key, null)` with write failures only logged, then the answer is the current JVM system property of that key as text/plain with 200, or 204 with no body when there is none.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` and its POST, PUT and DELETE are the only resource marked both administrator-only and websudo-required at resource level: a logged-in non-administrator gets 403 `permission violation` from the common gate; no websudo session gets the platform's own refusal. Which of the two comes first for a non-administrator without websudo depends on the platform and is not determined here.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/date/validate`: the text is parsed by Jira's `DateTimeFormatter` for the logged-in user (`forLoggedInUser()`) with style `DATE_PICKER`; on success `isValid` true, `resultDate` the same date formatted with style `ISO_8601_DATE`, `error` null. An `IllegalArgumentException` from the parser gives 200 with `isValid` false, `resultDate` null and `error` its localized message. Empty text is parsed like any other and fails that way.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/date/validate`: only `IllegalArgumentException` is turned into `isValid` false; any other exception from Jira's parser reaches the mapper as a 500. A missing `date` passes null to the parser, so its answer is whatever Jira does with null.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/calendar/list`: walks extension-service's calendar providers: the built-in provider first (simple-calendar-provider), then the others by plain string order of module key. Each provider's calendars come in the provider's order, with `id` = `<provider complete module key>/<calendar id>`, and `name` and `description` as the calendar reports them. There is no anonymous access; `use` is checked by the gate.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/automation`: lists extension-service's generator and effector descriptors in the descriptors' order. A module is left out when its descriptor's module cannot be resolved, resolves to the wrong type, or its `isAvailable()` is false. Generators and effectors are not sorted. `generatorConfigurationAllowed` and `effectorConfigurationAllowed` are `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed` for `CoreAppPermissions.CONFIGURE_GENERATORS` and `CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS` with the `StructureAuth` user.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/automation` generator entry: `type` is the first of `StructureGenerator.Inserter`, `.Grouper`, `.Extender`, `.Sorter`, `.Filter` the module implements; a module implementing none fails the whole call with an `IllegalArgumentException`, so 400 `Invalid request data`. `notConfigurable` is true when the module's class carries `NotConfigurable`. `label` null becomes empty. `presets` is absent unless the module is a `ConfigurableGenerator` returning non-null presets. `module` is the complete key and `group` the descriptor's group.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/automation` presets: each preset has `label` (null becomes empty), `description`, and `params` as a JSON-encoded string of its parameters. When dark feature `structure.generator.defaults.disableUpdates` is true (read per call), `disableActions: true` is added to every preset's parameters; a preset that already has that key then fails the call, as a map with a duplicate key cannot be built (as the original does).
`GET /rest/structure/2.0/automation` effector entry: `module` complete key; `label`, `icon` (icon span class) and `title` (dialog title) from the descriptor, each null replaced by empty.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/accounts`, `GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/teams` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/roles`: blank or missing `ids` means no restriction; otherwise it is split on commas without trimming, and `1, 2` keeps the space. Teams and roles parse each piece as an integer, so a space or a non-number empties the result with `total` 0.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/accounts`: passes `query` and `limit` unchanged (null when omitted) to tempo-integration's account search, whose rules apply, including that archived accounts are left out unless dark feature `structure.tempo.showArchivedAccounts` is true. `status` is the localized text of the account's status (`s.tempo.accounts.status.open`, `.closed`, `.archived`). Pieces of `ids` go into Tempo's query as strings, unchecked. Absent Tempo Accounts or a failure gives `options` empty and `total` 0, status 200.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/teams` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/roles`: a negative `limit` with at least one match fails inside the search and answers `options` empty and `total` 0 (as the original does); the limit rules of tempo-integration otherwise apply.

`GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/teams` and `GET /rest/structure/2.0/tempo/roles` answer tempo-integration's team and role searches as `{"options": [...], "total": n}`, each option with only `id` and `name`, 200 even when Tempo Teams is absent.

The resources of `rest-cfd` have no common access gate, no `use` check and no exception mapper: `POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta`, `GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/status`, `GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate` and `POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd` all accept anonymous callers. `loggedIn=true` in the query has no effect here.

`POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta`: answers cfd-meta-maker's result with status 200 whatever validation finds, and sets no `Cache-Control` of its own. A JSON `null` body or unparseable JSON gets the platform's generic error.
`GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/status`: answers `{"enabled": <bool>}` from cfd-meta-maker for any caller, with no `Cache-Control` of its own.

`GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate`: runs the same checks as `POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta`. Each of the four attribute spec parameters is parsed as JSON into an attribute spec; absent, empty or unparseable text (logged as a warning) counts as absent. So a garbled `teamAttributeSpec` gives the field error `teamAttributeSpec`, and a garbled `whenAppearedAttributeSpec` gives no error at all. `adjustments` cannot be sent.

`GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate`: with no errors answers 200 `{"empty": true}`; with any, 400 and the `validation-errors` object as JSON. With the feature off that object has one general message and no field errors. Both carry `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`.

`POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd`: answers cfd-simulator's result as JSON with status 200 and no `Cache-Control` of its own. All its refusals (feature off, missing input) reach the caller as the platform's generic error, since the checked errors it raises are not web exceptions and nothing maps them.

Every page in this group first asks `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureLocked()`. When it answers true, the page does nothing else and shows the 'not ready' page, titled `str.+stopped+.title` ("<product> Isn't Ready") with `str.+stopped+.description.html`. The same page results when the work fails with a `StructureStoppedException` as the root cause (the error message then is `<product> plugin is not ready`). This holds for `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa`, `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa` and all others; the only exception is that `StructureHelp` commands check for an administrator before the lock (see their claims).

The 'not permitted' page has the title `s.structure.op.disabled` ('Operation Not Permitted') and the text `str.+disabled+.description.html`; it is what a page's 'disabled' outcome shows. A 'security breach' outcome shows Jira's standard security-breach page (`/secure/views/securitybreach.jsp`).

A page's 'error' outcome shows a page titled `common.words.error` that lists the action's error messages (one each, HTML-escaped) under the note `str.error.description.html`. It adds a Back link to the action's return URL when one is set, and a login link to `/login.jsp?os_destination=<this page's URL, encoded>` when the user is anonymous. Field errors are not listed on it.
A `StructureException` that escapes a page's work (one the page does not handle itself) gives the error page with the exception's localized message.

Changes are made only through the `!apply` command of a page (`/secure/DeleteStructure!apply.jspa`, `/secure/StructureArchive!apply.jspa`, `/secure/EditStructure!apply.jspa`, `/secure/StructureCopy!apply.jspa`, `/secure/StructureViews!apply.jspa`, `/secure/StructureImport!apply.jspa`, `/secure/StructureExport!apply.jspa`, `/secure/CreateStructure!apply.jspa`), which runs Jira's XSRF check on `atl_token`. A request that asks for the change without `!apply` (plain alias, or `!default`, which behaves like the plain alias except that it skips validation) gets the security-breach page and changes nothing.

In this group a boolean request parameter is true only when its single value equals `true`, ignoring case; a missing or other value is false. Pages `DeleteStructure`, `StructureArchive`, `StructureViews`, `StructureCopy`, `StructureImport` and `StructureExport` decide between 'show the form' and 'do it' by the parameter `execute`; `EditStructure` uses `confirm`.
A numeric request parameter read with a default (for example `default-<page>-view`, `targetProject`, `stepId`) that is missing or not a number counts as 0.

A page's fixed redirect target is only a default: when the request has Jira's `returnUrl` parameter, that value is used instead. In Jira inline-dialog mode (`inline=true`) a finished page does not redirect: it answers 200 with header `X-Atlassian-Dialog-Control` set to `DONE` for 'finished' answers, or `redirect:<context path + URL>` for 'finished with a redirect' answers. Outside a dialog both are ordinary redirects to the URL.
The default return URL of the pages for a selected structure is `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?view=recent`.

`DeleteStructure`, `StructureArchive`, `StructureViews` (with a structure), `StructureImport` and `StructureExport` take the structure id from parameter `id`. A missing, zero or negative id redirects to the default return URL. Otherwise the structure is read with `StructureManager.getStructure(id, ADMIN)`. If that fails: a non-administrator who can still view the structure gets the error page with `s.manage.edit.noaccess` ('You don't have Control permissions on structure <id>'); everyone else, a Jira administrator included, gets `s.manage.edit.notfound` ('Structure with id <id> does not exist or you don't have permissions to view it.').

Where these pages show a user, the text is the user name, followed by ` (<display name>) ` when the display name is not empty and differs from it, HTML-escaped. A user that the viewer may not see is shown as `s.manage.user.someone` ('someone'); a viewer may see a user who is themselves, or when they are a Jira administrator or have the global `USER_PICKER` permission. A null user or empty name shows nothing.

A permission subject is shown as: `s.permissions.subject.anyone` for `Anyone`; `s.permissions.subject.user` with the user's name for `JiraUser`; `s.permissions.subject.group` with the group name for `JiraGroup`; `s.permissions.subject.role.anyproj` with the role name when a `ProjectRole` has project id 0, else `s.permissions.subject.role` with project and role names, `?` standing for an unknown project or role. Names are HTML-escaped. A null subject shows nothing, and any other subject shows `?`.

`/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` accepts GET only. When `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` is false, a logged-in user gets the 'not permitted' page and an anonymous user the security-breach page. Otherwise the page is shown, also to anonymous users.

When it shows the board, `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` asks `StructurePluginHelper` to include the widget's web resources and the issue keyboard shortcuts (`requireWidgetResource()`, `requireIssueShortcuts()`).

Parameter `view` of `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` is a saved view id. It is passed to the page as the initial view only when `StructureViewManager.isAccessible(view, VIEW)` is true; an inaccessible or unknown view is ignored silently and the board still opens.

`/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` presents as current structure the answer of recents-manager's 'most recent accessible structure' for the current user, or none. Parameter `s` and the URL fragment are not read on the server; the page's script handles them.

`/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` tells the page whether a newly created issue is added to the open structure: the dark feature `structure.feature.createIssueAddsToBoardStructure`, default true, read when the page object is created.

`/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` and `/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa` present Jira's issue operation links: for each section Jira returns for location `opsbar-operations` for the current user, all links of that section, ignoring their conditions, computed with context parameter `issueId` = the literal `{0}` (a placeholder the page fills in).

`/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` accepts GET and POST. Its parameters are `forestSpec` (JSON of a `forest-spec`), `viewId` (number, default 0), `viewSpec` (JSON view specification), `expand` (the board's expansion state) and `clientFilter` (the board's quick-filter state). No XSRF token is needed and nothing is changed except the usage statistic below.

`/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` gives the security-breach page when `isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` is false. A missing or unreadable `forestSpec` gives the error page with `s.error.forest.inaccessible` ('The requested structure is not accessible, sorry!').

When preparing the export fails with a `StructureException`, `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` shows the error page with `s.printable.error.config`: 'Printable page could not be displayed (error code: <numeric error code>, <localized message>)'.

After a successful preparation `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` records the unique-user statistic `activeUser` (asynchronously) and requires web resource `com.almworks.jira.structure:printable-rc` and resource context `structure.printable`. Its `<head>` carries the rendered required resources directly, and the page has no Jira decorator.

`/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` presents: as title `ForestService.getDisplayName(spec)`; as icon the absolute URL of `structure-icon.png` of `com.almworks.jira.structure:printable-rc`; the Jira version; and the indent per depth, from 0 to the deepest row's depth, as `<depth × 3>.5em` (depth 0 is `0.5em`, depth 2 is `6.5em`).

The columns of `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` come from the saved view `viewId` when it is not 0 and accessible at `VIEW`, and a missing or inaccessible `viewId` goes straight to the default view without trying `viewSpec`; with no `viewId`, from `viewSpec` when it is not empty and readable; else from a default view of the `issuekey` field column followed by the main column. An inaccessible view or a bad `viewSpec` falls through silently.

Columns with key `handle` or `actions` are never printed. In view column display mode 2, pinned columns come first in pin order and the others follow in view order; in any other mode columns keep view order.

For each column of the printable page, export renderer providers are asked in this order, and the first set that gives a renderer wins: (column key, `printable`), (column key, any format), (any key, `printable`), (any key, any format). A column with no renderer, or whose provider fails with `StructureProviderException`, is left out (a warning is logged). A provider that throws anything else is ignored for the rest of the export. A renderer that throws while preparing is dropped, one that throws later prints nothing from then on, and the page itself still succeeds.

`clientFilter` of `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` is a sign followed by a dot-separated list of delta-encoded row ids (each number is added to the previous one). Sign `+` keeps only those rows, `-` removes them. `+` alone keeps no row, `-` alone or an empty value filters nothing. A value with another first character, or an unparsable number, is ignored with a warning, so nothing is filtered. Example: `+5.2.3` keeps rows 5, 7 and 10.

`expand` of `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` is a dot-separated list: a number sets the default expanded depth (not below the minimum level, which is 1 when the forest spec has a title row, else 0), `++` expands everything, `--` sets the minimum level, `+<row>` and `-<row>` expand or collapse a row. A row counts as expanded when the default level exceeds its depth, unless it is listed the other way. Empty means all expanded. Malformed items are skipped.

`/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` prints the forest rows in order, after removing rows rejected by the client filter, automation rows (generators and effectors) and rows that no longer exist. A collapsed row is printed but its subtree is skipped. At most the first 20000 rows after filtering are used; the rest are dropped silently. Rows the user may not see stay in place, but every attribute value of such a row is null.

If reading the forest times out on its lock, the printable page keeps retrying. After 120 s of accumulated waiting (dark feature `structure.export.trySnapshotTimeout`) it uses the last generated forest if there is one, and warns with `s.export.forest-outdated`. After 600 s (dark feature `structure.export.forestLockTimeout`) it fails with error `AUTOMATION_FAILED` and message `s.export.error.forest-lock-timeout` for that many seconds, which shows as the configuration error page.

Attribute values for the printable page are first read consistently with the forest (dark feature `structure.export.tryConsistentAttributes`, default true). If that fails, they are read normally and the page shows `s.export.inconsistent` ('The exported information may be inconsistent due to concurrent changes in Jira or <product> during the export.'). Columns whose parameter `forestSpec` is `unfiltered` read their values from the forest spec without its trailing filter and sort transformations.

On the printable page a number cell is formatted in the export context's locale with no grouping; with a rounding of N decimals set on the column it shows exactly N decimals, rounded half up. `setRounding` with a negative value throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Null shows an empty cell.

A percentage cell with style `PERCENT_TEXT` shows the value as locale percent text. With any other style it shows a bar plus percent text, both with the value clamped to 0..1, the bar's length being value × 10 em. Null shows an empty cell.

On the printable page a date cell uses Jira's user `DATE` style and a date-time cell Jira's user `COMPLETE` style. A duration (seconds) is formatted by format-helper for the current user, or as calendar time when the column asks for that. Null shows an empty cell.

A hyperlink cell with a null URL is empty. With a URL that `java.net.URL` rejects, it shows the text only. Otherwise it is a link to the URL with the text, or the URL when the text is null. Text and URL are HTML-escaped. `setText` escapes and `setHtml` does not.

Each printed data row has the CSS class `d<depth>`, plus any row classes its cells added, in order and without repeats. A cell's content is wrapped so that it does not break lines unless its column is multiline.

`/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` accepts GET only and reads `structureId`, `rowId`, `issueId` and `jobId` (numbers, default 0). It returns a fragment, with no Jira decorator, for the issue page.

Without `jobId`, `/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` runs the calculation as a job on job-manager's `attribute` executor and waits for it up to the REST async timeout (dark feature `structure.rest.async.timeout`, see structure-async-request-handler). With `jobId` it starts nothing and waits for that job. If the job finishes in time, the job is cancelled in job-manager and the data is shown. If not, the fragment carries only the job id, so the client can ask again.

`/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` answers an empty fragment (job id 0, no data) when the job cannot be submitted (the job id then stays 0), when `jobId` is unknown, when the job failed, or when the job's result is of another type. An interrupted wait leaves the job id in place and restores the thread's interrupt flag. None of these is an error page.

The calculation of `/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` gives empty data when `structureId` <= 0, `rowId` < 0, both `rowId` and `issueId` are 0, or Jira's option `jira.option.timetracking` is off. These are checked before access. When `StructureManager.isAccessible(structureId, VIEW)` is false, it gives the security-breach page.

With `rowId` not 0, `/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` takes the issue from that row (an existing row whose item is an issue, else empty data) and ignores `issueId`. With `rowId` 0 it uses `issueId` and then finds the first row, in forest order of the unsecured structure, that holds the issue; no such row, or a forest error, gives empty data.

`/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` gives empty data when the issue does not exist, or when `StructurePluginHelper.getIssueError(issue, false, true)` reports a problem (no access, or Structure not enabled for the project).

`/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` reads `CoreAttributeSpecs.TOTAL_ORIGINAL_ESTIMATE`, `TOTAL_REMAINING_ESTIMATE` and `TOTAL_TIME_SPENT` for the row from the unsecured structure forest (null = 0), and divides each by 1000 (integer) to get seconds. When none of the three is above 0 it gives empty data. Otherwise it builds Jira's time-tracking graph (`Style.SHORT`) from an aggregate bean of those three values with sub-task count 0.

`/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` offers the 'log work' link (`/secure/CreateWorklog!default.jspa?id=<issue id>`) only when there is data, the user has the issue permission `WORK_ISSUE` (Jira legacy id 20) on the issue, and `IssueManager.isEditable(issue)` is true.

When the async backoff is overridden, the fragment of `/secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa` carries the list as comma-separated numbers. The JVM long property `structure.testing.rest.async.forceDelay` (ms, default 0) adds that delay before the calculation, after the access check.

`/secure/ViewStructureShortcuts.jspa` accepts GET only, is open to anyone (no <product> access check) and lists keyboard shortcuts as 8 groups of lines; each line is a label and one or more shortcuts. Group and line labels are the i18n keys `str.help.shortcuts.+<key>` (for example `str.help.shortcuts.+section.navigation`). Parameter `mac` (boolean, default false) selects the Mac keys. The title is `str.help.shortcuts.title`.

Group `section.good-to-know`, lines in order (PC keys; Mac in brackets): create = enter; editing = tab or mouse double-click; move-item = ctrl+arrows (ctrl+command+arrows); drag-anywhere = shift+mouse drag; pasteUnder = ctrl+shift+v (command+shift+v); search = ctrl+alt+/; hide-resolved = r,r; pin = ctrl+.; run-all-effectors = e,e.

Group `section.handling`, lines in order: switch-structure = s,s; automation = ~; single-grid = ctrl+alt+1; double-grid = ctrl+alt+2; grid-details = o; switch-panel = \; switch-view = v,v; add-column = ctrl+shift+| (Mac command+|); switch-to-query = ctrl+alt+'.
Group `section.navigation`, lines in order: up = up; down = down; expand = right; collapse = left; expand-all = plus,plus; collapse-all = -,-; expand-level = alt+plus; collapse-level = alt+-.

Group `section.search`, lines in order: search-change-type = ctrl+alt+/; close-search = esc; toggle-filter = ctrl+alt+;; next-matching = ctrl+alt+]; prev-matching = ctrl+alt+[; focus-grid = enter; quick-transform = q,q; hide-resolved = r,r.

Group `section.changing`, lines in order (PC; Mac in brackets): moveup = ctrl+up (ctrl+command+up); movedown = ctrl+down (ctrl+command+down); indent = ctrl+right (ctrl+command+right); outdent = ctrl+left (ctrl+command+left); dnd = shift+mouse drag; remove = delete; cut = ctrl+x (command+x); copy = ctrl+c (command+c); paste = ctrl+v (command+v); pasteUnder = ctrl+shift+v (command+shift+v); undo = ctrl+z (command+z); redo = ctrl+shift+z (command+shift+z).

Group `section.edit`, lines in order: create = enter; createUnder = shift+enter, and on PC only also insert; createAbove = alt+enter; editing = tab or mouse double-click; edit.save = enter or ctrl+enter; edit.cancel = esc; edit.next = tab or ctrl+alt+right; edit.prev = ctrl+alt+left; edit.nextItem = ctrl+alt+down; edit.prevItem = ctrl+alt+up; edit.switchToDialog = alt+enter.

Group `section.select`, lines in order: select = space; select-all = ctrl+a (Mac command+a); select-subitems = shift+right; unselect-subitems = shift+left; select-down = shift+down; select-up = shift+up.
Group `section.jira`, lines in order: jira.operations = .; jira.edit = e; jira.assign = a; jira.comment = m; jira.labels = l; jira.dropdown = alt+down.

A shortcut text splits on `+` into modifiers and a final part; the final part splits on `,` into keys pressed one after the other (`r,r` is two presses of r, shown as separate keys). A key with the prefix `mouse:` is marked as a mouse action and shown without the prefix.

Key names are shown as follows, ignoring case. Both systems: up, down, left, right are the arrows `↑`, `↓`, `←`, `→` (these are marked as arrows); `plus` is `+`; `comma` is `,`. Mac: ctrl `⌃`, shift `⇧`, alt `⌥`, command `⌘`, del `delete`; other names stay as written. PC: del `Delete`, esc `Escape`; any other name of two or more letters or hyphens gets a capital first letter and lower case for the rest (`enter` is `Enter`, `double-click` is `Double-click`, `ctrl` is `Ctrl`); single characters stay as written.

`/secure/ManageStructure.jspa` accepts GET only. It gives the security-breach page when `isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` is false; otherwise it shows the page (also to anonymous users). The page content comes from the script, using REST; the server passes one JSON object to it. Parameter `view` (for example `view=recent`) is not read on the server.

The JSON object of `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa` has these keys: `addonLogos`, a map from plugin name to product icon URL, one entry per integration-details provider (later duplicates of a name overwrite earlier ones); `myUserKey`, the current user's key, left out for anonymous; `maySearchUsers`, whether the user has global `USER_PICKER`; `licensed`, always true; `mayApplyBasicAdminRights`, always true; `mayApplyAllAdminRights`, true for a logged-in user; `mayCreateNew`, `StructurePluginHelper.isCreateStructureAllowed(user)`; `mayManageSynchronizers` and `mayImExPort`, both `isSynchronizationAllowed(user)`; `showSynchronizers`, the answer of sync-hide-helper's 'enabled or installed' check.
In the JSON text of `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa` every `</` is written as `<\/`, so that it cannot end the script element.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` accepts GET and POST. It checks in this order: an anonymous user gets the outcome `login`, for which the page has no view, so Jira shows its error page rather than a login prompt (as the original does); `isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` false gives the security-breach page; then the structure is loaded.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` with `id` missing or 0 is the 'new structure' form. It needs `isCreateStructureAllowed(user)`, else the error page with `s.manage.create.noaccess` ('You don't have permissions to create new structures'). An unsaved structure owned by the current user is used, and nothing is stored until the form is applied.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` with `id` not 0, negative ids included, needs the `ADMIN` level. Failure gives `s.manage.edit.noaccess` or `s.manage.edit.notfound` as for the other selected-structure pages. Unlike them, a negative id is not redirected, it gives the not-found error. An archived structure is not refused by the page itself.
`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` uses request parameter `return` as its default return URL when present; else `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?view=recent`.

The form of `/secure/EditStructure.jspa` for an existing structure holds: `name`, `description`; `permissions`, a JSON array of `PermissionRule.toEncodedString()` strings; a JSON map of user key to display name (empty for a missing user) for every user in the `SetLevel` rules; `editRequiresParentPermission`, from `isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission()`; `favorite`, from `StructureFavoriteManager.isFavorite`; `generationTimeLimit` of the structure; `allowManualAdjustments`, whether adjustments are on for the structure; `descriptionShown`, structure property `showDescription` parsed as boolean (default false).

The 'new structure' form of `/secure/EditStructure.jspa` starts with `favorite` true, the global generation time limit, `allowManualAdjustments` from the default for new structures, and `descriptionShown` false.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` also presents: the generation time limit's minimum (5 s) and hard limit; whether the manual-adjustment feature is on; the levels `VIEW`, `EDIT`, `AUTOMATE`, `ADMIN` in that order with names `s.permission.level.<serial>`; the user's projects (`getProjectsForCurrentUser()`), the available roles, and whether the user may pick users (global `USER_PICKER`); for a saved structure, the number of synchronizers installed on it.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` reads `justCopied`, `justCloned`, `syncCopyError` (booleans) and `issueCloneErrors` (number) only to show a notice after a copy: `s.manage.edit.justcopied` or `s.manage.edit.justcloned`, a synchronizer message (`s.manage.edit.copied.synchronizers.error` or `s.manage.edit.copied.synchronizers`), and `s.manage.edit.copied.clone.error` with the count when it is above 0.

`/secure/EditStructure.jspa` offers for 'apply structure' rules the structures the user can administer (`getAllStructures(ADMIN)`). When editing a saved structure it leaves out every structure that reaches the edited one by following `PermissionRule.ApplyStructure` rules (or is that structure); a referenced structure that cannot be read is skipped in that walk.

The owner is editable on `/secure/EditStructure.jspa` when the user is a Jira administrator, or has global `USER_PICKER` and either has `ADMIN` on the structure or is its owner. The field shows the owner's user name, or `s.manage.user.someone` when the user may not see it.

`/secure/EditStructure!apply.jspa` with `confirm=true` updates the structure, in this order: XSRF check (failure: security breach); name validation; name, description, permission rules, parent-permission flag and owner are set; `saveChanges()`; favorite, generation time limit, manual adjustments and the `showDescription` property are stored; the structure is marked recent for the user. Without `confirm=true`, even on `!apply`, the form is shown and nothing changes.

The structure name is trimmed for validation. A blank name gives the field error on `name` `s.manage.edit.noname` ('Please enter a name for your structure'). A trimmed length above 190 gives `s.manage.edit.too-long-name` ('The name should be 190 characters or less'). On either error `/secure/EditStructure!apply.jspa` shows the form again and stores nothing.
On apply, name and description are stored trimmed; a missing description is stored as the empty string.

`permissions` on apply is a JSON array of encoded rules. Missing or empty gives no rules. A string that is not a valid rule gives the error page `s.manage.perm.error` ('Illegal permission required: <parse message>') and nothing is saved. Text that is not valid JSON at all also gives no rules, so saving silently removes all the structure's rules (as the original does).

When the user may edit the owner, `newOwner` (a user name) changes the owner only when it names an existing Jira user other than the current owner. Empty or unknown names leave the owner unchanged, with no error.

On apply, the booleans `favorite`, `editRequiresParentPermission`, `allowManualAdjustments` and `descriptionShown` take false when the parameter is absent, so a request that omits them turns them off.

On apply, `generationTimeLimit` (seconds) is written only when it differs from the structure's current limit; the change is logged as a warning naming the user.
