Showing a memo or planning task sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/genericItem/details/{itemType}/{id}` and, unless cached, `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/userPickerPermission`. The answer is used only if the same row is still current. With item data: the content is drawn with `item`, `fields`, the permission, the row's editable attribute and the structure id. With no item data: the content is cleared and the show fails with stub key `memo.noItemData` as an information message. Whether a failed permission request alone also gives that message depends on how Jira's jQuery combines a native promise, and could not be determined.
The user-picker permission is requested once per page and shared by all details; a failed request is forgotten, so the next show asks again.

The memo and planning-task provider has `refreshOnStructureUpdate` true, and `refreshDetails` does the same as showing. `extendFocusedRowData` waits for the row's editable attribute before resolving, so a slow attribute gives the `timeout` message. The panel is not editable when the attribute says so or when the grid panel is read-only.

Top to bottom: the summary editor with its error under it, on the same line a convert button for planning tasks; planning-task intro text; for memos the icon picker; the `Description` section; the `Fields` section. Changing item resets the content, so section states and errors are not kept.

`Convert to Jira issue` shows only in the details panel, for a planning task, when the item is editable and the server config `canRunEffectorsOnQueryResults` is true. Clicking opens the effector process dialog for module `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-conversion` with params `{selectedItems: [itemId]}` and forest spec `{structureId}`.

For a planning task, `Add details about this task.` shows when the item is editable or in the creation dialog. In the creation dialog a `Learn more` link with an external-link icon follows it, opening a link to the plugin's documentation in a new tab. In the details panel the link is absent.

The `Description` section shows when editable, or in the creation dialog, or when the description has non-blank text. Editable or in the dialog it is a rich-text editor that is enabled only when the description field is visible; the placeholder is `Add description here...` when visible and `None` when not. Read-only it shows `descriptionHtml`. The section has a required mark when the description field is required. Its error shows inside it. Cancel needs confirmation in the panel, not in the dialog.

The content is shared with the planning-task creation dialog. There the summary and description are always editable, non-editable fields are hidden, confirmations are not shown, and finishing an edit returns focus to the dialog.
Field edits send through `updateItemData`: summary as `{summary: value}`, description as `{description: value}`, memo icon as `{params: {...}}`, each other field as `{params: {<field id>: value}}`.

Errors show under their field. After a reply, errors of the sent fields are cleared and `fieldErrors` of the reply are applied, keyed by field id, with `summary` and `description` shown under those editors. An error also clears when the value of that param changes on the server, and when the user cancels editing that field. Moving to another item clears all errors. A reply with `success` false counts as a failure for the editor.

Unfinished edits mean an editor is open, or a field was added with `Add field` and not yet saved. Leaving-confirm drops both. Saving a field clears its entry; saving either time estimate field clears both estimate fields. Removing a field clears its entry too. Starting an edit marks the panel as stolen focus (`genericItem`), and finishing it returns focus to the panel.

For memos the picker shows `params.iconClass` and `params.color`, with unsupported icons shown as such. It is enabled unless the item is not editable. Choosing a colour sends `{params: {color}}`, unless the current icon is the unsupported one, then nothing is sent. Choosing an icon sends `{params: {iconClass}}`; replacing an unsupported icon sends `{params: {iconClass, color}}`. Failure shows `Error updating memo icon`, which clears when the value next changes.

The `Fields` section lists field entries built from `fields`. Fields that are not visible are left out, and non-editable ones too in the creation dialog. `summary` and `description` never appear. Fields `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent`, those that remain, form one grouped entry `Time tracking` with id `timetracking`, in that order. Entries are ordered with `project`, then `issuetype` first, others by name.

The fields shown are the entries with a non-null value in any of their fields, those with a required field, and those already chosen; this is recomputed when values or fields change, and a chosen entry stays until removed.

Above the shown fields is `You can add additional fields` with an `Add field` button (tooltip `Add field`), disabled when not editable. Its menu lists chosen entries, ticked, then the others, unticked. Required entries never appear among the chosen. Entries whose fields are all non-editable are hidden. The menu stays open on click, focus stays on the clicked entry, and entries are disabled while a change is applying, with a spinner by the button.
For planning tasks only, the menu has a search box, focused on open, that filters entries by name, ignoring case, anywhere in the name. Closing the menu clears it. Memos have no search box.

Unticking an entry with no value just hides it. With a value, in the details panel a confirmation shows `The memo field value(s) will be removed. Are you sure you want to proceed?` or, for planning tasks, `The planning task field value(s) will be removed. Are you sure you want to proceed?`; Confirm hides the entry and sends `{params: {<each field id>: null}}`, and cancel keeps it. The creation dialog does the same with no confirmation.

Each field shows its name as label, a red `*` when required, its editor, and any error below. It is editable only if the item and field are. An unknown type shows `Field "<id>" of type "<type>" is not supported` in place of the editor.

Editor by field type. Plain text: `single-line-text`, `single-duration`. Date: `single-date`. Date and time: `single-date-time`. Number: `single-number`. Multi-line: `multi-line-text`. Rich text: `rich-text`. Labels: `multi-label`. Option picker: `single-user`, `multi-user`, `single-project`, `single-version`, `multi-version`, `single-issue-type`, `single-priority`, `multi-component`, `single-sprint`, `single-group`, `multi-group`, `single-option`, `multi-option`. Rich-text values come from `<field id>Html`. Pickers receive `project` and `issuetype` of the values to scope options. The editors themselves are claimed under `planning-task-common`.
Date editors use Jira's date format from the widget's Jira configuration, converted to the picker's format, with no time part.

`issue-details` depends on Jira's issue navigator `common` and `viewissue` resources and the `issueviewer` component, and on load registers a provider for the issue item type. If it is not on the page (C-1216), issues show the `detailsUnsupported` message.

The panel embeds Jira's own issue viewer. It sets page metadata `viewissue-max-cache-size` to 100 unless already set, starts Jira's issue application (a start failure is logged and setup continues), and gets its issue editor to draw in the panel's viewport. The provider has `refreshOnStructureUpdate` true, `timeoutMessageKey` `noKey`, and the focus target is the viewer's issue container.

For an issue row, the issue id comes from the item id, and the key from the row's key attribute. If the key is not known yet, the promise waits for an attribute update of that row and so gets the 1000 ms `noKey` limit.

Showing an issue aborts any pending load, closes any open inline dialog, blurs open field edits, loads the issue into the viewer by id and key, and prefetches the rows just above and below in the displayed forest, when those are issues with known keys. Prefetch uses Jira's issue data cache and shows nothing.

When an issue with a stored unsaved-field error is shown (see `save-errors`), the load finishes on `fieldsLoaded`. If fields loaded, 10 ms later the viewer's save error display is triggered and focus moves to the panel, the event carrying no issue id because it reads the wrong property of the row (as the original does).

Before hiding, in the next tick, the viewer's own hide runs (a thrown error is logged and ignored), and any inline dialog is closed. Switching details off also resets the viewer's model to its default.

`hasUnfinishedEdits` is true when Jira's comment form holds a draft that Jira would warn about on leaving and the form is not marked dismissed. Leaving confirmed marks it dismissed. Refused leaving focuses the comment form again.
The viewer switches to Jira's narrow layout when the panel is under 900 px wide and to its very narrow layout under 600 px.

Jira's selected-issue API is pointed at the panel. Selected issue id, key and object are the panel's. Is-accessible means details are on and there is a key. Is-visible means the panel can interact. Is-currently-loading means the viewer loads or the panel blocks actions. Open-focus-shifter works only when interactive. Refresh runs only when interactive, otherwise resolves at once. Get-fields and edit-field act on the viewer's fields, and editing only an editable one. Next, previous, return-to-search, switch-layouts, view-selected, toggle-filter-panel, update-issue, focus-search and toggle-fullscreen do nothing. Query-valid and fullscreen-visible answer true. An inline load error shows Jira's error message, closeable.
Before an issue dialog opens it waits until saves in progress end: checked after 10 ms, then at each inline save completion.
Jira's `issueaction` keyboard shortcuts are ignored while the issue is loading, or actions are blocked, or there is no current issue data.

Jira dialogs whose URL holds `id={0}` have it replaced with the selected issue id; with none selected the dialog's request is not made. Each dialog request sends `decorator=dialog` and `inline=true`. Each shown dialog gets the current issue id.

Finishing an issue form dialog or dialog2: a dialog that is not an issue dialog keeps Jira's handling. Clone keeps Jira's redirect. Delete hides the dialog and then updates. Others show the footer loading indicator, update, and then, on any outcome, emit Jira's update trace, hide the indicator and hide the dialog. Labels dialogs answer submits as form dialogs do.

Dialog update: the command comes from Jira's notifications for that dialog, with the current key and id as defaults. With details off it just finishes. For another issue it finishes and notifies an update. For the current issue it runs a non-silent refresh. Either way Jira's message for the update shows at the end. With no current issue the update fails.
When the clone dialog is closing, unless by cancel or Escape, and details are on with a current issue, its hide is held until the update finishes.
Jira's `QuickEdit.sessionComplete` and `QuickCreateSubtask.sessionComplete` events replace earlier listeners and trigger the dialog update for the current dialog.

On new content, workflow transition links get the current `atl_token`, and the viewer's login link gets `os_destination` set to the current page path and query without the context path, so login returns to the board.
With a `baseURL` on the page, page metadata `viewissue-permlink` is set to `<baseURL>/browse/<key>` on changes of key or details-on, and with an empty key when details are off.
Focusing the add-comment text area scrolls the panel to its bottom.

A failed save in the viewer is stored per issue with fields and response, and removed by a successful save or inline edit cancel. So moving away and back shows the error again. The save error display's issue link opens details and moves grid focus to the issue's row (preferring a row shown recently, else the first row of that issue, else clears focus); for the same issue it shows the issue again by key.
The viewer does not change the browser window title.
When Jira merges a fetched issue into the cached one and their parent ids differ, the fetched parent is kept. Without that merge function a warning is logged.

When Jira's attachments drop zone module exists, it does not attach when no issue is selected, and its window-wide mask sits next to the panel and shows only during drag and drop. A relocation failure is logged. Without the module nothing happens.

An issue link click in the viewer navigates the page to that issue's URL, after saving a navigation hint (cookie `structure3.navigation.hint`, claimed with navigation) holding the structure id, time and key. Failure is logged.

The viewer's model and edit controller hold back the update following a field save when no grid edit runs, and the saved fields pass with the next update. A successful save for the current issue requests a silent refresh.

Dialog show and inline edit start, and lock of the panel refresh for the add-comment module, report details edit started. Dialog hide, inline edit cancel or blur, and panel refresh unlock report stopped.
While a save runs, all rows with that issue are marked as changing externally and repainted. On success or error the details report an update, marks clear, and rows repaint.
The last 20 shown rows are remembered in the page, newest first, for `save-errors`.

After a field submit or a replaced focused panel, or inline edit blur or cancel, focus moves to the panel. Dialogs count as stealer `issueDialog`, layers as `layer`, and the issue operations shifter as `focusout`. When panel focus changes with the shown row different from the focused one, Jira's issue environment is prepared for the shown row, or back for the grid's row.

`refreshDetails` waits for any pending fetch of the key and then refreshes the viewer if it shows that issue and is not loading; otherwise it refetches the key's data for the cache, passing the shown entity.

Attachment sort and order links and sub-task show-all and show-open links update the viewer with the link's query in place, and move the check mark, unless ctrl, meta or shift is held. Sub-task reorder links do `GET <link>` with `disableRedirect=true`, then refresh the issue; failure shows Jira's error, closeable.
After the user expands more links, the links module expands again upon reload until the row changes.

When issue-page time-tracking code is present, once the panel is visible it tracks the structure and shown row, and is on when details are on and the page's show-time-tracking parameter is set. Otherwise nothing happens.
Each inline edit start in the viewer records `inlineEdit.issueViewer` in local statistics.
When details die, the viewer's data is reset, the viewer dismissed, and all listeners removed.

`structure-info` depends on `uikit` and is required with the widget (C-1217). On start it looks for the footer's info slot; a widget with no such slot gets no dialog. It renders the trigger after the widget configuration has loaded.
The trigger is a link `Info` with tooltip `Show information about <product>` and an info icon. While loading, it has a spinner instead and is marked disabled.

Clicking the trigger shows the dialog, or hides it if visible; clicks during loading are ignored. The widget action `openInfoPopup` does the same and reports handled. No shortcut was found bound to it.

The first opening sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/info-popup` once per page through the widget's request queue, and shows the dialog when it finishes. Later openings use the same data, and a failed first load is not retried.
If the request fails, the dialog opens with empty data: title with `v?`, no node line, the Help and Support sections, no companion rows.
An empty or null `structureVersion` in the reply leaves a spinner as the only content.

Clicking outside closes it; clicking inside closes only when on a link. It auto-hides after 8000 ms with the usual inline dialog rule. It joins the widget's popup handling, so it counts as an open popup and can be closed with others.

It opens at the trigger, in the footer. If there is more room above and it would not fit below, it moves above with its arrow at the bottom and scrolls within the space. It also scrolls if it would overflow the bottom.
The top line shows the replacement's own display name (SPEC.md 1.1, never the original's name or vendor), followed by `v<structureVersion>`.
With a non-empty `jiraClusterNodeId` a line reads `DC Node: <id>`. On single-node Jira there is no line.
No update indication ever appears: every update flag is false (SPEC.md 1.8), so no `update available` label is shown and no link to the app manager appears.

Licence states are the fixed answers: no `unlicensed` label, no serial, no copy-to-clipboard control and no related messages ever show, for the plugin or a companion. The dialog has no licence text at all.

Section `Help` links, opening in a new tab: `Welcome to <product>` to `<context>/secure/StructureWelcome.jspa`, same tooltip; `Keyboard shortcuts`, tooltip `Show keyboard shortcuts cheat sheet`; `Documentation`, tooltip `Open documentation in a separate browser window`, a link to the plugin's documentation.
`Keyboard shortcuts` is absent on an Agile board tab and on the issue page. A click stays on the page, and in the next tick shows the widget's keyboard hints.

Section `Support` has one link: `Clear caches`, tooltip `Clear <product> caches`, to `/secure/ClearStructureCaches.jspa` in a new tab. The original's support request link, which leads to the vendor, is left out.
No feedback section: nothing to the vendor, so its heading, text and its idea and community links do not exist. The dialog sends nothing outside.

One row per entry of `plugins`, in order. It shows `name`; then `version` when non-empty, otherwise the label `not installed`. A row has no links: `links` is all null (C-4721), so the original's `Getting started` and `Documentation` do not exist here, and the dialog holds no address of its own for these.
A row that is not installed shows nothing on the right: `links.tryIt` is always null (C-4721), so the original's `Try it` link does not exist here.

`/secure/ClearStructureCaches.jspa` screen: page title and heading `Clear <product> caches`, a warning message `Clearing caches may affect your instance performance!`, then the form. No licence warning ever appears on it (SPEC.md 1.1).

The form field `Action` has the options, with `action` values: `Clear current user caches` (`clearOwnCaches`, preselected); for administrators also `Clear caches of the specified user` (`clearUserCaches`), `Clear all caches on this node` (`clearAllCaches`), and on a cluster `Clear all caches on all nodes` (`clearClusterCaches`). For others the list is disabled and a hidden field sends `clearOwnCaches`.
A `User` user picker (`user`, default the current user's name) shows only while `Clear caches of the specified user` is selected.

Button `Clear caches` sends a POST to `ClearStructureCaches!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `confirm=true`, `apply` and `redirect`. `redirect` is `returnUrl` when given, otherwise the page's own link. With `returnUrl` a `Back` link to it shows, tooltip `Go back to the <product> Board page`. The same form is on the support page (C-5192).

`/secure/ViewStructureShortcuts.jspa` screen, in Jira's popup layout: heading `Keyboard Shortcuts: <product>` with `Ctrl + ?` at the right, then each group (C-4950 to C-4958) with its heading and lines of label and keys. Alternatives join with ` or `, modifiers each end with ` + `, and keys in a sequence stand next to each other as separate keys. The footer has a `Close` link, fixed text. The form has no submit control, so nothing is sent.

Web-resource `jsutil`, depending on exactly `com.almworks.jira.structure:tslib`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:stacktrace.js`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:events`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:structure-aui`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:inline-dialog`, `jira.webresources:underscore-1.5.2` and `jira.webresources:jira-events`. It holds the shared browser utilities every other plugin script builds on; the plugin's other scripts depend on it, so it must load before them.

When the shared utilities fail to initialise while the script loads, the browser shows an alert box reading `failed to initialize package jsutil ` followed by the error text; the page itself goes on loading.

Message lookup by key, used by all browser code: an empty key gives an empty string; a key not in the loaded message table gives the key itself; a known key with no arguments gives its text with every placeholder left as written ('Hello {0}, {1}' stays so); arguments replace the placeholders. With text 'Hello {0}, {1}' and only 'Bob' passed the result is 'Hello Bob, {1}': a placeholder whose argument is missing, null or undefined is left as written. Arguments are inserted as they are, without HTML escaping.

Placeholders in message texts have these forms. `{n}`: argument n, as text. `{n,number}`: the number as text (2.6 gives 2.6). `{n,number,integer}`: rounded to the nearest whole number (2.6 gives 3). `{n,choice,...}`: see the separate claim. Any other format name (for example `{0,date}`) or number sub-format leaves the placeholder as written. Message texts come from the server already resolved, per `widget-i18n-transformer-cache`.

A `{n,choice,LIMIT#text|LIMIT<text|...}` placeholder picks a text by the numeric argument, in the usual message-format way: `L#text` applies from L inclusive, `L<text` from just above L; below the first limit the first text applies; above the last the last applies. Parts that do not parse are skipped. The picked text then has its own placeholders replaced with the same arguments. For '{0,choice,0#no rows|1#one row|1<{0} rows}': 0, 0.5 and -1 give 'no rows'; 1 gives 'one row'; 2 gives '2 rows', 7 gives '7 rows'. A non-numeric argument (the text '3') leaves the whole placeholder as written.

Client-side text templates replace `{name}` placeholders from named values (dotted paths such as `{a.b}` walk the object's own properties) and otherwise from the message table. Replaced text is HTML-escaped unless the placeholder is written `{name:html}`. Numbers and booleans are shown as text, an empty string gives nothing, and a placeholder with neither a value nor a message stays as written. `{key,a,b}` looks up message `key` with up to 3 arguments taken from the named values, with `?` for a missing value. Positional formatting works the same way: pattern '{0} of {1}' with 1 and 3 gives '1 of 3', and a pattern shorter than 3 characters, or with no values, comes back unchanged.

Text put into HTML by the utilities escapes exactly `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` (to `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`). A value that is not a string escapes to an empty string, numbers included. Unescaping turns those five back. Tag stripping removes anything of the form `<...>` and keeps the text between, so 'b' gives 'b'.

Labels shortened for display: with the default limit of 40 characters a text of 40 or fewer stays whole; a longer one becomes its first 37 characters plus `...` (40 in total). With limit 7, 'abcdefghij' gives 'abcd...'. An empty value is returned as is. Capitalising upper-cases only the first character ('ab' gives 'Ab').

A failed request is turned into a report with a title, details and the response body, with these fixed English texts (not translated). Reason `timeout`: 'Request timed out. Please check your connection and try again.', details 'HTTP request timeout'. Reason `connection`: 'Connection problem. Please check your connection and try again.', details 'Browser failed to establish HTTP connection.'. Status 401 or 403: 'Permissions problem. Please check that you are logged in.'. Any other non-zero status: 'Server-side error. Please contact JIRA administrator.'. For those two the details are 'HTTP <status> <status text>', then a blank line and the response body when there is one. Status 0 or none: 'Network error. Please check your connection and try again.', details 'Browser failed to send HTTP request (<status>)'. Each feature decides where the report is shown.

Browser-side logging goes to the browser console and nowhere else: no error, log line or stack trace is sent to any server, the vendor's included. Debug lines are off by default, warnings and errors are always written, and an error's stack goes to the console's error channel. An exception raised inside a listener or a guarded callback is logged and does not stop the other listeners. Lines carry a running number and the seconds since page load, then DEBUG, WARN or ERR, then the text.

A feature may register one receiver for error-level log lines; it gets the line's text, then a blank line and the stack when there is one. Warnings never reach it, and a later receiver replaces the former. Catching window errors, when a feature turns it on, logs 'JavaScript error: <message>' followed by a line '@line <n> (<url>)' at the level the feature gives, and always calls any handler that was there before; turning it off restores that handler. A failure inside this handling is swallowed.

If another script on the page has added a `toJSON` to `Array.prototype` that breaks JSON output (the check is that an object holding [1] must serialise as `{"x":[1]}`), the utilities disable it on load and warn in the console, so request bodies are valid JSON. Parsing with a default gives the default for an empty text or invalid JSON, without an error.

Local URLs are built from Jira's context path. With context `/jira`: 'rest/x' and '/rest/x' both give '/jira/rest/x', and an empty path gives '/jira/'. With an empty context, '/rest/x' gives '/rest/x'. Every same-server URL that the UI requests or links to is built this way.

Building a query string from a set of values gives `?a=1&b=2`, with names and values URL-encoded. An array repeats the name once per element. A value that is empty, zero, false, null or undefined is left out altogether, so 0 is never sent by this path (as the original does). With nothing left the result is empty, with no `?`.

Setting a query parameter on a URL replaces its first occurrence in place, drops further occurrences and keeps the other parameters in order; the value is URL-encoded; a new name is appended; a null value removes the name. Anything after `#` is not treated separately, so a fragment stays attached to the last parameter and a new parameter lands after it (as the original does). Reading a parameter looks only between `?` and `#`, returns the first match with `+` read as a space and the value URL-decoded, and gives null when absent.

General rules for cookies the UI writes: lifetime 365 days unless given, path `/` unless given, a path always ending in `/`. A value containing `;` or `=` is URL-encoded, other values are written as they are. Writing an empty value deletes the cookie by expiring it. Reading matches the exact name, strips surrounding double quotes, URL-decodes and gives an empty string when the cookie is absent. Since reading always decodes but writing does not always encode, a value with a stray `%` does not survive a round trip (as the original does).
The utilities track whether the browser's load event has happened. The state resolves at that event, and is rejected after 60 seconds without it, so code waiting for page load gives up then.

Shortcuts are written as key names joined with `+`, the last being the key and those before it the modifiers `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt` and `meta`, case-insensitively: 'ctrl+shift+x'. A comma separates the steps of a sequence: 'g,s'. Key names are letters, digits, `f1` to `f19`, names such as `enter`, `escape`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, `insert`, and the punctuation keys. A shortcut that does not parse is logged as an error and not registered; a later registration of the same keys replaces the earlier one with a warning.

A key press reaches plugin shortcuts only under these rules. Focus in an input, textarea, select or button: ignored unless the modifiers are exactly Ctrl+Alt or Ctrl+Alt+Shift, or that control lists the shortcut as allowed. Focus inside a Jira picker: ignored. A control marked as pass-through always accepts them. For a shortcut set bound to one part of the page: ignored while that part is hidden; accepted when focus is inside it; accepted when nothing in particular has focus (page body) or focus is on an ancestor of that part; otherwise not, unless a feature's own rule says so.

After the first step of a sequence, the next key must arrive within 500 ms; later, or a key that does not continue the sequence, abandons it, and that key does nothing else. A sequence can start only from a key reaching the document or the shortcut set's own element. When a key is both a shortcut and the start of a sequence, its action waits 500 ms and is cancelled if the sequence continues. A shortcut that handled the key suppresses the browser's default for it and the matching keypress and keyup, until a different key arrives.

Shortcuts are displayed as follows. Not on a Mac (the user agent does not contain 'mac os', in any case): each key name capitalised and joined with `+`: 'ctrl+shift+x' shows 'Ctrl+Shift+X'; sequence steps run together: 'g,s' shows 'GS'. `minus` shows `-`, `plus` shows `+`, `apos` shows `'`, and the arrows `left`, `right`, `down`, `up` show the arrow characters. On a Mac the same, without `+` and with symbols: `meta` as U+2318, `shift` U+21E7, `alt` U+2325, `ctrl` U+2303, `enter` U+23CE, `delete` U+2326, `escape` U+238B: 'ctrl+x' shows U+2303 then X.

Each toolbar entry, menu entry and shortcut runs a named action. The action is asked for its availability just before it runs: when it answers no, or fails with an error (which is logged), it does not run and a key press goes on to the browser. When it runs and reports that it handled the event, the event is stopped there. Availability changes reach the bound controls at once: a disabled button has `aria-disabled` set and clicking it does nothing, a split button's arrow follows its main part, a toggled button has `aria-pressed` true, and a checkbox or radio menu entry shows as checked.

Form controls stay in step with their data in both directions: a value set in code shows in the control, and a user's change (for checkboxes, selects and radios on change, key release and click; for text fields also on blur) updates the value at once. A radio group is every radio with the same name in the same form. A value with no matching option leaves nothing selected.

When a form's block is disabled by the shared binding, a text input or textarea becomes read-only, not disabled, so its text can still be selected and copied; all other inputs become disabled. Enabling removes this. A field can opt to be always truly disabled.

Whenever Jira reports new content on the page (page load, an opened dialog), inside that content: selects the plugin marks are turned into Jira's searchable select box, per `structure-aui`; and show/hide rules are wired. A rule says 'hide this element while checkbox X is checked' or 'show it while checkbox X is checked', several can be combined on one element, and the element follows the checkbox at once and on every change. When the checkbox cannot be found a warning is logged, a 'hide' element stays visible and a 'show' element stays hidden.

A dialog or popup borrows keyboard focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes: 250 ms after closing, focus goes to the most recent remembered element still on the page and visible, walking back through nested borrowers. If the user has meanwhile focused a visible element outside the closing popup, focus stays there. If nothing remembered remains, focus moves to the page body. Focus on anything other than an input or an element with a tab index counts as the current focus only after 2 seconds.
In a scrollable list set up this way, wheel scrolling past either end stops at that end and does not scroll the page behind it.

An auto-growing text area grows with its text while it has focus, following each key and input, up to its maximum height, then scrolls. When it loses focus, 300 ms later, it shrinks back to its original height and scrolls to the top.

Displaying content that depends on a pending load: already loaded, the content shows at once with no spinner. Otherwise the content is hidden, and if still pending after 500 ms a spinner appears in its place. On success the spinner goes and the content shows. On failure the spinner goes, the content stays hidden, and before it appears an error icon (with accessible text 'Error') and 'Cannot load data'. There is no retry here.

A control with separate single-click and double-click actions waits (500 ms by default) after a click before the single-click action; a double click within that time cancels it and runs the double-click action instead.

Dropdowns the plugin positions open below their trigger, unless there is more room above than below and the content (when its height is known) would not fit below. When a dropdown would pass the window's edge, its height is limited so that it ends 5 px short of the top edge, or short of the bottom edge by 5 px plus its top margin; otherwise there is no limit. A hidden dropdown entry is also marked disabled, so it cannot be reached by keyboard.

Reorderable items in banners are dragged by their handle, inside their parent only, without scrolling. Items swap when the dragged item overlaps the neighbour by more than half its width and sits within half its height of it. When the drop lands on a new place the feature gets the old and new positions. In Firefox the click that ends the drag does not reach a button underneath.

A bar with responsive width modes measures each mode in order, in its full-to-compact order, hidden while measuring, and uses the first mode whose measured width fits the available width; when none fits, the last. Its minimum width is then the chosen mode's width.

On Jira 9.12 tooltips work through Jira's own tooltip component and apply inside the board on the structure page, the structure tab on an agile board, the structure panel on an issue page, and otherwise the plugin's own structure areas and toolbar. Each area is set up once. An element takes part when it is marked as having a tooltip or carries a `data-tooltip` or `original-title` attribute, including elements added later.

The text of a tooltip comes, in order, from a feature's text for that element, then its `data-tooltip` attribute, then its native `title` (which is removed so that the browser does not show its own, and kept as `data-tooltip`), then `original-title`. Tooltips may contain HTML unless the feature says otherwise, when the text is escaped. A Jira status lozenge ignores `data-tooltip`. With no text there is no tooltip. The tooltip sits to the lower right of its element.

A click anywhere outside a tooltip box hides the tooltip showing and suppresses new ones for 300 ms. No tooltip shows for an element placed exactly at the window's top left corner (0,0), since it is not really laid out. A feature can hide all tooltips at once, and turn off the tooltip of one element, putting its text back as the `title`.

Text cut off by its container gets a tooltip with the full text, HTML-escaped, only while it really overflows: the text's width is greater than the element's inner width without its padding. Text that fits has no tooltip. Entries of a searchable select box that overflow get a native `title` with their text.

The reactive values, lifecycles, event dispatch, collections, caches and object helpers in this resource have no behaviour of their own at any boundary: nothing in them sends a request, stores anything or shows anything. A rebuild can use any equivalent.

Web-resource `events`, with no dependencies and one script. It defines the names of the UI's internal application events (loading, edits, selection, views, polling, dialogs and the like), which plugin scripts use to talk to each other, available as a module and on the plugin's global namespace, since the gadget script reads it there.

Event identifiers are assigned at load, as `_e` plus a running number, so they carry no meaning, are not stored and never reach the server. The set is private to the plugin and a rebuild may name them freely; what companion apps can call is the browser-side API under `structure/api/`.

Web-resource `widget-i18n`, depending on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil`, with a `transformation extension="js"` using `widget-i18n-transformer`, and one download resource named `structure_messages.js` at location `i18n/structure_messages.js`. The packaged file holds only a comment: its real content is generated per locale, as `widget-i18n-transformer-common` and `widget-i18n-transformer-cache` claim.

The generated bundle calls `window.almworks.util.resources(locale, messages)`. The call sets `window.almworks.locale` to the locale and merges the messages into the table used for all lookups, later bundles adding to it and overwriting equal keys. Until a bundle has loaded, lookups give the key itself.

Web-resource `hints`, depending on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil`, with the stylesheet `structure-hints.css` (content type text/css) and the script `hints.js`. The stylesheet only spaces the action link within a page-wide hint and gives it a pointer cursor. The helpers exist only when the plugin's jQuery has loaded.

Dismissing a page-wide hint with a given id removes the hint that holds the clicked element from the page, remembers the dismissal, fires a window resize so that the layout closes the gap, and cancels the link's default action. It is remembered in the browser's local storage with no expiry. If storage is unavailable or the write fails, it goes to a cookie named with the hint's id, value `hidden`, for 365 days, path = Jira's context path, or `/`. It is per browser, not per user. No request is sent.

A hint counts as dismissed when local storage holds any non-empty value for it, or a cookie with its id is set. Unavailable storage counts as nothing stored, so only the cookie decides. `end-of-life` uses this check; nothing in the plugin itself calls the dismissal helper at present.

Web-resource `page-util`, depending on `com.atlassian.auiplugin:ajs`, `jira.webresources:jira-global`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-rc`, with one script: helpers for the plugin's server-rendered pages. They exist only when jQuery has loaded.

The checkbox multi-selector (used by the sync and rollup forms) keeps its value in a hidden form input: a comma-separated list of option ids, in selection order, or `*` for 'all'. The initial value is read from that input and every change is written back to it.

Loading options: a GET to the given local URL (with Jira's context path), expecting JSON. A `#name` at the end of the URL is not sent: it picks that field of the answer as the list. Only the latest request counts: an older answer is dropped. The loading state ('Loading...') shows only when a load is still running after 300 ms, and ends with the load.

Each option in the answer makes one labelled checkbox. Its id, name and description are read from `id`, `name`, `description` unless the page supplies its own readers, and are HTML-escaped; the description is the tooltip. An option without id or name is skipped. No options at all shows 'None'. Reloading replaces the options and re-applies the current value.

A failed load marks the selector as failed, but no stylesheet or script reacts to that, so the user sees the loading state end and no options and no message, and the mark stays after a later successful load (as the original does).

Checking 'All' checks every option and makes the value `*`. Unchecking 'All' clears every option. Unchecking any option while 'All' is checked clears 'All' and the value becomes the ids still checked, in display order, since `*` has no order. With value `*` every box is shown checked. Other changes keep the stored order: an unchecked id is removed; a newly checked id goes before the first id of an option listed after it that is already in the value, or at the end.

Where the form has an order list, it shows one draggable row per selected option in value order, with the option's name and description tooltip, and a reorder hint only when there is at least one row. With value `*` the list is empty. Dragging a row sets the value to the new order, unless 'All' is checked.

On form submit, ids in the value that are no longer among the loaded options are removed from the input; `*` and an empty value are left alone. Since the options are empty until loaded, submitting before the load has finished or after it has failed removes every id and saves an empty selection (as the original does).
Binding a select to a callback calls it once when the page is ready, with the current value and the select, then on each change and key release. The sync-type selector uses this.

Moving items between two select lists (the project picker's arrows) moves the selected options of the source into the target, keeping the target in order by locale comparison of the option text: each goes before the first option that sorts equal or after, or at the end, with the search continuing from the previous item's place. It presumes both lists are sorted and the selection is in order.

An integer-only field accepts in its keydown only: digits, numeric keypad digits, Home, End and arrow keys, Backspace and Delete, plus Ctrl or Cmd with A, C, V, X. All other keys are blocked, Tab and Enter included, so Tab cannot leave the field and Enter cannot submit the form (as the original does). Shifted digit keys are not told apart, so Shift+1 is let through.

On every key release, input, change and blur, an integer-only field's text is replaced by its whole-number reading: '007' becomes 7, '12abc' becomes 12, '-5' stays -5. Text with no leading number ('abc', or empty) stays as it is.

Web-resource `dialog-common`, depending on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil` and `com.atlassian.auiplugin:dialog2`, with one stylesheet and the scripts of the shared modal dialog, its size names, its stacking and the confirmation dialog. The stylesheet centres the error line below the body in Jira's form error colour.

The shared modal dialog has a title, a body, an error line that starts empty, a primary submit button with the caller's text, and a 'Cancel' link button. Sizes are small (default), medium, large and extra large, as Jira's dialog sizes. Title and submit text are escaped, the body is HTML. It is modal, so a click on the backdrop does not close it, the submit button has focus when it opens, Jira's own keyboard shortcuts are off while it is open, and it leaves the page when it closes.

While a modal dialog is the top one, Enter anywhere submits and Escape cancels, and neither reaches the page behind. Enter on the Cancel button cancels. Enter in a text area of the body also submits. With another dialog on top, it ignores both keys. Clicks inside it or on its backdrop do not reach the page behind.

Submitting clears the error line, shows the submit button as busy and runs the caller's task. On success the dialog closes, then the caller's success step runs with the triggering event. On failure the button is idle again, the dialog stays and the failure text shows in the error line as plain text.
Nothing blocks a second submit while the first is running: another click or Enter starts the caller's task again (as the original does).
Cancelling closes the dialog and then runs the caller's cancel step, if any, with the event. No request is sent by the dialog itself.

The confirmation dialog is that modal dialog with title 'Confirmation', the message as one paragraph, submit text 'Confirm' and small size by default. Confirm closes it at once and runs the confirm step; Cancel closes it and runs the cancel step. The message is inserted as HTML, unescaped, so callers must escape what they pass.

A dialog opened over another stays on top: its backdrop is raised 500 above the current one (from 2500 when none shows) and the dialog 20 above that. Closing it puts the backdrop back to where it was and keeps it showing when a dialog lies below. When no dialog lay below, the backdrop's level is cleared.
Web-resource `confluence-auth-utils`, depending on `jira.webresources:almond` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil`, with one script.

Showing the Confluence login opens the given URL in a popup window of 640 by 520 pixels without scrollbars, centred on the browser window, with the window name 'Log In to Confluence'. Every 200 ms it checks whether the popup is closed. Once closed, the caller's step runs, or without one the Jira page reloads. The URL comes from the caller; this helper makes no request of its own, and with Confluence absent it is simply not called.

When the browser blocks the popup, a dialog of 500 by 300 pixels opens, titled 'Pop-up window blocked', with the text 'Your browser prevented the login window from opening. Please open this URL manually in another window:', the URL as a link, and a primary 'OK' button that closes the dialog. A click outside also closes it. No reload follows.

Starting the login again while an earlier popup is being watched replaces the watched window, and the first check's timer is never stopped, so after closing the caller's step runs repeatedly, every 200 ms (as the original does).
Web-resource `confluence-templates`, with no dependencies and one script: the template of the banner shown in the widget's Confluence content when it cannot be loaded.

The Confluence error banner shows the caller's message (escaped) as a paragraph, then a row with a retry loading indicator, an optional action button supplied by the caller, and a 'Try Again' button. When each appears, and what the buttons do, is in the Confluence handling of `widget-bare`.
Web-resource `jquery`, depending on `jira.webresources:almond`. It supplies the plugin's own jQuery 3 level copy; the version and files are the implementer's choice.

Loading it must not disturb Jira's jQuery: when the loaded copy differs from Jira's, the page's global `$` and `jQuery` go back to what they were, and the plugin's copy is reachable only as `window.almworks.$` (kept if already set) and as a private module. When it is the same object as Jira's nothing is restored.
In the plugin's copy, a cross-domain response is never run as a script just because of its content type, unless a request asks for that data type explicitly.
The plugin's copy must offer the short event methods `blur`, `click`, `focus`, `select` and `submit`: with arguments they bind, without they trigger.

Web-resource `jquery-ui`, depending on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery`. The plugin needs from it: sortable lists, dragging, resizing with its styles and images, and a delayed-hover helper. Library and version are the implementer's choice.

The plugins install onto the plugin's jQuery, not Jira's: the global `$` and `jQuery` point to the plugin's copy only while they load and are put back straight after. With the plugin's copy missing, nothing is switched.

Web-resource `react`, with no dependencies. It supplies React and React DOM to the plugin's UI. When both `React` and `ReactDOM` were on the page beforehand they are put back after it loads (otherwise the loaded copies stay as globals); the plugin's copies stay on `window.almworks` and as private modules, also under the plain module ids that the UI kit asks for. It presumes `window.almworks` exists, so another plugin resource must have loaded first.

Web-resource `momentjs`, depending on `jira.webresources:almond`. It supplies a date library to the date picker and the cumulative flow diagram, registered as a module. It is not hidden: the library's own global stays on the page.

Web-resource `tslib`, with no dependencies: runtime helpers for the plugin's compiled scripts, registered as a module. It must exist because `jsutil` depends on it, and what it contains is the implementer's choice. The module loader's AMD flag is on only while it loads and is removed after, as Jira's loader expects.
Web-resource `c3`, depending on `jira.webresources:almond`, supplying the charting library and its stylesheet that the cumulative flow diagram needs.

Any global `d3` and `c3` on the page before go back after it loads, and the plugin's copies are reachable only as private modules. Chart creation switches the global `d3` to the plugin's copy just for that call and restores it afterwards, even on an error, so Jira's or other apps' copies keep working.

Web-resource `stacktrace.js`, with no dependencies. It must exist because `jsutil` depends on it, but no plugin script calls it: stack traces in logs come from the errors themselves. While it loads, the globals `exports`, `define` and `printStackTrace` are set aside and afterwards all restored, so that the page's loader is untouched. Nothing it produces is sent anywhere.

Web-resource `uikit`, depending on `com.almworks.jira.structure:react`. It supplies the component kit, translation and CSS-in-JS libraries behind the plugin's newer React parts (structure info, details panels, planning tasks); its contents are the implementer's choice.

Loading the kit must leave Jira's global `_` as it was: a utility library inside the kit that takes over `_` is given back straight after the kit loads. The kit's dependencies are private modules, and with one missing the registration is skipped.

React content is rendered into a given page element inside the theme for Jira Data Center, so that it follows Jira's look, and rendering the same element again updates it. Unmounting one element clears it; unmounting the renderer clears every element it has rendered, so a closed panel leaves nothing mounted.

Web-resource `vendors`, with no dependencies and one script resource named `vendors.js`: the shared third-party code (React, a state store, CSS-in-JS and the like) of the management single-page app, which `manageSpa` depends on. Its content is the implementer's choice and it only needs to serve that app. It contains no error reporting and no calls to the vendor, and nothing of the kind may be added.

Web-resource `fonts`, with no dependencies: a `fonts/` download folder at location `css/structure/fonts` with `allow-public-use` true, and the stylesheets `font-awesome.min.css` and `structure-font.css`.

The server and module descriptors emit icon class names (see C-2855, C-2879, C-3476, C-3692), so these must work on any page holding this resource. `alm alm-fw` plus: `alm-checkbox`, `alm-effector`, `alm-flag`, `alm-group`, `alm-issue-icon`, `alm-memo`, `alm-sort-asc`, `alm-sort-desc`, `alm-status-category`, `alm-version-name`. `s-fa` with `s-fa-fw` plus: `s-fa-angle-up`, `s-fa-check-circle`, `s-fa-exclamation-triangle`, `s-fa-filter`, `s-fa-link`, `s-fa-pencil`, `s-fa-plus`, `s-fa-star`, `s-fa-tasks`, `s-fa-trash-o`.

Icon classes carry their own prefixes, so they do not collide with Jira's or other apps' icon fonts. The `alm` font is not read aloud by speech output. A rebuild draws its own glyphs; the vendor's logo glyph is left out.

Web-resource `widget-css`, with no dependencies, holding an `img/` folder at location `css/structure/img/` and the structure widget's stylesheets: board, toolbar, footer, inputs, forms, tooltips, panel header and banners, structure selector, item details, history, table header and body, rows, text wrapping, inline editor, column panels, each column type, view selector and management, dialogs, spinner, colour and date pickers, memo, planning task, quick actions, help, gadget, error and decision panels, and the Jira page and dialog adjustments. How they split into files is the implementer's choice.
The `img/` folder must hold `structure-logo-label.png`, since mails link to it (C-2313). The rebuild supplies its own image there, with no vendor branding.

All colours come from named theme values that follow Jira's own design tokens, with a light default when a token is absent, so the widget follows Jira's light and dark themes with no setting of its own. On Jira's dark theme the images of the pages promotional banner have a dark variant.

Some controls show only on hover, in stylesheets: the pencil of an inactive editable field appears when the pointer is over the field; the 'more' button of a transformation in the group dialog appears when the pointer is over that transformation, half-visible, and fully while its menu is open. A disabled banner edit control stays half-visible on hover.
A link marked as opening a new window shows its small indicator only on hover, press or focus.

In the formula editor dialog, the content area keeps a fixed height relative to the dialog on windows up to 700 pixels high, so it stays scrollable; its formula box is resizable vertically from a minimum height of 110 pixels, 300 by default.
Web-resource `structure-aui`, depending on `com.atlassian.auiplugin:aui-select2`, with the stylesheet `structure-aui.css` (content type text/css) and the script `structureAuiSelect2.js`.

The stylesheet adapts Jira's components to the plugin: the look of disabled toolbar buttons, the mark of checked radio entries in plugin dropdowns, the select box search field, the active badge in the structure selector, and the wiki editor. In the wiki editor of generic items it hides the attachment button, since generic items have no attachments.

The plugin's searchable select box is Jira's, working on Jira's jQuery, with 'No matches found' as its empty-result text unless the caller gives its own. Calling with a command rather than with options passes it through unchanged.

Web-resource `formula-icons`, with no dependencies, and exactly four download resources by name, with no file extension in the name: `partly-cloudy` at `images/formula/partly-cloudy.png`, `shine` at `images/formula/shine.png`, `spacer` at `images/formula/spacer.gif` and `thunderbolt` at `images/formula/thunderbolt.png`.

All four names are contract, because formulas store them: the bundled Item Health formula (C-1747) calls `structure_icon_url` (C-2025) with `shine`, `partly-cloudy`, `thunderbolt` and `spacer`, and a column saved from it keeps those names in its stored formula. `spacer` is a 1 by 1 image used for padding; the other three are icons shown at 20 by 20 by that formula, from 64 by 64 sources. The rebuild draws its own images.

The `web-item` `wi-structure-link` (name 'menu:<product>') sits in section `system.top.navigation.bar` with weight 41, label '<product>', tooltip 'Open structure', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` with link id `wi-structure-link`. It is shown only when the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped. It is also the dropdown of Jira's top bar: the sections with location `wi-structure-link` make up its menu, in weight order: welcome (40), recent (50), favorites (60), default (70), query (150), manage (200), processes (250).

The `web-item` `wi-welcome-to-structure` (name 'menu:<product>|Welcome to <product>') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-welcome-to-structure` with weight 10, label 'Welcome to <product>', tooltip 'Welcome to <product>', and links to `/secure/StructureWelcome.jspa` with link id `wi-structure-welcome`. It has no condition of its own; it appears with its section.

The `web-item` `wi-default-project-structure` (name 'menu:<product>|Default Project Structure') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-default-structures` with weight 10, label '<abbreviated structure name> - Structure (<project key>)', tooltip 'see this module's tooltip claim', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>` with link id `wi-default-project-structure`. The structure is the default structure of the project in Jira's current web context. It is shown only when there is such a project, the project is enabled for <product>, its default structure exists and is not archived, differs from the system default structure, and the user can VIEW it. All of that is read for the current user, and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped.

The tooltip of `wi-default-project-structure` is the message '{2} - default structure for project {0}' filled with {0} = the fixed word 'Structure', {1} = the structure name and {2} = the structure description, so it reads '<description> - default structure for project Structure' and never names the project (as the original does).

When the structure of a default link cannot be read (no permission, or the plugin stopped), or the project gives no structure id, the menu entry's context still answers: a project with no positive default id uses the system default, and an unreadable structure is presented with the name '?', an empty description and the requested id. The same holds for `wi-default-system-structure`.

The `web-item` `wi-default-system-structure` (name 'menu:<product>|Default System Structure') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-default-structures` with weight 20, label '<abbreviated structure name>', tooltip '<structure description>', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>` with link id `wi-default-system-structure`. It is shown only when the system default structure exists, is not archived and the current user can VIEW it, and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped. Label and tooltip are plain templates in the descriptor, not i18n keys. Name abbreviation is the rule of `slf-structure-configs-factory` (40 characters).

The `web-item` `wi-structure-query` (name 'menu:<product>|Query') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-structure-query-section` with weight 10, label 'Query', tooltip 'Search for issues using <product> Board', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=%7B%22sQuery%22%3A%7B%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22jql%22%7D%7D` with link id `wi-structure-query`. The `s` value is the URL-encoded forest spec with an empty JQL query, `{"sQuery":{"query":"","type":"jql"}}`. It has no condition of its own.

The `web-item` `wi-structure-create-wiz` (name 'menu:<product>|Create via Wizard') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-structure-manage-section` with weight 20, label 'Create Structure', tooltip 'Create a new structure', and links to `/secure/CreateStructure.jspa` with link id `wi-structure-create`. It has style class `new-structure-wizard`, which is how the front end catches the click and opens the new-structure wizard in place (see `new-structure-wizard-js`); with no script the link opens the page. It is shown only when `StructurePluginHelper.isCreateStructureAllowed(user)` is true for the current user (the original's licence test always passes, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped.

The `web-item` `wi-structure-manage` (name 'menu:<product>|Manage Structures') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-structure-manage-section` with weight 30, label 'Manage Structures', tooltip 'Create, copy, delete and manage sharing of structures', and links to `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?view=recent` with link id `wi-structure-manage`. It has no condition of its own.

The `web-item` `wi-processes` (name 'menu:<product>|Processes') sits in section `wi-structure-link/ws-processes-section` with weight 10, label 'Manage Effectors', tooltip 'Manage Effectors', and links to `/secure/StructureProcesses.jspa` with link id `wi-processes`. It has no condition of its own.

The `web-item` `wi-structure-jira-home-51` (name 'menu:My JIRA Home') sits in section `system.user.options/set_my_jira_home` with weight 30, label '<product>', tooltip 'Set my Jira Home to the <product> Board.', and links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa` with link id `structure-my-jira-home-set`. It is a choice in the 'My Jira Home' group of Jira's user menu, handled by Jira, and is shown only when the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped.

The `web-panel` `structure-helper-panel` (name 'issue-page:<product> Helper Panel') has location `atl.jira.view.issue.right.context`, weight 1000000 (last in the right column) and label '<product> Helper Panel'. It has no visible content: it only hands data to the issue page script.

The helper panel gives the issue page script, per rendering of the issue: the issue id and key; whether to show Structure on this issue; whether the issue is 'unstructured'; whether the panel is auto-collapsed; whether a navigation hint was used; and whether to show time tracking. With no issue in the context the id and key are empty, and show, unstructured and auto-collapsed are false. While the plugin is stopped nothing is filled in, and the script treats all flags as false.

On the issue page 'show Structure' is true only when the issue exists, the user can browse it, its project is enabled for <product> (`getIssueError(issue, false, true)` is null) and `StructureManager.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true.

When 'show Structure' is true the panel configuration is computed for the issue page with the issue, its project and the `structure3.navigation.hint` cookie (matched ignoring case on the cookie's name). 'Unstructured' is true when that gives no initial structure or the issue is not in the initial structure (read without an access check). 'Auto-collapsed' is true only when the issue is unstructured and the user's auto-collapse setting is on. 'Navigation hint used' is true when the cookie is not empty, whatever its content and even when Structure is not shown.

The 'show time tracking' value is the dark feature `structure.issuePage.showTimeTracking` (default true), read once when the panel's context provider is created, so changing it needs a plugin restart to take effect.

The `web-panel` `structuremodule` (name 'issue-page:<product> on Issue Page') has location `atl.jira.view.issue.left.context`, weight 899 and label 'Structure'. It is shown only when all hold: the dark feature `structure.feature.showOnIssuePage` is not false (default true); the current user may use <product> (`StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()`; the original's licence test always passes here, SPEC.md section 1.1), and it is hidden while the plugin is stopped; and `StructureManager.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true.

The panel's content must be non-empty for Jira to render the module at all, but it shows nothing: it is one HTML comment. The module stays hidden until `issuePageDecorator` has fitted it out. The `web-panel` `wp-projectnav-structure` has location `com.almworks.jira.structure:wi-projectnav-structure` and no weight or label. The project page panel requires Jira's issue keyboard shortcuts, the widget's web resources and `wr-project-page`, and shows in this order: the hidden issue operation links; an error message box when the context's error text is not empty (the provider always gives empty text); the hidden project key and id for the script; a toolbar place labelled '<product> toolbar' for assistive technology; and the place of the widget. The issue operation links must come before the widget in the page, for the reason in `ww-structure` (see the claim on issue operation links).

The project panel also carries a scope name, Jira's word for project followed by ': ' and the project's name ('Project: <name>'), and a scope JQL that is never filled in. Nothing reads either one on the client, so they have no visible effect.
With no project object in the panel's context, its context provider logs a warning and answers an empty context.

`gadget-resources` is a dependency-only web-resource: Jira's global, static, fields, set-focus and throbber resources, the small AUI spinner, the gadget publisher's scripts, Jira's common gadget resources, `widget`, `gadget-bare` and Jira's English calendar. The gadget page needs all of them before its start-up script runs.

`cfd-gadget-resources` is a dependency-only web-resource: as `gadget-resources` but with Jira's field templates, the AUI date picker and Jira's light common gadget resources instead of the full one, plus `widget`, `c3` and `cfd-gadget-bare`. The gadget's page requires Jira's English calendar separately.

`macro-resources` gives the external gadget page the widget (`widget`), the visibility helper (`visibility-observer`), the gadget's view-link and transform helpers (shared with `gadget-bare`) and the gadget stylesheet. It contains no gadget framework, because the page is a plain Jira page.

On Jira 9.12 the web-resource `adjustIssuePage` (name 'web-resource:Issue Page Resources for Jira 9', restricted to Jira [9.0.0,10.0.0)) is bound to context `jira.view.issue`, depends on `widget-atlas-deps` and `adjustIssuePageCond`, and is delivered only when the dark feature `structure.feature.showOnIssuePage` is not false (default true). The check takes part in the resource URL as a URL-reading condition, so the answer is cached with the batch. A second declaration with the same key covers Jira 10 and later.

On Jira 9.12 the web-resource `adjustIssuePageCond` (name 'web-resource:Issue Page Decorator for Jira 9', restricted to Jira [9.0.0,10.0.0)) depends on `issuePageDecorator` and is delivered only when the current user may use <product>. The condition is URL-reading: a user who may not use <product> gets a resource URL with `s_disabled=y` and no script. A second declaration with the same key covers Jira 10 and later.

`structure-projectnav-css` is stylesheet only: the icons of the <product> sidebar entry and of the Agile tab. It depends on `fonts` and is bound to contexts `jira.browse.project`, `jira.admin`, `gh-rapid`, `gh-rapid-plan` and `gh-rapid-work`. It has no behaviour.

`visibility-observer` watches the widget's container in a gadget or macro. The first time at least 1% of it (or a given threshold) enters the viewport, the widget's caches are cleared and its layout forced, then an optional callback runs; after that it stops watching, even if the callback fails (the failure is logged as a warning). This exists because a widget laid out while hidden, such as inside a collapsed expand macro, has no size. With no container on the page it logs a warning and does nothing.

When the document is ready, on a page where the issue page script is loaded, it starts unless a structure widget's place already exists on the page (as on the <product> Board's issue details), in which case it does nothing at all. On start it declares the page as the `issue` page (the value sent as `forPage`) and marks the page as the issue page for styling.

The script reads the helper panel's data (`structure-helper-panel`) at start, and again each time Jira fires its issue-refreshed event, even when nothing changed. On a Jira without that event it re-reads on Jira's new-content event for the page load and for a refresh of the helper panel only. With no helper panel the issue id is 0, Structure and time tracking are off, 'unstructured' and 'auto-collapsed' count as true, and the panel is noted as missing.

For each distinct issue id, the script sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui?forIssue=<issue id>` once, and shares the answer with the section, the settings dialog and time tracking. Showing the same issue again sends no new request. Issue id 0 sends nothing. A failed request only logs a warning: the settings button stays hidden and no structure is opened.

After the `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui` for an issue finishes (success or failure), the script clears the `structure3.navigation.hint` cookie and keeps its value in memory. Before a settings `POST` for an issue it puts that value back, and clears it again when the POST finishes, so that the POST's recomputed configuration sees the same hint.

When the issue shows Structure and Jira's Structure module is on the page, the script fits it out once: it replaces the module's operations with one settings button, adds a place for the 'not in structure' warning to the header and a widget place to the content, swaps the module for this version and makes it visible. Without Jira's module on the page it logs a warning and does nothing.
When the issue must not show Structure, the section is taken off the page (kept in memory), and any widget errors on display are dismissed.

When Jira redraws the issue and drops the section, while the new issue shows Structure, the same section, with its widget and its state, replaces the new module. If the widget exists, it is anchored and pinned on the new issue, focuses it initially, re-binds its mouse handling and help panels, lays itself out, and Jira's new-content event fires with the reason `structureSectionReinserted`; a failure of that event only logs a warning. The settings button is shown and rebound to the kept dialog.

The section header's warning reads '(does not include <issue key>)' with the tooltip 'The currently viewed issue is not in the selected structure'. The key is refreshed each time the section is placed on a page.

The warning is shown when the widget's primary panel has reported that the issue has no rows in the open structure. Until the widget reports (including when no widget exists yet) it is shown when the issue page's 'unstructured' flag is true and Structure is on. Once the widget has reported, the report decides; a report of 'not known' (null) goes back to the flag.

After each new reading of the page data with a real issue, the section is set collapsed when Jira's own remembered collapsed state lists this module, or when the issue is unstructured and auto-collapsed and no navigation hint was used; otherwise it is expanded. Example: an issue not in the structure with auto-collapse on starts collapsed, unless the user came to it from a structure grid.
10 ms after a click on the section's toggle in its header the section's expanded state is read again. Off the page it counts as not known.

The widget is created the first time the section is expanded, not before; a collapsed section sends none of the widget's requests. When expanded again it only lays itself out. Its options: height follows the grid's content, at most 15 rows, and the panel can be hidden.

On creation the widget is anchored on the page's issue: it pins that issue and focuses it initially. When the URL fragment is a positive number, that row is focused initially and the fragment is cleared (`#1234`).
Errors of the section's widget are displayed only while the page's issue id is positive and the issue shows Structure; otherwise an error is dismissed without display.
The widget opens `initialStructure.id` of the panel configuration, whenever that value becomes a positive id. The single-structure mode follows `singleStructure` of the configuration.

On creation of the section's widget, footers become responsive and the structure info dialog is available. While the user drags Jira's split-view divider (in the issue navigator) the widget lays itself out 100 ms after the drag events stop, when the section is on the page.

The section's title depends on the open structure (or, before one is open, `initialStructure`) and on the expanded state. Collapsed, with more than one structure available and a known name: 'Structure: <abbreviated name>', tooltip the description. Expanded, or in single-structure mode: 'Structure', tooltip '<abbreviated name> - <description>' (no ' - ' with no description). With no name: 'Structure' with no tooltip. Names are abbreviated to 40 characters. With no configuration or an unknown expanded state the title is not touched.

When an edit made in the section's widget finishes uploading successfully, and the changed item is an issue that is the page's issue, or appears in Jira's issue links module, or in Jira's sub-task list, the script fires Jira's refresh-issue-page event for the page's issue. Other edits leave the issue page alone. A failure logs a warning.

A Jira issue dialog opened from a row of the section acts on that row's issue, not the page's issue, by making Jira's 'current issue id' answer the id on the dialog's trigger while such a dialog is current. After it, Jira's sub-task refresh runs only when that id is the page's issue. When Jira's labels dialog is opened from a row of another issue, Jira is given nothing to update, so the page issue's labels on display stay untouched.
When Jira announces new content for the module `structuremodule`, the script fires Jira's lock-panel-refreshing event for it, so that Jira's panel refresh does not replace the section.
On Internet Explorer only, the section is detached before Jira's issue viewer redraws an issue on initialization. Jira 9.12 does not support that browser, so a rebuild may leave this out.

The <product> time tracking section is loaded with `GET /secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa?decorator=none&structureId=<open structure>&issueId=<page issue>`, always with Jira's cache-busting parameter, as HTML. It needs: 'show time tracking' on, an open or initial structure, and an issue. It is sent when one of these changes, when Jira refreshes its time tracking module, and after a poll that reports changes. A request with the same parameters while one is under way is not repeated, and a change of parameters drops the older answer.

When the answer to the time tracking request carries a job id instead of data, the script waits and asks `GET /secure/StructureTimeTrackingSection.jspa?decorator=none&jobId=<id>`. The waits come from the shared async back-off list, default 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 15000, 30000, 60000 ms, the last one repeating. An answer that carries the back-off override replaces that list for the page. Each poll is skipped if a newer request has started.

When a time tracking request fails, or the page got no reply, a warning is logged and whichever section exists is shown: the Structure one when present, else Jira's. No error message is displayed. The next trigger may send the same request again.

An answer with no section (empty fragment) when none is on the page yet leaves Jira's time tracking module on display. With a Structure section already on the page, it stays, structure data then counts as absent, and the section takes the state for that case (Jira data only, or hidden).

The <product> time tracking section is placed in the right column after Jira's time tracking module, else after Jira's dates module, else after Jira's people module, else at the column's end. Jira's own module is hidden while it is shown. The collapsed state starts from Jira's remembered collapsed state for this section's module.
In the <product> time tracking table, each term of the data list gets the prefix 'Σ' and a no-break space, after trimming: 'Estimated' becomes 'Σ Estimated'.

The <product> time tracking section has four states. No structure data and no Jira data: the section is hidden. No structure data but Jira data: Jira's data with no checkbox. <product> data and the checkbox 'Include structure sub-issues' off: the checkbox and Jira's data. <product> data and the checkbox on: the checkbox and the aggregated structure data.

The checkbox 'Include structure sub-issues' (tooltip 'Calculate aggregate estimates and time spent that include sub-issues of this issue in the selected structure') starts on, unless the user turned it off earlier. The choice is remembered in the browser across issues and visits, for all structures, by a text 'true' or 'false'. A change only switches the display; no request is sent.

With no time tracking data of Jira's own the non-aggregated part shows 'This issue does not have its own time tracking information.'. With Jira's data it shows a copy of what Jira's module holds, and a 'include sub-tasks' checkbox in that copy keeps working: it switches between single and aggregate figures.

The section's Log Work link (`/secure/CreateWorklog!default.jspa?id=<issue id>`, Jira's title and text) appears when the server says so. When a new answer with structure data updates an existing section, the link's target comes from the answer; otherwise from Jira's module. With no target it stays as it is.
While the widget exists, a poll answer with a non-empty change of any forest or of the items list triggers a reload of the time tracking section. An empty poll answer does not.

When Jira announces a refresh of its time tracking module (panel-refreshed or new-content for that module) and parameters are known, Jira's module is hidden again if the Structure section exists, and the Structure section reloads; a failure logs a warning.

When the page's data says Structure is off (and the helper panel is present), the <product> time tracking section is hidden and Jira's module is shown. When 'show time tracking' is off, requests stop and an answer on its way is dropped; turning it on loads the section.
After updating the section, the script fires Jira's new-content event for it with the reason `timeTrackingPanelUpdatedByStructure`, so that Jira binds its controls. A failure logs a warning.

The issue section's settings button (tooltip '<product> on the Issue Page Settings') stays hidden until the settings have loaded from the configuration, then shows and opens the settings dialog '<product> Settings'. Its dialog is built on first opening.

The issue settings dialog holds, in order: 'Auto-switch to:' (checkbox); radio 'Structure with the displayed issue'; radio 'Default structure: <abbreviated default name, or ?>'; 'Keep structure selection when navigating to another issue' (checkbox); 'Auto-minimize panel when issue is not in structure' (checkbox). Below them: a link to the plugin's documentation on panel settings, reading 'Help' with the title 'Open documentation on <product> panel settings' (the implementer's own link), and the button 'Close'. In single-structure mode only the last checkbox is shown.

The auto-switch controls map to the value `autoSwitch`: checkbox off gives `off`; on with the default radio gives `default`; on with the other radio gives `withIssue`. From the server's value: `default` or `withIssue` checks the box and that radio; `off` unchecks the box and leaves both radios unchecked as a value. Example: checking the box with no radio checked gives `withIssue`. Each click, key press or change is evaluated.

When `userConfigurable` is false (anonymous users), every input in the settings dialog is disabled and labels look disabled. The two radios are also disabled when auto-switch is off: they are enabled only with `userConfigurable` true and the value `default` or `withIssue`.

The settings dialog of the issue and project pages is an inline dialog 460 wide, offset -360 from its trigger, that closes on a second click of the trigger and hides by itself after a delay of 20 seconds (Jira's inline dialog option `hideDelay`). Clicks in it do not close it. 'Close' hides it. Its content is built once and kept.
The settings dialog shows the configuration's `defaultStructure` name, abbreviated to 40 characters, or '?' with no default.

While a settings upload runs, a small spinner is visible in the dialog; its state changes at most every 500 ms. When an upload fails, the dialog shows 'Failed to upload settings' and re-fits itself; the message goes away when the next upload starts.
