A field error from the server shows under its field for `name` and `description`.

`Owner`: when the user may change it (C-4973) it is the plugin's user picker with field `newOwner`, showing the current owner; otherwise a read-only line with an icon and the formatted subject (C-4916), the icon being a single-user one for a user, and a shared one for others.

The field `Options` has the checkbox `Require Edit Issue permission on parent issue to rearrange sub-issues` (`editRequiresParentPermission`) and, only when the manual-adjustment feature is on, `Allow manual adjustments of generated content` (`allowManualAdjustments`). With the feature off, the present value goes along in a hidden field.

`Time limit`: a required number box `generationTimeLimit` followed by `seconds (for automation)`, bounded by the minimum and the hard limit of the page (C-4970). Only digits, navigation and editing keys and the clipboard shortcuts are accepted, and the value is normalised to an integer as it changes.

Footer: a first submit button `Create` for a new structure or `Update` for a saved one, tooltip `Save changes and open Manage Structures page`; a second submit `Create and Open` or `Update and Open`, with field name `openStructure`, tooltip `Save changes and open <product> Board with this structure`; and a link `Cancel` to the return URL, tooltip `Do not create new structure and get back to Manage Structures page`, also when editing.

When the first submit button is clicked with the owner field different from its starting value, the browser asks `By changing the owner you might lose access to this structure.`; declining stops the submit. The `Update and Open` button submits without asking (as the original does).
The form posts to `EditStructure!apply.jspa` with hidden `atl_token`, `id` and `confirm=true`.

`/secure/StructureArchive.jspa` is titled `Archive Structure - <name>` in the browser and `Archive Structure` as page heading, with the section heading `Archive Structure "<name>"`, a help link to the plugin's documentation, a note of four short paragraphs saying that archiving makes the structure read-only and hides it from menus, issues stay in Jira, synchronizers get disabled and the action can be reversed, any error messages, read-only `ID`, `Structure`, `Description`, `Owner`, and the warning `The structure is synchronized. All installed synchronizers will be disabled.` when C-5038 asks for it. Buttons: submit `Archive Structure`, link `Cancel` to the return URL. The form posts to `StructureArchive!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id` and `execute=true`.

`/secure/DeleteStructure.jspa` is titled `Delete Structure - <name>` in the browser and `Delete Structure` as page heading, with the section heading `Delete Structure "<name>"`, a help link to the plugin's documentation, a note saying that only the hierarchy data goes, items are not affected and synchronizers are uninstalled, any error messages, read-only `ID`, `Structure`, `Description`, `Owner`, `Items in Structure` with the count and the hint `Does not include generated parts.`, and a warning `There is no Undo! Please make sure you delete the correct structure.`. Buttons: submit `Delete Structure`, link `Cancel`. The form posts to `DeleteStructure!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id` and `execute=true`.

`/secure/StructureRemoveAdjustments.jspa` is titled `Remove Manual Adjustments - <name>` in the browser and `Remove Manual Adjustments` as page heading, with the section heading `Remove Manual Adjustments for Structure "<name>"`, a help link to the plugin's documentation, a note saying that generated content goes back to its original state and this cannot be undone, any error messages, and read-only `ID`, `Structure`, `Description`, `Owner`. Buttons: submit `Remove Adjustments`, link `Cancel`. The form posts to `StructureRemoveAdjustments!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id` and `execute=true`.

The field `Adjustments` on that screen shows, first match wins: `Manual adjustments are disabled for this Jira` when the feature is off; `Manual adjustments are disabled for this structure`; `None` when the structure has no adjustments; otherwise the number of adjustments. The submit button is there in every case.

`/secure/StructureViews.jspa` with a structure is titled `Views - <name>` in the browser, `Views` as page heading and `Views for Structure "<name>"` as section heading, with a help link to the plugin's documentation, in Jira's general layout. Without one it uses Jira's admin layout (page `wi-structure-defaults` under `structure-admin/structure-admin-main`), both titles being `Default View Settings for Structures`, with no help link. A short note explains views, the menu and defaults, in two different texts for the two cases. Error messages follow the note.

With a structure the page shows `Structure` with name, `(ID: <id>)` and description, and then, under `View Settings`, two radio options `Default` (`useDefault=true`) and `Customized` (`useDefault=false`), the current state preselected. The global page has no radio options. The behaviour of the options, drag and add is in `structure-views-js`.

Two panels of the same layout are present: a read-only one headed `Default settings:` with the global settings, and an editable one, holding the structure's settings when customized, otherwise a copy of the global settings as a starting point. Each has a part `Views Menu`, with `No views are added to the menu.` when empty, and a part `Default Views`, with one line per page that has a default view.

A view in a list shows a drag handle; a `Remove` link, tooltip `Remove this view from the list`; its name as a link to `StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>&view=<view id>` in a new window, with the description as tooltip (plain text on the global page); and a link `Offered on:` with a summary of pages, tooltip `Select which pages should have this view on the menu`. That link opens the text `Which pages should have this view included in the Views menu?` with a checkbox per page, field `v<view id>-<page id>-menu`, value `true`. The summary words are `All pages` and `No pages!`. A view the user cannot see shows as `? (Unknown View)` and cannot be opened.

The editable panel adds `Add view:`, a select of all views the user can see and an add icon with tooltip `Add`. Its `Default Views` selects, field `default-<page id>-view`, group views as `Public views - shared with everyone`, `Shared views - shared with some users`, `Private views - usable only by owners`, an empty group being hidden. A view with a name shared by another reads `<name> [<id>, <owner>]`. The read-only panel shows the default view's name, or `-` when there is none.

The form posts to `StructureViews!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id`, `execute=true` and `view-sequence`. Buttons: submit `Apply`, link `Cancel` to the return URL. A view added just before opening the page is marked for highlighting in the editable panel.

`/secure/StructureCopy.jspa?id=<id>` has page heading `Copy Structure` and browser title `Copy Structure "<name>"`, repeated as section heading, with a help link to the plugin's documentation, and shows read-only `Structure` as `<name> (ID <id>)`, `Description`, `Owner`, and `Permissions` reading `Permissions will not be copied` when they cannot be copied.

When synchronization is allowed and the structure has active synchronizers, the form shows `Synchronizers` with the count and one line per synchronizer, and under `Options` the unchecked checkbox `Copy Synchronizers` (`copySynchronizers`). Checking it reveals, for a Jira administrator, `Synchronizer ownership:` (tooltip `Here you can choose to have all synchronizers in the copied structure run on your behalf`) with radios `keepSynchronizersOwner`: `Leave as is` (`true`, default) and `Make me (<user>) the new owner` (`false`); for others the text `You (<user>) will become the new owner of all copied synchronizers`.

`Options` also has the unchecked checkboxes `Copy Quick Transformations` (`copyQuickTransforms`), when the structure has quick transformations, and `Copy Notes Column Data` (`copyNotes`), when it has notes data. The whole group is absent when none of the three checkboxes applies.

`Non-automated Content` lists `All items: <n>`, `Issues: <n>`, `Generators: <n> (<a list by type such as 2 inserters, 1 grouper>)`, `Effectors: <n>`, with the hint `Does not include generated parts.` when there are generators.

With generators, `Visible Content` shows `All items: Not calculated`, `Issues: Not calculated` and a link `Calculate` to `StructureCopy.jspa?id=<id>&visibleStats=true`. After calculating it shows the numbers with the hint `Includes generated parts.`.

With generators, the select `Generators` (`generatorMode`) offers `Copy generators to the resulting structure` (`copy`, default), `Replace all generators with the generated content` (`replaceAll`) and `Do not copy generators` (`skip`). When generation is stopped, `replaceAll` is disabled and a warning says `"Replace all generators with the generated content" option is disabled because automation is paused.`. Without generators a hidden `generatorMode=copy` is sent.

A user with Jira's bulk change permission sees `Clone Issues?` with radios `cloneIssues`: `No — the new structure will contain the same issues as the original structure` (`false`, default) and `Yes — the new structure will contain copies (clones) of the issues from the original structure` (`true`). Others send a hidden `cloneIssues=false`, and have no cloning section.
Choosing Yes reveals the section `Issue Cloning Parameters`, with a short explanation, and renames the submit button from `Copy Structure` to `Start Cloning`. Choosing No reverses both.

The cloning section has a warning that follows `generatorMode` and the number N of manually added issues. `copy`: N = 0 `No issues will be cloned. Some issues may be inserted by the copied generators.`, otherwise `Only N manually added issue(s) will be cloned. Other issues will be inserted by the copied generators.`. `skip`: N = 0 `No issues will be cloned.`, otherwise `Only N manually added issue(s) will be cloned.`. `replaceAll`: `Both manually added issues and issues from dynamic content will be cloned.`. The word is `issue` for N = 1, `issues` above that.

The cloning section's fields: `Create in Project` (`targetProject`), first option `-- same as original issue --` with value 0, then the available projects; `Summary Prefix` (`summaryPrefix`); `Summary Suffix` (`summarySuffix`); `Labels` (`labels`, separated by spaces); each with a one-line hint.

When linking is possible, `Link Back` has the unchecked checkbox `Link each clone to its original issue` (`linkBack`) and the line `Link type: cloned issue` <select> `original issue`, disabled until the checkbox is on. The select `link` has two options per link type, values `<id>:outward` and `<id>:inward`, labelled with the type's outward and inward text, and Jira's system clone link type's outward option selected.

`Options` has unchecked checkboxes, each shown only when the action is possible: `Copy comments` (`cloneComments`), `Copy attachments` (`cloneAttachments`), `Clone Jira sub-tasks of the cloned issues (even if the sub-tasks are not in the structure)` (`cloneSubTasks`), `Copy issue links` (`cloneLinks`), `Copy watchers` (`cloneWatchers`). `Notifications` has `Send e-mail notifications for cloned issues` (`sendMail`), checked, when mail can be disabled; otherwise a hidden `sendMail=true` is sent.

Submitting asks no question unless issues are being cloned. When cloning, the number to clone is N for `copy` and `skip`, and the visible issue count for `replaceAll`, unknown when not calculated. From 0 to 9 there is no question. At 10 or more the browser asks `This operation will create a copy of each issue in this structure (total number of issues to be created: <count>). Would you like to proceed?`. For an unknown count it asks the same without the number. Declining stops the submit.
A confirmed submit disables the submit button. The form posts to `StructureCopy!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id` and `execute=true`. A link `Cancel` goes to the return URL.

`/secure/StructureCopy.jspa?processId=<id>` while the process is in progress has page heading and browser title `Copy Structure "<name>"`, the activity as section heading, a progress bar, the text `<n>% complete`, a `Refresh` button that reloads the page, and a link `Cancel`.

While in progress the page asks every 3000 ms for its own URL plus `progress=true&decorator=none`, the next request being timed from the previous answer. It updates activity, bar and percent text from the answer. An answer holding the word `refresh` (C-5017), or a failed request, reloads the page.
The progress fragment is a bare HTML body: while in progress three blocks with the activity (HTML-escaped), the bare percent number and the percent text; otherwise one block with the word `refresh`.

The `Cancel` link while in progress asks `Are you sure you want to cancel cloning? New issues that have been already created will be assembled into a new structure. If you would like to delete them, use bulk action on this structure.`; agreeing opens `/secure/StructureCopy.jspa?processId=<id>&cancel=true`. The link on a finished page has no question.

When not in progress the page shows the title and explanation of C-5018, then a numbered list of messages, errors emphasised, each with its exception text below it when it has one, and the link `Cancel`. When the status is success there is also a submit button `Continue`, posting to `StructureCopy!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `processId`, `stepId` and `execute=true`.

`printable-rc` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:fonts`, and provides `structure-printable.css`, `structure-printable.js` and `structure-icon.png`.
`/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` is a bare page with no Jira chrome: a control bar on top and under it one table holding the export's header row and data rows (C-4927, C-4933).
When printing, the control bar is not printed, the page background is white, and the header row repeats on each printed page.
The control bar's `Print` button opens the browser's print dialog.

The control bar has `Font size:`, a text box of at most 3 characters, and two buttons `A` (bigger) and `a` (smaller). The font size starts at 10 pt and the box shows `10`. It applies to the table only.

Bigger adds 2 when the size is 8 or more, otherwise 1. Smaller subtracts 2 when above 8, never going below 8 that way, otherwise 1. The result stays within 2 to 72 and is written to the box. Examples: 10 to 12; 7 to 8; 8 to 10; 72 stays 72; smaller from 10 to 8; 9 to 8; 8 to 7; 2 stays 2.

Typing in the box applies the size on each key release: a whole number from 0 up is clamped to 2 to 72 and the table follows, while the box keeps what was typed. A blank box or text that is not a number changes nothing. When the box loses focus after a change, it is rewritten with the size in force, for example `200` becomes `72` and `abc` goes back to the last size.

When the forest was outdated or the loaded data was inconsistent, the control bar shows one warning line for each case, with a warning icon and the export's text, followed by a help link to the plugin's documentation in a new window.

`new-structure-wizard-js` has no files of its own. It is in the contexts `atl.general` and `atl.admin`, so the wizard is ready on every Jira page, and depends on `com.atlassian.auiplugin:ajs`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:aui-select2`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:jsutil`, `:widget-i18n`, `:structure-aui`, `:template-common`, `:template-backlog`, `:template-agile` and `:template-personal-backlog`.

On every page, a click on a link marked as a wizard trigger, or on the menu item of `wi-structure-create-wiz` (link id `wi-structure-create`), opens a large Jira form dialog that loads the link's URL with `decorator=dialog`, `inline=true` and `__structurePage=<true when the page's URL contains /secure/StructureBoard.jspa, else false>`. The web item carries the style class `new-structure-wizard`, which is the trigger mark, and it is also the mark on the welcome page's links.

When the wizard finishes with response header `X-Wizard-Structure-Id` (C-5000), the board is asked, once ready, whether its primary panel may change structure silently. If so it switches to the new structure in place. If not, Jira shows a success message that cannot be closed: `New structure has been created.`, where the words `New structure` link to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`. Without the header nothing else is done here, and the redirect of C-5000 applies.

In the dialog, pressing Enter in any control except the `description` field clicks the primary button. On a full `/secure/CreateStructure.jspa` page without a dialog this rule does not apply, and Enter submits the form the normal way, which goes forward, because a hidden first submit button comes before Back.

The template chooser is titled `Select Template` (window and header). Templates are shown in rows of two, each with a 48 px icon, its label and description, and a selected state. The selected one is the template given by `__templateKey`, otherwise the first (C-2891), even if that one is disabled. The footer has `Next` (Jira's `common.words.next`), tooltip `Proceed to the next step`, and a `Cancel` link.
The chooser's form posts to `CreateStructure.jspa` with hidden `atl_token`, `__structurePage`, `__templateKey`, `__params`, and `__prevTemplateKey` when a template was given.

Clicking an enabled template selects it, removes the selection from the others and sets `__templateKey`. A disabled one is dimmed, and a click on it does nothing. Each template can take keyboard focus and reports its selected state.

Enter or Space on a focused template selects it and clicks `Next`. On a disabled template it does not select, yet still clicks `Next` for the template already selected (as the original does). A double click on the selected template clicks `Next`.

A step page has the header of the step's title, the browser title `Select Template`, the step's fragment, and a footer with `Back`, tooltip `Go back to the previous step`, then the primary button and a `Cancel` link. The primary button reads `Next` with tooltip `Proceed to the next step`, or on the final step `Create` with tooltip `Create and open new structure`. `Back` is left out on the initial step of a welcome-screen wizard (C-5002).

A step's form posts to `CreateStructure.jspa`, or to `CreateStructure!apply.jspa` on the final step, with hidden `__structurePage`, `__welcomeScreen`, `__step`, `__params`, `atl_token`, `__templateKey` and `__back=false`.
Clicking `Back`, or pressing Enter or Space on it, sets `__back` to `true` and submits, so the server goes back without validating (C-4989).
`Cancel` closes the dialog. Nothing has been created at that point, as the structure is only made by the final step.

The wizard's server-backed pickers (share with, projects, boards, versions) wait 250 ms after typing, then send `GET` with `query=<text>&maxResults=10` to their URL under `/rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/`. A `picker-search-result` is shown so that a group with a label is a titled section and one without shows its items directly. A group's `footer` is a last disabled line. An item shows its `html`, with its `title` as tooltip. A chosen item shows its escaped `label`.

On each change, a picker writes the chosen items as JSON to its companion hidden field (`roles-selection`, `projects-selection`, `agile-boards-selection`, `backlog-projects-selection`, `backlog-versions-selection`), and the picker's own field gets the ids, comma-separated when multiple. When a step is shown again, the picker's selection is restored from the hidden field.

The general step (C-4991) shows a short text on the side, about naming the structure, choosing who can edit it, and adjusting permissions later in the structure's configuration, and the heading `Specify Name and Permissions`. The fields are `Name` (required mark, `name`), `Description` (a two-row text box, `description`), `Share With` (`roles`), and `in projects` (required mark, `projects`). Errors from the server appear under `name`, `description`, `roles` and `projects`.
`Share With` is a single-choice picker on `create-structure/share-with`, preselected as in C-4995. `in projects` is a multiple-choice picker on `create-structure/projects`.

The `in projects` field is visible only while the value of `Share With` starts with a number and is not `-1`, which is a project role. `Nobody` hides it. A group whose name starts with digits, such as `123-team`, also shows it (as the original does).

`template-common` has no dependencies, and provides `utils.js`, `createStructureWizard.js`, `theme.css`, `create-structure-wizard.css` and `select.css`, covering the wizard's look and the plugin's colour variables, in light and dark themes.

`template-agile` has no dependencies. It provides the script for the Agile steps, `agile-template.css` and four side images, with a dark variant of each of the two kinds used on the Stories and Sorting steps when Jira is in dark mode: `agile-stories.png`, `agile-stories-dark.png`, `agile-sorting.png`, `agile-sorting-dark.png`.

On the sorting step, `Allow changing Rank via <product>` is enabled only while `Add Rank Sorter` is checked, and it is also disabled on first display when that box starts unchecked. Its checked state stays as it was while disabled, and a disabled box does not send its value.

On the epics step the board field becomes a multiple-choice picker on `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/agile-boards`. In a dialog the script runs on each Jira new-content-added event, so that it works for each step.

The `epics` step shows a side text saying that epics of the chosen boards go at the top level and how to build the same by hand with the `Agile board` generator, and the heading `Add Epics from the Boards`. It has one required field, `Boards` (`agile-boards`), placeholder `Select boards`. A server error shows under it.

The `stories` step shows a side text saying that stories linked to the epics form the second level and how to build that with the `Stories under Epics` extender, and the heading `Additional Options`. It has the checkbox `Allow changing Epic via <product>` (`agile-update-epics`), with a one-line note saying that a story can then be reassigned by moving it.

The `sorting` step shows a side text about ordering by rank and the `Rank` sorter, and the heading `Order Issues by Rank`. Checkboxes: `Add Rank Sorter` (`agile-rank-sorter`), noted as making the order match Jira boards; and `Allow changing Rank via <product>` (`agile-update-issues`), noted as letting rows be moved to update rank. Each checkbox has a hidden companion field of the same name with value `false`, which gives the two-value rule of C-2909.

`template-backlog` has no dependencies. It provides the script for the Backlog steps, `backlog-template.css`, side images `backlog-group-by.png` and `backlog-group-by-dark.png` (the latter when Jira is in dark mode) and `progress.gif`.

On the project step, `Projects` is a multiple-choice picker on `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/projects`, and `Versions` a multiple-choice picker on `GET /rest/structure/2.0/create-structure/versions/?projectIds=<ids of the chosen projects, comma-separated>`, the URL being rebuilt for each request.

With no project chosen `Versions` is read-only and empty. On each change of `Projects`, chosen versions of projects no longer chosen are removed, and the others stay. With one project a chosen version shows its name, and with more than one its `versionFullName` from the item's `params`, also for those already chosen.
On the group-by step, `Field` becomes a searchable select working in the browser, with no request.

The `project` step shows a side text saying to choose projects and optionally versions, and how to build the same with the `JQL Query` generator, and the heading `Select Projects and Versions`. Fields: `Projects` (required mark, `backlog-project`, placeholder `Select projects`), with a server error under it, and `Versions` (`backlog-version`, placeholder `Select versions`).

The `group-by` step shows a side text suggesting a field to group by, with Assignee as the example, and how to use `Group` generators, and the heading `Select Field to Group Issues`. It has `Field` (required mark, `backlog-field`, placeholder `Select field`), an empty first option, then the choices of C-2902, the last value selected, a server error under it, and the checkbox `Allow changes via <product>` (`backlog-allow-changes`), noted as meaning that moving an issue between groups updates the field. The checkbox has a hidden companion `false` (C-2901).

`template-personal-backlog` has no dependencies. It provides the script of its step, `personal-backlog-template.css`, and the side images `issues.svg` and `issues-dark.png` (the latter when Jira is in dark mode).

The field `personal-backlog-columns` becomes a searchable multiple-choice select working in the browser. Any change to it sets `personal-backlog-columns-changed` to `true`, which is what makes the server use the submitted list (C-2919).
Each of the three tracking checkboxes has a hidden field of the same name. Clicking the box sets its hidden field to `true` or `false`, so an unchecked box still sends `false` (C-2914).

The final step `__end` has the side text `Manage all the issues important to you, with all the data you need to see.` and these fields: `Name` (required mark, `personal-backlog-name`); `Issues I want to track` (required mark), checkboxes `Assigned to me`, `I'm Reporter`, `I'm watching` (`personal-backlog-assigned`, `personal-backlog-reporter`, `personal-backlog-watching`), starting as the step's values, with the error of field `personal-backlog-track` under them; and `Information I want to track` (`personal-backlog-columns`, multiple).
The columns select lists the step's preselected columns first, in their order and selected, then the other choices (C-2922), each with its label as tooltip.

`welcome` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:help-widget`, `:page-rc`, `:widget-i18n`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:ajs` and `com.atlassian.auiplugin:dialog2`. It provides the page's scripts and styles and the image folder `img/`, whose absolute URL the page uses (C-5069). The pictures are the implementer's own.

`/secure/StructureWelcome.jspa` has the browser title `Welcome`, uses Jira's general decorator, and shows from top to bottom: the intro with buttons, a picture carousel, the use cases block, and at the bottom a two-column part with app panels on one side, help and video panels on the other. The administrator's help panel (C-5068), in `interactive` mode of `help-widget`, sits beside it when present; at a window width of 1670 px or less it pushes the main content aside rather than overlaying it.

The intro has a logo of the implementer's own, one heading line, about ten words on organising and viewing Jira projects as needed, and a row of buttons, which is always present, since licensing always answers yes.

The primary button `Create a new structure` links to `/secure/CreateStructure.jspa` and opens the wizard dialog. It is shown only when the user may create structures. If the wizard is not available it works as a plain link.
The drop-down button `Recent structures` is shown only when the user has recent structures (C-5069).

The `Recent structures` menu holds a search box, placeholder `Search`, and a results area. The results come from `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structureWelcome/search?query=<text>`, sent 250 ms after the last change of the text, and once 250 ms after the page starts, with an empty text. A request still running is aborted when a new one starts.
The text goes into the URL as typed, without URL-encoding, so a text like `a&b` searches for `a` (as the original does).

Each entry of `result` is a menu link to `<base>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, labelled with the `name` as HTML from the server, so a match shows bold. An empty `result` shows `Not found`. When `total` is larger than the entries shown, a last line says `There are more results. Try refining search.`. Any entry whose text is cut off gets its full text as tooltip.
While a request runs the results area is hidden, and after 500 ms a spinner replaces it. A failed request, other than one aborted, adds the message `Cannot load data` above the area.
Each opening of the menu clears the search text, which brings back the recent structures. When the menu element receives focus, focus moves to the search box.
With the first result highlighted and focused, the Up key removes the highlight and moves focus to the search box. Up in the search box removes any highlight from the results and keeps focus there.

The carousel has five slides, in order, each a small screenshot with a caption of about five to seven words on, respectively: managing projects in one place; building a view that suits you; live calculations; insights at a glance; and seeing dependencies on a Gantt chart. The pictures are the implementer's own.

As many whole slides are shown as fit the width. When all fit, they are centred, with no arrows. Otherwise, at the first position only the next arrow shows, at the last only the previous arrow, in between both. An arrow moves by one slide, with no wrap-around, and a fade shows on the side where more slides exist.

A click on a slide marks it selected and opens the lightbox at that slide. Keyboard focus on a slide marks it selected, and leaving it clears the mark. Enter on a focused slide opens the lightbox without changing the mark. Only the slides now in view can take keyboard focus. Closing the lightbox clears the mark.

The lightbox fades in over the whole window, blocks scrolling of the page and takes focus. It shows a large picture of the slide with previous and next buttons and a close button, and under it a strip of the same five slides as small pictures, 128 by 64 px, with no captions, which works like the carousel. Clicking a strip slide shows it large. The strip marks the slide shown large.

The previous and next buttons move by one slide with no wrap-around. They do nothing at the ends, and neither button is hidden. The large picture fits the window and follows resizing. Clicking the large picture does nothing. Clicking outside it does not close the lightbox.

Once all large pictures have loaded, keys work on the whole document: Escape closes the lightbox, Left and Right arrows go to the previous and next slide. Each is swallowed, also while the lightbox is closed, so Escape closes nothing else on the page and the arrow keys do not move the cursor in the search box (as the original does).
With the lightbox open, Tab on the last strip slide moves focus to the previous button, and Shift+Tab on the previous button moves it to the last strip slide, keeping focus inside.
The close button or Escape fades the lightbox out, restores page scrolling and tells the carousel to clear its mark.

The use cases block has a header of a few words and, on one side, a list of five buttons with icon and label: `Personal backlog` (the icon is the user's avatar), `Reporting`, `Sprint planning`, `Release management`, `Scaled Agile Framework`. The other side shows the banner of the selected one. The first is selected at start, and a click selects another, showing its banner only.

A banner has a picture, a title and one sentence, all marketing of about ten to twenty words, on the use case. The titles equal the list labels, except that the last is a short line on visualising SAFe.

The `Personal backlog` banner has a primary button `Create` (Jira's `common.words.create`), only when the user may create structures. It opens the wizard on the template of C-5071. Without that right the banner has no button.
The other four banners have a button `Learn more`, which opens a large modal dialog titled with the use case's label: `Reporting`, `Sprint planning`, `Release management`, `Scaled Agile Framework`.

Each such dialog has a banner picture, a body, a footer with a link button `Close` (Jira's `common.words.close`) that closes it, and a hint link `<product> Guide` to the plugin's documentation in a new window. The body can scroll.

The reporting dialog's text (about 100 words) says the plugin gives a visual overview with the data to track, gives steps (create a structure from the Jira menu, add issues by hand or by automation, add columns with the add button at the top right of the grid), and shows a short animation. It then suggests columns to try: progress, work logged, time in status, last comment, formulas, and aggregating values from children, each a link to the plugin's documentation.

The sprint dialog's text (about 90 words) says all upcoming sprints can be tracked on one screen, gives steps (create a structure, insert the issues of an Agile board, group by assignee, group by sprint, turn on the Sprint and Version attributes in the Summary settings), and shows two short animations: one on grouping, one on summing a field over sub-items in the column settings.

The release dialog's text (about 90 words) says releases can be tracked by organising issues by version, gives steps (create a structure, add issues, group by fix version, or by version name if projects share names, turn on the Sprint and Version attributes in the Summary settings), and shows two short animations as in the sprint dialog.

The SAFe dialog's text (about 110 words) says the framework's hierarchy can be shown, gives steps (create a structure, insert initiatives by JQL, extend with epics through linked issues, extend with stories under epics and with sub-tasks, sort by rank), says the plugin can be tailored, and ends with an info box on keeping strategy documents next to issues, with a link to the plugin's documentation. It has no pictures but the banner.

The bottom part has a section with one panel per companion app: Gantt and Pages under one short heading, Colors, Testy and Deliver under another, each with a one-sentence description. A panel has a `not installed` marker image when that app is absent (C-5070). The links to the vendor's Marketplace listings are left out. Gantt's panel has a `Create` button under C-5071, opening the wizard. With all apps absent the section is only descriptions and markers.

Beside them a panel with a short heading on getting help has a picture and a short intro. The vendor's support, community, demo and newsletter links are left out, and the implementer provides its own or none.

A panel with a short heading on watching videos lists three entries (formula writing, feature discovery, how-to series), each with a picture, a play icon, a title and a visible link. The vendor's video links are left out, and the implementer provides its own. A click anywhere in an entry opens its link in a new window, and Enter on the entry's focusable icon does the same.
Nothing on the welcome page sends data to the vendor: no analytics, no feedback, no error reports. The only server call of its own is the search of `Recent structures`.

The web-resource keeps its key, type and dependencies, but nothing ever loads it (see `end-of-life-decorator`, C-4144), because the licence state is fixed as licensed, valid and not expiring. No licence or maintenance hint appears on any page, for any user, and the page makes no REST call on its behalf. If an implementer ships a file in it, the file does nothing: nothing warns, nothing blocks.

The web-resource keeps its key, type and dependencies, but nothing ever loads it (see `plugin-manager-helper`, C-4151). Jira's plugin manager page shows nothing added by the plugin: no licence note, no warning and no extra button. If an implementer ships a file in it, the file does nothing: nothing warns, nothing blocks.

The screen of `/secure/admin/StructureLicenseDetails.jspa` (C-5212) shows the fixed state only: licensed, valid, not expiring, for the plugin and every recognised extension (SPEC.md section 1.1). It has no control to enter, change or remove a licence, and never shows a warning, an expiry notice or a blocked state. The page has no other view: the original's debug view is not part of the rebuild's behaviour.

No administration screen ever shows a licence warning, and no control on them is ever disabled on licence grounds. This holds for: configuration, defaults, backup, restore, migrate, maintenance, help tool, dark features and the setup guide. In particular 'Configure Scheduled Maintenance', 'Run Maintenance Now', 'Restore', the restore and migrate file name fields, 'Select Structures to Restore', 'Create Help tool' / 'Edit Help tool' and 'Clear' are always enabled, and the maintenance page's scheduled state depends only on whether scheduling is on.

When the web-resource is on a page (see `stats-offer-decorator`, C-4146 to C-4148), an information banner is put at the very top of the page header, once the document is ready. It reads 'Would you like to help us make <product> better by enabling anonymous usage statistics?' followed by three links: 'Yes, enable!', 'More details' and 'No, don't ask me again'. 'More details' opens the plugin's documentation in a new window, with the tooltip 'Open documentation in new window'.

Clicking 'Yes, enable!' does not follow the link. The offer banner slides up over 200 ms, then a success banner slides down over 200 ms. At the same moment `PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` is sent with no body. The answer is ignored: an error shows nothing and the success banner still appears. It records the setting locally; nothing is uploaded, now or later (C-4513).

Clicking 'No, don't ask me again' does not follow the link. The banner slides up over 200 ms and `PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/dismissOffer` is sent with no body. The answer is ignored. The offer is gone for that administrator from then on (C-4514); no thank-you banner is shown.

The success banner reads 'Thank you! You can turn anonymous usage statistics on or off on the Support page.', where 'Support page' links to `<base URL>/secure/admin/StructureSupport.jspa` in a new window, with the tooltip 'Open Support page in new window'. It ends with a 'Dismiss' link, which slides the banner up over 200 ms. That click sends nothing to the server.

The setup guide page has the title '<product> Setup Guide', a one-sentence welcome note, and then these sections in order: required configuration, 'Optional Configuration', 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' (system administrators only) and 'Next Steps'. Each step of the required section has a done or alert marker, a heading and a text.

The heading of the required section is 'Required Configuration — Completed' when any project is enabled, otherwise 'Required Configuration' (the licence step always counts as done, C-5086). Licence step: done marker, heading 'License is Installed', and a sentence linking to the 'License Details' page `StructureLicenseDetails.jspa`. Projects step when done: heading '<product> is Enabled for One Project' for 1, '<product> is Enabled for <n> Projects' for more, and a sentence linking to the 'Configuration' page `StructureAdmin!view.jspa`. Projects step when not done: alert marker, heading 'Select <product>-Enabled Projects', a link 'Enable <product> for at least one project' (the URL of C-5087), and a few sentences explaining that the choice limits queries and hides the interface from users without access to such a project, ending with a link to the plugin's documentation.

'Optional Configuration' is a bullet list: 'Specify users who can work with <product>' (a link, followed by a note that a user also needs access to a structure-enabled project); 'Limit who can create new structures' (a link, with a note that the creator also needs general access); 'Adjust <product> defaults' (a link, followed by what can be changed there); and, for a system administrator only, 'Review maintenance settings' (a link, followed by what it adjusts). The URLs are those of C-5088.

For a system administrator the section 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' shows one of two states, by the stored value. Enabled: done marker, heading 'Anonymous Usage Statistics Is Enabled', and a sentence that it can be turned on and off and viewed on the 'Support Page' (`StructureSupport.jspa`). Disabled: alert marker, heading 'Anonymous Usage Statistics Is Disabled', the same sentence, and a link 'Enable Anonymous Usage Statistics'. The wording must not say that data leaves the instance, because nothing is uploaded (C-5089).

Clicking 'Enable Anonymous Usage Statistics' switches the section to the enabled state at once, without waiting, does not follow the link, and sends `POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` with no body, ignoring the answer. The resource accepts only PUT, so the setting is not stored and the section shows disabled again on the next visit (as the original does).

'Next Steps' is a bullet list holding one entry: a link to the plugin's documentation with a short note on what it covers. The original's two other entries, a Marketplace listing to watch and a vendor support contact, are not part of the rebuild.

The resource gives server-rendered plugin pages their shared look: the theme, page layout and select styling, plus its images, for both Jira's light and dark colour modes. It has no script. Pages that use it depend on its dependencies `fonts` and Jira's `jira.webresources:autocomplete`. One behaviour is visible: a link that opens a structure in a new window reveals a small new-window marker on hover, focus and press.

The resource gives the three Help tool screens their styling and has no script. It depends on `help-widget`, `page-rc` and `widget-i18n`. On the screen with no help yet, the placeholder picture follows Jira's dark colour mode.

The resource has no file of its own. It only pulls in what the page needs: Jira's expander and date-picker, `page-rc`, `jquery`, `jsutil` and `widget-i18n`. The attribute troubleshooting screen must work with exactly these dependencies, and uses neither the expander nor the date picker.

The resource has no file of its own. It only pulls in what the page needs: Jira's expander and date-picker, `page-rc`, `jquery`, `jsutil` and `widget-i18n`. The performance audit log screen must work with exactly these dependencies.

The help tool box shows a question-mark marker with the title, then the content already rendered to HTML, then one entry per contact: linked to the user's profile, with avatar and display name. A narrow side bar next to the box repeats the title and has a chevron. When there are no contacts that part is empty.

In interactive mode only (the welcome page) the box can collapse into its side bar and expand again, with a 300 ms width animation. It toggles on a click on the side bar, on Enter while the side bar has keyboard focus (it can take focus), and on the `[` key pressed anywhere on the page. Collapsed, the side bar shows the question-mark marker; expanded, the chevron. The state is not remembered: a new page load starts expanded. Outside interactive mode (the admin screens) the box does not collapse, and clicks and keys on it do nothing.

`StructureHelp!view.jspa` (C-5074) has the heading 'Help tool' and the note 'Add a custom Help tool to the Welcome to <product> page.'. With no saved help: a button 'Create Help tool', a placeholder and the text 'This is only a preview'. With saved help: a button 'Edit Help tool', a 'Clear' control with a trash marker, a link 'View Welcome page' to `/secure/StructureWelcome.jspa`, and below them the help box in its non-interactive form. The Create or Edit button links to `/secure/StructureHelp!edit.jspa` and has keyboard focus when the page opens.

'Clear' does not post at once. It opens the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`) with 'Are you sure you want to clear the Help tool? All content will be deleted.'. Confirming posts `StructureHelp!clear.jspa` with the page's `atl_token`; cancelling sends nothing.

`StructureHelp!edit.jspa` shows the heading 'Help tool', the same note, and a form: 'Title' (required, text field `title`), 'Content' (required, Jira's wiki editor, field `content`) and 'Contacts' (optional multi-user picker, field `contacts`, placeholder 'Enter username or email', filled from the contact details of C-5075). The contacts picker uses the plugin's multi-user picker and needs the resources of Jira's issue view context, which the page requests. The title field error is shown under the title and the content error under the editor.

The edit form has three submit buttons, each posting all fields to its own command: 'Preview' to `StructureHelp!savePreview.jspa`, 'Apply' to `StructureHelp!save.jspa`, and 'Cancel' to `StructureHelp!cancel.jspa`. All carry `atl_token`.

`StructureHelp!showPreview.jspa` has the heading 'Help tool' and the note, then the help box as it will look, non-interactive, and three buttons: 'Continue editing' (a link to `StructureHelp!edit.jspa`), 'Apply' and 'Cancel'. Apply and Cancel post to `StructureHelp!save.jspa` and `StructureHelp!cancel.jspa` with hidden fields `title`, `content`, `contacts` (the comma-separated keys) and `atl_token`.

The fragment of `/secure/StructureHelpDialog.jspa` (C-5084), with saved help, shows the title as a heading with a question-mark marker, the rendered content, and each contact with avatar and profile link; hovering a contact's name shows Jira's user hover card above the dialog. With no help it shows the heading 'No admin tips'. Both have a 'Close' link that closes the dialog.

Pages sit in Jira's administration frame in the section `structure-admin/structure-admin-main`, with this web item active. `wi-structure-admin`: configuration, projects and permission forms. `wi-structure-defaults`: defaults and its sub-pages. `wi-backup-link`, `wi-restore-link`, `wi-migrate-link`: their pages. `wi-maintenance-link`: both maintenance pages. `wi-support-link`: support, statistics, database troubleshooting, the synchronizer and performance audit logs, and attribute troubleshooting. `wi-attribute-sensitivity-link`: attribute sensitivity. `wi-help-link`: help tool. `wi-structure-setup-guide`: setup guide. The migration configuration pages use the section `structure-admin/structure-admin-other` with `wi-migrate-to-cloud-link`. The dark features page names the main section and no active item. The project settings page uses Jira's project administration frame with `wi-admin-project-structure`.

First section 'Projects with <product>': '<product> enabled for projects:', then 'All projects', or 'None' when none is picked, or a boxed list of project names, then the button 'Enable/disable <product> in projects'. The note of the `synchronization` section (C-5099), which also appears on the support page, is a short paragraph: the synchronizers feature is being deprecated, none is in use and it is hidden from users, and installing new ones needs the dark feature `structure.feature.synchronizers.enabled` set to `true`.

`StructureAdmin!editAppPermission.jspa` shows a form with the permission's section title as both page title and heading, and its edit subtitle. Under the permission's edit label are two radio buttons named `permissionMode`: value `anyone` labelled with the permission's 'anyone' text, and value `selection` labelled 'Users in selected groups/roles', the second with the list of subjects beneath it. Then 'Add group/role' with its controls, and at the bottom 'Apply' and a 'Cancel' link to the cancel target of C-5104. On opening, the radio shows whether the permission is allowed for anyone.

Apply posts to `StructureAdmin!setAppPermission.jspa?permission=<key>` with `permissionMode`, `atl_token`, `returnUrl` when the page received one, and the hidden field `permissionSubjects`: the listed subjects joined by commas with no trailing comma, each being `group:<name>` or `role:<project id>:<role id>`. The list is sent in both modes. A second click on Apply while the page is submitting sends nothing more.

The subject list starts with the permission's current subjects in stored order. Each line reads 'Group: <name>', 'Project: <project> Role: <role>', or 'Project: Any Role: <role>' for project id 0, followed by a trash marker. An unknown project or role shows its raw id instead of a name. Clicking the trash removes that line and its entry from `permissionSubjects`. When the list is empty it shows 'No groups or roles selected'.

While the `anyone` radio is selected the subject list and the 'Add group/role' row are disabled: the add controls cannot be used, the Add button does nothing, and the trash markers do nothing. The subjects stay listed, and return to use when `selection` is chosen.

The 'Add group/role' row has a kind dropdown with 'Group' (`group`, the initial choice) and 'Project' (`role`), and an 'Add' button. For 'Group' one searchable picker of groups is shown; for 'Project' two searchable pickers are shown, project and role. Each picker starts on its first option; the project picker's first option is 'Any' (id 0). Changing the kind shows only its controls and updates the description line.

Clicking 'Add' appends the chosen subject to the list. When the subject is already listed, nothing is added and the existing line is highlighted briefly. Adding to an empty list first removes the 'No groups or roles selected' text. With no group available the group picker is empty, and 'Add' then adds a subject with an empty name (as the original does).

The three pickers search only in the browser, in lists the page received; no request is sent. With an empty search each lists the first N options in the order received, N being the limit of C-5105 (20 by default); for the project picker that is 'Any' and the first N-1 projects. With search text, options whose name matches are listed, shortest name first, at most N; 'Any' is not searched. When more match than are listed, a footer reads 'Showing <N> of <total> matching groups' (or 'projects', 'roles').

Below the row a line describes the subject currently chosen, updated when the kind or a picker changes. For `use`: ' will be enabled for all users in the '' group', '... in the project role '' for project '

'', or '... in the project role '' for any project that is enabled for'. For the others: 'Allow users in '' group to ', 'Allow users in the project role '' for project '

' to ', 'Allow users in the project role '' for any project that is enabled for to ', with X: create new structures, control synchronizers, access automation, configure generators, configure effectors, execute effectors, execute effectors on query results, manage global saved columns.

`StructureAdmin!editProjects.jspa` has the title 'Projects with <product>' and two radio buttons named `allSome`: `all` 'Enable <product> for all projects' and `some` 'Enable <product> for selected projects'. Under the second are two multi-select lists showing 25 rows, 'Selected projects:' (picked projects) and 'Available projects:' (the others), with the buttons '<< Enable' and '>> Disable' between them. The radio is set by the stored choice. While `all` is chosen both lists and both buttons are disabled.

'<< Enable' moves the options selected in 'Available projects:' to 'Selected projects:', and '>> Disable' does the reverse. Moved options are placed in the target list in alphabetical order for the browser's locale. Nothing is sent until Apply.

'Apply' posts to `StructureAdmin!setProjects.jspa` with `allSome`, `projectsList` (the ids of every option in 'Selected projects:', comma-joined, also in `all` mode), `atl_token` and `returnUrl` when the page received one. A second submit is ignored. 'Cancel' links to the page's cancel URL.

`StructureDefaults.jspa` has the title '<product> Defaults' and these sections in order: 'Default Structure' (with a help link to the plugin's documentation), 'Default View Settings', '<product> User Interface Defaults' and '<product> Automation Defaults', each with a short explanatory note, and, under the condition of C-5108, 'Other Defaults', with no note. The first has two halves side by side: 'System Default Structure' and 'Project Default Structures'.

The 'System Default Structure' part shows the label, then the structure's name as a link opening `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>` in a new window with its description as tooltip, or '?' when there is none. Its 'Change' button is a GET form to `StructureDefaults.jspa` with `selectDefaultStructure=true`.

'Project Default Structures' has a checkbox 'Show only projects with overridden default structure', checked on load, and a scrolling table: Project, Default Structure, and a 'Change' link. A project with no own default shows 'system default'. While the checkbox is checked those rows are hidden; unchecking shows them at once, with no request. When the checkbox is checked and every project uses the system default, including when there are no projects, a single row reads 'All projects are configured to use the system default structure'; otherwise that row is hidden.

'Default View Settings' shows 'Views Menu:' with one row per view (name in bold with its description as tooltip, the limit text when limited, and 'ID: <id>') and 'Default Views:' with one row per page that has a default view ('<page name>:' and the view's name). Its 'Change' button is a GET form to `StructureViews.jspa` with `id=0`.

'<product> User Interface Defaults' shows, each with a short help note beside it, 'Auto-switch (Issue Page):', 'Auto-switch (Project Page):', 'Keep Structure Selection When Navigating:' and 'Auto-minimize <product> Panel:', with the current values in the On and Off wording of the form. 'Change' is a GET form with `selectUIDefaults=true`. '<product> Automation Defaults' shows 'Default generation time limit (in seconds):' with its value and 'Change', a GET form with `selectAutomationDefaults=true`. 'Other Defaults' shows 'Allow manual adjustments of generated content:' with the On or Off wording and 'Change', a GET form with `selectOtherDefaults=true`.

The sub-page 'Select System Default Structure' has one dropdown 'System Default Structure:' named `sid`, listing the structures by abbreviated name with the description as tooltip, the current default selected, and a 'Change' button. It posts to `StructureDefaults!apply.jspa` with `selectDefaultStructure=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A `sid` error is shown under the dropdown.

The sub-page has the heading 'Select Default Structure for Project: <name>', the line 'Project: <name> (<key>)', and a dropdown 'Default structure for this project:' named `sid` whose first option is 'Use system default' (value -1), selected when the project has no default of its own, followed by the structures. 'Change' posts to `StructureDefaults!apply.jspa` with `selectProjectDefaultStructure=true`, `projectId`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A `sid` error is shown under the dropdown.

The sub-page '<product> User Interface Defaults' has dropdowns 'Auto-switch (Issue Page):' `autoSwitchIssuePage` and 'Auto-switch (Project Page):' `autoSwitchProjectPage`, whose options are the strategies of C-5112 with their stored codes as values, and two radio pairs with values `true` and `false`. `keepStructureWhenNavigating`: 'On - When going from structure widget to an issue page, show the same structure' and 'Off - On the issue page, the structure initially shown is chosen according to the Auto-Switch settings'. `autoCollapse`: 'On - <product> panel initially minimized if issue is not in structure' and 'Off - <product> panel is shown'. 'Change' posts with `selectUIDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. Each field's error is shown under it.

The sub-page 'Select <product> Automation Defaults' has one required number field 'Default generation time limit (in seconds):' named `generationTimeDefaultLimit`, holding the current value, with the minimum and maximum of C-5113. The field accepts only digit keys, Backspace, Delete, navigation keys and Ctrl or Cmd with A, C, V or X, and normalises its value to a plain integer on each change (leading zeros go). 'Change' posts with `selectAutomationDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

The sub-page 'Other Defaults' has the radio pair `allowManualAdjustments`: `true` 'On - Manual adjustments of generated content will be enabled for newly created structure', `false` 'Off - Manual adjustments of generated content will be disabled for newly created structure', with the current value selected. 'Change' posts with `selectOtherDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

`StructureProjectSettings.jspa` (C-5116) sits in Jira's project administration frame, titled '<product> Defaults - <abbreviated project name>'. It lists 'Project:' with name and key. For an enabled project: '<product>: Enabled for this project'; 'System Default Structure' as a link opening in a new window, or '(structure not visible)'; and 'Project Default Structure' the same way, with a 'Change' button.

Clicking 'Change' on the project settings page, with no request, replaces the structure link with a dropdown `sid` (first option 'Use system default', value -1, selected when the project has no default of its own) and the button with 'Apply'. Apply posts to `StructureProjectSettings!apply.jspa` with `projectKey`, `sid`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. When the page returns with a `sid` error it opens already in this state, with the error under the dropdown.

For a project not enabled, the page shows 'Disabled for this project' in bold and, for a user allowed to enable it, a link 'Select which projects are enabled for <product>' to `/secure/admin/StructureAdmin!view.jspa`; for others the text 'Please contact your Jira administrator to enable <product> for this project.'.

`StructureBackup.jspa` has the title '<product> Backup', a short note on what is and is not backed up (structure data as a zipped XML file, only relationships and references to items; Jira's own data is backed up with Jira's tool), and the warning 'Backup is only enabled into "export" directory in your Jira home.' when there is no export directory. Form: 'File name' with the directory path shown before the field `backupFilename`, and its error under it; 'Backup History' with checkboxes 'Include full change history in the backup. If off, only the current state of the structures is backed up.' and 'Include full change history of memos and planning tasks in the backup.'; and 'Backup Extensions', shown only when there are extensions, with one checkbox per extension. The button 'Create Backup' has access key S and posts to `StructureBackup!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The overwrite page (C-5122) has the title '<product> Backup: Confirm File Overwrite', the warning 'File with that name already exists. Proceeding with backup will overwrite its contents.', the question 'Overwrite <path>?' with the path in bold, a button 'Overwrite File' and a 'Cancel' link. A second submit is ignored.

The result page has the title '<product> Backup Successful', the line '<product> is successfully backed up to:', and a read-only field with the destination path, which has focus with all its text selected when the page opens.

`StructureRestore.jspa` has the title 'Restore Structure from Backup', two notes that say the restore replaces all current <product> data and when to use it rather than Migrate (with a link to `StructureMigrate.jspa`), the warning 'During the restore operation, Structure will not be available.', and, when structures already exist, a warning that all current data will be removed before the import, with a link to `../ManageStructure.jspa?view=recent` in a new window. Form: 'File name (.xml or .zip)' with the directory path shown before the field `restoreFilename`, its error under it; 'Options' with the checkbox `restoreHistories` 'Restore structure history', checked on display. The button 'Restore' has access key S, submit name `restore`, and posts to `StructureRestore!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The confirmation page (C-5133) has the title 'Confirm Clearing <product> Data', a warning that the current structure information will be removed and other Jira data is not affected, a note 'You can create a backup of the current <product> data first.' whose middle part links to `StructureBackup.jspa` in a new window (tooltip 'Backup Structure in a Separate Window'), the button 'Clear Current <product> Data and Restore It from Backup' and a 'Cancel' link to `StructureRestore.jspa`. A second submit is ignored.

The restore result page shows a success message '<product> data has been successfully restored from backup.', or, when aborted, a warning 'Restore process was aborted. <product> data was not fully restored. It is recommended that you restore again.'. For an unowned structure 1, a warning says the backup contains that structure with no owner, that automation does not work without an owner, and links 'Edit Structure Settings' to `<base URL>/secure/EditStructure.jspa?id=1` in a new window. Warnings follow the order of C-5138. Sub-headings are 'Structure "<name>" (#<id>):', 'Could not include the following items in the structure (all other items are included):', 'Could not include the following items in the change history (as a result, the change history may have become partially incorrect):', 'Could not restore the following synchronizers in structure (all other synchronizers have been restored):', and synchronizer lines read 'Synchronizer #<id>' with ': <message>' when there is one.

`StructureMigrate.jspa` has the title '<product> Migration / Partial Import', two notes that say structures are restored from a backup without affecting existing ones unless overwriting is chosen, that issues must already be in Jira and are matched by Issue Key, and when to use it rather than Restore (with a link to `StructureRestore.jspa`), and the warning 'During the restore operation, Structure will not be available.'. Form: 'File name (.xml or .zip)' with the directory path before the field `restoreFilename`, its error under it. The button 'Select Structures to Restore' has access key S and posts to `StructureMigrate!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The options page has the title 'Select Structures to Restore', a note on choosing structures and overwriting, and a table with columns Action, ID, Name, Items, Projects, 'Has Synchronizers?', 'Has Adjustments?' (only when manual adjustments are enabled), 'Has History?' and 'Has Memo and Planning task history?', the 'Has...' columns reading Yes or No. Each Action cell has a checkbox `migrate-st-<id>` 'Restore', checked; when the structure would overwrite, also a checkbox `st-<id>-overwrite` 'Overwrite existing', unchecked. The Name cell shows the abbreviated name, an 'Archived' marker when archived, the description, and the warnings of C-5150 and C-5151. An unknown project shows its bare key as a warning.
Above the table are the buttons 'Clear Selection' and 'Select All', then 'Overwrite All' only when some structure can overwrite, and 'Deselect All Archived' only when some structure is archived.

Unchecking a structure's 'Restore' disables its 'Overwrite existing' block, greyed out and with its inputs not sent; checking enables it again. The 'Restore Selected Structures' button is enabled only while at least one 'Restore' is checked.

None of the bulk buttons submits the form. 'Select All' checks every 'Restore' and enables every overwrite block, leaving 'Overwrite existing' as it was. 'Clear Selection' unchecks every 'Restore' and every 'Overwrite existing' and disables the blocks. 'Overwrite All' checks every 'Overwrite existing', also in disabled blocks. After 'Select All', 'Clear Selection' and 'Deselect All Archived' the submit button's state is updated.
'Deselect All Archived' unchecks 'Restore' and 'Overwrite existing' of each archived structure, but leaves that structure's overwrite block enabled (as the original does).

The option 'Restore view settings for structures' (`migrateViewAssociations`), indented under 'Restore views', and its label are enabled only while 'Restore views' (`migrateViews`) is checked; disabled, it is not sent.

Under 'Options' the checkboxes of C-5152 read, in order: 'Restore structure permissions', 'Restore synchronizers', 'Restore manual adjustments', 'Restore structure history', 'Restore user favorites', 'Restore views', 'Restore view settings for structures', 'Restore structure properties', 'Restore structure item properties', 'Restore configuration', 'Restore dark features', 'Restore saved columns', 'Restore generic item history', 'Restore notes', then 'Restore <name> app data' per extension. There is no perspectives option. The warnings of C-5151 appear directly below 'Restore synchronizers' and 'Restore configuration'.

The form ends with 'Restore Selected Structures', which ignores a second submit, and a 'Cancel' link to `StructureMigrate.jspa`. When some structures are unrestorable a warning at the top links to the fragment `#unrestorable`, and after the form the heading 'Unrestorable Structures' introduces a read-only table with the same columns minus Action. With no selectable structure there is no form, only an error note saying that Jira must contain the projects referred to and suggesting Project Import, plus that table if any.

The migrate result page has the title '<product> Migration Completed Successfully' and the success message 'Selected structures were restored from the backup.'. Warnings use the sub-headings of the restore result page, and then 'Some structure perspectives were saved under new IDs:' with rows 'Perspective <old> has now ID of <new>.'. The warnings block also appears when only perspective ids changed.

`StructureMaintenance.jspa` has the title '<product> Maintenance' with a help link to the plugin's documentation, and a two-paragraph note on what maintenance does. Section 'Scheduled Maintenance': an info note 'Scheduled maintenance is enabled and runs daily.' with 'Last run:' and 'Next run:' times, or a warning 'Automatic maintenance is not scheduled. It is recommended to enable daily maintenance procedure.', then the button 'Configure Scheduled Maintenance', a GET to `StructureMaintenance.jspa` with `editScheduledParams=true`. An error note 'Last run of the scheduled maintenance finished with errors, please check Jira logs for details.' appears above when the last run failed.

Section 'Run Maintenance Now': while a process runs, the note 'Maintenance is running now.' with the link 'Open Progress Page', and no form. Otherwise 'Last manual run: <time>', the task list, and the button 'Run Maintenance Now', which posts to `StructureMaintenance!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

The scheduled form has the title 'Scheduled Maintenance Settings' and the checkbox `scheduled` 'Enable scheduled maintenance'. Under it are two radio buttons named `crontabEnabled`: `false` 'Run daily at' with dropdowns `scheduledHour` (00 to 23) and `scheduledMinute` (00 to 55 in steps of 5) followed by the time zone in brackets, and `true` 'Crontab schedule' with the field `crontabSchedule` and a help link to the plugin's documentation. Then the task list. 'Apply' posts to `StructureMaintenance!apply.jspa` with `editScheduledParams=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`; 'Cancel' links to `StructureMaintenance.jspa`. After a crontab error the crontab radio is selected, the rejected text stays in the field, and 'Invalid crontab schedule: <text>' is shown. A form error is shown as an error note at the top.

Each task has a checkbox named by its key, a label and sometimes a description. In order: `backup` 'Backup <product> data', with sub-option `backup-saveHistory` 'Include full change history of all structures in the backup'; `removeOldBackups` 'Delete old backups'; `cleanupFavorites` 'Optimize favorites' (delete marks of users no longer in Jira, fix popularity counters); `cleanupForests` 'Optimize structures' (remove references to permanently unavailable items); `cleanupViews` 'Optimize view settings' (remove references to deleted views); `cleanupSynchronizers` 'Optimize synchronizers' (remove those of deleted structures); `cleanupStructureProperties` 'Optimize properties' (remove those of deleted structures); `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords` 'Delete old synchronizer audit log records'; `reindexHistory` 'Reindex change history' (so entries appear in filtered activity streams); `cleanupPerspectives` 'Optimize structure perspectives'; `reindexStructures` 'Reindex structures' (recalculate which structures contain an issue); `removeOldChangeHistory` 'Delete old change history'; `removeOldEffectorProcesses` 'Delete old effector processes'; `removeOldProcessStates` 'Optimize old background processes' ('Delete old background process records'); and, on Data Center only, `cleanupItemTracker` 'Clear item events table' ('Highly recommended after removing or renaming Jira DC cluster nodes'). Values come from `maintenance-manager`'s form values: run-once values on the main page, scheduled values on the scheduled form.

Number fields, each a text field of at most 3 characters between a prefix and a suffix, with name | text | whether 0 is allowed. `removeOldBackups-minFilesToKeep` | 'Always keep <n> latest backups.' | no. `removeOldBackups-minDaysToKeep` | 'Always keep backups made during last <n> days.' | no. `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords-daysToKeep` | 'Keep records for the last <n> days (0 means remove all).' | yes. `cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep` | 'Delete perspectives that were not used during the last <n> days.' | no. `removeOldChangeHistory-daysToKeep` | 'Always keep changes made during last <n> days.' | yes. `removeOldChangeHistory-changesPerStructureToKeep` | 'Always keep <n> latest changes for each structure.' | yes. `removeOldEffectorProcesses-daysToKeep` | 'Always keep processes finished during last <n> days.' | yes. `removeOldEffectorProcesses-waitingPreviewHoursToKeep` | 'Always keep processes waiting for a preview confirmation <n> hours.' | yes. Each belongs under the task of the same prefix.

On submit each enabled number field is checked in the browser: a field that does not allow 0 needs an integer above 0, the others an integer of 0 or more. A failing field shows its message below it: 'Please enter a positive number.' for all of them, also where 0 is allowed; messages of passing fields hide. On the run-now form, and on the scheduled form while `scheduled` is checked, at least one top-level task must be checked (a sub-option such as `backup-saveHistory` does not count), otherwise 'Please select at least one task to execute.' is shown. Any failure stops the submit. A field that allows 0 shows that same message, although 0 is valid there (as the original does).

A task's sub-options and number fields are enabled only while the task's checkbox is checked and, on the scheduled form, `scheduled` is checked too. Disabled fields are skipped by validation and not sent.

On the scheduled form, unchecking `scheduled` disables all task checkboxes, both radios, the hour and minute dropdowns and the crontab field. With `scheduled` checked, the crontab field is enabled only for `crontabEnabled=true`, and the hour and minute dropdowns only for the other choice. Changes apply at once, without a request.

`StructureSupport.jspa` has the title '<product> Support' and these sections in order, each with a short note: 'Troubleshooting', 'Collecting Support ZIP', 'Synchronizer Audit Log', 'Performance Audit Log', 'Attribute Troubleshooting', 'S-JQL Troubleshooting', 'Database Troubleshooting', 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' and 'Clear Caches'.
