`PerformanceAuditLogView.jspa` has the title 'Performance Audit Log', the warning 'Please note that the log may contain sensitive data. Please review it before sending.', a 20-row text area with the dump of C-5202, and the button 'Save to File', a GET to the same page with the submit name `save` and any non-empty value (C-5204). It does not ask about leaving the page.

`StructuredJqlTroubleshooting.jspa` is framed as a general Jira page, not an admin page. It has the title 'Structured JQL Troubleshooting', a note with numbered steps: enter the structure's name or id and the query as in the `structure()` JQL function; tick the relations option only when asked to; click 'Run Query', and a correct query downloads the log file `S-JQL_Troubleshooting.zip`, and a form: 'Name' ('Name or ID of the structure to search in.'), 'S-JQL' (a multi-line field, described as the parameter of the `structure()` JQL function) and a checkbox 'Include output from relations (very verbose, please do not check unless we asked you to)', unchecked; then the button 'Run Query'. The form never submits as a page. The note's links go to the plugin's documentation and it does not name the vendor.

'Run Query' trims the query text and, when it is longer than one character and starts and ends with the same quote, `'` or `"`, removes that pair. Examples: `  'folder'  ` is sent as `folder`, `"a"` as `a`, `'a"` stays, a lone `'` stays. Only the outer pair goes. The structure text is sent as typed.
'Run Query' sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check?structure=<text>&query=<query>`, asking for JSON. The checkbox is not part of this call.

When the check succeeds the error box hides and the browser goes to `/rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs?structure=<text>&query=<query>&includeRelOutput=<true|false>`, which downloads the ZIP (C-4502), so the page stays where it is. `messagePattern` is never sent.

On a 400 whose body is a non-empty JSON array, the error box shows the messages, HTML-escaped: the single message as plain text, or a bullet list when there are several. Any other failure, including a body that does not parse, shows the shared HTTP error report (a title and details, as `jsutil` formats it). The box stays visible until the next successful check, and no download starts.

`StructureDarkFeatures.jspa` has the title '<product> Dark Features and Fine Tuning' and the warning 'Please be careful! Entering an incorrect value for a property may lead to unpredictable results. Make sure you follow the instructions from support.'. On opening the page sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`. Until the answer nothing else shows. On failure it shows 'Failed to load property values. More information should be in the logs.' and no form. On success it shows the add form 'Property Key' (`darkFeatureKey`) with 'Add Property', and, when at least one row exists, a table with columns Key, Value and actions. Neither form triggers Jira's unsaved-changes warning.

Rows from the load keep the server's order. A key added later goes to the top of the table, and the table appears if it was hidden. Rows are never removed: a deleted key stays listed until the page is reloaded.
A row at rest shows the key, the value (empty when null) and two icons: pencil and trash. The trash icon is disabled, not clickable and out of the tab order, when the server's `removable` is false.

Clicking the pencil replaces the value with a text field holding the current value, focused, and the icons with a tick and a cross. The cross, or Escape in the field, leaves edit mode without a request and discards the typing. The next edit starts from the stored value again.

The tick, or Enter in the field, sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the JSON body `{"key": <key>, "value": <text>}`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Success shows the new value and enables the trash icon. Edit mode ends on success and on failure. A failure shows no message and the old value stays.

The trash icon opens the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`), medium size, with 'Property "<key>" will be removed and it will assume its default value. Proceed?'. Confirming sends `DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the key as raw body text and `Content-Type: application/json`. On success the row stays, its value becomes the text of the answer (the JVM value, empty for a 204), and the trash icon is disabled. A failure shows nothing and changes nothing. Cancelling sends nothing.

Submitting the add form, by button or Enter, trims the text. A key already in the table shows 'This key is already in the table below. Click the pencil icon to edit the value.' under the field, clears the field and sends nothing; the row is not highlighted. Otherwise it sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the key as raw body text and `Content-Type: application/json`. Success adds a row from the answer, clears the field and any error. Failure shows the answer's text under the field and keeps the field. Typing in the field hides the error.

`StructureAttributeSensitivity.jspa` has the title 'Attribute Sensitivity Settings', a note of a few paragraphs on the trade-off between protecting data and all users seeing the same totals, and 'Loading...'. On opening it sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity` and also loads the attribute metadata needed for labels, through the shared attribute registry of `widget-bare`. When both finish the loading text goes and the form shows. When either fails, an error flag that cannot be closed says 'There was a problem loading data from the server. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.' and the page stays on 'Loading...'.

The answer is cleaned in the browser. `sensitivityMode` outside 0 to 2 counts as 0. A spec lacking a string `id` or `format` is dropped. A non-object `params` is dropped. Each spec is normalised as attribute specs are in the widget. Specs are sorted by id, then format, then their JSON text. Saves send this cleaned list, so a dropped entry disappears from the server on the next save.

Section 'Attribute Sensitivity Mode' has a dropdown 'Mode' with Standard (0), Strict (1), Permissive (2), the button 'Change Attribute Sensitivity Mode', and a description: Standard: all attributes are sensitive except numeric and date-based. Strict: all attributes are sensitive. Permissive: no attribute is considered sensitive (recommended only if all your Jira users can see all issues). The button is enabled and emphasised only while the dropdown differs from the saved mode and no save is running, updating within 50 ms.

Every change is saved by `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity` with JSON body `{"sensitivityMode": <n>, "nonSensitiveAttributeSpecs": [...]}`, always the whole settings. On success the page takes what it sent as the new state, without a reload, and shows a success flag that closes by itself: 'Attribute sensitivity mode has been changed.', 'Non-sensitive attribute has been added to the list.', 'Non-sensitive attribute specification has been edited.' or 'Non-sensitive attribute specification has been removed from the list.'. On failure a flag that the user closes says 'Error uploading changes. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.', and the dropdown returns to the saved mode.

Section 'Additional Non-Sensitive Attributes', with the button 'Add Non-Sensitive Attribute', is shown unless the saved mode is Permissive; changing the dropdown alone does not hide it. Table columns: Name, Attribute Specification, and icons. Name is the attribute's suggested label, or 'Customized' when none can be made. Attribute Specification is the spec's JSON, also as tooltip. Icon tooltips: 'Edit non-sensitive attribute's specification' and 'Remove specification from the list of non-sensitive attributes'.

The Add dialog, titled 'Add Non-Sensitive Attribute' with buttons 'Add' and 'Cancel', and the Edit dialog, titled 'Edit Non-Sensitive Attribute Specification' with 'Update' and 'Cancel', are modal and have the same fields: 'Spec', a multi-line JSON text with the placeholder 'Enter attribute specification in JSON format. See documentation for details.' and no browser autocomplete or spellcheck; 'Attribute', the shared attribute editor; 'Format', a dropdown with the placeholder 'Select format...' and options Any format (`any`), Text (`text`), HTML (`html`), Number (`number`), Boolean (`boolean`), Time (`time`), Duration (`duration`). Add opens empty; Edit opens on the row's spec. Closing discards the fields.

The three fields stay in step. After typing pauses for 300 ms in 'Spec' (50 ms for the first update), when the text is valid JSON the attribute editor loads it and 'Format' shows its `format`; invalid JSON leaves the editor alone and clears 'Format'. A change in the attribute editor rewrites 'Spec' at once and updates 'Format'. Choosing a format sets `format` in the JSON of 'Spec' when that text parses; otherwise it has no effect on 'Spec'.
While a save runs, the fields in the open dialog are disabled, and any button inside its content area is disabled. The footer buttons stay enabled.

'Add', in this order: text that is not valid JSON shows an error flag 'Cannot parse JSON specification. Please check if it is valid.' that closes itself; a spec deep-equal to a listed one shows 'The specified attribute is already in the list.' the same way; otherwise `POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity/validate` is sent with the spec as JSON body. A failed validation shows a flag the user closes, 'The entered attribute specification cannot be validated: <answer text>', and the dialog stays. A valid spec is appended and saved; on success the dialog closes, on failure it stays.

'Update', in this order: invalid JSON gives the same parse flag as Add. When the spec is unchanged, or the original is no longer listed, the dialog just closes and nothing is sent. A spec deep-equal to another listed one gives the duplicate flag. Otherwise it is validated as for Add, replaces the original in the list, and is saved. On success the dialog closes, on failure it stays.

The trash icon opens the dialog 'Remove Attribute from Non-Sensitive List', not modal, with the text 'If you remove an attribute from the non-sensitive list, its sensitivity will be determined by the selected Attribute Sensitivity Mode.', the question 'Would you like to remove the following attribute from the list?', the spec's JSON in a read-only box, and the buttons 'Remove' and 'Cancel'. 'Remove' saves the list without the spec and closes on success. When the spec is no longer listed it just closes.

When saving a removal fails, two identical error flags appear, 'Error uploading changes. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.', and the dialog stays open (as the original does).

`SyncAuditLogView.jspa` has the title 'Synchronizer Audit Log' and the heading 'Find log entries' over a GET form to `SyncAuditLogView.jspa` that does not trigger Jira's unsaved-changes warning. 'Earliest entry': 'Date' `dateFrom` (Jira's date picker) and 'Time' `timeFrom`. 'Latest entry': 'Date' `dateTo` and 'Time' `timeTo`. 'Other conditions': 'Sync instance ID' `syncInstanceId` ('Display only entries for a synchronizer instance.'), 'Structure ID' `structureId` ('Display only actions for sync instances installed on a structure.') and the checkbox `showEmpty` 'Show entries without actions'. Date and time errors are shown under their fields. Buttons: 'Show' and 'Save to File' (submit name `save`). Fields hold the request's values.

Field help. `dateFrom`: 'Leave blank to show log entries from the beginning of time.'. `timeFrom`: 'Time of day (18:43), timestamp (1455715432286) or complete date and time (2016-02-26 19:11:09.460 +0400). Leave blank for midnight (if date is specified).'. `dateTo`: 'Leave blank to show log entries until now.'. `timeTo`: 'Time of day (18:44), timestamp (1455715433286) or complete date and time (2016-02-26 19:12:09.460 +0400). Leave blank for midnight.'. Tooltips: 'Date of the earliest log entry to display', 'Time of day of the earliest log entry to display', 'Date of the latest log entry to display', 'Time of day of the latest log entry to display', and, on `structureId`, 'Numeric structure ID. Leave blank to show entries for all synchronizer instances.'; on `syncInstanceId`, a tooltip says how to find the id on the synchronization settings page and that blank means all instances.
While 'Sync instance ID' holds non-blank text after trimming, 'Structure ID' is disabled, so it is not sent. This is applied on page load and on each change.

With no selected group, the page shows only 'No entries found.' below the form. Otherwise it shows the anchor `entries` and two tabs, 'View' (active) and 'Undo'. The View tab has the heading 'Selected log entries', the links 'Expand all actions' and 'Collapse all actions', the table, and then the cut-off warning of C-5286 or, when more than 5 groups are shown and none is cut off, '<n> entries displayed.'.

The third part of the cut-off warning is 'You may specify more precise time to select fewer entries.' when `timeFrom` or `timeTo` is empty; otherwise 'You may specify synchronizer instance ID to select fewer entries.' when no instance id is given; otherwise nothing.

Table columns: a checkbox column whose header checkbox selects all; 'Time'; 'Structure'; 'SIID' (tooltip 'Synchronizer instance ID'); 'Synchronizer'; 'Entry description', with the links 'Expand all' and 'Collapse all' in its header. A group's row holds the values of C-5287. A group with actions has a second row with its checkbox (only when undoable, C-5290, tooltip 'Select these actions for bulk undo') and 'Actions (<n>):', an 'expand' link that turns into 'collapse', and, when undoable, a link 'undo'. Actions are collapsed at first. The structure link opens in a new window.

Description and action data are JSON objects rendered as nested lists of `key: value` lines, in the object's order, on page load; a spinner shows in the cell before that. An object with `type` = `link` and non-empty `url` and `text` renders as a link. An object with more than 2 keys is collapsed behind a `+` control that turns into `-`; one with 1 or 2 keys is shown open. An empty array shows `[]`. An array of plain values is a bullet list of their text. A one-element array of objects shows that object inline. A longer one is a list of them. Each action at the top level of a group's list is shown open. Under the keys `jiraEvents` and `structureEvents`, and for objects of at most 2 keys, the object is shown on one line, not collapsed. Null shows as the text `null`.

'Expand all actions' and 'Collapse all actions' expand or collapse every group's action list. 'Expand all' and 'Collapse all' in the 'Entry description' header do the same to every collapsed object in descriptions and actions. No request is sent.

The header checkbox has the tooltip 'Select all actions for undo', changing to 'Deselect all actions' while checked, and is hidden when no group is undoable. It selects or clears all groups. It becomes checked when every group is selected and unchecked when none is. Selecting only some leaves it as it was.
Clicking a group's 'undo' link selects that group and switches to the 'Undo' tab. It keeps earlier selections and sends nothing.

With nothing selected, the 'Undo' tab shows the hint 'Select some actions in the View tab to undo them.'. Otherwise it shows the heading 'Selected actions', each selected group's actions with a checkbox that is checked (clearing it deselects the group here and in the View tab), and the button 'Undo'.

'Undo' disables the inputs of the Undo tab, shows a spinner, hides any earlier results, and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`, a 60-second timeout, and the body `{"actionGroups": [...], "syncModuleKeys": [...]}`: for each selected group in page order, its actions as the JSON text received with the page, and its synchronizer's module key at the same index.

When an answer carries `jobId`, the same POST is sent again at once with the body `{"jobId": <id>}`, with no delay and no limit on the number of calls, until an answer has no `jobId`. Each call has its own 60-second timeout.

When the undo ends, successfully or not, the inputs are enabled, the spinner goes, the 'Undo results' area shows with its old content cleared, and all selections are cleared. Success: a success message 'Undo has completed. See below the list of actions that we've taken.', then each non-empty group of `actionGroups` from the answer rendered as action lists; a group that is not valid JSON or is empty adds nothing. Failure: an error message 'Failed to retrieve undo results. The actions might or might not have been executed. For more information, please refer to Jira logs.', then 'Technical details', 'textStatus: <status>' and 'errorThrown: <error>'.
The 'Undo results' area has the heading 'Undo results' and the button 'Acknowledge', which hides the area. It is hidden until the first undo ends. The page's log table is not reloaded after an undo.

`StructureMigrationConfigurations!list.jspa` has the title '<product> Migration Configurations' and an information note: specify which structures go in each migration when using Jira's Cloud Migration Assistant, limiting each to structures whose projects are migrated or already were; with a link to the plugin's documentation. With no configurations: 'There are no configurations yet.' and the primary button 'Create new configuration'. Otherwise that button, then a table with columns Name, Structures, Created By, Status, Completed On and Actions. The button links to `StructureMigrationConfigurations!create.jspa`.

Each row's Actions cell is a menu button. Entries in order: for a draft 'Edit' (`!edit`) and 'Make Ready for Migration' (tooltip 'Change status to "Ready"'); for a ready configuration 'View' (`!view`) and 'Move to Draft' (tooltip 'Change status to "Draft" and edit this configuration'); for others 'View'; and always 'Delete'. The URLs are those of C-5180.

'Delete' in the list, and 'Delete Configuration' in the form, open the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`) with 'Are you sure you want to delete this configuration?'. Confirming sends `POST StructureMigrationConfigurations!delete.jspa?id=<id>&atl_token=<token>` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, following redirects. When the answer was redirected the browser replaces the current page with the final URL, without any leave-page warning. A failed call, or one not redirected, shows nothing. Cancelling sends nothing.

The form page has the browser title 'Create Migration Configuration', 'Edit Migration Configuration' or 'View Migration Configuration' (C-5182, C-5183). It begins with a breadcrumb: a link 'Migration configurations' to `!list`, ' / ' and the name in bold; then a warning line 'Configuration name must match the migration name from the Jira Cloud Migration Assistant.'. Fields: 'Name' (required, `name`) with its error beneath; 'Status' showing the status marker and its description; one checkbox `migrate-ext-<key>` per extension labelled as C-5182; a warning note listing what does not carry over to the cloud (the projects of the selected structures must be migrated in the same or an earlier migration for their issues to appear, some automations including effectors are not supported, memos become folders, and only custom views associated with the selected structures are migrated), with a link to the plugin's documentation; and the heading 'Structures'. The `structureIds` error is shown under the structures.

Status texts, as label: description. Draft: 'The configuration is being created. When it's all set, click "Save and Make Ready for Migration."'. Ready: 'The configuration can be used to migrate to Cloud. To change it, move it to the Draft status first.'. Running: 'Migration is currently in progress.'. Done: 'Migration has been completed.'. Failed: 'Migration has been completed with errors.'.

For any status but Draft the form is read-only: the name, the extension checkboxes and the all-structures toggle are disabled, the structure picker and the Actions column are absent, and the Save buttons are absent.

Form buttons. Left: 'Delete Configuration' (tooltip 'Delete this migration configuration') when the configuration has an id; 'Move to Draft' when Ready, submitting to `!draft`. Right: for a draft, 'Save and Make Ready for Migration' (tooltip 'Save changes and change status to "Ready"'), submitting to `!publish`, and 'Save as Draft' (tooltip 'Save changes to this draft'), submitting to `!save`; and always 'Cancel', a link to `!list`. Submits carry `atl_token`, `id`, `name`, the extension checkboxes, `allStructures` when on, and `structureIds`.

'Cancel' with no changes just follows the link. With changes it opens the shared confirmation dialog with 'The changes made to this configuration were not saved. Are you sure you want to dismiss them?'; confirming goes to the list without a leave-page warning. A change is: the name differs from the page's initial value; an extension checkbox differs from its initial state; the all-structures toggle differs; or the id list differs, order included. Adding a structure and removing it again is no change.

Leaving the page by other means with unsaved changes triggers Jira's unsaved-changes warning. That covers the name, the extension checkboxes, the structure list and the all-structures toggle, although the last two are not plain form fields.

A toggle 'Migrate all structures and views', field `allStructures` with value `true`. On: the table is replaced by 'Structures: <total>' and `structureIds` is sent empty. Off: the table shows and `structureIds` is the listed ids joined by commas. The list is kept while the toggle is on, so turning it off brings it back.

The table has columns Name, Statistics, Description, and, when editable, Actions. With no ids a single row says 'No structures selected'. Rows follow the id list; a newly added structure goes to the top.

When editable, a search field with the placeholder 'Add structure' sits above the table. It sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure?name=<text>&archived=true&limit=20&page=<n>&skip=<ids joined by dots>` after 500 ms of pause in typing, and offers `structures` with more pages while `haveMore` is true. An option shows the name, with the tooltip '<name> [#<id>]'. Picking adds the structure, unless it is listed, and clears the field. `skip` holds the ids listed at that moment, so listed structures are not offered.

Each row loads its structure with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/<id>`, at most once per id per page. While loading, the row shows 'Loading...' across the first three columns; on failure 'Structure #<id> is unavailable' there. The Actions cell shows in all states. Loaded, Name is a link to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>` in a new window, and Description is the structure's description. A failed load stays failed until the page is reloaded.
The 'Remove' link in the Actions column removes the row at once, with no request and no confirmation.

The Statistics cell starts as the link 'Collect'. Clicking it shows 'Loading...' and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/<id>` with body `{}`, polling through the shared transport while the answer holds only `jobId`. The answer is cached per id for the page, so a removed and re-added row shows it again without a request, or joins a running request. On failure the cell shows 'N/A' and cannot be retried until the page is reloaded.

With `size` 0 the Statistics cell shows 'Empty structure'. Otherwise it shows lines of a bold label and a value, each only when its value is non-zero, in this order: 'Size:' only when `size` differs from issues + folders + memos + pages + generators + effectors; 'Manually added issues:'; 'Projects:' (`projects` joined by ', ', only when issues are present and the list is not empty); 'Folders:'; 'Memos:'; 'Pages:'; 'Generators:'; 'Effectors:'. The generators value is the count followed by the non-zero kinds in brackets. Example: size 12, issues 5, folders 1, generators 2, inserters 1, groupers 1 gives 'Size: 12', 'Manually added issues: 5', 'Folders: 1', 'Generators: 2 (inserters: 1, groupers: 1)', with a non-breaking space after each kind's colon. Kinds are listed as inserters, extenders, groupers, filters, sorters. With no non-zero kind the brackets are empty (as the original does).

Web-resource `filtersync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`. The `sync-filter` form requires it when rendered and starts its behaviour as soon as the form is on the page; loading the resource alone does nothing except fetch the JQL search data (see the next claims).

On the `sync-filter` form the filter choice has two radio buttons. With `savedFilter` chosen the saved-filter area shows and the JQL area hides; with `jql` chosen the JQL area shows and the saved-filter area hides; with neither chosen both are hidden. The switch happens at once on change, and the state is applied on page load from the rendered selection.

On load the `sync-filter` form starts fetching Jira's JQL autocomplete data once. The first time the JQL area is shown, once that fetch has finished (success or failure), autocomplete with live validation is attached to the JQL text area, its status shown beside the field. Later the same instance is only re-enabled. Each time the area shows the text area gets focus. Switching to the saved filter disables autocomplete.

Clicking Select on the `sync-filter` form opens Jira's own filter picker in a popup window named `filter_sf_window`, 800 by 500, resizable with scrollbars, at `/secure/FilterPickerPopup.jspa?showProjects=false&field=sf` (context path prepended), and focuses it; the link itself does not navigate. For the picker to report back, the form exposes the elements Jira's popup looks for with field `sf`: `filter_sf_id` on the hidden `filterid` input, `filter_sf_name_h` on the hidden `filtername` input and `filter_sf_name` on the visible name.

When the `sync-filter` form is submitted with a picked saved filter id, the visible filter name is copied into the hidden `filtername` field first, so that a form redisplayed after a validation error still shows the name. With no id nothing is copied.

Dependent controls of the `sync-filter` form enable and disable live, and disabled ones are not submitted: unchecking Add disables both placement radios; the parent issue key input and the Allow move checkbox are enabled only when Add is checked and the placement is `under`; unchecking Remove disables its two sub-options (`removeWhereAdd`, `forceReCheck`).

The `sync-filter` form's first field is labelled `Filter`, with radios `Saved filter` (`filtertype=savedFilter`) and `JQL query` (`filtertype=jql`). The saved-filter part has hidden `filterid` and `filtername`, then the filter's name when one is known, styled as a success value, or `No filter selected`, then a `Select` link. The JQL part is a 2-row, 45-column text area `filterjql`. Field errors for `filterid` and `filterjql` show under their parts.

The `sync-filter` form's field `Add` has checkbox `add` with text `If an issue passes the filter, add it to the structure.`; radios `addWhere`: `root` `Place added issue at the top level` (selected unless the value is `under`) and `under` `Place added issue as a sub-issue of` followed by a 10-wide text input `addUnder` whose tooltip is `Please enter issue key of the parent issue.`; and nested under them checkbox `addMoveForced`: `Allow move: if the matching issue is already in the structure, but it's not under this "parent" issue, move it.` The `addUnder` error shows under the radio.

The `sync-filter` form's field `Remove` has checkbox `remove` with text `Remove from structure issues that don't pass the filter.` and sub-options `removeWhereAdd` `Remove only from where added issues are placed` and `forceReCheck` `Double-check sub-issues when parent issue no longer passes the filter`. The error under key `remove` shows at the end of this field.
Web-resource `ghsync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util`. The `sync-gh` form requires it when rendered and starts its behaviour once the form is on the page.

On the `sync-gh` form choosing mode `rapidview` shows the board part and hides the projects part; any other mode, including no mode radios at all (boards not supported), shows the projects part and hides the board part. The ranking options (description, Independent and Consecutive radios, explanation) are one block that moves between the two parts, so there is one set of them in the form.

On the `sync-gh` form the multi-select of projects is initialised on load from the hidden comma-separated `projects` value, and on each change the selected ids are written back to it joined with `,`. Only `projects` carries the selection to the server.

When no project is eligible on the `sync-gh` form the project controls are not rendered, and the form's script stops with an error at the project step, so the ranking block is never enabled or disabled by the rules of the next claim (as the original does).

The ranking options of the `sync-gh` form are enabled when, in board mode, `Synchronize Rank` is checked, and in projects mode when a rank field is selected (non-empty); otherwise their inputs are disabled, hence not submitted, and the description is shown as disabled. The rule follows live, and survives the rank field select being rebuilt when the project selection changes.

The `sync-gh` form starts with the Source of Truth field and, under it, its description `Directs the resolution of conflicts between changes. A conflict is always resolved in favor of either Structure or Jira. Also defines the resync direction.` Then, only when boards can be used, field `Use` with radios `mode`: `rapidview` `Agile Board configuration` and `classic` `Custom projects and fields`, `classic` selected when there is no `viewId` or the mode is `classic`.

The board part of the `sync-gh` form has select `viewId` labelled `Agile Board` listing the boards the user sees by name; a stored id not among them adds a selected option `?`. Then checkbox `syncRank` `Synchronize Rank` and the ranking block: description `Rank will only be synchronized if Ranking is configured for Agile Board.`, radios `independentRanking` `true` `Independent ranking: rank parent issues separately from their sub-issues` and `false` `Consecutive ranking: rank all issues in the order they appear in structure`, the latter selected when the value is not true, and a note saying consecutive ranking is what older versions used. A `viewId` error shows under the select.

On the `sync-gh` form the `Synchronize Rank` checkbox is rendered disabled whenever the epic service is unavailable, so with Jira Software's epic service absent rank cannot be chosen, although rank does not depend on epics (as the original does).

The projects part of the `sync-gh` form has field `Projects`: a multi-select of eligible projects by name, with hidden `projects`, or, with none eligible, the text `No projects suitable for synchronization available`. Then select `rankField` labelled `Rank field`: first option value empty `Don't synchronize`, then each rank custom field as `<name> [<field id>]`; a stored value not listed adds a selected option `?`, which stays through option rebuilding. The options are limited to fields applicable to the selected projects (the shared cascading select). Errors for `project` and `rankField` show under their fields.

The `sync-gh` form ends with, only when the epic service is available, checkbox `syncEpics` `Synchronize Epics` with the description `Jira Software (Jira Agile 6.1+) Epics will be used for synchronization.` and any `syncEpics` error; and always checkbox `subtasks` `Auto-add sub-tasks` with a sentence saying sub-tasks are added under their parent, like the sub-tasks synchronizer.

The shared Source of Truth field, on the `sync-gh` and `sync-links` forms, is labelled `Source of Truth` with radios `sourceOfTruth`: `jira` `Jira`, selected unless the value is `structure`, and `structure` `Structure`. An error under `sourceOfTruth` shows below them.

Web-resource `linksync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`. The `sync-links` form requires it, and loading it starts fetching Jira's JQL search data once.

On the `sync-links` form the two options of the `direction` select take their text from the chosen link type: `out` shows its outward description, `in` its inward one, `?` when the chosen option has none (an unknown stored type). This runs on load and on each change of the link type.
On the `sync-links` form the checkboxes `expandchild` and `expandparent` are disabled while `useall` is `true` and enabled otherwise, live and on load.

On the `sync-links` form the description under the primacy checkbox follows the Source of Truth: with `structure` it reads `Structure primacy: Reverse issue link creation/deletion if it contradicts structure`, otherwise `Links primacy: Reverse structure change if it contradicts issue links`.

The `sync-links` form has two filters, parent and child, each with the behaviour of the `sync-filter` form's filter choice with these differences: a third radio `none` hides both areas and disables autocomplete; the picker opens with field `parentsf` or `childsf`, in window `filter_parentsf_window` or `filter_childsf_window`, same size and URL pattern; the elements for Jira's popup are `filter_<field>_id`, `filter_<field>_name_h` and `filter_<field>_name`; each JQL area has its own autocomplete.

When the `sync-links` form is submitted, each filter with a picked id copies its visible name into hidden `parentfiltername` or `childfiltername`. This is attached through the link type select, so with no link types available it does not happen.

The `sync-links` form has the inputs on the left and a help text beside each on the right, in sections: `1. Select Source of Truth and Primacy`, `2. Select Link Type and Direction`, `3. Issue Filters (Optional)`, with a line saying that several links synchronizers on one structure should each have a limited scope to avoid conflicts, and `4. Adjust Advanced Options (Optional)`, with a line saying these give more control but need understanding.

Help texts of the `sync-links` form, each a paragraph or a few, naming the field in bold: Source of Truth (how conflicts resolve, resync direction, which contradicting changes are reverted with primacy); Primacy, 4 or 5 paragraphs (what incremental sync does with primacy off, Structure primacy, Links primacy, no effect during Import, Export and Resync); Link Type (one sentence); Link Direction (one sentence); both filters together, 4 paragraphs (what is not touched, and a warning against filters on conditions that change without the issue changing); Scope (Expand options, and a warning that Synchronize all can delete all links of the type on Export or Resync to links); Removal (Move Upwards versus Remove).
Field `Primacy` of the `sync-links` form is checkbox `useprimacy` `Reverse contradicting changes during Incremental Sync`.

Field `Link Type` of the `sync-links` form is select `linktype` of link types by name, followed by, when hidden types exist, a group `Hidden Types` of them; each option carries its outward and inward descriptions. A stored id not found adds a selected option `?`. With no link types: the text `No link types available` in place of the select.
Field `Link Direction` of the `sync-links` form reads as a sentence: `parent issue`, select `direction` with options `out` and `in`, `sub-issue`. A `direction` error shows under it.

Fields `Parent Issue Filter` and `Sub-Issue Filter` of the `sync-links` form have radios `parentfilter` / `childfilter`: `none` `Not set (all issues allowed)`, `savedFilter` `Saved filter` with hidden `<prefix>filterid`, `<prefix>filtername`, the name or `No filter selected` and link `Select`, and `jql` `JQL query` with 2-row 45-column text area `<prefix>filterjql`. Errors for the id and JQL fields show under their parts.

Radio `none` of the `sync-links` filters is selected only when the field has no value, so when the form comes back after an error with `parentfilter=none` or `childfilter=none`, no radio of that filter is selected; submitting that way still means no filter (as the original does).

Field `Scope` of the `sync-links` form has radios `useall`: `false` `Synchronize issues that are already in the structure`, selected unless `useall` is true, with sub-options `expandchild` `Expand to sub-issues: also include issues with incoming links from other synchronized issues` and `expandparent` `Expand to parent issues: also include issues with outgoing links to other synchronized issues`, and `true` `Synchronize all issues that have links of selected type`.

Field `Removal` of the `sync-links` form has radios `orphanaction`: `move-up` `Move a sub-issue without incoming link upwards in the hierarchy`, selected unless the value is `remove`, and `remove` `Remove sub-issues without incoming link`.

Web-resource `statusup-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery-ui` (drag-and-drop ordering) and `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` (the checkbox multi-selector, see `page-util`). The `sync-status-rollup` form requires it.

On load the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects` with no parameters and lists the reply's `projects`, each a checkbox by `name` with value `id` and tooltip `description`, plus `All projects enabled for <product>` (value `*`). The selection goes to hidden field `projects`.

On load and whenever the project selection changes, the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types?projects=<value>`, the hidden field's value URL-encoded (`*` or ids joined with `,`), and lists the reply's `constants`, plus `All types` (value `*`), into hidden `types`.

On load and whenever projects or types change, the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses?projects=<value>&types=<value>`, both URL-encoded, and lists the reply's `constants` with no All option. Each status shows its icon at 16 by 16 before the name when `iconUrl` is set and not `/`, with tooltip `<name> - <description>` when there is a description.

Statuses selected on the `sync-status-rollup` form also appear in a separate ordered list, where they are reordered by drag and drop; the hint `Use drag-and-drop to specify status order:` shows only while the list has entries. Hidden `statuses` holds the ids in that order, comma-joined. A newly checked status goes before the next checked one in the option order, or at the end.

For each selected status known from the loaded options the `sync-status-rollup` form shows one transitions block, in status order, headed by the status (icon, name, tooltip), with a checkbox list that includes `Any possible` (value `*`). When no block exists the text `None` shows instead. Unchecking a status removes its block; a reordering moves blocks without reloading them.

Each transitions block sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions?projects=<value>&types=<value>&status=<status id>`, URL-encoded, when it is created and again on every change of projects or types. It lists the reply's `transitions`. An option's value is `<URL-encoded workflow>:<action>`; entries without workflow or action are skipped. The label is `<name> (from <source A>, <source B> - <workflow>)`, or `<name> (<workflow>)` without source statuses. The word `from` is the text `from`.

Each status's transition selection is sent in hidden field `transitions-<status id>`, pre-filled from the stored values or created empty for a new status. These fields stay when a status is unchecked, so re-checking the status in the same page visit brings back its earlier value.

All selectors of the `sync-status-rollup` form follow the checkbox multi-selector of `page-util`: `All` checked means value `*` and checks every option; unchecking any option clears `All`; `Loading...` shows after 300 ms of waiting; an older answer is ignored; an empty list shows `None`; a failed load marks the selector as failed. On submit, ids no longer among the loaded options are dropped from the field, unless the value is `*`, so submitting before a list has loaded empties that field.

The `sync-status-rollup` form has, with help beside each field: hidden `projects` with label `Enabled projects`; hidden `types`, `Enabled issue types`; hidden `statuses`, `Statuses rolled up`; `Allowed transitions`; and select `resolution` labelled `Resolution`. Errors under `projects`, `types`, `statuses`, `transitions` and `resolution` show in their fields.

Select `resolution` of the `sync-status-rollup` form has first option, value empty, `Use current or default value`, then Jira's resolutions by localized name. A stored value not found adds a selected option `?`.

Help of the `sync-status-rollup` form, to be written in the implementer's own words: Projects and Types, one or two sentences each, say the parent issue must match and sub-issues need not; Statuses, 4 short paragraphs, explains the earliest-to-latest rule with an example; Transitions, 3 paragraphs, says transitions are tried in order, that with none a status is still counted but not set, and that they run as the installing user and may fail; Resolution, 2 sentences, suggests a dedicated value and says it only applies when the transition allows it.

The `sync-subtasks` form has field `Sub-Task Types`: with no sub-task types the text `No sub-task types are available.`, otherwise the entity selector (`select-entities` claims) on field `types`, offering All and None, with everything selected by default on a new form and the stored value otherwise. An error under `types` shows below it.

The `StructureSync` list page has browser title and page heading `Synchronization Settings - <structure name>` and the current section `wi-structure-link`. Under heading `Automatic Synchronization`, with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window: a warning when one applies (see the page's claims), then a text of about 4 paragraphs saying what synchronization is, that enabled synchronizers apply changes incrementally within seconds or longer, that they can make massive changes with no undo, and to read parameters and back up; then the table.

The `StructureSync` table has columns `Type`, `Description`, `Run as User`, `State` and `Operations`. Description holds the instance description then its detail lines. State holds the state word then, below, one link per line. Operations holds the links separated by ` | `. Without the app permission the Operations cell shows `Restricted`, with no links; for an archived structure with the permission it is empty.

Below the `StructureSync` table, with the permission and not archived, the add form has `Set Up Synchronization With:`, a select of types, the selected type's description beside it updating on change, and button `Configure and Install Synchronizer`. It submits by GET to `StructureSync.jspa` with `id`, `synctype` and `create=true`.

With the app permission the `StructureSync` page has a section `One-Time Synchronization` with two short paragraphs saying Import and Export run the chosen synchronizer once, as Resync would, then links `Import into Structure` (not on an archived structure) and `Export from Structure`. When a return URL is set, a `Back` link closes the page.

The warnings on the `StructureSync` page: without permission, a bold `You currently do not have the permission to manage synchronizers.` and a sentence to ask a Jira administrator; for an archived structure, a bold `This structure is archived.` and sentences saying synchronizers do not work there and to unarchive it first.

The install form of `StructureSync` has title and page heading `Install Synchronizer - <structure name>`, heading `Install Synchronizer : <type label>` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, a note with the type's description and rules, error messages when any, read-only `Structure` and `Run as User`, the synchronizer's form, and buttons `Create` and `Cancel` (a link to the return URL). It posts to `StructureSync!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id`, `create=true`, `execute=true` and `synctype`.

The `Synchronizer Installed` page has title and heading `Synchronizer Installed - <structure name>` and heading `Synchronizer Installed`, then `A new synchronizer has been installed (id <id>).`, two paragraphs saying the synchronizer is `Disabled` and does not track changes, that `Resync and Enable` loses no changes, and that this can be done later; error messages when any; button `Resync and Enable` with `Rescans structure and all relevant issues, synchronize and enable automatic synchronization.`; button `Enable without Resyncing` with `Enable synchronizer without full synchronization`; and `Done`.

The `StructureSyncEdit` form has title `Edit Synchronizer - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>` and heading `Edit Synchronizer`. Below, in order: the success-styled message when the page has just disabled the synchronizer, a note with the synchronizer's description and rules, error messages, read-only `Structure`, the `Run as User` group, the synchronizer's form, and buttons `Apply` and `Cancel`. It posts to `StructureSyncEdit!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `execute=true`, `syncId` and `askOnCancel`.

On the `StructureSyncEdit` form a Jira administrator who is not the owner sees radios `keepOwner`: `true` `Current synchronizer owner — <owner>` and `false` `Current user — <current user>`. `Current user` is selected on first opening, since the `keepOwner` flag is then absent. Anyone else sees the current user as plain text, with `keepOwner=false` sent hidden.

When `StructureSyncEdit` shows errors after validating as the owner (not as the current user), the form ends with `The synchronizer parameters are invalid for user '<owner>'. Please fix the errors above and apply changes again.`

The `StructureSyncEdit` done page has heading `Synchronizer Parameters Updated` with `Synchronizer parameters have been updated.`, or for a cancel `Editing Has Been Cancelled` with `Synchronizer editing has been cancelled.`; browser title `<that heading> - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>`; then the same offer, buttons and explanations as the `Synchronizer Installed` page.

The `StructureSyncDelete` confirmation has browser title `Delete Synchronizer - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>`, heading `Delete Synchronizer`, two sentences saying that it stops and removes the synchronizer, a running synchronization is allowed to finish, and changes already made stay; error messages; read-only `Structure` and `Synchronizer` (description and detail lines); buttons `Delete Synchronizer` and `Cancel`.

The `StructureResync` confirmation has browser title `Resync Now - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `Resync Now`, heading `Please Confirm Running Full Synchronization` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, 3 paragraphs on resync as a one-time scan in the selected direction versus continuous incremental sync, and its duration; error messages; `Structure`; `Synchronizer`; a hint box `Possible effects during resync:` with a bulleted line per effect; the warning `WARNING: Full synchronization may effect massive changes.`; then, when they apply, a checked and disabled checkbox with the enable notice and the error box on the index. Buttons: `Start Resync`, styled as dangerous, and `Cancel`.

`StructureImport.jspa` without `synctype` has title and page heading `Import Structure - <name, abbreviated to 40 characters>`, heading `Select Import Source` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, `Please select where would you like to import from.`, then `Import From:`, a select with the description beside it and button `Configure Import Parameters`, plus `Cancel`. The export page is the same with `Export Structure - <name>`, `Select Export Target`, `Please select where would you like to export to.`, `Export To:` and `Configure Export Parameters`. With no synchronizers the text is `No import sources available (no synchronizers are capable of importing into structure)` or `No export targets available (no synchronizers are capable of exporting from structure)`. Both submit by GET with `id`.

The import form has title and page heading `Import Parameters - <name, abbreviated to 40 characters>`, heading `Import from <label>` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, a note with description and rules, error messages, read-only `Structure` and `Run as User` (the current user), the synchronizer's form, and a warning saying import may completely change the structure, issues are not altered, and a copy makes a backup. Buttons `Run Import` and `Cancel`. It posts to `StructureImport!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id`, `create=true`, `execute=true`, `synctype`. The export form is the same with `Export Parameters - <name>`, `Export to <label>`, a warning saying export may massively change issues, with no Undo, `Run Export` and `StructureExport!apply.jspa`.

Submitting the import or export form first asks in the browser's own confirm box `Run Import?` or `Run Export?`. On Cancel nothing is sent; on OK the submit button is disabled and the form is sent, so a second click cannot send it twice.

Web-resource `effector-common` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:tslib` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:structure-aui`. It provides the status icons and shared styles of effector processes; no behaviour of its own.

Each effector process status has an icon wherever status is shown: pending (never started), calculating, calculated, queued, in progress, completed, failed (`CALCULATION_FAILED`, error icon), stopped (shared by `CALCULATION_STOPPED` and `APPLY_STOPPED`), and completed-with-errors (shared by `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` and `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`).
Web-resource `effector-processes` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util`. The `StructureProcesses` page requires it and starts the view inline.

`/secure/StructureProcesses.jspa` has title and heading `Manage Effectors`, a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, and current section `wi-structure-link`. Above the table sit, in a row: text input with placeholder `Effector name`, single-selects with placeholders `Structure` and `Status`, `Run by` for Jira administrators only, and button `Clear all`. Pagination sits below the table. The form never submits.
After the `StructureProcesses` page has started, the query string is removed from the address bar without reloading, so `structureId` pre-selects the filter only on arrival.
Rows per page on `StructureProcesses` are computed once at load: free height is window height minus page height minus 100 px, divided by 35 and rounded down, kept within 10 to 50.

`StructureProcesses` first loads the attribute metadata (see `widget`). Only after it succeeds are filters and table installed; on failure a warning is logged and the page stays without rows or working filters. The page clears the browser's leave-page confirmation, so leaving it never asks.

The table on `StructureProcesses` has columns `ID`, `Effectors`, `Structure`, `Run By`, `Started`, `Finished`, `Status` and `Actions`. Cells of Effectors, Structure, Started, Finished and Status truncate and carry their full text as a tooltip.

Rows of `StructureProcesses` come from `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/list` (the original's URL ends with `/`, which the server treats the same) with JSON body `startAt`, `maxResults` and `params` holding strings `effectorName`, `user`, `status`, `structure`, empty when unset. The page reads `items` and `pagination.total`. The empty, error and loading states are those of the shared paginated table, with texts `No records available` and `Failed to retrieve records from the server`. There is no polling: rows change only on filter, paging or an action.

With a non-blank effector name filter `StructureProcesses` sends `maxResults=-1`, `startAt=0` and empty `effectorName`, caches that full list, keeps entries whose displayed name contains the text, case-insensitively, trimmed, and pages through them in the browser. For a revert process the displayed text matched is `Revert of <id>`; otherwise a process matches when any of its effectors' name does. The total is the filtered count.

On `StructureProcesses` the cached full list is reused while the name filter is non-blank and user, status and structure are unchanged; any other filter change drops it, so the next name search fetches again.

In the `Effector name` input of `StructureProcesses` any key other than Enter schedules a filter update 350 ms after the last key; Enter updates at once and does not submit. Choosing an entry in a select updates at once. An update that leaves all four values unchanged sends nothing; a changed one returns to the first page. Text changed without the keyboard is not noticed until the next key.

The `Structure` filter of `StructureProcesses` is a single-select with a dropdown button that asks `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure` with `filterById=true`, `limit=20` and `name` set to the typed text, or empty when a structure is already selected. It lists the reply's `structures`, each with value `id` and label `<name> (id: <id>)`.

The `Run by` filter of `StructureProcesses` is a single-select that asks Jira's own `GET /rest/api/2/user/picker` with `showAvatar=true` and `maxResults=20`, with the typed text as Jira's select sends it. It lists the reply's `users` by `displayName`, with `avatarUrl` and highlighted `html`, value `key`, and shows the reply's `header` as the group footer.
A filter select of `StructureProcesses` showing text that matches nothing displays `The value is invalid.`; leaving it empty shows no error.
`Clear all` on `StructureProcesses` empties the name input and all selects, sets all filters to empty and removes error messages in the filter row.
The `ID` cell of `StructureProcesses` links to `<context>/secure/StructureEffectorAudit.jspa?processId=<id>`.

The `Effectors` cell of `StructureProcesses`, for a revert process, reads `Revert of <id>` with the id linked to that process's audit page. Otherwise it lists effectors joined by `, `, each linking to `<context>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>#itemId=com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector/<effector id>`, or plain text for a one-off effector with no id. Names run through the attribute label rule. With no `structure` in the record the cell is empty, also for a run that has a name.

On `StructureProcesses` displayed effector names are cached by effector id for the page's life, and all one-off effectors share the empty id, so every one-off row shows the name of the first one rendered (as the original does).

The `Structure` cell of `StructureProcesses` links the name to `<context>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, shows `#<id> (deleted)` when the record has no name, and is empty with no structure. `Run By` links `displayName` to the user's `profileUrl` with Jira's user hover (`name`); with no `user` it shows the escaped `userKey`.

The `Status` cell of `StructureProcesses` has the status icon, then `<percentComplete>%` for `CALCULATING` and `IN_PROGRESS`, otherwise the status name: `Pending`, `Calculated`, `Queued`, `Completed`, `Completed with Errors`, `Calculation Stopped`, `Execution Interrupted`, `Execution Stopped`, `Failed`.

`Actions` of a process on `StructureProcesses`, in this order: `Resume` for `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`; `Revert` for `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`, `APPLY_STOPPED`; `Stop` for `PENDING`, `CALCULATING`, `CALCULATED`, `QUEUED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, shown as disabled text when `status.canceled` is true. Other statuses have none.
On `StructureProcesses` no action leaves the cell empty, one action is a plain link, and two or more go in a dropdown opened from a "more" icon with tooltip `Actions`.

Each action on `StructureProcesses` first asks through a confirmation dialog, titled `Confirmation` with `Confirm` and a cancel choice. Confirmed, it sends a JSON POST with body `{}` and the table is in its loading state until the answer. On failure an error flag shows the reply's `localizedMessage`, or `There was an error communicating with the server: <HTTP status>` when the reply is not JSON. Flags close automatically.

`Revert` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to revert changes made by process #<id>?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/undo`. On success a success flag says `Revert process #<new id> successfully created`, with the id linked to its audit page. The table is not refreshed.

`Stop` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to stop process #<id>?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/cancelAndWait`. By `status.status` of the reply: still stoppable gives success flag `Process #<id> has received a stop request and will handle it after some time`; `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `APPLY_STOPPED` gives success flag `Process #<id> was stopped`; anything else gives error flag `Process cannot stop because it has already finished`. In all cases the row is redrawn from the reply.

`Resume` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to resume applying previously calculated effects?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/resume`. On success a success flag says `Process #<id> was successfully resumed`, with the id linked to its audit page, and the row is redrawn from the reply.

Web-resource `effector-audit` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:dialog-common`. The `StructureEffectorAudit` page requires it and starts the view inline.

`/secure/StructureEffectorAudit.jspa` has title and heading `Effector Process Audit` and a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window. Below: a trail `Manage Effectors` (link to `StructureProcesses.jspa`) ` / ` and the process id in bold; then labelled rows `Effectors`, `Structure` (only with a structure; the link opens in a new tab), `Run by` (Jira's user hover and profile link at `/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<name>`, new tab), `Started`, `Finished` and `Status` (icon and name).

After the attribute metadata has loaded, effector names in the head of the `StructureEffectorAudit` page show the current label of their attribute, falling back to `Attribute`; a metadata failure only logs a warning and the rest of the page works.

On `StructureEffectorAudit` the Status row of an `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` process has a `Resume` link. It asks `Are you sure you want to resume applying previously calculated effects?` in a confirmation dialog; on Confirm the page sends `GET StructureEffectorAudit!resume.jspa?processId=<id>&atl_token=<token>`, following redirects, and when the answer was redirected replaces the location with the final URL. A failure gives no message.
Rows per page on `StructureEffectorAudit` are computed once at load: free height (window height minus page height) divided by 35, rounded down, minus 1, kept within 8 to 50.

Rows of `StructureEffectorAudit` come from `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/records` (the original's URL ends with `/`) with JSON `startAt`, `maxResults`, and `params` `{itemKey}` only while a filter is set. Empty, error and loading states are those of the shared paginated table. The page clears the browser's leave-page confirmation.

The table on `StructureEffectorAudit` has columns: a select-all checkbox, `Items`, `Reverse action`, `Effect`, and an unnamed one with the row's `Revert` link. `Items`, `Reverse action` and `Effect` show `affectedItems`, `undo` and `effect` as drawn by the effect renderer, with a missing value marked as such (see `widget-bare`).
A record with `isError` on `StructureEffectorAudit` has no checkbox and no `Revert` link, and its effect text is styled as an error.

The filter on `StructureEffectorAudit` is a text input with placeholder `Enter item key` and button `Filter`; Enter acts as the button and does not submit. A value must match one or more characters, then `-` or `:`, then a number without a leading zero (`ABC-12`, `MEMO:5`); otherwise `Invalid item key format` shows and nothing is sent. Typing hides that message. An empty value removes the filter. A changed value returns to the first page and clears the selection; the same value sends nothing.

On `StructureEffectorAudit` the selection survives paging. The header checkbox acts on the rows of the current page, shows ticked only when all of them are, is hidden when the page has no selectable row, and is disabled while loading. `Revert selected` shows the count and is disabled at 0.
When the record count is known `StructureEffectorAudit` shows `<n> records in total`, and the footer with pagination, total and revert buttons is shown only when the count is above 0.

`Revert all` on `StructureEffectorAudit` is rendered disabled when the process has no successful records. With an item filter set it still reverts all records of the process, not only those shown. It submits `selectedIndexes=null`, read as all.

Any revert on `StructureEffectorAudit` goes through a confirmation dialog `Are you sure you want to revert changes made by process #<id>?`. On Confirm the form posts to `StructureEffectorAudit!undoEffects.jspa` with `atl_token`, `processId` and `selectedIndexes`, a JSON array of record indexes, or `null` for all. A row's `Revert` link submits just that record's index.

On `StructureEffectorAudit`, after a row's `Revert` is cancelled in the dialog, the hidden `selectedIndexes` still holds that row until the selection next changes, so `Revert selected` right after it reverts the cancelled row instead of the checked ones (as the original does).

The `StructureEffectorEdit` dialog has the descriptor's title, the optional description, field `Name` with placeholder `Enter effector name`, the effector's own form, then buttons. Name is marked required only without generated names, is disabled when not configurable, and shows any `effectorName` error. Hidden fields: `atl_token`, `execute=true`, `effectorId`, `structureId`, `moduleKey`, `formAction`. The form posts to `StructureEffectorEdit!apply.jspa`.

With generated names the `StructureEffectorEdit` dialog also shows the summary beside the name field, with edit and clear controls, driven by the effector editor code from the descriptor's summary template with the effector's module key and whether it is configurable (see `widget-bare`).

Buttons of `StructureEffectorEdit`: configurable and executable: `Save and Run`, `Save`; configurable only: `Save`; executable only: `Run`; neither: none. `Cancel` is always there. Clicking one sets `formAction` to `save-and-run`, `save` or `run`.

When `StructureEffectorEdit` is not configurable the page disables every visible input except `Run`, hides the attribute editor's menu, shows plain selects instead of enhanced ones, and focuses `Run` when present.
The error view of `StructureEffectorEdit` is dialog content: the title `Error` and one error box per message.

Every `StructureEffectorProcess` view opens with title `Run Effectors`, row `Effectors` with the effectors title and, for an existing process, row `Status` with icon and name. When the board's widget is present, attribute labels in the title are filled in after the metadata loads; otherwise the title stays as rendered.

The text format starts with the settings URL in brackets, indented.

Once the `widget-bare` script has run, `window.almworks.structure.api` is an object with exactly these members besides the class helpers: `ColumnGroup`, `registerColumnGroup` (same function as `ColumnGroup.register`), `ColumnType`, `registerColumnType` (same function as `ColumnType.register`), `ColumnConfigurator`, `Column`, `SpecOption`, `ColumnOption` (same object as `SpecOption`), `registerCoreExtension`, `ItemDetailsProvider`, `registerItemDetailsProvider` and `automationRegistry` (the object also exposed as AMD id `structure/api/AutomationRegistry`).

`window.almworks.structure.api` also carries the class helpers `subClass`, `baseClass`, `isSubClass`, `isInstance`, `addSuper` and `getClassName`. `subClass(name?, superclass, props)` makes a constructor: it calls the superclass as a plain function with the single options argument, copies the non-function entries of `props` onto the new instance, then calls `init(options)` found on the new class's prototype. Function entries of `props` go on the prototype; `prototype._super` is the superclass prototype and `prototype._class` the new class. `name`, when given, must match letters and underscores only, otherwise it throws `invalid function name [<name>]`; a superclass that is not a function throws `bad superclass <value>`; a `props` that is not an object throws `bad props <value>`. `baseClass(name, props)` does the same on a root class whose constructor stores its argument as `this.options`. `isSubClass(a, b)` is true when b is a or derives from it, and true for an empty a; `isInstance(cls, obj)` is true for instances, also through the `_class` chain, and false for an empty obj; `getClassName(obj)` gives the constructor's name; `addSuper(cls, obj)` copies cls's prototype methods, bound to obj, into `obj._super` and returns a function that applies cls to its arguments.

Because `subClass` calls its superclass as a plain function, every public class that companion apps extend (`Column`, `ColumnConfigurator`, `ColumnType`, `SpecOption` and its six option classes, `ColumnGroup`, `ItemDetailsProvider`, `StructureCoreExtension`, `AttributeDescriptor`, `GeneratorDescriptor`, `EffectorDescriptor`) must work when called as `Base.call(this, options)` on an object whose prototype derives from it, not only with `new`.

These AMD ids are public and each resolves directly to the value it names, not to an object with a `default` member: `structure/api/Column`, `structure/api/ColumnConfigurator`, `structure/api/ColumnType`, `structure/api/ColumnGroup`, `structure/api/SpecOption`, `structure/api/AttributeDescriptor`, `structure/api/GeneratorDescriptor`, `structure/api/EffectorDescriptor`, `structure/api/AutomationRegistry`, `structure/api/ItemDetailsProvider`, `structure/api/ItemDetailsBridge`, `structure/api/SecondaryPanelRegistry`, `structure/api/StructureCoreExtension`, `structure/api/StructureCoreExtensionRegistry`. The global does not carry `AttributeDescriptor`, `GeneratorDescriptor`, `EffectorDescriptor`, `ItemDetailsBridge`, `SecondaryPanelRegistry` or `StructureCoreExtension`: those are reached by AMD id only.

The global is created by the widget's own script: a companion script that registers columns or providers must load after `widget-bare` (for example through the web-resource context `structure.widget`). Column types and groups registered that way are visible at once, because all registries are page-wide singletons read on use. `window.namespace(path)` is the plugin's global helper for reaching or creating a dotted object path, and the bundled item-details scripts use it to reach the global.

The jar carries a file of empty placeholder declarations for the global, which no web-resource loads. It names `registerColumn` and `ColumnConfiguratorGroup`, which do not exist on the live global: the live registration calls are `registerColumnType` and `registerColumnGroup`. The replacement does not provide `registerColumn` or `ColumnConfiguratorGroup`. The five browser-side type declaration scripts of the original (effector, progress, details, editor and generic details types) define nothing at run time.

`ColumnType.register(typeOrColumnClass, keys)` (also `registerColumnType`): `keys` is a column key string or a non-empty array of them; anything else throws `expected a non-empty array of column keys, but got <first argument>`. The first argument is either an instance of `ColumnType`, or a subclass of `Column`, which is wrapped in a type whose `createColumn(context, spec)` returns `new columnClass({context, spec})` when `spec.key` is one of `keys` and null otherwise. Anything else throws `expected subclass of ColumnType, but got <value>`. Each key maps to the type; a later registration of a key replaces the earlier mapping, while the earlier type stays in the list of all types.

`ColumnType.getAllColumnTypes()` returns a copy of the registered types in registration order, `ColumnType.getAllColumnTypeKeys()` all keys, and `ColumnType.getColumnTypeForKey(key)` the type for a key or undefined. A column spec whose key has no type yields no column and logs the warning that no column type is registered.

A `ColumnType` instance has these overridable methods with these defaults: `createSwitchTypePreset(context)` null, `createAddColumnPresets(context)` an empty array, `createConfigurator(context, spec)` null, `createColumn(context, spec)` null, `getMetadataRequests(context)`, `getPresetMetadataRequests()`, `getColumnMetadataRequests()` and `getConfigMetadataRequests()` all null.

For each column spec of a view, with a `csid`: an existing column with that csid is reused when its key matches and its spec is deep-equal. Otherwise the type's metadata for the phase `column` is loaded, `createColumn(context, spec)` is called with a copy of the panel's column context extended with that metadata, and then the column's own `getMetadataRequests()` is loaded and added to `column.context`. A null result means no column; the load never fails the view.

When the add-column list opens, for every registered type the phase `preset` metadata is loaded and `createAddColumnPresets(context)` is called with the metadata-extended context; each returned spec gets a configurator. When the edit panel opens with type switching allowed, every other type gets `createSwitchTypePreset(context)` likewise. A non-null spec gets the edited column's `csid` and a configurator through `createConfigurator`. A type returning null is left out of the Type selector.

Metadata requests are a map from a name to a request object. A request with `promise` uses that promise. Otherwise it needs `url` and is sent as an AJAX call with its own settings, `dataType` defaulting to `json`. With `cacheable: true` the promise is kept per url for the page, so the call is made once. `extract(response)`, when a function, turns the answer into the stored value. The result maps each name to its value. A request that fails, or has neither promise nor url, simply leaves its name out and never fails the whole load; an empty or null map resolves to an empty result at once.

A type's metadata is cached on the type, per phase. `getMetadataRequests(context)` is loaded once and applies to all phases; the phases `preset`, `column` and `config` load `getPresetMetadataRequests()`, `getColumnMetadataRequests()` and `getConfigMetadataRequests()` once each. The two results are merged, the phase's values winning. The result is available to the type's create methods through `context.getMetadata(name)`, which falls back to any earlier `getMetadata`; names not found give undefined.

The column context passed to types, columns and configurators has: `jira.getAllIssueFields()` (a copy of all Jira fields), `jira.getIssueFieldById(id)`, `getMetadata(name)`, `isConfigurationPanelResizeAllowed()` (true on a project page or the structure board) and `structure` with `isPrimaryPanel()`, `isSecondaryPanel()`, `isIssuePage()`, `isGreenHopperTab()`, `isPCVPage()`, `isProjectPage()` (the last two the same answer), `isComponentPage()` and `isVersionPage()` (always false), `isGadget()`, `isLocalGadget()`, `isRemoteGadget()`, `isStructureBoard()`, `isConfluenceEnabled()` and `onExternalParametersChanged()`, which makes the panel treat its columns as changed so that they re-render.

`new Column({spec, context?, csid?})` needs a spec. `csid` is `spec.csid` or else the option; with neither it throws `cannot create column without csid`. `options`, `spec`, `context` and `csid` are kept on the instance. `spec.name`, when set, is rendered as a template with `{column: this}` to give the display name: braces in it are substituted.

On `Column`: `getColumnSpec()` returns the spec, `getCsid()` the csid, `getColumnKey()` `spec.key`, `isColumnOfType(key)` compares keys, `getName()` is the rendered name or else `getDefaultName()` or else the empty string, and `getDefaultName()` is empty.

`Column` defaults: `isUniversal()` false, `isResizable()` true, `canShrinkWhenNoSpace()` false, `isAutoSizeAllowed()` false, `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` true, `getMinWidth()` 27, `getDefaultWidth()` 120, `getSortAttribute()` null, `isSortDescendingByDefault()` false, `getMetadataRequests()` null, `getSuggestedAttributeSpecs()` null, `getCellValueHtml(context)` the empty string, `collectRequiredAttributes(set)` and `updateRowClasses(context)` do nothing.

`Column.setWidth(w)`: an empty w clears the manual width (`getWidth()` gives null); otherwise the stored width is the larger of w as an integer and `getMinWidth()`. So with the default minimum, setWidth(10) gives 27 and setWidth(200) gives 200. When a view is restored, manual widths are applied through `setWidth`, and preferred widths only to columns with `isAutoSizeAllowed()` true. A column's initial width is `getDefaultWidth()`, or the minimum width if that is 0. `isResizable()` false gives the column no drag handle, and it takes no part in width distribution. `canShrinkWhenNoSpace()` true lets the column go below its width when the grid lacks room.

`Column.renderHeader(cell)` sets the header cell's HTML to `getHeaderCellHtml()`, which is the column's name in the standard header layout, or the empty string when the name is empty. The name is inserted as HTML, unescaped by this step.

For each row on screen and each column, the grid calls `column.render(context)`. The default `render` calls `renderCellView(context)`: it gets `getCellViewHtml(context)`, replaces the cell's HTML only if it differs, and then calls `updateRowClasses(context)`. `getCellViewHtml` wraps `getCellValueHtml(context)` through `wrapInCellDiv(html, extraClass = "")`, the standard cell layout with the fade and the overflow indicator. An exception from `render` logs a warning and empties that cell; other cells still render.

The render context offers: `getRowId()`, `getItemId()`, `getMeta()`, `getSemantics()`, `isIssue()`, `isNotAccessible()`, `getAttributeValue(attributeSpec, forestSpec?)` and `repaintWhen(promise)`, which re-renders the row when a still pending promise ends and does nothing for a settled one. `forestSpec` is omitted or `displayed` for the shown forest, or `unfiltered`. `getAttributeValue` returns undefined for a value not loaded. The cell and row elements are at `context._cell$` and `context._row$`, valid only during the `render` call; a column overriding `render` writes to them directly.

When a `render` call read at least one attribute and every value read was absent, the row is accessible and `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` is true, the grid replaces the cell with its absent-value display. A row whose data has not arrived yet is not rendered at all: its cells get the same display, under the same two conditions. If a value read is known to be outdated, the cell is marked as outdated. Returning false from `isRenderingAbsentValueAllowed()` means the column's own output stays.

Whenever the panel's columns change, `collectRequiredAttributes(set)` is called on each column, with `set.requireAttribute(attributeSpec, forestSpec?)` to declare what it needs. The union is what the grid subscribes to and what `getAttributeValue` can return. An exception logs an error and that column contributes what it declared before the exception.

`Column.shouldFlash(flashContext)`: true if any attribute declared through `collectRequiredAttributes` is flashed according to `flashContext.isAttributeFlashed(attributeSpec, forestSpec)`. When true the grid plays the changed-value flash on the cell. An exception from it is logged and means no flash.

`getSortTransform()` gives, when `getSortAttribute()` returns an attribute spec, `{module: "com.almworks.jira.structure:sorter-attribute", params: {attribute: <spec>}}`, otherwise null. A null transform means clicking the column's header does not sort. It may also return a promise of the transform. On the first sort by this column the sort is descending exactly when `isSortDescendingByDefault()` is true; clicking the same sort again reverses the direction.
`getSuggestedAttributeSpecs()`, when it returns specs, offers them in every attribute selector of the widget under Used in Columns, named after the column.

`Column.safeSetHtml(element, html)` sets the HTML of a non-empty element and never lets an exception out. On an exception it logs one warning per column name for the page's life, with the column's name, spec, the cell HTML and the error's stack. An empty or missing element is ignored. The warning names no vendor and sends nothing anywhere.

`new ColumnConfigurator({spec, context?})` needs a spec. It takes `presetName`, `description` and `groupKey` out of the spec, when they are set, into the configurator, so they never reach the saved column spec. `getContext()` returns the context, `shareSpec()` the spec itself (not a copy), and `getColumnSpec()` the same spec.

`getPresetName()` is the taken `presetName` or else `getColumnName()`; `getColumnName()` is `spec.name`, or else `getDefaultColumnName()`, or else `getColumnTypeName()`. `getDefaultColumnName()`, `getColumnTypeName()` and `getColumnTypeInfoLink()` default to the empty string, `getDescription()` to the taken description or the empty string, `getGroupKey()` to the taken key or false.

`ColumnConfigurator` defaults: `getOptions()` false (no custom options), `isConfigured()` true, `getMetadataRequests()` null, `isConfigurationPanelWide()` false, `isConfigurationPanelResizable()` false. `isConfigurationRevertible(originalSpec)` is true when the current spec is not deep-equal to originalSpec. `matchPreset(spec)` compares `comparablePreset(spec)` with `comparablePreset` of its own spec, and by default `comparablePreset` keeps only `key`.

In the add-column list each configurator is one entry, named by `getPresetName()`, with `getDescription()` as its tooltip. Entries are sorted by the rendered name and placed under the group with `getGroupKey()`; an entry with no key, or a key of no registered group, goes under the group with an empty key, and with no such group it is not listed. Choosing an entry adds `getColumnSpec()` when `isConfigured()` is true and otherwise just closes the list, adding nothing.

A configurator is obtained by loading the phase `config` metadata, calling `createConfigurator(context, spec)` with the extended context, and then loading the configurator's own `getMetadataRequests()` into `configurator.context`. Failure at any step gives no configurator, never an error.

`ColumnGroup.register(options)` (also `registerColumnGroup`) adds a group of the add-column list. Options: `groupKey` (a string, otherwise it throws `no valid groupKey`), `title` (non-empty, otherwise `no title`) and `order` (a number, default 0, otherwise `bad order type`).
