For the generators named in a poll result, the banner asks `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/generatorDescriptions` with a JSON array of generator ids (with `?loggedIn=<bool>` except in gadgets) and matches answers by `id` to read `description`. An empty or failed answer, or no generators in the result, closes the auto-opening banner and shows no details. The request is sent for each matching poll result that has generators; a poll result without the panel's spec changes nothing. A banner that opens automatically therefore opens only after that answer.

A generator details row has: the generator's description as an automation summary, re-rendered once if attribute metadata was still loading, its value, and a pencil. No pencil for a transient generator. With info `generatorConfigurationAllowed` the pencil has the title 'Edit this generator' and opens the generator edit dialog for that id; without, it is inert with title 'You don't have the required permissions to edit this generator'. The details show only while expanded and non-empty.

The query box is a growing one-line text area with a status icon on one end, a clear icon (tooltip 'Clear') on the other, and a placeholder per type: text 'Enter text query', jql 'Enter JQL query', sjql 'Enter S-JQL query', cql 'Search Confluence pages by title or CQL'. It is used for the source query (types text, jql, cql) and the search banner (text, jql, sjql). The placeholder is updated 50 ms after a type change.

For types jql and sjql, a non-empty text is checked 500 ms after typing stops, or 50 ms after a type change, with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/query/validate?q=<text>&type=<type>`. An answer for a text other than the current one is dropped. On answer `errors` non-empty the query stays as before and the error state is set. On answer `errors` empty or null the query value becomes the trimmed text, if different. A failed request changes nothing. Text and cql types are never validated; there the trimmed text is taken after the same 500 ms.

The status icon is a neutral quote mark for text and cql types, a success check for a valid jql or sjql query, and an error mark when the query has errors. Hovering the error mark shows each error as its own paragraph. Empty jql or sjql counts as valid and clears errors.
Clicking the clear icon empties the box and keeps focus in it.

Pressing Enter in the source query box applies the current text right away with no wait, then removes focus. It is not applied, and does nothing else, while the JQL autocomplete's list is displayed. No line break is ever inserted by Enter.

Only for type jql the box offers Jira's JQL autocomplete, loaded through Jira's search data (Jira's own REST) when the type becomes jql; it is removed on leaving jql and rebuilt when the box height changes. A parse problem reported by the autocomplete becomes the error state when none is set. Accepting a suggestion updates the query text.

While the box has focus and its content overflows, 100 ms after text or focus changes the clear icon is moved aside by the scrollbar's width, and with the caret at the end of the text the box scrolls to the bottom. Without focus the box collapses, and the icon returns.

The left of the header shows the selector button with the current source's icon and label, followed by the source's controls. For a structure: the name, a tooltip 'Current structure: <name>', and when the info says `isArchived` a lozenge 'archived'. With a null info the label is 'Unknown'. For a query the label is 'Text', 'JQL' or 'Pages' and the query box follows. For the clipboard: 'Clipboard'. For the project query: 'Current Project Issues'. Non-structure sources have no tooltip.

The structure parts of the header (name, archived mark, description button, favourite star) are updated 10 ms after the spec or info settles. While the info is not yet known or the source is not a structure, the description button, the star and the archived mark are hidden and the source's controls shown.

On the board page, when the structure info is null (a structure which does not exist or is not visible) the update of the favourite star fails with a script error after the name 'Unknown' has been shown, so no star is shown or refreshed (as the original does).

On the board page only, for a known structure, a star is shown after the name, reflecting `favorite` from the info. Clicking it sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/favorite` with {`favorite`:<the opposite>} as the page's shared favourites control does (see the `favorites` resource); on success the star follows the answer, its label changes on the button too, and the rest of the widget is told that the structure was updated. Other pages show no star.

The selector loads `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`, with `?anchorIssue=<id>` when the widget has a positive anchor issue, timeout 30 s, at install and each time the dropdown is opened (by mouse down on the closed selector, or keys `s`,`s`). There is at most one request in flight.

A failed list request schedules a retry after 1 s, 2 s and so on up to a cap of 20 s, but the guard for a load in progress is still set then, so no retry and no later load of the list happens during that page's life and the dropdown keeps what it had (as the original does).

Each list of the answer is mapped through `structures`, keeping ids found there with a positive id. It is cut to `maxItems` (10 when absent) entries, or one more when the list holds the structure being shown. An entry's label is its name, or `[<id>]` when nameless; names over 40 characters are cut to 37 plus `...`, and the full name is the tooltip. `containingAnchor` is used only when the answer's `anchorIssue` equals the widget's anchor issue. Counts of further items (`totalFavorites`, `totalContainingAnchor`) are not shown anywhere.

The dropdown has, top to bottom: a search box (placeholder 'Search Structure'); 'Structures with This Issue'; 'Recent Structures'; 'Favorite Structures'; 'Default Structures'; the structure search results (only while searching, when the sections before it are hidden); 'Tools'; and the Manage entry. A section with no items is not shown. 'Default Structures' is shown only when recents or favourites have no items in the answer. The structure being shown is left out of every section except favourites; a section left with nothing is dropped, but still counts as having items for that rule.

The sections are rebuilt only if the answer or the shown structure changed. The active (highlighted) entry after a rebuild is the existing active one, else the last hovered structure, else the first entry. Moving the mouse over an entry makes it the active one.

Each structure entry links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, but a plain click stays on the page: 10 ms later, if the panel state may change and no listener vetoes it, `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/recents?id=<id>` is sent (result ignored), the header shows the name and the panel's base spec is set to {`structureId`:<id>}, with the manage entry updated. If the current spec already equals that, only the recents request goes out. The click never loads the board page again.
On the board page in the primary panel, the first spec with a structure id also sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/recents?id=<id>` once per page load.

After a structure is picked in the dropdown, a 'Manage Structure' entry is added below Tools, opening `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?id=<id>`. It is also added when the spec has a structure id plus other fields. It is not added for a spec that is only {`structureId`:<id>}, as on a plain page load, and it stays with the old target when another source than a tool is opened by other means; choosing an entry from Tools hides it (as the original does).

The 'Tools' section offers 'Text Search', 'JQL Query', 'Confluence Pages', 'Clipboard' with a badge of the clipboard's row count (shown when not 0), and 'Current Project Issues'. Choosing one, 10 ms later and if the panel state may change and nothing vetoes it, switches the source, focuses its input and hides the Manage entry. 'Current Project Issues' exists only on the project page. The Tools section is not offered on the issue page or the Jira Software tab, and all sections are hidden during a structure search.

'Confluence Pages' is available only when the Pages companion app is present, that is, the bootstrap config's `extensions` entry `com.almworks.structure.pages:pages-extension` has `licensed` true. The check is applied when the dropdown opens and its search box is empty, with the 500 ms delay of that box, so in the first half second of the first opening the entry may still be displayed. Without the companion app the entry is hidden.

Choosing a query source sets the spec to {`sQuery`:{`query`:<text>,`type`:<type>}} on each change of the valid query, with `query` empty when nothing was typed yet. Choosing 'Clipboard' sets {`type`:`clipboard`}. On the project page the project source sets its fixed query spec. Switching among text, JQL and Pages keeps the box and its text.

The selector follows the spec from outside: a structure spec selects no source; an `sQuery` with `projectQuery` selects the project source; another `sQuery` fills the text and selects its type; a spec with `type` selects that source.
On the project page the project source's spec is {`sQuery`:{`type`:`jql`,`query`:`project = "<KEY>"`,`projectQuery`:true}}.

A change of source or structure is refused when the panel's state cannot change right now. Before changing, the widget asks listeners, naming the panel, and any of them may veto. Both cases leave everything as it was, and the dropdown stays as the user left it.

With the dropdown open, the focus goes to its search box. Up and Down move the active entry among visible entries, stopping at the ends; with no active entry Down takes the first and Up the last. Enter clicks the active entry. Esc closes the dropdown and returns focus to the selector button; Tab closes it. Each of those keys goes no further. The key sequence `s`,`s` opens it; not in gadgets.

Typing in the dropdown's search box hides the sections and Tools; 500 ms after the last change `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure?limit=20&name=<url-encoded text>` goes out (timeout 30 s). With results: heading 'Structures Found' and each entry with its full name, linking as in the other sections. No results: heading 'Not found'. Failure: heading 'Search Error'. Emptying the box restores the sections, and Tools when available. Opening the dropdown resets the box. Answers arriving late are not dropped.

Ctrl+Alt+' (not in gadgets, on the issue page or Jira Software tab): if a text, JQL or Pages source is on and its box lacks focus, focus it. Otherwise switch the source: Text to JQL, JQL to Pages when the Pages app is present or else to Text, any other source to Text.
The widget can lock the selector to its structure (single-structure mode): the selector button is then aria-disabled.
The dropdown opens below the selector, or above when there is more room above; its height is limited to the room in the window.

The duplicates footer shows 'N rows with duplicates' with N from the panel's statistics `duplicateRowsCount` (0 if absent), a 'Filter' button (tooltip 'Hide items that have no duplicates'), a 'Pin' button (tooltip 'Pin selected item'), next and previous buttons ('Next duplicate', 'Previous duplicate') and the checkbox 'Mark duplicate rows'.
The 'Filter' button is a toggle telling the panel to show duplicates only. Any open or close of the footer, and its close control, turn it off.
The footer's Pin button runs the toggle-pin action, shows as pressed while an item is pinned, is disabled while transformations are disabled, and warns in automation editing mode.

Footer wording adapts to width, 10 ms after each layout change: when its content does not fit, it steps up a level, up to 3. Level 1 drops the Filter and Pin button texts. Level 2 shortens the count to only the number. Level 3 lays out the footer on several lines. It steps down when the room is larger than what was saved by stepping up. A hidden footer (width 0) is left alone.

When the panel can show duplicates, the footer's open state and the states of 'Mark duplicate rows' and 'Filter' (per panel, booleans as text, default false) are restored from the browser and from a perspective, where the paths are `<panel>.pf.duplicates.mark` and `<panel>.pf.duplicates.filter`. Restoring happens the first time the panel is visible; opening a perspective applies them to a live page.
The board toolbar sits above the grid wherever the page provides a place for it (board and project pages). It does not exist on the issue page or the Jira Software tab.

The toolbar's left side, in order: the split button 'Add' (tooltip 'Create a new item and add it to the structure'; its arrow: label 'Add items by type', tooltip 'Add new issues or other items to the structure, or search and add existing items'); 'Expand all' (tooltip 'Fully expand structure'), 'Collapse all' (tooltip 'Collapse all sub-items'), and an arrow 'Expand to a level...'; move up ('Move selected items up'), move down ('Move selected items down'), outdent ('Outdent selected items one level at a time'), indent ('Indent selected items one level at a time'); edit ('Edit focused item'), cut, copy, paste, remove, whose labels are 'Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Remove' and whose tooltips are 'Cut - mark selected items for moving to another place', 'Copy - mark selected items for copying to another place', 'Paste copied or cut rows after the currently focused item', 'Remove selected items and their sub-items from the structure (this does not delete issues or other Jira items)'; then 'Automation'.

The toolbar's right side, in order: 'Help' (menu), 'Share' (tooltip and label 'Share perspective'; hidden on the project page), 'Export' (menu), and the layout split button with an arrow 'Layout settings'.

Each toolbar button or menu entry performs a named grid action on the focused panel, or at widget level when no panel has focus. It takes its enabled state from that action: aria-disabled while unavailable, in which case a click does nothing; a split button's arrow goes with its main button. A toggle action shows as pressed or checked. Updates from a panel that does not have focus are ignored. Clicking a button removes focus from it.

The Add arrow opens a menu: 'New Issue', 'New Folder', 'New Memo', 'New Planning task', then, in order, the entry for pages and one per third-party item type, then in a section of its own 'Search & Add'.

The menu's 'New Page' entry, which starts creating a Confluence page row, is there when the Pages companion app is available (see claim selector-cql-entry). Without the app there is no such entry: the original's promotional entry for that app, which sends the user to the vendor's Marketplace listing, stays out of the replacement under the vendor identity rule.

For each entry of `externalGenericItemTypes` in `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`, the Add menu gets an entry labelled with `newItemTitle`, which starts creating an item of `type`. Entries are added once when the config has loaded, with their text HTML-escaped.

The expand arrow opens a menu with radio entries 'Level 1' to 'Level 8' and 'All Levels'. On opening, nothing happens if no panel has focus. Otherwise the focused panel's current level is checked, and each level is listed only when it is at most the maximum level of the forest, or the current one; 'All Levels' is always listed. Choosing an entry expands the focused panel to that level (0 for 'Level 1', up to 7 for 'Level 8', 10000 for 'All Levels').

The layout main button shows the current layout's icon and has the tooltip '<current>. Click to switch to "<next>".' with layout names 'Single Grid', 'Double Grid', 'Grid + Details', 'Grid + History', or a registered external panel's icon. Clicking it switches to the next layout and removes focus from the button.

The layout arrow's menu holds these sections. 'Layout': radio entries 'Single Grid', 'Double Grid', 'Grid + Details' (only when details are available) and 'Grid + History'. 'Layout Options': checkboxes 'Full Screen' and 'Mark Manual Adjustments'. 'Item Link Action': see claims item-link-*. Their behaviour is that of the layout management.

The toolbar's text shrinks by steps as it gets narrower: normal; no labels on the right side; also no 'Automation' label; and last the group edit, cut, copy, paste, remove is replaced by a single 'Edit' menu ('Edit focused item or change hierarchy') with entries 'Edit', 'Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Remove'. The first step whose measured width fits is used, and the last step if none fits; widths are measured with visible content, on start 200 ms after install, again when the help button or automation plus button appears, and the fit is rechecked on each window resize. Without permission to edit automation the 'Automation' label is not displayed.

When the config's `hideHelp` is absent, the 'Help' menu is shown with: 'Welcome to <product>', opening `secure/StructureWelcome.jspa` in the same window; 'Tips from your admin'; 'Documentation', a link in a new tab to the plugin's documentation; and 'About <product>', which opens the plugin's about dialog. The original's entry pointing at the vendor's community site is left out of the replacement. With `hideHelp` true the Help button, the menu and the first-use hint are not there at all.
'Tips from your admin' opens a Jira form dialog loaded from `/secure/StructureHelpDialog.jspa`. The entry is left out when the config's `hideHelpAdminTips` is true.

The first time the toolbar is shown in this browser with help available, a small popup at the Help button says 'Any questions?' / 'You can search for the answers here.' with a button 'Got it', which closes it. This is remembered in the browser at the moment it appears, without expiry, so it does not reappear.
The automation mode is remembered as `none` or `automation`, default `none`, in the browser and, in a perspective, at the top-level path `toolbar`. It is restored when storage is ready.

With `#devmode` in the URL fragment (as the only or a slash-separated part), or by the debug action at runtime, the toolbar adds developer buttons: 'Poll' (request a poll now), 'Upload Tree', 'Debug Mode' (toggle), 'Block Ajax' (toggle; turning off resumes sending), 'Exception', 'Error', 'Stop generation'. 'Stop generation' posts the focused panel's spec as `forestSpecs` to `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/stopIfRunning`, or `.../generation/stop` with Shift held. 'Upload Tree' has no effect from this toolbar.

The toolbar supports extra rows, each opened by a toggle button: at most one extra row shows at a time below the main one (opening another closes the open one), height 30 px, and its buttons are disabled while the focused panel is read-only. Nothing in the plugin itself uses this at present.
The 'Export' menu has 'Printable Page', 'Export to Excel (XLS)' and 'Export to Excel (XLSX)', each acting on the focused panel; no focused panel means nothing happens.

Exports send these parameters: `forestSpec`, the focused panel's REST spec as JSON text, for a structure with history shown using the shown version and no `transforms`, and in automation editing mode with `title` true and no `transforms`; `viewSpec`, the current view as JSON with each nameless column getting the name of its live column, or else `viewId`, the base view id, when there is no current specification; `expand`, the encoded expansion state; `clientFilter` when user filters exist; `signature`, the forest version signature or 0; `atl_token`; and, for Excel, `xlsx` true or false.

Excel exports open `/plugins/servlet/structure/excel` in the same window. 'Printable Page' opens `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` in a window named per panel, so that a repeat replaces that window's content. Parameters go by GET unless the sum over them of (URL-encoded name length + URL-encoded value length + 2) exceeds 400; then by POST.

The items of web-item location `structure.export.menu` come from `exportLinks` of `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget` (those having `label`, `url` and `moduleKey`) and form a separate section after the built-in entries, in the order given. With none, there is no section. Each item shows `label`, an icon from `iconClasses` or the default export icon, `title` as tooltip, and opens in a new tab.

An export link's target is recomputed from the primary panel's REST spec (always the primary panel, whichever panel has focus), at every change of that spec. If the `url` holds `${forestSpec}`, its first occurrence is replaced by the spec's JSON, URL-encoded. Otherwise the URL gets a query parameter `forestSpec` with that JSON. With no spec the target is `#`.

The web item `export-structure-as-json` puts 'View as JSON', weight 1000, in location `structure.export.menu`, with the link `/rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest?s=${forestSpec}`. It is shown only when the server runs in development mode.

The 'Item Link Action' section (radio 'Open Details', 'Navigate to Item', 'Do Nothing') becomes active when the details panel is first initialized. Then `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction` (timeout 30 s) loads `type`; it selects that radio only if none was picked meanwhile, and that does not send it back. A failed request only logs; nothing is selected.

Picking a radio sends `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction` with body {`type`:<showDetails|openIssuePage|doNothing>} through the upload queue. A failure only logs, and the selection stays.

The section and its entries are disabled, with a tooltip, in two layouts: with history shown 'Item link will always navigate to item in Grid + History layout'; with details shown 'Item link will always open item details in Grid + Details layout'; if both, the details text. Otherwise they are enabled and the tooltip is empty.

Clicking an item link in a grid, with history not shown: with details open, or in a non-primary panel, the link is not followed. Otherwise the choice decides: 'Open Details' opens the details panel and does not follow the link; 'Navigate to Item' follows it; 'Do Nothing' does not. With history shown this rule does not apply. The link loses focus in all those cases.
The first time a choice has a value after load, the statistic `issueDetails.issueLinkAction.<type>` is recorded once.
The section is hidden unless details are available in this widget (`showIssueDetails` configuration).

The 'Automation' toggle button (tooltip: a sentence of about 170 characters saying it turns on editing of generators and effectors and that added transformations are disabled meanwhile) turns automation editing mode on and off. It shows as pressed while on. It is disabled while history is shown or a new row is being edited. Keys `` ` `` and Shift+`` ` `` toggle it. After Enter on it focus stays on it.
When the structure gives neither `generatorConfigurationAllowed` nor `effectorConfigurationAllowed`, the Automation button's label is not displayed; the button itself stays.

An add button (tooltip of about 110 characters, accessible label 'Add an automation', saying that it adds a generator or effector under the focused item) appears beside the Automation button only when all hold: automation mode is on, the focused panel shows a structure, that panel is neither locked nor read-only, the structure allows configuring generators or effectors, and no new row is being edited. When a condition fails, an open menu from it closes and the button goes away.

The add button's menu lists one entry per generator kind known to the automation registry when generators are accessible, with that kind's icon, label and tooltip, then 'Effectors' (tooltip 'Create an effector under the current item') when effectors are accessible. Choosing an entry replaces the add button with a button named after the choice (the kind's action label or 'Effectors') and opens that list's menu at once. Closing that menu restores the add button, and when closed by Esc focus returns to it.

The list for a generator kind or for effectors shows the presets built for it by the automation dropdown. Choosing a preset with parameters adds it at once. Choosing one without opens the generator or effector edit dialog with the module key and the structure's id, and it is added on confirmation. Cancelling adds nothing.

New automation goes in by the focused row: when it is itself a generator or effector, right after it under the same parent. For any other row, as its first child. With no focused row, at the top of the root. `before` is the row following that position.

On adding, the grid shows a temporary row with a negative id at that spot right away. Its text is, for an effector, the effector's label; for a generator 'Filter by {0}', 'Insert {0}', 'Extend with {0}', 'Group by {0}', 'Sort by {0}' by generator type, where {0} is the matching preset's label or else the generator's.

A new automation is sent by `POST /rest/structure/2.0/item/create` through the upload queue with: `forest` the panel's versioned spec, `version` updated to the current one at sending; `items`.`version` the current items version; `parameters` {}; `rowId`, `under`, `after`, `before`; and `item` {`type`: `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator` or `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`, `values`: {`moduleKey`, `params`}}. It waits while `under`, `after` or `before` is a temporary row or one with a pending upload. The answer's `itemId` is recorded and handed to the dialog's callback.

Dragging a new automation row whose creation has not been sent, or is waiting for a decision, changes its position in the pending request (and resets `parameters` to {}) and retries it, with `before` recomputed. Otherwise no move is made this way.

When a control marked for it (Pin, a filter or Save, transformation controls) is clicked while automation mode is on and history is not shown, the user is told: the first times, a popup at the Automation button says 'All additional structure transformations, such as sorting or filtering, are temporarily disabled when Automation Editing Mode is On.', with a button 'Got it' and the Automation button marked as in error till it hides. 'Got it' is remembered in this browser without expiry; afterwards the Automation button only flashes.

The Add Column panel has a text box (placeholder 'Search', at most 20 characters), the list, a 'Not found' line that shows only when a search finds nothing, and, on board and project pages but not in gadgets, the issue page or the Jira Software tab, a last entry 'Manage saved columns...'.

Groups are sorted by their order, then by title; presets are sorted by preset name. Each group that has presets gets a heading that cannot be selected, followed by its presets. Presets with no group, or a group that is not registered, go under the group that has no key. Column types whose metadata cannot be loaded contribute nothing. A preset with a description has it as tooltip.

Searching trims and lower-cases the text, and works on each change or key release. Group headings go away. Presets match when the name contains the text; the order is: exact name, then names starting with it, then the rest, in list order within each. Presets with the same column spec and name appear once. The selection stays when it is among the results, otherwise moves to the first result. Emptying the box brings the full list back.

Choosing a preset that is fully configured reports its column spec for adding. Choosing one that is not, or having no matching one, counts as cancelling. Choosing 'Manage saved columns...' reports that. Esc and Tab count as cancelling, also from the search box.

Each time the panel opens, the search box is emptied and takes focus, the selection is cleared and the list scrolls to the top. On closing, focus returns to where it was. The panel does not get narrower than at its first display.

In this list control Down selects the next visible item or, with none selected, the first. Up selects the previous visible item and does nothing with none selected or at the top. Enter chooses the selected item, and with none selected does nothing and lets the key pass. Moving the mouse over an item selects it, and clicking chooses it. The selected item is scrolled into view. Handled keys go no further.
Keys `s`,`q` open the Quick Actions box: a text box (placeholder 'Find <product> action...') with a list below it. It takes the keyboard focus. It closes when it loses focus (after 50 ms).

The box finds actions by name: an action's own title if it has one, else the text below for its grid action; an action with neither is not listed. The list is built once per page, from the widget's actions and those of the panel it first opened in; two actions with the same name raise an error. Names, each listed only if that action exists on the page: Toggle full screen mode; Undo; Redo; Toggle unresolved; Quick transformations; Toggle query; Switch panel; Hide all other panels; Show Secondary panel; Show Details; Show History; Add column; Select subtree; Deselect subtree; Select to the root; Collapse node; Expand node; Expand all; Collapse all; Expand next level; Collapse next level; Expand 1 level, Expand 2 levels ... Expand 8 levels; Next matching; Previous matching; Select; Select all; Copy; Cut; View thumbnails; Bulk change; Move item up; Move item down; Outdent item; Indent item; Delete subtree; Paste; Paste under; Edit; Create child; Create with dialog; Create under; Create; Create above; Create issue; Create folder; Search and Add; Add Confluence page; Edit next field; Edit previous field; Pin; Cancel issue edit; Cancel edit; Open issue; Actions drop-down; Assign issue; Edit issue; Assign issue to me; Comment issue; Manage views; Show shortcuts; Printable page; Export to Excel; Automation; Focus search; Toggle search filter; Swap panels; Run all effectors.

After a pause of 50 ms from a key release, with at least 2 characters typed, the list shows every action whose name contains the text, ignoring case, with the matching part in bold, the action's keyboard shortcut if it has one, and greyed if the action is currently unavailable. The first entry is selected. With fewer than 2 characters the list is empty.

In the box, Down and Up move the selection, wrapping at the ends and keeping it in view; Enter or a click runs the selected action, on the panel where the box was opened, closes the box and returns focus to where it was. An unavailable entry is run too (as the original does). Hovering an entry selects it.

The last search text of at least 2 characters, in lower case, is remembered in the browser. On the next opening it is filled in, selected and searched at once. Falling back below 2 characters clears what is remembered.

The pagination bar shows, left to right: back '<', page 1, a gap '…', the previous page, the current page, the next page, a gap '…', the last page, forward '>'. Page 1 shows when current index is above 1; the first gap above 2; the previous above 0; the next when below last-1 (0-based, with total pages N: index < N-1); the last when index < N-2; the last gap when index < N-3. Example: 10 pages, on the 5th: < 1 … 4 5 6 … 10 >.
The bar is shown only when there is more than one page: total pages = total records / page size, rounded up. Before the first answer it is hidden.

Back and forward go one page, stopping at the ends, and are disabled at those ends; forward also while the total is unknown. All buttons are disabled while loading, and the whole bar is disabled during that. Number buttons go to that page.

A page's records are requested once with offset = index × page size and count = page size, then cached with their scroll position, so going back shows them with no request and with the scroll where it was; a new page starts at the top. A failed page is not cached. Starting a new search goes to the first page and clears cache and scroll positions.

A paginated table posts to the URL given by its screen with content type `application/json; charset=UTF-8` and body {`startAt`,`maxResults`,`params`}. It reads `items` and `pagination.total`. It is used by the effector processes view, which claims the URL and columns.

Empty result: the message 'No records available'. Failure: the table's rows are removed and 'Failed to retrieve records from the server' is shown; the next load clears it. During a load the table and bar are in a loading state.

The loading spinner appears only if the wait lasts 500 ms, and once shown stays at least 500 ms; a wait that ends sooner shows no spinner at all. The control counts as busy until the spinner has gone.

The colour picker offers exactly, in this order: gray, blue, green, orange, red, purple. Initial value is the one given, or gray when that is missing or not one of these. A click on a colour selects it; with keyboard navigation turned on the colours can be tabbed to and Enter selects. While disabled nothing changes the value. Exactly one colour is marked as selected.

The tabbed dropdown is a searchable single-choice list with tabs at the top, used for choosing a saved column. The search placeholder is 'start typing...'. It opens on the tab holding the current value, or on the first tab. Clicking a tab shows that tab's options. Tab and Shift+Tab in the search box go to the next and previous tab, wrapping around.

When a tab has no options and nothing was typed it shows the text given by its screen, whose links open in a new window. When something was typed and nothing matches it shows 'No matches found', and Enter closes the dropdown.

Choosing an option sets the value and closes. When the screen installs a check, the dropdown closes first, the check runs, and the value is set only if it agrees. On closing, focus goes back to the trigger when there is one. A change of the value from outside updates the shown tab and choice. Near the window's edge the list shifts to stay on screen.

This tooltip appears 150 ms after the pointer or focus enters an element that has a tooltip text, and goes 300 ms after leaving. Moving from one such element to another, or onto the tooltip itself, within those 300 ms keeps it open, with the new content in the first case. Elements with no text show nothing. The text is HTML-escaped unless the element's text is declared to be HTML.
The tooltip opens 5 px below its element, left-aligned to it, moved left so that it stays inside the nearest scrolling container, and has a scroll limit to the room left in that container.

At widget start the UI sends one `GET /rest/structure/2.0/automation` (timeout 30000 ms) and keeps the answer for the life of the widget; it is not refreshed. Any failure, including the timeout, is silent: the lists stay empty, both permission flags stay false, nothing is shown to the user, and code waiting for the registry is released as if the call had succeeded.

From the `/automation` answer the UI keeps each generator's `label`, `type`, `module`, `notConfigurable`, `group` and `presets`, and each effector's `label`, `module`, `title` and `icon`. Generators are sorted by `label`, effectors by `label`, and all presets of all generators are flattened into one list sorted by `label` (plain string order, so case-sensitive; the server's order is not kept). Each preset's `params` string is parsed as JSON, and a preset takes `type` and `module` from its generator. Lookups by kind return the whole list when no kind is given.

`generatorConfigurationAllowed` and `effectorConfigurationAllowed` from `/automation` decide whether generators and effectors count as accessible to the user; a missing flag or a failed call means not accessible.

The UI knows five generator kinds in this fixed order: inserter, filter, sorter, grouper, extender. Their label, title and action texts are: Insert / 'Insert content under the currently selected item' / 'Insert…'; Filter / 'Filter content under the currently selected item' / 'Filter by…'; Sort / 'Sort content under the currently selected item' / 'Sort by…'; Group / 'Group content under the currently selected item' / 'Group by…'; Extend / 'Extend each item under the currently selected item' / 'Extend with…'. Each kind has its own icon.

A generator spec is recognised as a preset of its module as follows. A preset without params matches a spec with no or empty params. For a kind with platform parameters, these are compared leniently: grouper `level`, `includeGroups`; extender `from`, `to`; sorter `desc`, `from`, `to`, `locale`; filter `hard`, `showSubItems`, `pinnedItem`, `level`. On a copy of the spec's params, each platform parameter the preset defines is filled from the preset when absent, and each one the preset does not define is dropped; the copy must then deep-equal the preset's params. Inserters have no platform parameters and need exact deep equality. The first match in the generator's preset order wins. For example a sorter spec with params {attribute X, desc: true, from: 2} matches a preset {attribute X, desc: false} only if the values of the other keys are equal, so `desc: true` against `desc: false` does not match, but an absent `desc` does.

The label of a generator spec is worked out in this order: a spec without `module` gives a rejected answer with null; a spec matching a preset gets the preset's label; a module with a registered generator descriptor gets that descriptor's suggested label, as a value or a promise; a module without a descriptor gives a rejected answer with null. Registered factories run first, on the first request for a label or an effector name.

Descriptor factories registered through the public automation registry of the browser-side API are held in one list for the whole page and that list is emptied the first time any widget asks for a label or effector name. A second widget on the same page therefore gets no descriptors and falls back to preset labels and kind labels (as the original does).

`addDescriptor` ignores a null descriptor. A descriptor without `moduleKey` throws `invalid module key <value>`. A generator descriptor whose module already has a generator descriptor throws `Descriptor for module "<key>" is already registered`. A descriptor that extends neither the browser-side API's generator descriptor nor its effector descriptor throws `Unsupported descriptor superclass for module "<key>".`. A second effector descriptor for the same module is not detected and replaces the first without an error (as the original does).

Asking for an effector's generated name with a missing module key or missing params, or for a module without an effector descriptor, gives a rejected answer with null; otherwise the descriptor's generated name is returned, as a value or a promise.

The plugin registers these generator labels. Fixed text: `grouper-version-name` 'Version Name'; `grouper-portfolio-parent` 'Parent Issue'; `grouper-tempo-account` 'Account'; `extender-portfolio-children` 'Child Issues'; `extender-agile` 'Stories under Epics'; `grouper-sprint` 'Sprint'; `sorter-manual` 'Manual'; `filter-sprint` 'Sprint'; `grouper-agile-epic` 'Epic'. Computed labels: `sorter-attribute`, `grouper-text`, `filter-attribute` (attribute), `sorter-agile-rank`, `extender-links`, `grouper-links`, `extender-subtasks`, `filter-text`, `filter-jql`, `filter-sjql`, `filter-by-field`, as the following claims state. Any other module gets the generic kind label.

Label of `extender-subtasks`: no params gives null. With a non-empty `typeIds` the UI reads Jira's `GET /rest/api/2/issuetype` (through the cached Jira configuration) and shows the names of the sub-task types whose id is listed, in Jira's order, joined by a comma without a space, for example `Sub-task,Review`. If none of them is found, or `typeIds` is empty or absent, the label is 'Sub-tasks'; if the call fails the label is also 'Sub-tasks'.

Label of `filter-by-field`: no params, no `fieldId` or no `fieldValues` gives null. Otherwise the UI waits for the Jira field list and for the option labels of the selected values (`POST /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field/options` with `fieldId` and `fieldValues`, only when values are selected). The label is `<field name>: <labels joined by ', '>`, or `<field name>: All` with no labels. When the field is not in Jira's field list the label is 'Selected field is no longer accessible'. A failure of either source rejects with null.

Label of `filter-text`, `filter-jql` and `filter-sjql`: the query text itself, taken from parameter `text`, `jql` or `sjql` respectively. The three module keys and these three query types map one to one; `text`, `jql` and `sjql` are the query type names used by the panel search.

Label of `sorter-attribute`, `grouper-text` and `filter-attribute`: no params or no `attribute` gives null. Otherwise, once attribute metadata is loaded, the label is the attribute registry's suggested label for the stored attribute spec.

Label of `extender-links` and `grouper-links`: no params or no `linkTypeId` gives null. Otherwise the UI reads Jira's `GET /rest/api/2/issueLinkType`, finds the type whose `id` equals `linkTypeId` as text, and shows its `inward` name when parameter `inward` is true and its `outward` name otherwise; an unknown type gives null, a failed call rejects with null. Only the legacy boolean `inward` is read, not the `direction` parameter the form stores, so a generator with direction `inward` or `any` shows the outward name (as the original does).

Label of `sorter-agile-rank`: no params or no `fieldId` gives null. Otherwise, once the Jira configuration is loaded, the label is the name of the agile rank field whose custom id equals `fieldId`, or null when there is none.

Opening the generator dialog sends `POST /secure/StructureGeneratorEdit.jspa` with the caller's parameters plus `atl_token`, and shows the answer in a Jira form dialog, which closes by itself when the server finishes it. The widget's callers pass `moduleKey`, optional `params` (JSON text) and one of `transform` or `quickTransform`, with `quickTransformName` for a quick transformation.

When the generator dialog is submitted successfully and the answer's `Content-Type` starts with `application/json` and has a body, the body is parsed and handed to the caller as the new parameters. Any other successful answer (an existing generator saved on the server) calls nothing. Parameters whose value is null are not removed from the parsed result, although the code tries to (as the original does).

The effector dialog sends `POST /secure/StructureEffectorEdit.jspa` in the same way. With a `structureId` and a result callback, a JSON answer goes to the callback, together with a run function when response header `X-Structure-Effector-Callback` is `run`; calling it with the new item opens the effector process dialog for that effector and structure. With `structureId` and `effectorId` and no callback, the header value `run` opens the process dialog right after the dialog closes. Otherwise the JSON answer goes to the callback alone.
Pressing Esc in a generator or effector dialog while the autocomplete list of a text area in it is open closes only that list; the dialog stays open.

A generator or effector menu arranges its entries in sections, one per `group` value of the entry. An entry without a group goes to section 300 when its `notConfigurable` is false, otherwise to section 200, which is where presets go. Sections are ordered by their key compared as text, so '10' (the filter-by-field generator, `group="10"`) comes before '200' (presets) and then '300' (configurable generators). Within a section the given order is kept.

Each menu entry shows its label, followed by `...` when it has no preset parameters, which tells the user it opens configuration. Its tooltip is the entry's description, or the label when there is none. Clicking an entry never follows a link; it calls the menu's handler with the entry's kind, module, label and parameters. When the list is empty no menu is built and the caller is told so.

A menu with two or more entries has a search box with the placeholder 'Search' at the top; a menu with one entry has none. Each time the menu opens the search text is cleared and the box takes the focus. Filtering runs at most once per 100 ms: a case-insensitive substring match on the entry text. Sections with no visible entry are hidden, the first enabled visible entry becomes the active one, and when the text is not empty and nothing matches 'Not found' is shown.

The generator menu of a kind lists all presets of that kind first, then every generator of that kind that has a non-empty label and is configurable. A kind with no generators at all gives an empty menu, even if it has presets. Non-configurable generators are offered only through their presets. The effector menu lists every effector with a non-empty label.

A transformation has one of the kinds `filter`, `sorter`, `grouper`, `extender` or `group`. The first four have these labels and action texts: Filter / 'Filter by...', Sort / 'Sort by...', Group / 'Group by...', Extend / 'Extend with...'. Each kind has its own icon. A generic transformation counts as configured when it has both a key and a module. Spec entries with the legacy keys `unresolved` and `assigned2me` are treated as filters.

A filter on `filter-text`, `filter-jql` or `filter-sjql` is edited through the panel's search box, never through a dialog. A query of type `text`, `jql` or `sjql` becomes the spec {key `filter`, module, params {<type>: query}} merged over the existing spec, so an old parameter of another type stays when the type changes. An empty query means no transformation (the filter is removed). While the query has an error, the spec stays as it was. A text filter and a JQL or S-JQL filter have different icons.

The dropdown of a sorter transformation starts with a two-button choice 'Ascending' / 'Descending'; the current direction comes from `params.desc` (absent means ascending). Choosing the other direction changes `params.desc` at once (true for descending), so the view is re-sorted without any further action, and the transformation's icon follows the direction.

Choosing an entry in a sorter's dropdown does not carry over the direction selected there, or the previous parameters, when the entry is a preset: the new transformation has exactly the preset's parameters, so a sorter set to Descending goes back to Ascending unless the preset says otherwise (as the original does).

A filter on `filter-by-field` counts as configured only when it has a `fieldId`. Choosing the generator itself in the Filter menu creates the chip and does not open the dialog; a configured chip can still be edited through 'Edit'. It uses a checkbox icon.

A configured Filter by field chip has a dropdown with a search box and a checkbox list of the field's values, at most 10 options per search, replacing the generator list. Checking a value appends it to `params.fieldValues`, unchecking removes it, and a clear action empties the list; each change updates the transformation at once, so the view is re-filtered. A value is never listed twice. Opening or focusing the dropdown puts the focus in the search box. When the transformation changes from elsewhere while the dropdown is closed, the list refreshes; while it is open, the refresh waits for it to close. Closing clears the search text.

An unconfigured Filter by field chip's dropdown shows a spinner while the list of fields loads with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field`. An empty answer shows 'No data found', a failed call 'Cannot load data'. Otherwise the fields are listed as an automation menu, with search when there are two or more. In all cases the spinner goes away and the Remove action is added below.

The field list is requested at most once per page: every later Filter by field chip reuses the first answer, and a failed first request is reused as well, so 'Cannot load data' stays until the page is reloaded (as the original does).

Each field from `GET /rest/structure/2.0/issue-field` becomes an entry labelled with its `label`, for a filter on `filter-by-field` with params {`fieldId`: the field's `id`, `fieldValues`: [], `keepNonIssues`: the text `true`}. Choosing it turns the chip into a configured one that keeps the same transformation id, and its dropdown opens 10 ms later.

Once Jira's field list is available (or has failed) the attribute picker gets one entry per non-custom Jira field that maps to a known system attribute, labelled with the Jira field name. Formats offered: number first for number fields, time for date and date-time fields, duration for duration fields, then text, HTML and order for all. A field with no mapping is skipped, with a logged warning unless it is `thumbnail`, `lastViewed`, `issuelinks` or `subtasks`.

Custom fields appear in the picker as one 'Custom Field...' attribute (id `customfield`) plus one preset per field, labelled with the field name, with params {`fieldId`: the numeric id}. Fields with a positive numeric id only get a preset. Fields of these eight custom types are left out entirely: `aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-attachment-indicator`, `-comments-indicator`, `-issue-count-progress`, `-progress`, `-status-category-progress`, `-story-points-progress`, `-type-allocation` and `-time-progress`.

The picker also offers these attributes. Listed as presets, any format: Attachments (`attachments`), Worklogs (`worklogs`), Issue Links (`issuelinkobjects`), Issue Links (Including System) (`allissuelinkobjects`), Remote Links (`remoteissuelinkobjects`), Sub-Tasks (`subtasks`), Parent Issue (`parent`), Epic Stories (`epicStories`), Item (`item`), Comments (`comments`), History (`history`). Listed as presets with primary format then text, HTML, order: Depth (`depth`, number), Item Type (`itemtype`, text), Sequential Index (`seq`, text), Status Category (`status-category`, text), Project Category (`project-category`, text), Last Comment (`comment`, text). Known but without a preset: Progress (`progress`, number), Work Logged (`worklogged`, duration), Notes (`itemProperty`, text).

The picker offers as presets: Version Start Date (`version-start`), Version Release Date (`version-release`), Sprint Start Date (`sprint-start`), Sprint End Date (`sprint-end`), each in time then text, HTML, order; and Version Description (`version-description`), Sprint Goal (`sprint-goal`), each in text, HTML, order.

The attribute registry also gets the sum, count, links count, user property, time in status, query match and formatted number attributes; a transition date attribute once the status configuration is available (skipped when it cannot be read); the formula attribute once saved columns and Jira fields are ready; and the Tempo work-logged and Tempo time-planned attributes, each only when the Tempo Timesheets or Tempo Planning API is enabled, after the user-picker permission check. When Tempo is absent these two simply do not exist.

The transformations banner holds the current transformations as chips in spec order, ending with an add button whose tooltip is 'Add structure transformation (it does not change how others see this structure)'. The button reads 'Add transformation' only while there are no transformations and no chip dropdown is open; otherwise it shows just its icon.

The add button opens a menu with Filter, Sort, Group and Extend, in that order. Choosing one hides the add button for 100 ms and adds an unconfigured chip of that kind, labelled 'Filter by...', 'Sort by...', 'Group by...' or 'Extend with...', whose dropdown opens 10 ms later. The spec does not change until a generator is chosen.

The UI remembers the previous spec when the panel moves between two different structures, or between a structure and a query. While that spec has transformations the add menu has one more entry, 'Previously selected transformations', at the end. Choosing it appends the previous spec's non-permanent transformations after the current ones, without their `id` and `quick` data; there is no check for duplicates. The entry is one element shared by all panels of the page, so in two-panel mode only the panel updated last shows it (as the original does).

The transformations button of the panel header has a tooltip only while the spec has at least one transformation. It reads 'You are viewing transformed structure:' followed by one line per chip that has a transformation id: its icon and its label. Without any such chip the tooltip is empty.

The banner has two closing actions. Hide ('Hide') only hides the banner and keeps the transformations in force. Remove ('Remove') hides it and replaces the spec's transformations with the permanent ones only; when a query filter was selected the panel's search box returns to search mode and the selected filter is dropped.

Chips can be reordered by dragging their handle, within the banner; the add button is not draggable. Starting a drag closes any open chip dropdown. Dropping moves the transformation in the spec to the new position, which changes the order in which transformations apply. Only configured chips have a drag handle.

After a reorder or a change of a chip the UI sends the chips' transformations to the spec. When the spec has a different number of transformations than the chips, those in the spec with no chip (matched by id) are put first, followed by the chips' transformations, so that none is lost.

When the panel's spec changes for a transformable spec (anything except a clipboard forest) and the banner is not itself changing it, the chips are rebuilt to match: a chip with the same transformation id is kept and updated, new ones are created, those no longer in the spec are removed, and a transformation of unknown kind gets no chip. A spec without transformations clears all chips. No rebuild happens when the chips already equal the spec, in order and content.

When the panel moves to a different base spec (another structure, another query type, another `type`), all chips are cleared, and the new spec's transformations are shown only after that spec's quick transformations have finished loading.

Spec transformations with the same `quick.group` show as one chip for the whole group, placed at the first member, when the group exists among the quick transformations and its members match it exactly, by count, order and quick id. Otherwise each member is shown as its own chip. A group chip shows the group's name and colour, its tooltip lists the members, and removing it removes every member from the spec.

While the toolbar's automation mode is on, the add button is disabled, chips cannot be dragged, each chip's remove control is hidden and each chip is marked disabled. Leaving automation mode restores them. A rebuild of the chips applies the current mode again.

Selecting a query filter chip makes it the panel's selected filter: any other selected filter is unselected, the search box leaves search mode, and takes the chip's query and query type, and the panel's filter mode is on. Unselecting it switches filter mode off. Only one query filter can be selected at a time, and the selection survives a rebuild of the chips for the chip with the same transformation id.

While a query filter chip is selected, a change in the search box of the query, the query type or the error state goes straight to that chip's transformation. When the search box turns filter mode on with a new query, a new selected chip is added for the given transformation and any previous selected chip is unselected.

'Save as Quick Transformation' on a chip (only when the panel is adminable) adds a quick transformation with the chip's kind, module and parameters, named with the chip's label, and replaces that transformation in the spec by the quick one, so it stays active and the chip becomes a quick chip.

A chip is one of four kinds. A quick chip stands for a quick transformation or a group: it has a remove control and no dropdown. A query filter chip is for `filter-text`, `filter-jql`, `filter-sjql`. An unconfigured Filter by field chip offers the list of fields. Every other chip is a configurable chip with a dropdown.

A chip's label is the quick name for a quick transformation, otherwise the suggested label of the generator spec. If the suggestion is rejected or null the label is the kind's label: Filter, Sort, Group or Extend. An empty text is kept as a valid label. The label is recalculated each time the transformation changes, and a long label gets a tooltip when it overflows.

Each change of a chip's transformation that has a module and parameters is written to the panel's spec at once: replacing the transformation with the chip's id when it has one, otherwise appending it and taking the id it was given. Non-quick and quick chips work the same; the view then reloads through the normal spec change.

A configurable chip's dropdown holds, from the top: the kind's own control (direction for sorters, values for Filter by field), the generator menu of that kind, and a footer with 'Edit' (not for non-configurable generators), 'Move to Group', 'Save as Quick Transformation', and 'Remove'. Edit, Move to Group and Save as Quick Transformation are shown only when the chip has a module; the last two also need the panel to be adminable, re-evaluated when the panel's structure information changes.

Choosing a preset or a query filter in a chip's dropdown replaces the transformation with the chosen one, keeping the chip's transformation id. A query filter is the exception: the old transformation is removed from the spec first and a new one created. A new query filter (without a query yet) is selected at once, so the user types its query in the search box, and its chip stays hidden until it has a query.

Choosing a generator without parameters that supports the dialog opens the generator dialog for that module with `transform=true` and without `params`; when the same module was already on the chip, nothing of its parameters is sent. On Apply the transformation gets the returned parameters and the chip's id, and the chip is added back to the banner if the closing dropdown had dropped it. Cancelling leaves things as they were, so a chip that had no module disappears.

'Edit' opens the generator dialog with `moduleKey`, `transform=true` and the current parameters as JSON in `params` (only when the chip has a transformation id). On Apply the returned parameters replace the current ones under the same id.
When a chip's dropdown closes and the chip has no module, the chip is removed. Opening a dropdown makes the add button lose its text, and closing it restores the text according to the state.
Removing a chip takes it and its dropdown off the banner, and removes its transformation (for a group chip all members) from the spec by id. A chip that never got an id only disappears.

A permanent transformation's chip does nothing when clicked and its remove control does not work; a permanent query filter has no remove control at all. Removing all transformations from the banner keeps permanent ones. A permanent transformation comes from the project page's forced project filter.

A query filter chip is a toggle button with an icon, a label and, unless permanent, a close control. It is shown only while its query is not empty. Clicking it, when not disabled and when the transformation has an id, selects or unselects it. If it is unselected with an empty query it is removed. Closing a selected chip also ends the panel's filter mode.

Clicking a quick chip in the banner has no effect apart from dropping the focus, with one exception: for a user who cannot administer the panel and a `filter-by-field` quick chip, the click makes the chip the user's own copy, as the action Copy on the quick button does (statistic suffix `click`).

An unconfigured Filter by field chip is labelled 'Filter by field'; its dropdown offers the field list and a footer with only 'Remove'. Choosing the `filter-by-field` entry from the Filter menu creates this chip and does not open a dialog; its dropdown opens 10 ms later.
The UI can open a chip's dropdown on request: the chip is first scrolled into view.

Whenever the panel's base spec changes, the quick transformations are reloaded: a spec with a structure sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms`, and an empty answer gives the default set. A spec without a structure (a query) gets the default set without a call. A failed call logs a warning and leaves the list empty, with no defaults and no message. An answer for a spec that is no longer current is ignored. Transformations changing within the same base spec cause no reload.

The default set, in order: 'Unresolved' (filter, `filter-jql`, `jql` = `resolution is empty`); 'Assigned to me' (filter, `filter-jql`, `jql` = `assignee = currentUser()`); 'By Assignee' (grouper, `grouper-field`, `fieldId` = `assignee`); 'By Status' (`grouper-field`, `status`); 'By Version' (`grouper-field`, `fixVersions`); 'Sub-tasks' (extender, `extender-subtasks`, empty params). Defaults are not stored until the user changes the list.

A new quick id is `<structure id>-<n>`, for a group `<structure id>-g-<n>`; without a structure the prefix is the literal `jql`. `n` is one more than the largest number found after the last `-` of all existing ids, group members included; ids without a number count as 0. So with structure 12 and ids `12-1`, `12-g-7`, `12-3`, the next id is `12-8`.

Every change of the list sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/quick-transforms` with the complete list as a JSON array, content type `application/json; charset=UTF-8`. A transformation entry has `key`, `module`, `params` and `quick` {`name`, `id`}; a group entry has `key` = `group`, `quick` {`name`, `id`, `color`} and `transforms`. There is no save without a structure. A failed save logs a warning and shows nothing to the user; the change stays on screen. The list is not reloaded after saving.

A quick transformation goes into the spec as `key`, `module`, `params` and `quick` {`id`, `name`}, and for a group member also `quick.group` = the group's quick id; a transformation's `id` and `permanent` are included when set.

The quick transformations banner shows one toggle button per top-level entry, in list order, each with an icon and the name, and a tooltip when the name overflows. A group's icon takes the group's colour while it is off; when it is on the button takes the colour as background. The icon of a transformation comes from its kind, as for chips.

Turning a quick button on appends its transformation to the spec, or all members of a group, in order; nothing is added if already active. Turning it off removes those transformations by id. An unknown quick id is ignored. Clicks on a disabled button are ignored.

10 ms after any spec change within the same base spec, the buttons follow the spec: a transformation in the spec with a `quick.id` turns that button on; a group's button is on only when its members are in the spec with that `quick.group`, in the same order. A button whose transformations left the spec turns off. This means undoing or editing transformations elsewhere keeps the buttons right.

After each sync, a spec transformation whose `quick.id` and group are unknown to this structure's list loses its `quick` data, and members of a group that no longer matches lose `quick.group` and act alone. If anything was changed the spec is rewritten. So a spec copied from another structure keeps working as ordinary transformations.

When the panel's structure information and the loaded quick transformations do not belong together, the group is collapsed and the buttons are cleared, until the right pair is available. A key that is not a number counts as 0 and matches a panel with no structure id.
The quick banner has the same two closing actions as the transformations banner. Hide ('Hide') keeps active quick transformations. Remove ('Remove') also turns all of them off.

When the panel is adminable, top-level buttons can be reordered by dragging their handle; dropping moves the entry and saves the list. Starting a drag closes any open quick menu. Dragging is off while a group is expanded.

When the panel is adminable each button has a chevron that opens its menu, marked pressed while the button is on. Quick transformation: 'Toggle', 'Edit', 'Move to Group', 'Delete'. Group: 'Toggle', 'Expand', 'Edit', 'Ungroup', 'Delete'. Expanded group: 'Toggle', 'Edit', 'Ungroup', 'Collapse', 'Delete'. Member inside an expanded group: 'Edit', 'Move Out', 'Delete'.

When the panel is not adminable, buttons can only be toggled and have no chevron and no drag handle, except `filter-by-field` quick transformations, which have a chevron with 'Toggle' and 'Copy'. Group buttons have no menu, so such a user cannot expand a group.

For a user who cannot administer the panel, a `filter-by-field` quick button separates click and double click: a click takes effect 400 ms later and toggles the button; a second click within that time cancels it and makes the user's own copy, statistic suffix `dblclick`. This handling does not check whether the button is disabled, so a click toggles it even in automation mode or history view (as the original does).

Copy makes a quick Filter by field editable by the user. If the quick transformation is in the spec, its chip becomes a normal chip with the same parameters and the quick button turns off; otherwise a new normal chip is added with its parameters. The transformations banner is then shown and 250 ms later the chip's dropdown opens. The UI records the local statistic `filterByField.transform.own` and, for click and double click, `filterByField.transform.own.click` or `.dblclick` (`POST /statistics/record`).

Edit opens the generator dialog with `quickTransform=true`, `moduleKey`, `params` as JSON and `quickTransformName`. On Apply the returned `quickTransformName` becomes the name, and everything returned except `quickTransform` and `quickTransformName` becomes the parameters. The list is saved, the button's name and icon are updated, and if the quick transformation is on, the spec's transformation is updated under its id.
Delete removes the entry from the list without confirmation, saves, removes the button and, when it was on, removes its transformations from the spec. Deleting an expanded group first collapses it.

Saving a transformation as quick works only when the panel is adminable: the new entry has the given name and a new quick id, goes at the end of the list, gets a button, and if the source transformation has a spec id, it is replaced in the spec. A quick filter from the search box's 'save as' is created this way after the generator dialog with `quickTransform=true`.

While the toolbar's automation mode is on or the history view is visible, all quick buttons and chevrons are disabled, and dragging is off, including inside an expanded group. The state applies also to buttons built later.

Actions: 'q' then 'q' shows or hides the quick banner. 'q' then a digit 1 to 9, also on the numeric keypad, toggles the top-level entry at that position, if it has an id; on a disabled button nothing happens. 'r' then 'r' toggles the first top-level quick transformation on `filter-jql` with exactly the JQL `resolution is empty`; without one it does nothing.

Expand replaces the group's button with an expanded box in the same place: the group's name with its icon, one button per member (each with its own menu and drag handle when adminable), or 'Group is empty.' when it has no members, and a dropdown button with the group's menu. Only one group is expanded at a time; expanding another collapses the first. Collapse brings the single button back. The expansion resets when the structure changes.

Clicking the group's name in the expanded box toggles the whole group. While it is on the box is highlighted in the group's colour, and all member buttons look pressed. Members cannot be toggled one by one.
Dragging a member within an expanded group changes the order of the group, saved at once; when the group is on, the spec's transformations follow the new order.

In an expanded group: Edit opens the generator dialog for the member, with its name, and saves the changed member in the group. Move Out takes the member out of the group and appends it at the end of the top-level list. Delete removes it from the group. Each action saves the list and rebuilds the buttons.
Ungroup moves all members of a non-empty group to the end of the top-level list, in order, and the group stays in the list, empty. Nothing happens for an empty group.

Saving a group applies each member's change: added members get a new quick id and lose their spec id; moved-in ones leave the top level; moved-out ones are appended to the top level; deleted ones disappear; others stay. The group's name and colour change only if given. A new group goes at the end of the list. The list is then saved, the group counts as most recently used, and the buttons are rebuilt.

After a group change the spec follows. Group on, no member moved in, or an active one moved in: the group's entries in the spec are replaced in place by all current members in the new order, followed by members just moved out, which stay active on their own. Group on and an inactive transformation moved in: the group's transformations leave the spec, so the group turns off. Group off and an active transformation moved in: that transformation leaves the spec. A chip moved into a group from the transformations banner always leaves the spec as a chip.
Hovering a group's name shows the group's name with one line per member: its icon and name. An empty group shows 'Group is empty'.

'Edit' on a group opens a modal 'Group Settings' with: 'Name' prefilled, 'Color' with the colour picker on the group's colour, and the member list. The footer has 'Ungroup' at the left, shown only for a non-empty group, then 'Save' and 'Cancel'.

'Move to Group' opens a modal 'Add to group' with the text 'You can add the transformation to an existing group or create a new one.', a 'Group' selector with the placeholder 'Choose group or create a new one', and 'Add' and 'Cancel'. Choosing an existing group shows its members plus the new one. Choosing 'Create New Group' also shows 'Name' (empty) and 'Color' (no colour chosen), above the list with only the new member.

The selector lists the existing groups, each with its name and colour, most recently used first, then 'Create New Group'. A value clears the selector's error. Choosing another entry rebuilds the lower part of the dialog.

Save or Add with an empty name shows 'Please enter group name' and keeps the dialog open; Add with no group chosen shows 'Please choose a group or create a new one'. The name error clears only on the next attempt.

Each member row shows a drag handle, icon and name, with a tooltip when the name overflows. Rows can be reordered by dragging or the keyboard, and the new order is what is saved. In 'Add to group', existing members are shown as disabled, and rows have no action menu. In 'Group Settings' each row has a menu titled 'Transformation Actions' with 'Move Out' and 'Delete'.

Choosing an action on a row marks it disabled, hides its menu and shows a warning text: 'Move out of the group.' or 'Delete from structure.'. Nothing is applied until Save. An action cannot be undone in the dialog except by Cancel. 'Ungroup' applies Move Out to every row.

In a group dialog Enter saves and Esc closes, unless the focus is on a button or a row's action button. With the focus on a row: Enter opens that row's menu and moves the focus into it (a row with no menu saves the dialog), Left or Up moves the row up one place, Right or Down moves it down one, and the focus stays on the row. In the row menu Enter runs the action and Esc closes it, each returning the focus to the row. The dialogs ignore Jira's keyboard shortcuts.

Save or Add applies the change through the group saving rules and closes the dialog. Cancel closes it with no change. A chip from the transformations banner (it has a spec id and no quick id) is added as a new quick transformation; an existing quick transformation is moved in.

Groups in the selector are ordered: both not recently used, by name in locale order; both recently used, most recent first; recent against not recent, the recent one first. The most recent group, compared with a group that is not recent, is treated as equal, so it may stay behind it (as the original does).

The last 5 used groups are remembered per panel and per structure (or query type) in the user's stored widget settings, most recent first. Using the group that is already first changes nothing. Ids that no longer exist are simply ignored. The list is read again whenever the quick transformations are loaded.

The generator dialog's form (`StructureGeneratorEdit`) has the descriptor's title as its heading, the width of C-5368 and posts to `StructureGeneratorEdit!apply.jspa`, with hidden fields `atl_token`, `execute` = true, `generatorId`, `moduleKey`, `quickTransform` and `transform`. Below the heading comes a name or run-as field, then the generator's form, then 'Apply' (submit) and 'Cancel' (closes the dialog). Leaving the dialog with unsaved changes gives no browser warning.

For a quick transformation the first field is 'Name', marked required, a single-line text field with the given `quickTransformName`, or empty, posted as `quickTransformName`; its error shows below it. 'Runs As' is then not shown.

Otherwise the first field is 'Runs As'. With a run-as user it shows a small avatar and the user's display name linking to `/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<name>`, with Jira's user hover; an inactive user reads `<display name> (Inactive)`. The avatar is `/secure/useravatar?ownerId=<key>&size=small&ts=<timestamp>`. With no such user the field stays empty.

The error content of the generator dialog is the heading of Jira's text for `common.words.error` ('Error') and one error message box for each message, with no form and no buttons of its own.

The Manage Views dialog is created on first use per panel and has two pages that share one window: a selection page and a details page. Opened from the entry 'Manage Views...' of the view menu it shows the selection page; opened from the sharing 'Change' action it shows the details page of the panel's current view. Every opening selects the first tab ('Current') of the selection page, loads the requested view if any, re-reads the list of the visible tab, and moves keyboard focus to the first button in the dialog.

Opening the details page of the current view from the sharing 'Change' action asks for the Sharing tab, but the request names the tab without the panel's prefix, so no tab matches and the details page opens on whichever tab was active before (Properties on first use) (as the original does).

The selection page has the heading 'Manage Structure Views', four tabs and a 'Close' button. Tabs, each with a heading and a one-sentence explanation above its list, except Search: 'Current' (heading 'Current View', says this is the view in use: 'This is the currently used view.'), 'Managed' (heading 'Managed Views', says these are views you created or can manage), 'Associated' (heading 'Associated Views', says these are the views selected in the View Settings of the displayed structure and offered in its menu), 'Search'.

What each selection tab lists. Current: only the panel's current view; nothing when there is none or when it is the fallback view with id -1. Managed: `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view?withPermissions=true&withOwner=true&permission=admin`. Associated: `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/menu?forPage=<page id>&forStructure=<structure id>` for the panel's structure (the `forStructure` parameter is left out when the panel shows something that has no numeric structure id; a negative id or no panel content gives an empty list without a request). Answers are cached in the page by the view loader until a view is saved or deleted.

Each selection tab reloads its list when it becomes the active tab, when the dialog opens, and when the panel's current view configuration changes while the selection page is visible. A reload requested while that tab's previous reload is still running is ignored. On dialog opening and on a configuration change the list is redrawn even if the answer is identical, so the check marks and adjusted marks are always current.

A tab with nothing to list shows 'No views to show.'. This covers a null answer (including a failed Managed, search or all-views request) and an empty answer. The Search tab shows an empty area, with no message, before any search and when searched with blank text.

Each row of a selection list shows, in order: a check mark for the panel's current view (with the tooltip 'This is the current view'; other rows keep the space with no mark or tooltip), a sharing icon, the view name as a link, a '*' with the tooltip 'You have adjusted this view and the changes have not been saved on the server yet.' when the view has unsaved adjustments that count as modifications, and the description below (blank line when there is none). Entries without an id are skipped.

The sharing icon of a row depends on the view's `shared` and `sharedWithAll`: `sharedWithAll` true shows a group icon with the tooltip 'Shared with everyone'; `shared` true otherwise shows a people icon with the tooltip 'Shared with some users'; not shared shows no icon and no tooltip.

A 'Details >' button in a selection row is visible only on the row the mouse last entered (it stays visible after the mouse leaves until another row is entered). Clicking the button, or clicking anywhere on the row except a link or a button, opens the details page of that view on its first tab (Properties). Clicking the name link switches the panel to that view through the view-switching action and leaves the dialog open.

The Search tab has a text field 'Find View' with the hint 'Enter view name (or a part of it).', a submit button 'Search' and a button 'Show All Views'. Submitting (button or Enter) trims the text: blank text clears the list without a request, other text searches through `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view?name=<URL-encoded text as typed, trimmed>`. 'Show All Views' empties the text field and lists `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view?withPermissions=true&withOwner=true`. When the Search tab is re-entered it repeats the last mode: all views after 'Show All Views', else a search with the text in the field.

The details page has the heading 'View Details', a summary, five tabs and a footer. The summary shows 'View:' with the view name and description, and 'Access:' with a sentence. The tabs are, in order: 'Properties', 'Sharing', 'Associations', 'Advanced', 'Delete'. The footer holds '< Back to View List', 'Save Changes' and a Cancel or Close link.

The 'Access:' line of the details page reads, from the view's flags: `adminable` true: 'Manage - you can change all properties of this view'; else `writable` true: 'Update - you can change this view's columns but you cannot change other properties'; else 'Use - you can use this view but you cannot update it'. The first word is emphasised. While no view is loaded the name and the access line show '?' and the description is empty.

Opening details asks for `GET /rest/structure/1.0/view/<id>?withPermissions=true&withOwner=true`, unless full details of that view are already cached in the page. The page shows no view data until the answer arrives and drops an answer for a view other than the last requested one. A failed request leaves the summary at '?' with all fields empty and disabled.
